    datamunge/algorithms/addition_chain.hpp

    Functions

    binary_chain()The left-to-right binary ("square-and-multiply") chain for e: one doubling per bit below the leading one, plus one step for each further 1 bit, so its length is \(\lfloor\log_2 e\rfloor + \nu(e) - 1\) with \(\nu\) the number of 1 bits.
    chain_lower_bound()A proven lower bound on the length \(\ell(e)\) of the shortest chain: \(\lambda(e) + [\nu(e)\ge 2] + [\nu(e)\ge 3]\), with \(\lambda(e)=\lfloor\log_2 e\rfloor\).
    chain_steps()For each term after the first, the indices (i, j), i >= j, of two earlier terms that sum to it: the multiplications \(x^{c_k}=x^{c_i}x^{c_j}\) to perform.
    is_addition_chain()true if chain starts at 1, increases strictly, and every later term is the sum of two earlier terms.
    mod_pow_chain()\(x^{e} \bmod m\) for the last term e of chain, using one modular multiplication per chain step (128-bit products, so any modulus up to \(2^{64}-1\) works).
    window_chain()The left-to-right sliding-window chain for e with windows of up to k bits.

    datamunge/algorithms/aho_corasick.hpp

    Classes

    AhoCorasickAn Aho-Corasick automaton compiled once from a dictionary and reused for many texts.
    AhoCorasickMatchOne reported occurrence: pattern pattern_index occurs in the text starting at position (a zero-based index into the searched text).
    AhoCorasickScanStatsWork done by one scan of AhoCorasick::scan_stats(): characters read, goto (trie) edges taken, failure links followed, dictionary links visited and matches reported.

    Functions

    aho_corasick_search()The Aho-Corasick multi-pattern string-matching algorithm (Aho & Corasick 1975). Given a text and a whole set of patterns, it finds every occurrence of every pattern in a single left-to-right pass over the text, rather than running a separate single-pattern search per pattern (which would cost O(|text| * #patterns)).

    datamunge/algorithms/aks.hpp

    Classes

    AksTraceWhat each step of the AKS test found for one n; see aks_trace().

    Functions

    aks_congruence_holds()true if \((x+a)^n \equiv x^{n} + a\) in \((\mathbb Z/n)[x]/(x^r-1)\).
    aks_power()The coefficients \(c_0,\dots,c_{r-1}\) of \((x+a)^n\) in \((\mathbb Z/n)[x]/(x^r-1)\), by repeated squaring: \(O(r^2\log n)\) coefficient operations.
    aks_r()The AKS modulus: the least r with \(\gcd(n,r)=1\) and \(\operatorname{ord}_r(n) > (\log_2 n)^2\), or the least r reaching n.
    aks_trace()Runs the AKS test on n and records how it reached its verdict.
    euler_totient()Euler's totient \(\varphi(n)\), the count of \(1\le k\le n\) coprime to n, by trial division ( \(O(\sqrt n)\)). \(\varphi(0)=0\).
    multiplicative_order()The multiplicative order of n modulo r: the least \(k\ge1\) with \(n^k\equiv1\pmod r\), or 0 when \(\gcd(n,r)\ne1\).
    perfect_power()If n is a perfect power \(b^e\) with \(e\ge2\), the pair (b, e) with the largest e; otherwise (n, 1).

    datamunge/algorithms/alignment_types.hpp

    Classes

    AlignmentOwned score and equal-length gapped rows from a pairwise byte alignment. A '-' denotes an inserted gap; to recover inputs unambiguously their literal alphabet must exclude '-'. Global results cover whole inputs; local results may cover substrings. No input or callable references are retained.
    AlignmentScoringSymmetric linear-gap integer scores, with no affine gap-open term. match scores equal bytes, mismatch unequal bytes, gap one byte against a gap. Defaults2,-1,-2. Specific algorithms validate their own arithmetic/input domains. Positive gap scores are representable but may favor opposing inserted gaps.

    datamunge/algorithms/arc_consistency.hpp

    Classes

    Ac3ResultThe result of running AC-3: the (possibly reduced) variable domains and whether the network is still consistent (no domain was emptied).

    Functions

    ac3()The AC-3 algorithm (Mackworth, 1977) for enforcing arc consistency in a binary constraint-satisfaction problem. A directed arc (i,j) is consistent when every value in variable i's domain has at least one supporting value in j's domain that satisfies the constraint. AC-3 keeps a worklist of arcs; it repeatedly revises an arc, deleting unsupported values from i's domain, and whenever a domain shrinks it re-queues the arcs pointing into i (their support may have vanished). It runs in O(e·d^3) and is the standard constraint-propagation step inside CSP solvers – pruning the search space before (and during) backtracking, sometimes solving the problem outright.

    datamunge/algorithms/arithmetic_extra.hpp

    Functions

    addition_chain()Addition-chain exponentiation: computes x^e using a short addition chain – a sequence 1=c_0,c_1,\dots,c_L=e in which each term is a sum of two earlier terms, so each corresponds to one multiplication. The shortest chain minimizes the multiplications needed for x^e (fewer than the standard binary square-and-multiply for many exponents, e.g. x^{15} in 5 rather than 6). This routine returns a chain: the binary-method chain for general e, refined by a bounded search that finds a provably shortest chain for small e.

    datamunge/algorithms/association_rules.hpp

    Classes

    AprioriLevelWork done by Apriori at one itemset size \(k\).
    AssociationRuleAn association rule \(A \Rightarrow C\) with its quality metrics.
    FrequentItemsetA set of items found frequent, with the number of transactions containing it.
    TransactionDataTransactions built from table rows, with a label for every item id.

    Functions

    apriori_frequent_itemsets()Apriori: level-wise frequent-itemset mining with downward-closure pruning.
    apriori_levels()The per-level work of apriori_frequent_itemsets(): joined, counted and frequent candidates.
    association_rules()Generate association rules from a set of frequent itemsets.
    eclat_frequent_itemsets()Eclat: canonical frequent sets from conditional sorted tidset intersections.
    encode_transactions()One transaction per row of data, one item per non-null cell of columns.
    fp_growth_frequent_itemsets()Mine canonical positive-support patterns from shared FP-tree prefixes. Baskets are sets: sort and deduplicate each without changing the caller. Empty/repeated rows retain their identities; IDs are opaque size_t including SIZE_MAX. No empty itemset is returned. Positive thresholds return all sets whose row count meets the threshold; above N returns none. Threshold0 retains the historical positive-support-only FP behavior, unlike Apriori/Eclat0. Build order is support descending then ID ascending; mining order is support ascending then ID ascending. Explicit DFS preserves the original emit/base/ child-build/descent schedule without recursive call-stack depth. No single-path shortcut, Apriori candidate join or extra database scan per candidate is used. Output can have exponentially many sets and item IDs. Sorting, hash operations, conditional rebuilding and output copying remain real work; no universal compression/runtime guarantee. Independent calls share no mutable state. Counts/capacities are checked; errors return no partial result.
    itemset_label()Text for an itemset, such as {Sex=female, Pclass=1}.
    rule_improvements()Improvement of each rule over its simpler versions (Bayardo, Agrawal & Gunopulos 1999).

    datamunge/algorithms/automaton.hpp

    Classes

    DFAOwned deterministic finite automaton with optional missing transitions/start. delta has num_states rows of num_symbols entries, and accept has num_states bytes. Each target is -1 or a valid state. -1 denotes an implicit rejecting sink, which loops on all symbols; start=-1 denotes the empty language. A zero-state DFA requires start=-1. Zero symbols permits only the empty word. Aggregate field order/types remain unchanged; default construction is now a valid empty zero-alphabet machine. Containers own their storage. Read-only calls share no mutable state, provided the aggregate is not concurrently changed.
    NFAOwned epsilon-free nondeterministic finite automaton, possibly with multiple initial states. States/symbols are contiguous integer labels. delta has num_states rows of num_symbols destination lists; accept has one byte per state, nonzero meaning accepting. Duplicate destinations/starts are allowed. No epsilon transitions are represented. Zero states with empty starts accepts no words. Aggregate field order/types are unchanged; default construction now denotes that empty zero-alphabet machine. Containers own their storage; concurrent read-only use is permitted if nobody mutates the aggregate.

    Functions

    dfa_accepts()Run a validated DFA on integer symbols, treating -1 as a rejecting sink. Validates the entire machine and entire word before simulation, including symbols after an eventual missing move. Empty input tests the explicit start's acceptance, or rejects for start=-1. O(states*(symbols+1)+word length) work, O(1) auxiliary storage, with no allocation, borrowed result or mutation.
    validate_dfa()Check the complete shape and every index of a possibly partial DFA. Requires nonnegative counts, exact row/flag dimensions and targets/start in {-1,0,...,num_states-1}. For zero states the only valid start is -1. Nonzero acceptance bytes are accepted. O(states*(symbols+1)) work and O(1) storage, with no allocation, repair or input/shared-state mutation.
    validate_nfa()Check the complete shape and every index of an epsilon-free NFA. Accepts duplicates, nonzero acceptance bytes, empty starts and zero symbols. Requires nonnegative counts, exact row/flag dimensions, and valid explicit start/destination indices. O(states+symbols*states+listed destinations+starts) work, O(1) auxiliary storage, without allocation, repair or mutation.

    datamunge/algorithms/automaton_operations.hpp

    Classes

    DFAEquivalenceResultExact whole-language comparison result, optionally with a shortest counterexample. equivalent=true means all reachable product pairs were exhausted, not a bounded word test. If false, witness is a shortest distinguishing word, lexicographically first among that length; an empty witness then denotes epsilon. No witness is provided when equivalent=true. Counters include the implicit rejecting sinks when reached. Containers own their storage.

    Functions

    complete_dfa()Materialise an implicit rejecting sink when any move or the start is -1. Retains all original states, acceptance bytes and numbering, including unreachable states; it does not minimise. Adds one fresh rejecting self-loop state only when needed and redirects missing entries/start there. A valid zero-state machine therefore becomes one rejecting state. O(n*(k+1)) work and owned output storage, without input/shared-state mutation.
    dfa_equivalence()Decide exact DFA language equivalence with sparse BFS over reachable state pairs. Requires the same indexed alphabet size. Each missing move/start behaves as an implicit rejecting sink. A mismatch yields a shortest differing word, with ascending-symbol lexicographic ties; epsilon can distinguish the starts. Otherwise exhausting the finite product proves equivalence for every word. For P reached pairs and alphabet size k, O(input sizes+k*P*log(P+1)) work and O(P) auxiliary storage, rather than preallocating the full Cartesian product. Inputs are borrowed only during the call; no shared/input data are changed. A positive pair budget throws before discovering an excess pair, never returning a truncated search as equivalent. Zero (default) is unlimited.
    dfa_reachable_states()List reachable explicit DFA states in BFS order, scanning symbols ascending. Missing targets and the implicit sink are not returned. start=-1 yields an empty list. O(n*(k+1)) work including validation and O(n) auxiliary/output storage. Inputs are borrowed only for the call and never modified.
    reverse_dfa()Reverse every explicit DFA edge and swap initial/accepting roles into an NFA. Multiple accepting states become starts in ascending state order; the old explicit start is the sole accepting state. Missing moves are omitted, and start=-1 yields no accepting NFA state. Represents exactly the reversed word language, without epsilon transitions. O(n*(k+1)) work/storage for n states and k symbols. Validates before allocation, borrows only during the call and returns owned containers, without input/shared-state mutation.

    datamunge/algorithms/bellman_ford.hpp

    Classes

    BellmanFordResultResult of bellman_ford() and bellman_ford_queue().

    Functions

    bellman_ford()The Bellman-Ford single-source shortest-path algorithm (Bellman 1958; Ford 1956). Given a weighted directed graph – a vertex count n and an edge list of (from, to, weight) triples whose weights may be negative – it computes the shortest path weight from source to every vertex. Unlike Dijkstra's algorithm it tolerates negative edge weights, and it detects a negative-weight cycle reachable from the source (a cycle around which one may loop to drive path weights to (-\infty), so no shortest path exists). It works by relaxation: repeatedly, for every edge ((u,v,w)), replacing (d[v]) with (d[u]+w) whenever that is smaller. After (n-1) full passes over the edge list every true shortest path – which uses at most (n-1) edges when no negative cycle exists – has been found; one further pass that can still relax an edge proves a reachable negative cycle exists.
    bellman_ford_queue()Queue-based Bellman-Ford (Moore 1959; often called SPFA): only the out-edges of vertices whose distance fell in the previous round are examined.
    shortest_path_to()Vertices of the path from the source to target, read from the predecessor tree; empty if target is unreachable or the tree is broken by a negative cycle.

    datamunge/algorithms/bilinear_interpolation.hpp

    Functions

    bilinear_interpolate()Interpolate a rectangular grid by two successive linear blends. Rectilinear axes may be unevenly spaced. Values use x-major layout: z[i*ys.size()+j] belongs to (xs[i],ys[j]). Reproduces a+b*x+c*y+d*x*y up to floating error. Queries outside either axis extrapolate using the nearest end cell; they are not clamped. Inside a cell, the four nonnegative corner weights sum to one, so the result remains in the corner-value range. Validation costs O(nx+ny+nx*ny) per call, followed by binary cell lookup and constant arithmetic; O(1) auxiliary storage, no mutation or shared state. Comparable to SciPy RegularGridInterpolator(method="linear", bounds_error=false, fill_value=None), restricted to two increasing axes and finite real data.

    datamunge/algorithms/binary_gcd.hpp

    Classes

    BinaryGcdStepOne binary-GCD subtraction after removing twos and ordering the odd operands. Values are exact unsigned integers. The next state is (smaller_odd,difference).
    BinaryGcdTraceOwned result and chronological subtraction states from the canonical binary-GCD loop. Zero-input cases return no steps, zero common_twos and zero initial_odd_a. Otherwise gcd equals the final smaller_odd shifted left by common_twos.

    Functions

    binary_gcd()Compute a greatest common divisor using Stein's shifts and subtractions. Supports the entire uint64_t range without division, multiplication or overflow. gcd(0,b)=b, gcd(a,0)=a, and gcd(0,0)=0. Count-trailing-zero operations are used only on nonzero words. For w-bit operands, O(w) word operations and O(1) auxiliary storage; this is not a multiprecision bit-complexity claim. Inputs are values, no shared state is mutated, and no allocation is performed.
    binary_gcd_trace()Record the same binary-GCD loop used by binary_gcd(), without report-side replay. Trace states are exact; removed_twos refers to the second operand before the optional swap. O(w) word operations and O(w) owned trace storage for w-bit inputs. Zero-input cases return the direct answer with no subtraction states.

    datamunge/algorithms/binary_search.hpp

    Classes

    BinarySearchProbeOne midpoint inspection of a closed binary-search interval. Values are snapshots before either bound is updated. No input pointer is retained.
    BinarySearchTraceOwned search answer and the chronological snapshots from the same binary-search loop. Empty inputs have an empty probe list. result.probes equals probes.size().

    Functions

    binary_search()Find an integer key by repeatedly halving a closed interval of a sorted vector. Precondition: a is sorted in nondecreasing order; sortedness is not checked. Returns the first equal midpoint encountered, which need not be the first or last occurrence of a duplicate key. Empty input returns an absent result with zero probes. Uses at most floor(log2(n))+1 element inspections for n>0, O(log(n+1)) word work and O(1) auxiliary storage. No allocation, mutation or shared state; concurrent reads require that the input remain unmodified.
    binary_search_trace()Record midpoint values and closed candidate intervals in binary_search(). Uses the same canonical loop and duplicate-key choice as the unrecorded call. Sortedness remains a precondition. O(log(n+1)) word work and owned trace storage; no input pointers survive the call. Empty input records no probes.

    datamunge/algorithms/binary_splitting.hpp

    Classes

    BinSplitNodeOne owned node of the balanced exponential-series product tree. For q(0)=1 and q(k)=k otherwise, den is the product of q(k) over [begin,end). num/den equals the sum over k in that interval of 1/product(q(j),j=begin..k). This is a normalised subtree, not generally the original sum of 1/k! there. Children are indices into the owning trace's postorder node vector; leaves use -1.
    BinSplitResultExact, possibly unreduced exponential-series fraction and its double conversion. num and den are owned unsigned integers; value rounds the ratio after converting both integers to double. Equality to a rounded exp(1) is not exact equality to e.
    BinSplitTraceExact result and owned postorder tree from the canonical binary-splitting routine. The last node is the root. N effective terms give N leaves and 2N-1 nodes. No pointers into inputs or shared mutable state survive the call.

    Functions

    binary_splitting_e()Evaluate sum(k=0..N-1,1/k!) exactly as an unreduced uint64 fraction. N is max(1,terms), preserving the historical lower clamp. N must be at most 21: the root numerator and denominator both fit uint64 through N=21; the raw denominator 21! for N=22 does not. The count is checked before recursion. Every merge uses P=P_left*Q_right+P_right and Q=Q_left*Q_right on normalised subtrees. Only the root represents the original factorial series. No reduction or multiprecision arithmetic is performed. O(N) fixed-word operations and O(log(N+1)) stack storage; no allocation, mutation or shared state.
    binary_splitting_e_trace()Record the same balanced exponential-series tree as binary_splitting_e(). Uses identical fractions and the same [1,21] effective term domain. Recording adds O(N) owned storage; the unrecorded routine retains only its recursion stack.

    datamunge/algorithms/birkhoff_interpolation.hpp

    Classes

    BirkhoffConstraintOne condition p^(order)(node)=value for ascending polynomial coefficients. Derivative orders at a node may have gaps. Orders above the proposed degree produce zero matrix rows and cannot establish uniqueness.

    Functions

    birkhoff_eval()Evaluate ascending polynomial coefficients with Horner's rule. Empty coefficients represent zero. O(N) work and constant auxiliary storage; no mutation or shared state. Finite input can still overflow.
    birkhoff_eval_derivative()Evaluate a derivative directly from ascending polynomial coefficients. Uses Horner evaluation of derivative coefficients. Order zero gives the polynomial value. Orders above the degree and empty vectors give zero after validation. O(N*(order+1)) work and constant auxiliary storage; no mutation or shared state. Results retain the corresponding derivative units.
    birkhoff_matrix()Assemble the square derivative-monomial system for Birkhoff interpolation. N constraints give an N-by-N nested vector, with columns for 1,x,...,x^(N-1). Empty input returns an empty matrix. Values are validated but omitted from the matrix. O(N^2) storage and up to O(N^3) work for falling factorials; no mutation or shared state.
    birkhoff_polynomial()Find a polynomial of degree at most N-1 satisfying N derivative conditions. Derivative orders may have gaps. Equilibrates rows and columns of birkhoff_matrix(), then applies pivoted Gauss–Jordan elimination. Pivots at most 64*N*epsilon on the equilibrated matrix are treated as numerically singular. Empty input or numerical singularity returns empty, whether a singular system has no solution or infinitely many. A nonempty result is not a proof of mathematical poisedness or good conditioning. Coefficients are restored to the original monomial units, lowest degree first. O(N^3) time, O(N^2) storage, no mutation or shared state.

    datamunge/algorithms/bisection.hpp

    Classes

    BisectionOptionsIndependent stopping controls for a recorded bisection search. Position tolerance has x's units; residual tolerance has f(x)'s units. A zero residual tolerance disables that test, while callback zeros still stop.
    BisectionStepPre-update bracket, callback values and midpoint from one bisection iteration. Records numerical values without retaining the callback. Endpoint signs are opposite when this record is created. Radius is rounded max(midpoint-lower, upper-midpoint), accounting for midpoint rounding to a noncentral double.
    BisectionTraceOwned bisection result, stopping reason and chronological bracket snapshots. Terminal endpoints describe the bracket before the returned estimate's test; a zero endpoint collapses it. Radius is meaningful for evaluated estimates, and remains infinity for a same-sign rejected bracket. It is a rounded interval distance, not an independently certified floating-point interval bound.

    Functions

    bisection()Bisect a sign-changing bracket using the historical combined tolerance. Shares the recorded loop with bisection_trace(), using x_tolerance=tol and residual_tolerance=tol. A small residual can stop with a wide bracket; it is not generally a coordinate-error guarantee. Finite endpoints are ordered internally. Same-sign nonzero endpoints return the default unconverged result. A zero endpoint returns immediately. Continuity and reliable callback signs are caller assumptions. Finite discontinuities can pass the interval test. O(max_iter) callback calls and constant auxiliary storage, with no recording. No shared state; callback side effects and exceptions remain the caller's.
    bisection_stop_name()Return a stable name for a bisection stopping reason. The string view refers to a program-lifetime literal; no allocation or shared mutation.
    bisection_trace()Record canonical bisection with independent position and residual tolerances. Default options disable residual-based stopping. Stopping on a callback zero is retained. Continuity and trustworthy function evaluations are required to infer a root from the bracket; the routine cannot check those assumptions. Opposite signs are compared without multiplying callback values. Uses an overflow-safe midpoint and reports exhausted precision instead of repeating an endpoint indefinitely. Same-sign endpoints are an ordinary failed result. O(max_iterations) callback calls and owned trace storage; no input mutation or shared state. Callback side effects and exceptions remain the caller's.

    Types and constants

    BisectionStopenum Reason the canonical bisection loop stopped, distinct from a root certificate.

    datamunge/algorithms/bitap.hpp

    Classes

    BitapMatchOne fixed-length matching window with its actual Hamming distance. Indices are byte offsets in a half-open interval [begin,end). Empty-pattern matches have begin=end. Records own their numbers and retain no input pointers.
    BitapStepCanonical post-update Shift-And state after one consumed text byte. In states[d], bit j represents a pattern prefix of length j+1 matching the suffix ending at position with at most d substitutions. One means active; all recorded levels use the same convention. Only pattern-length bits are kept.
    BitapTraceOwned overlapping matches, chronological prefix states and exact scan-work counts. Empty patterns match every boundary but consume no bytes and record no steps. State storage is O(n*(k+1)); match storage is O(number of reported windows).

    Functions

    bitap_fuzzy_search()Find the first Hamming-close window with the historical inclusive-end interface. Allows substitutions only; windows have exactly pattern.size() bytes. Negative budgets mean zero; budgets above the pattern length cannot admit extra windows. Empty pattern returns the historical special value zero. Patterns longer than 62 bytes return -1. Uses the canonical loop; no state vector is recorded. O(n*(k+1)+m+256) word work with k capped at m; constant word-state storage. No mutation or shared state. Byte, case and encoding semantics match bitap_search().
    bitap_matches()Return all overlapping byte windows within a substitution budget. Supports patterns through 63 bytes. Empty patterns match all n+1 boundaries, with empty intervals and zero substitutions. For nonempty patterns, reports actual minimum substitutions even when the supplied budget is larger. Uses O(n*(k+1)+m+256) word work, fixed word-state storage and owned output storage. No input mutation, retained pointers or shared mutable state.
    bitap_search()Find the first exact bytewise occurrence with the historical start-index interface. Empty pattern returns zero. Patterns longer than 63 bytes return -1, the same sentinel as a missing match. Searches are case-sensitive and support embedded NUL and arbitrary bytes; Unicode text is interpreted as encoded bytes. Uses the canonical Shift-And loop without recording. O(n+m+256) word work in the worst case, constant auxiliary storage and no input mutation/shared state.
    bitap_trace()Record the same coupled Shift-And loop used by the first-match and all-match APIs. Each consumed byte updates k+1 states. Records every state with one=active, independent of the older implementation's complemented-bit convention. Empty-pattern and byte semantics match bitap_matches(). O(n*(k+1)) trace storage in addition to matches; no input mutation or shared state.

    datamunge/algorithms/bitonic_sort.hpp

    Classes

    BitonicComparatorA fixed compare/exchange connection between two network wires. first<second. Ascending sends the smaller value to first; descending sends it to second. Stages are zero-based dependency layers with disjoint wire pairs.
    BitonicNetworkOwned, value-independent topology generated by the canonical bitonic visitor. Comparators are grouped in nondecreasing stage order. Empty/singleton inputs need no comparators or stages. Construction stores O(n log^2(n+1)) entries.
    BitonicStepActual values and swap decision at one canonical integer comparator. The trace follows sequential recursive execution; stage numbers can decrease between independent subproblems. Topology is fixed even when swaps differ.
    BitonicTraceOwned input/output and chronological integer compare/exchange events. The unrecorded sorter does not allocate these records. Recording uses O(n log^2(n+1)) storage plus the owned input/output vectors.

    Functions

    bitonic_network()Materialise the canonical value-independent bitonic comparator schedule. Construction and output storage are O(n log^2(n+1)), using linear bucket grouping by stage after emission. Every stage has disjoint wire pairs, so its comparisons can run independently; this function does not launch workers. No input data or mutable global state is used.
    bitonic_sort()Sort any vector length in ascending order with a fixed bitonic network. Comparisons follow the same topology as bitonic_network(), without allocating a network or trace. The loop and swap branches remain ordinary C++ execution: fixed wire accesses do not imply constant-time machine behavior. Not stable; descending comparisons retain the historical exchange-on-equality convention. O(n log^2(n+1)) comparisons and O(log(n+1)) recursion-stack storage. No shared state; comparison/move exceptions propagate with possibly partially changed input.
    bitonic_sort_trace()Sort an owned integer sequence while recording the canonical comparator decisions. Uses the same application loop as bitonic_sort(). Records values before and after each comparison, including comparisons that cause no swap. O(n log^2(n+1)) time and recording storage; no caller input or shared state is mutated.

    datamunge/algorithms/bkm.hpp

    Classes

    BkmDomainSupported unreduced input intervals for the 53-term real greedy variant. Logarithms accept [1,max_argument]; exponentials accept [0,max_exponent]. Limits are the actual double product/sum of all available factors, not rounded decimal estimates. Values are owned, immutable with respect to library state.
    BkmStepOne attempted real greedy factor and the resulting accepted state. Both candidate fields are computed from the preceding state. A rejected step keeps product/log_sum unchanged; a true accepted flag includes equality.
    BkmTraceOwned result and attempted factors from the same loop as the scalar API. Initial state is product=1, log_sum=0. There is one event per requested term, even after reaching a floating-point plateau. No shared state is modified.

    Functions

    bkm_domain()Inspect the actual finite domain of the real 53-term greedy implementation. Returns the accumulated double product of all 1+2^-k factors and the sum of their log1p entries. This is a restricted positive-digit variant, without range reduction or complex/signed-digit BKM. First-call initialisation is thread-safe; subsequent calls copy three scalars and allocate no storage.
    bkm_exp()Approximate exp(y) with 53 checked positive-digit shift/add attempts. Accepts log_sum+log1p(2^-k)<=y and mirrors accepted digits in the product. No range reduction, complex arithmetic or signed-digit hardware is provided. Double rounding/table error remains; the result is not guaranteed correctly rounded or below exp(y). O(53) work, O(1) auxiliary storage, thread-safe.
    bkm_exp_trace()Record the canonical sum-constrained exponential iteration. Uses the scalar loop with a configurable table prefix; every attempted digit is recorded. The input domain remains the full 53-term domain. O(terms) work and owned storage; no caller input or shared state is modified.
    bkm_ln()Approximate ln(v) with 53 checked positive-digit shift/add attempts. Starts with product=1 and log_sum=0; accepts product+ldexp(product,-k)<=v and accumulates log1p(2^-k). No automatic range reduction is performed. This double implementation is not correctly rounded: table generation uses platform log1p and arithmetic can plateau at roundoff. O(53) work, O(1) auxiliary storage, no input mutation, thread-safe shared read-only table.
    bkm_ln_trace()Record the canonical product-constrained logarithm iteration. Uses exactly the scalar loop, with a configurable prefix of the same table. The input domain is always the full 53-term domain, even for a short prefix. O(terms) work and owned recording storage; no input mutation or shared writes. Each term is an attempt, not a guaranteed additional correct bit.

    datamunge/algorithms/blast.hpp

    Classes

    BlastExtensionStepOne actually inspected byte pair outside an exact seed. Each direction starts running/best scores at zero. Best is updated strictly; equality keeps the shorter extension. A drop stops only when best-running>xdrop.
    BlastExtensionTraceOwned seed, best anchored segment and actual extension events. The HSP contains the seed even if a caller's search threshold would suppress it. Events include discarded negative tails; HSP endpoints use the best prefix in each direction. No input is modified or retained by reference.
    BlastSeedA pair of equal fixed-length byte words, described by their starting positions. Word length belongs to the enclosing operation. Positions are nonnegative; the seed API orders them by query start, then database start.
    HSPOwned ungapped segment pair with zero-based starts and half-open ranges. The same length applies to both sequences. Score is the sum of match/mismatch contributions; it is not a bit score, probability or E-value. No strings are borrowed.

    Functions

    blast_extend_trace()Trace the same two-sided ungapped X-drop extension used by blast_search(). Right and left prefix gains start independently at zero; the seed score is word_size*match. Extension stops on a boundary or a drop strictly greater than xdrop, in raw score units. Best-prefix ties keep the shorter prefix. O(L) time and owned event storage for L inspected pairs; no shared writes.
    blast_search()Find exact-seed, ungapped X-drop HSPs, retaining one best segment per diagonal. Visits seeds in query/database order, extending right then left with the same loop as blast_extend_trace(). A higher score replaces the diagonal's prior HSP; equal scores retain the first seed's result, even for distinct separated regions. Results sort by decreasing score, then query start, database start and length. This heuristic can miss unseeded or X-drop-separated optima. It provides no gaps, statistical significance, protein neighbourhood words or reverse complements. Expected time O((Q+M)w+SL+H log(H+1)), index storage O(Mw+H), where S is seed count, L bounds extension length and H<=S is retained diagonal count. Repetitive inputs can cost cubic time; no subquadratic or speedup guarantee is made.
    blast_seeds()Enumerate every shared exact byte word using the search engine's database index. Includes overlapping words and all repeated-word pairs. Case and embedded NUL bytes matter; no alphabet validation, reverse complement or normalisation. Empty/short sequences yield no seeds after validating word_size. Expected O((Q+M)w+S) time and O(Mw+S) storage for lengths Q,M, word length w and S seeds; hash-table collision behavior can be worse. Inputs are borrowed only during the call.

    datamunge/algorithms/bloom_filter.hpp

    Classes

    BloomFilterOwned approximate set of uint64 keys, using packed bits and deterministic double hashing. Insert/query use exactly the same probes, so inserted keys cannot test negative while the filter remains unmodified except by insertions. Positive queries require an exact backing-set check. There is no erase, resizing or insertion count: duplicates are idempotent and the object retains no original keys. Storage is 64*ceil(m/64) payload bits plus object/allocation bookkeeping. Copies own independent state; moved-from objects support destruction/assignment only. Mutation requires external synchronisation, while concurrent const reads are safe when no thread mutates the object. Probes retain the existing uint64 mapping: (h1+i*h2) wraps modulo 2^64 before reduction modulo m. Odd h2 need not give distinct probes for arbitrary m.

    Functions

    bloom_hash64()Hash the complete string byte sequence with standard 64-bit FNV-1a. Includes embedded NUL bytes and unsigned high bytes, with modulo-2^64 arithmetic and offset basis 14695981039346656037. This corrects the previous nonstandard basis, so hashes of strings change; callers retaining old hashes must rebuild them. O(length) work, O(1) storage, no mutation or shared state.

    datamunge/algorithms/blossom.hpp

    Classes

    BlossomContractionOne actual odd-cycle contraction, expanded to original vertex identities. members includes the base's existing group and every merged group, sorted by vertex index. It is an odd set, not a cyclic vertex ordering. Nested blossoms therefore appear as larger sets; contractions reset at the next root search.
    GeneralMatchingResultOwned maximum-cardinality matching, with symmetric mates and an explicit unmatched sentinel. mate has one entry per input vertex. Matched endpoints refer to each other; size counts pairs, not matched vertices. A maximum need not be unique and its selected edges can depend on input order. No graph storage is borrowed.
    GeneralMatchingTraceOwned final matching, actual contraction sets, lifted paths and search work counters. Root searches are numbered chronologically; contraction/augmentation vectors each preserve their own execution order. Edge scans count visited adjacency entries, including entries then skipped as matched or already contracted. Ignored self-loops add no adjacency entries; duplicates do add entries. Recording can require O(V^3) storage for expanded contraction sets, in addition to O(V+E) graph/work storage. The unrecorded function allocates no event records.
    MatchingAugmentationOne lifted augmenting path and the matching immediately after flipping it. path uses original vertices, begins/ends free before this event and alternates previously unmatched/matched edges. Its even vertex count gives one extra selected edge. The snapshot is owned and independent of later augmentations.

    Functions

    blossom_maximum_matching()Find a maximum-cardinality matching with Edmonds' unweighted blossom search. Vertices are 0,...,vertex_count-1. Self-loops are ignored after endpoint validation; duplicate undirected edges and input adjacency order are preserved. No caller input or shared state is mutated. Empty graphs are supported. For V vertices and E supplied edges, time is O(V^3+V*E), storage O(V+E). For simple graphs E=O(V^2), giving the usual O(V^3) bound. This is cardinality matching, not weighted matching or a guarantee of any particular tied solution.
    blossom_maximum_matching_trace()Run the same blossom search while recording actual contractions and lifted augmentations. Uses the same canonical kernel as blossom_maximum_matching(), with identical adjacency order and final result. Each snapshot contains original vertex IDs; no report-side reconstruction of blossom lifting is necessary. Recording keeps the O(V^3+V*E) time bound but can use O(V^3+E) storage. No input mutation or shared writes; copies in the returned records own their data.

    Types and constants

    kGeneralMatchingUnmatchedvariable Sentinel for an unmatched vertex; never a valid vertex index. Guard this value before indexing a mate vector or printing an edge: the comparison vertex<mate[vertex] alone also succeeds for unmatched vertices.

    datamunge/algorithms/booth_multiplication.hpp

    Classes

    BoothResultExact widened signed product and radix-2 recoding operation counts. Counts depend on multiplier bit transitions, even when the multiplicand is zero. An addition means signed digit +1, not necessarily a positive numeric contribution when the multiplicand is negative. No inputs or shared state are modified.
    BoothStepOne actual multiplier-bit decision and its widened accumulator state. previous is zero below bit zero, then the preceding lower bit. digit equals previous-current. All 32 decisions are recorded, including zero contributions.
    BoothTraceOwned operands, exact result/counts and the 32 canonical recoding decisions. Recording allocates O(32) entries. The ordinary function uses the same loop without allocating a trace. Data are owned; independent calls share no state.

    Functions

    booth_multiply()Multiply any two int32 values exactly by 32 radix-2 Booth decisions. At bit i the signed digit is b_(i-1)-b_i, with b_-1=0. Both current and preceding one means no operation; (1,0) subtracts and (0,1) adds. The final sign bit supplies the two's-complement negative weight without a 33rd step. Widened int64 products/sums stay representable, including INT32_MIN operands. Exactly 32 decisions, O(1) storage, no allocation or mutation of caller/shared data. Fewer nonzero digits for long runs is not a runtime or hardware speed guarantee.
    booth_multiply_trace()Record the exact same 32 Booth decisions used by booth_multiply(). Includes zero digits, widened terms and post-decision accumulators. Time and owned recording storage are O(32); no input or shared state is mutated.

    datamunge/algorithms/boruvka.hpp

    Classes

    BoruvkaChoiceOne component's cheapest outgoing edge at the start of a phase. Choices are recorded before any unions, so multiple components may choose the same edge. Acceptance is recorded separately in BoruvkaPhase.
    BoruvkaPhaseOne actual full edge scan followed by cycle-checked unions. Labels refer to components before this phase; choices use ascending internal root order, the same order used for acceptance. A disconnected forest can end with a phase with no choices or merges. Empty and singleton graphs have no phases.
    BoruvkaTraceOwned forest, component snapshots and logical edge-scan counters from the canonical kernel. Recording costs O(n*P) storage for P scans in addition to O(n) forest/work storage. No input or shared state is modified; edge indices refer to input order.

    Functions

    boruvka()Find a minimum spanning forest by each current component's cheapest outgoing edge. Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected; finite negative/zero weights, loops and parallel edges are accepted. Loops never join components. Equal weights prefer the first input edge. Choices are fixed before merging and processed in ascending union-find root order; union by rank retains the first root on ties. Each accepted edge joins different components. Disconnected inputs return an MST per component; empty/singleton graphs are connected by convention. For P scans, work is O(n+m+P*(n+m)*alpha(n)), P=O(log(n+1)); O(n) auxiliary space and O(n) owned output. The n term matters for sparse disconnected graphs. Weights accumulate in long double and the final double total is checked.
    boruvka_trace()Record component labels, cheapest choices and accepted merges from the same Boruvka kernel. Forest edge order and tie behavior equal boruvka(). Canonical labels are minimum original vertices, not implementation roots. Counter edge_scans counts whole scans, not elapsed time. Recording takes O(n*P) owned storage and O(n*P*alpha(n)) additional label work; caller data are unchanged.
    dyadic_path_edges()Build a dyadically weighted path, useful for reproducible spanning-forest studies. Edge i connects i-1 to i with weight 1+v2(i), where v2 counts trailing zero bits. Edges are in ascending i order. For n=2^k, Boruvka merges adjacent equal-sized blocks in exactly k productive phases. All path edges are needed in its unique spanning tree even though weights repeat. O(n) work/storage. No shared state or randomness; n<=1 returns an empty edge list.

    datamunge/algorithms/borwein_pi.hpp

    Classes

    BorweinStepOne actual completed quartic update, before any early-stop decision. Iteration is one-based. All values are owned doubles from the canonical loop; unchanged refers to the stored inverse-pi value, not exact convergence to pi.
    BorweinTraceOwned actual Borwein states and stopping information, without fabricated plateau records. The seed is separate from the update vector. Negative requested iteration counts are clamped to zero, matching the historical scalar/sequence API. A recorded unchanged update is included, then the kernel stops. Scalar calls use the same kernel without allocating records; sequences pad repeated final estimates to retain their historical requested length.

    Functions

    borwein_pi()Historical one-argument double pi estimator, using direct evaluation. Retains the original seed, lower clamp, short-run arithmetic order and unambiguous one-argument function signature. It now stops at the first unchanged stored inverse-pi value, retaining the plateau for large iteration requests rather than producing inf*0 and NaN. For K actual updates, O(K) fixed-precision operations and O(1) auxiliary storage, with no trace allocation or input/shared-state mutation. The result is not guaranteed correctly rounded and does not certify digits. Rationalised evaluation is available in the trace.
    borwein_pi_log10_error_bound()Approximate log10 of Brent's exact-arithmetic Borwein pi-error upper bound. Evaluates log10(pi^2*4^(n+2)*exp(-2*pi*4^n)) directly in the log domain, where n=max(0,iterations). This models exact arithmetic; it is not a bound on rounded scalar/trace results and is not interval/certified evaluation. Avoids exponentiating a tiny bound. Returns negative infinity when the negative logarithm exceeds double's range. O(1) work/storage, no allocation or input/shared-state mutation. Uses the standard-library rounded pi reference.
    borwein_pi_sequence()Historical owned seed and successive double pi estimates, using direct evaluation. Returns max(0,iterations)+1 values. After the first unchanged stored a, later entries copy the plateau without more arithmetic updates. The shared kernel ensures scalar/sequence equality at every requested prefix. Preserves the unambiguous original one-argument signature. For N effective requested updates, O(N+1) time/output storage even after stagnation, and O(1) auxiliary state. No input/shared-state mutation. Allocation failures propagate; no partial vector is returned. The output is a sequence of doubles, not certified digits.
    borwein_pi_trace()Record actual double Borwein updates, ending at a stored-value plateau. Uses the scalar/sequence kernel, with the seed separate and no fabricated repeated records. For K actual updates, O(K) time and owned record storage. An unchanged stored a is finite-precision stagnation, not proof of exact pi or a theorem-derived error certificate. No input/shared-state mutation.

    Types and constants

    BorweinEvaluationenum Algebraically equivalent ways to evaluate Borwein's next y in floating point. Both modes retain the historical seed 6-4*sqrt(2). Rationalisation preserves small y updates when the computed fourth root rounds to one; it does not guarantee a more accurate final pi estimate or undo earlier rounding.

    datamunge/algorithms/boyer_moore.hpp

    Classes

    BoyerMooreAlignmentOne actual right-to-left scan and the shift that follows it. Full matches use mismatch_index=pattern length, text_byte=0 and bad_character_shift=0; inspect matched to distinguish that sentinel from an actual NUL mismatch byte.
    BoyerMooreTablesOwned rightmost-byte and strong good-suffix tables for one pattern. Obtain populated values from boyer_moore_tables(); default field values are placeholders. Tables borrow no pattern storage and can be inspected concurrently.
    BoyerMooreTraceOwned tables, all matches, actual alignments and search-comparison count. No text or pattern bytes are copied into the trace. Sizes and positions are byte counts; preprocessing comparisons are excluded. Empty/oversized patterns produce no alignments, but the trace still contains their preprocessed tables.

    Functions

    boyer_moore_search()Find every overlapping bytewise occurrence by right-to-left Boyer-Moore scans. Uses bad-character and strong good-suffix shifts from boyer_moore_tables(). Empty or oversized patterns return no matches before preprocessing. Supports embedded NUL/high bytes, is case-sensitive and performs no Unicode normalization. Inputs are borrowed and unchanged; owned offsets are sorted; calls share no state. Preprocessing takes O(m+256) work/storage. This all-occurrences implementation does not reuse matched regions across alignments: worst-case search comparisons are O((n-m+1)*m), e.g. repeated identical bytes. Large skips are data-dependent. Output costs O(K) for K matches; the ordinary search does not allocate alignment records.
    boyer_moore_tables()Preprocess unsigned-byte last occurrences and strong good-suffix shifts. The two-pass border-position construction builds good_suffix[k] for a matched pattern suffix starting at k, with a mismatch just before k when k>0. Index zero holds the full-match period shift. Empty input yields last=-1 and good_suffix={1}. O(m+256) work/storage; input is borrowed and unchanged; no shared state.
    boyer_moore_trace()Record the same tables, matches, right-to-left decisions and shifts as ordinary search. Always preprocesses the pattern, including when it is empty or longer than text. Search costs match boyer_moore_search(); recording adds O(A+K) storage for A visited alignments and K matches, besides O(m+256) table storage. No bytes are copied, no caller data are mutated and independent calls share no state.

    datamunge/algorithms/branch_and_bound.hpp

    Classes

    KnapsackBoundExact fractional-relaxation components and its integer-objective upper bound. LP value is whole_value+fractional_numerator/fractional_denominator. Integer profits permit pruning with its exact floor integer_upper; relaxation_value is a rounded double for display only and never controls pruning.
    KnapsackInstanceOwned integer knapsack input, suitable for deterministic method studies.
    KnapsackNodeOne DFS entry, its exact bound, incumbent transition and incoming decision. Nodes are in visit order. Root parent/item_index are size_t maximum. A node's level counts decided positive-profit items in KnapsackTrace::item_order.
    KnapsackResultOptimal 0/1 knapsack value, original-index choices and actual visited-node count. The historical field types/layout are retained. Ownership is independent of input storage. Only strict improvements replace an incumbent solution.
    KnapsackTraceOwned optimal result, sorted original indices and actual search/pruning records. Nonpositive-profit items are excluded from the active order and remain unchosen. Empty original input has no nodes; a nonempty input with no active items has one root leaf. Recording adds O(N+k) storage for N visited nodes and k active items; no input is borrowed.

    Functions

    knapsack_branch_and_bound()Maximise 0/1 integer knapsack value with an exact fractional bound and take-first DFS. Values/weights must have equal lengths; weights and capacity are nonnegative. Signed profits are accepted: nonpositive items are omitted since the empty set is allowed. Positive-profit free items precede weighted items. Remaining density comparisons use exact widened cross-products; ties use original input index. At entry, strictly improve the incumbent, then prune when floor(LP bound)<=best. Both integrality and rational bound arithmetic are exact; no floating comparison controls search. An explicit O(k) stack avoids recursive call-depth limits. Preprocessing is O(n+k log k), with O(k*N) worst-case bound/copy work for N visited nodes; N can be exponential. Auxiliary/result storage is O(n+k), with no trace allocation. Inputs are unchanged and independent calls share no state. Empty input returns zero value, no choices and zero visited nodes.
    knapsack_branch_and_bound_trace()Record actual decisions, exact bounds, incumbents and pruning from the same solver kernel. Parent links refer to earlier visit indices; node state is determined before descendants execute. Result/tie behavior matches knapsack_branch_and_bound(). Recording adds O(N+k) owned storage and O(N) constant-size record work; no caller data are mutated and no shared state is used. Empty input produces no nodes.
    knapsack_random_instances()Generate independent-size knapsack fixtures from one local MT19937 stream. For each requested n, draw all n values then all n weights from inclusive uniform distributions; capacity is n*capacity_per_item. This preserves the original report's seeded experiment order. Instances are not nested prefixes. Engine output is standardised, but bounded-distribution mapping can vary between standard libraries. Work/storage is O(sum sizes); no input/shared state is changed.

    Types and constants

    KnapsackNodeStateenum Disposition of an actual visited node after updating its feasible incumbent.

    datamunge/algorithms/breadth_first_search.hpp

    Classes

    BreadthFirstStepOne actual dequeue and the discoveries made while expanding it. The goal dequeue is included but its adjacency is not scanned. Discovered vertices are recorded in input adjacency order and are marked before enqueueing.
    BreadthFirstTraceOwned BFS result, discovered distances/predecessors and chronological queue events. Distance sentinel n means undiscovered at stopping time, not necessarily unreachable when the goal ended the search early. Predecessor sentinel n is used for start and undiscovered vertices. Discovered vertices may still be queued after the goal is removed, including vertices one layer deeper. A full breadth_first_traversal() has goal_requested=false, empty result.path and result.found=false; result.order then exhausts all reachable vertices.

    Functions

    breadth_first_search()Find a minimum-edge start-to-goal path by FIFO breadth-first search. Vertices are 0..n-1. Every edge has unit cost. Mark vertices on enqueue, retain the first predecessor and visit adjacency in input order, so equal-length path ties are deterministic. Loops/parallel edges are accepted and inspected but do not cause repeated enqueues. Undirected input adds both orientations, including two entries for a self-loop. Stop when the goal is dequeued, before expanding it. Start=goal returns that single vertex; an unreachable goal returns an empty path. All endpoints/terminals are validated before adjacency allocation, even when start=goal. O(n+E) work and owned adjacency/work storage; search state alone is O(n). The returned path/order own O(n) storage. No trace records are allocated, inputs are unchanged and independent calls share no state.
    breadth_first_search_trace()Record actual BFS discoveries, predecessors, queue lengths and optional FIFO snapshots. Path/order and stopping semantics match breadth_first_search(). Omitting queue snapshots retains O(n+E) time/storage, including linear event storage. With capture_queue=true, copying the active queue before each dequeue adds O(Q) time/storage, Q=sum of those lengths, potentially O(n^2). Layer counts describe discoveries at stopping time; vertices can remain pending after the goal pop. Records own their data, inputs are unchanged and calls share no mutable state.
    breadth_first_traversal()Traverse all reachable vertices for minimum-hop distances without requesting a goal. Uses the same queue/discovery kernel as breadth_first_search_trace(). All reachable vertices are dequeued and expanded; distance sentinel n now means unreachable. Result order is complete, while result.path is empty and result.found=false because no target was requested; goal_requested=false. Queue snapshots default off, giving O(n+E) work/storage including events and adjacency. Enabling them adds O(Q) copying as in the single-goal trace. All outputs are owned; borrowed inputs are unchanged and calls share no state.

    datamunge/algorithms/bresenham.hpp

    Classes

    BresenhamStepOne actual current point/error and the coordinate moves selected after it. Both tests use the saved doubled_error, even when the x move changes error. The final endpoint has terminal=true and no outgoing move flags. All fields are owned values; the point is the centre selected by the canonical loop.
    BresenhamTraceOwned raster points and actual integer decisions from the ordinary loop. dx/dy are nonnegative coordinate extents. Move counters exclude the terminal record; a diagonal move increments both axis counters and diagonal_moves. Recording uses O(max(dx,dy)+1) storage beyond the returned points.

    Functions

    bresenham_line()Rasterise an integer segment to one centre per major-axis position, including both endpoints. Preserves the original four-argument signature and directed all-octant tie rule: step x when saved 2*error>=-dy and y when saved 2*error<=dx. Exactly halfway cases move the minor coordinate towards the destination. Reversing a segment can therefore choose a different tied centre. Coincident endpoints return one point. This is not a supercover of all geometrically touched cells and does not provide antialiasing. Arithmetic is widened before differences and doubling, covering all 32-bit int endpoints. O(max(dx,dy)+1) work and owned output storage, O(1) auxiliary state; no trace allocation or shared/input mutation. No clipping is performed. Large spans may fail to allocate.
    bresenham_line_trace()Record actual saved-error decisions from the same kernel as bresenham_line(). Returns the same centres and adds one owned pre-movement record per point; terminal flags have no outgoing moves. O(max(dx,dy)+1) time and storage, without shared/input mutation or extra geometric replay. A positive point limit rejects an oversized complete output before allocation; zero is unlimited. A limit failure never returns a misleading truncated segment.
    bresenham_point_count()Count inclusive Bresenham points without constructing or walking the raster. Returns max(abs(x1-x0),abs(y1-y0))+1 using widened arithmetic. This is O(1) work/storage with no mutation, allocation or shared state. The uint64 result can represent the entire inclusive span of 32-bit int endpoints.

    Types and constants

    GridPointtype Owned integer pixel-centre coordinates (x,y), shared by Bresenham results. No geometric cell-area coverage or intensity is implied by a selected centre.

    datamunge/algorithms/bron_kerbosch.hpp

    Classes

    BronKerboschNodeOne owned actual recursion-entry frame of pivoted Bron-Kerbosch. r is the current clique in search insertion order. Disjoint p/x contain vertices adjacent to every member of r: p may still branch, x was processed earlier at this frame's ancestors/siblings. They are not lists of already reported vertices. Each frame is captured before its own branch loop mutates p/x. Returned clique members are sorted separately, without changing records.
    BronKerboschTraceOwned maximal cliques, actual frames, histogram and logical search counters. Clique members are sorted; outer order is deterministic depth-first discovery order, preserving the historical implementation. The empty zero-vertex graph emits one empty clique. Counts describe this library's vector/matrix search, not wall time or a general optimal-time guarantee. Nodes add O((n+1)*C) retained vertex storage for C calls; ordinary enumeration allocates no diagnostic records.

    Functions

    bron_kerbosch()Enumerate every inclusion-maximal clique of a union-symmetrised integer graph. Preserves the original inline signature, sorted clique members and discovery outer order. This is not just one largest clique. Uses vertices 0..n-1; each used adjacency entry adds an undirected edge, duplicates collapse and valid self-loops are ignored. Extra rows are ignored, preserving legacy input semantics. The empty graph returns one empty clique. Inputs are borrowed only during the call and never changed; outputs own their storage. Pivot scoring scans p then x and keeps the first maximum; branches follow p order. With A used input entries, C actual calls and S returned vertex ids plus clique headers, conservative work is O(A+(n+1)^2*(C+1)+S*log(n+2)); storage is O(n^2+S), including the matrix and value-copied recursion sets. Ordinary calls retain no diagnostic records. Output and search can grow exponentially.
    bron_kerbosch_trace()Record actual recursion-entry sets, pivot branches and maximal-clique counts. Uses exactly the same kernel and output ordering as bron_kerbosch(). Snapshots precede each frame's branch loop; parent p/x must be updated by preceding sibling choices before deriving a later child. Records keep r in search insertion order. Adds O((n+1)*C) retained set/branch storage and O(n) histogram storage. A positive max_calls throws before entering an excess frame, returning no partial result; zero (default) is unlimited. This limit does not avoid adjacency-matrix allocation. Input validation, symmetrisation and ownership rules match ordinary enumeration.
    complete_multipartite_graph()Build a complete multipartite undirected graph with consecutive vertex groups. Every pair in different parts is adjacent; vertices in one part are not. Positive part sizes produce symmetric, sorted, duplicate-free rows. An empty list returns zero rows. For n total vertices, O(n^2) work and O(n+E) owned output/temporary storage, without randomness, borrowed results or shared mutation.

    datamunge/algorithms/brute_force_search.hpp

    Classes

    BruteForceStepOne actual entered simple-path prefix and its local decision/probe counts. Entry fields describe the incumbent before and after this visit's own goal decision; descendant improvements do not rewrite those historical values. Local edge/cycle counts accumulate while the visit remains active. Records are in DFS preorder, and parent ids identify the actual prefix search tree.
    BruteForceTraceOwned shortest-path result and actual DFS incumbent-bound diagnostics. Only vertices on the current path are marked, so the search can revisit a vertex along another prefix. Duplicate input arcs can repeat subtrees. Ordinary and traced calls share one explicit-stack kernel and preserve legacy tie order. Retaining full prefixes costs their total length; omitting copies retains O(V) records for V visits, in addition to the graph, live stack and final result.
    BruteForceTraceOptionsOptional complete-search visit budget and retained-path choice for diagnostics. Zero max_visits is unlimited. A positive budget throws before entering an excess prefix; no partial optimum is returned. It does not avoid adjacency allocation. record_paths=false omits per-visit path copies while retaining visit ids, parents, vertices, depths, decisions and counters.

    Functions

    brute_force_search()Find a minimum-edge directed path by DFS over simple prefixes with an incumbent bound. Preserves the original signature, result layout, input adjacency order and strict-improvement ties. Each input pair is one directed arc; loops and parallel arcs are allowed. Mark only vertices on the live path and unmark on backtracking. Goals are terminal. After finding an incumbent of L vertices, a non-goal prefix with at least L vertices is terminal too. Thus this does not enumerate every simple goal path after finding an incumbent. Equal shortest alternatives retain the first discovered path. start==goal returns [start] with one visit; failure returns an empty path. Validate all terminals/edges before graph allocation. Uses an explicit owned stack rather than native recursion, without trace records or input/shared-state mutation. With V visits, A examined entries and I total copied incumbent vertex ids, work is O(n+m+V+A+I), live storage O(n+m). The prefix search can have factorially many visits on simple dense graphs; parallel arcs can repeat even more equivalent prefixes. BFS is preferable when only a minimum-edge path is required.
    brute_force_search_trace()Record the ordinary path-prefix search's actual incumbents, decisions and work. Uses the same kernel, directed arcs, validation, visit order and tie rule as brute_force_search(). Adds O(V) record storage, plus O(total retained prefix lengths) when record_paths=true (default); the ordinary call records nothing. Positive max_visits stops before an excess visit and throws without returning a partial optimum. Input graph allocation still precedes search. Zero means unlimited; recording paths can be disabled independently of the budget.
    complete_directed_graph_edges()Build every directed non-loop arc between n labelled vertices. Rows are represented as pairs in lexicographic (source,destination) order. Zero/one vertex produces no arcs. O(n^2) work and O(n*(n-1)) owned output storage, without randomness or shared/input mutation. The count is checked before multiplication/allocation; large valid output can still fail to allocate.

    datamunge/algorithms/brzozowski.hpp

    Classes

    BrzozowskiOptionsSeparate optional output-state caps for the two determinisation stages. Zero is unlimited. Each positive cap is enforced before creating an excess subset; exceeding either throws without returning a partial minimisation. Caps count states, not bytes; source validation and large union temporaries can still cost substantial time/storage.
    BrzozowskiTraceOwned actual double-reversal stages, with final minimal DFA in second.dfa. first.subsets contains original input-state ids; second.subsets contains first.dfa state ids. Reversed NFAs are the actual sources passed to each construction. Reachable input labels exclude the implicit sink. The first DFA is reachable but need not be minimal if the original has unreachable explicit states. The second DFA is reachable, complete and language-minimal. All snapshots own their storage and can be exponentially large.

    Functions

    binary_kth_symbol_dfa()Build a binary DFA accepting iff the one-based position-th symbol exists and is one. All later symbols are ignored. The position+2 states consist of a prefix counter and accepting/rejecting sinks; every state is reachable. Its reversed language tests that position from the end and needs 2^position complete DFA states, making a deterministic reversal-growth fixture. O(position) work and owned storage, without randomness or shared/input mutation.
    brzozowski_minimize()Minimise a possibly partial DFA by reverse/determinise/reverse/determinise. Retains the original inline signature, complete output and deterministic subset-discovery numbering. Validates all input shapes/indices before allocation. The final DFA accepts exactly the original language, has start zero and is reachable and minimal among complete DFAs. Empty/no-start input produces a one-state rejecting machine; zero symbols are allowed. The first pass need not be minimal for an input containing unreachable explicit states, but its reachable deterministic result makes the second pass minimal. The map/vector subset constructions can grow exponentially; explicit subsets, union sorting and map comparisons determine work/storage. Ordinary calls discard diagnostic provenance/reversal snapshots once their stages finish. Inputs are borrowed only during the call; results own storage with no mutation.
    brzozowski_minimize_trace()Retain the ordinary minimiser's actual reversals, subsets and state tables. Uses the same two-stage kernel, ordering and complete final machine. Adds owned reversal/provenance snapshots and a reachable-input list; neither stage is replayed. A positive state cap throws without a partial result. Snapshots and union temporaries can be exponential; caps are not memory limits.

    datamunge/algorithms/bucket_sort.hpp

    Classes

    BucketSortBucketOwned scatter order, sorted contents and actual work for one bucket. Equal integers retain insertion order; no satellite payload API is exposed. Comparisons count evaluations of predecessor>key, shifts count successful predecessor moves, and placements count final key stores (one per insertion after the first item). Loop-bound tests, scattering and gathering are excluded.
    BucketSortTraceOwned snapshots and checked counters from one canonical bucket-sort run. Empty, singleton and all-equal inputs take the historical early exit, with shortcut=true, no allocated buckets/assignments and zero insertion counters. Otherwise bucket_count=input.size(), buckets includes empty buckets, and bucket_of_input records actual scatter destinations. Snapshots use O(n) extra storage; counters throw on size_t overflow rather than wrap. All values are owned; calls share no mutable state. Occupancy alone is an upper-bound predictor: actual shifts also depend on order within each bucket.
    BucketSortWorkloadsPaired synthetic samples for comparing bucket occupancy and actual work. Both vectors contain count integers in [0,999]. Uniform values use an integer uniform draw; clustered values use a normal draw with mean 500 and deviation 4, truncated toward zero and clamped. For count>=2 the first two clustered values are replaced by 0 and 999 to stretch the observed range. A local mt19937 engine consumes alternating uniform/normal draws. A seed repeats on a given standard library; distribution mappings are not promised identical across toolchains.

    Functions

    bucket_sort()Return an ascending integer copy using range buckets and insertion sort. Uses n buckets for n>1 nonconstant inputs; empty, singleton and constant inputs return immediately. Scattering is monotone in value, preserves encounter order, and handles INT_MIN/INT_MAX without signed overflow. Insertion moves only strictly greater predecessors. O(n+sum(bucket_size^2)) worst-case work and O(n) auxiliary storage; expected linear work requires suitably balanced random bucket assignments. All-equal inputs take O(n) despite maximal concentration. The function does not allocate trace records or alter caller-owned input.
    bucket_sort_collision_input()Construct matched occupancies with controlled insertion-order difficulty. Returns [0,1,...,m,(m+2)(m+1)] for ascending order, or [0,m,...,1,(m+2)(m+1)] for descending order. Here m=cluster_size, n=m+2 buckets, and the inclusive span sends 0 and all m interior distinct values to bucket zero, with the maximum in bucket n-1. Ascending uses m key comparisons and no shifts; descending uses m(m+1)/2 comparisons and m(m-1)/2 shifts. Zero gives [0,2]. O(m) generation.
    bucket_sort_index()Return the exact integer scatter index without allocating any buckets. Computes floor((value-minimum)*bucket_count/(maximum-minimum+1)), widening before subtraction and using quotient/remainder decomposition to avoid product overflow. Supports the complete 32-bit int domain and size_t bucket counts through SIZE_MAX. The inclusive span keeps the maximum strictly below the bucket count; some buckets may be unreachable when the span is small.
    bucket_sort_trace()Sort once and record the actual scatter buckets and insertion work. Uses the same canonical kernel as bucket_sort(); no insertion sort is replayed to generate counters. Output and each bucket's before/after values are owned. Shortcut behavior and exact counter conventions are defined by BucketSortTrace. Time is O(n+sum(bucket_size^2)); trace storage is O(n). No shared mutable state.
    bucket_sort_workloads()Generate reproducible-toolchain uniform and clustered comparison inputs. See BucketSortWorkloads for sampling details, endpoints and seed portability. Empty/singleton counts are supported; generation needs O(count) time/storage.

    datamunge/algorithms/buddy_allocator.hpp

    Classes

    BuddyAllocationTraceActual order search, splits and returned offset from one allocation call. offset=-1 means failure with unchanged state; a positive oversized request has no eligible order and examines zero free lists. Other failures examine every order from desired_order through the arena's maximum. Successful calls record only actual splits, in decreasing parent order. O(H) trace storage, no snapshots.
    BuddyAllocatorModel a binary buddy arena using offsets, ordered free sets and live maps. Does not allocate arena payload bytes or return pointers. Both dimensions must be positive powers of two, with minimum<=total. Allocation chooses the smallest adequate nonempty order, then its lowest offset, retaining the left child when splitting. Free coalesces only true same-order buddies. Unknown frees are no-ops. Positive oversize/exhausted requests return -1; nonpositive requests throw. Ordinary and traced calls share kernels. Metadata allocation failure leaves state unchanged; snapshots own their data. Copies are independent offset models. Concurrent mutations need external synchronization. For H orders and B current blocks, operations have conservative O(H log(B+1)) ordered-container cost, not a constant-cost-per-order guarantee. Metadata storage is O(H+B).
    BuddyBlockOne current free or allocated interval in an owned arena snapshot. Offsets and sizes are bytes relative to arena zero. Free blocks have requested=0; live blocks have positive requested<=size. No memory pointer or backing bytes are owned by this record.
    BuddyFreeTraceActual release, buddy probes and resulting coalesced block from one free call. Unknown, interior, negative and already-free offsets are no-ops: released=false, final_offset=final_order=-1, no probes. A valid offset releases the current live allocation at that offset; stale offsets cannot distinguish later offset reuse. O(H) trace storage, with no arena snapshots or operation replay.
    BuddyProbeOne actual same-order buddy membership test during a free operation. buddy_offset=offset XOR block_size(order), using arena-relative offsets. A successful test triggers one merge; a false test stops the cascade. No test occurs once the arena's maximum order has been reached.
    BuddySnapshotOwned, address-sorted partition and free lists from one allocator state. blocks covers [0,total_bytes) exactly once. Free blocks are maximally coalesced; adjacent blocks need not be buddies. free_offsets is indexed by order and sorted within each order. Copies remain valid after subsequent allocator changes. Construction takes O((A+F) log(A+F+1)+H) time and O(A+F+H) storage for live allocation count A, free block count F and number of orders H.
    BuddySplitOne actual allocation split of a parent into equal-sized children. Parent interval starts at offset and has order parent_order. The retained left child starts at offset; the free right buddy starts at offset+half_size.

    datamunge/algorithms/bully_election.hpp

    Classes

    BullyMessageOne actual logical send in deterministic kernel order. ELECTION sends visit higher ids in ascending order; a live recipient's ANSWER follows immediately. Candidate phases use FIFO activation order. Announcements are sent in ascending lower-id order after all candidate phases. phase indexes candidate processing, not physical time; announcements use the number of phases.
    BullyResultLeader and attempted-message counts for one explicitly chosen election model. Field order/types retain the original aggregate layout. Attempts to failed destinations count as ELECTION/COORDINATOR messages; only live responders send ANSWER. These are logical sends, not bytes, timings or network rounds.
    BullyRoundActual work and highest responder for one processed candidate. A phase sends to all higher ids and gathers their immediate logical answers. Fanout activates every previously inactive live responder once; the shortcut instead activates only the highest responder after completing this phase.
    BullyTraceOwned actual candidate phases, logical sends and final learned leaders. fanout distinguishes the full responder model from the legacy shortcut. result and counters come from the same kernel as the corresponding ordinary function; no election is replayed. learned_leader has one entry per process: live nodes learn the winner, down nodes remain -1. An all-down/empty system has no phases or messages and no leader. Records own their storage and inputs are unchanged; calls share no mutable state. See BullyTraceOptions for storage.
    BullyTraceOptionsMessage-recording and complete-call budget options for either trace model. max_messages=0 means unlimited; a positive cap counts every attempted logical send, including undelivered ones, and throws before the next send would exceed the cap. No partial trace or leader is returned. record_messages=false omits the O(M) message vector while retaining actual O(n) phase/learned-state records and all counters. Input flags are borrowed only during the call.

    Functions

    bully_elect()Preserve the original highest-responder shortcut and its valid-input message counts. Each candidate contacts every higher id and receives live replies; only the highest responder runs the next election. Thus at most two candidates run. Winner announcements target every lower id, including failed destinations. This O(n) shortcut is not the quadratic all-responder teaching model. O(n) local work storage; no trace records are allocated. Flags are not mutated.
    bully_elect_fanout()Run the static three-message model where every live higher responder activates once. A delivered ELECTION elicits ANSWER and schedules the live recipient if not already active in this epoch. Candidates execute in FIFO order; higher targets are visited in ascending id order. The no-higher-responder candidate wins and announces to every lower known id. Liveness never changes; no delays, restarts, partitions or recovery are simulated. The original paper's reorganization phases are omitted. O(n+M) time and O(n) work storage for M logical sends; worst-case M=n*n-1 for all-up nodes initiated by zero. No trace storage.
    bully_elect_fanout_trace()Record actual full-responder candidate phases and messages in one static epoch. Shares the bully_elect_fanout() kernel without replay. Full recording needs O(n+M) storage, lean recording O(n), while both still process every logical send and enforce the same complete-call budget. phase ids do not measure time.
    bully_elect_trace()Trace the actual legacy highest-responder cascade without replay. Shares the bully_elect() kernel and preserves its result fields. See that function for input and attempted-send conventions, and BullyTraceOptions for lean records and a positive complete-call message budget. O(n+M) time/storage with messages retained, O(n) trace storage in lean mode; here M=O(n).

    Types and constants

    BullyMessageKindenum Logical message categories in the static three-message teaching model. This abstraction does not reproduce the original paper's halt/reorganization/ ready phases or simulate crash recovery and communication failures.

    datamunge/algorithms/burrows_wheeler.hpp

    Classes

    BWTForwardOptionsOptional complete-call byte-comparison limit for forward tracing. Zero means unlimited. A positive budget counts actual byte-pair tests inside rotation comparisons and throws before exceeding it; no partial transform is returned. This bounds the deliberately naive sort's inspected-byte work.
    BWTForwardTraceOwned input, actual sorted rotation starts and actual comparison counters. No rotation matrix or comparator history is materialized. start offsets break full-rotation ties. Counters reflect this toolchain's std::sort calls and are not portable fixed formulas; overflow throws rather than wrapping. O(n) storage in addition to the input/result, with worst-case O(n^2 log(n+1)) forward work.
    BWTInverseStepOne actual LF inversion step and its right-to-left output write. Repeated rows are allowed: a periodic input can revisit a row before n steps have been taken. Exactly n bytes are written, independent of LF cycle length.
    BWTInverseTraceOwned encoded input, LF provenance, decoded bytes and actual inversion steps. Ordinary inversion shares the kernel but does not allocate step/rank/first-column records or copy the encoded input. Tracing uses O(n+256) storage and time, and never replays the inversion to fabricate a path. Calls share no mutable state.
    BWTLFMappingOwned stable last-to-first correspondence for any byte last column. counts[c] is the frequency of byte c; starts[c] counts bytes strictly below c. occurrence_rank[i] counts earlier equal bytes in L, so lf[i]=starts[L[i]]+rank[i] and first_column[lf[i]]=L[i]. lf is always a permutation, but that alone does not certify that an arbitrary last-column/primary-index pair is a valid cyclic BWT. O(n+256) construction time/storage; arrays use size_t, not narrowing int counts.
    BWTResultLast column and primary row of the sorted cyclic-rotation matrix. No sentinel is appended; every byte, including zero and 128..255, is data. Unsigned-byte lexicographic order is used.
