Equal rotations are ordered by start offset, so the primary row is the first row equal to the input. Field order and types retain the original aggregate layout; default construction is safely empty.

    Functions

    bwt_inverse()Recover exactly n bytes from a valid cyclic BWT pair with a checked primary row. Uses unsigned byte frequencies and size_t counters consistently with the forward transform. A periodic LF walk may revisit rows before n writes; it is not stopped at the first repeated row. O(n+256) time/storage; no trace records are allocated. Range checks do not certify transform-image membership: arbitrary in-range pairs decode deterministically but need not retransform to the supplied pair. This is not corruption detection. Empty input requires index=0. Input is not mutated.
    bwt_inverse_trace()Invert once and own the actual LF correspondence and right-to-left write path. Shares the ordinary inversion kernel without replay. Exactly n steps are recorded, including repeated LF rows for periodic inputs. Primary validation and arbitrary in-range pair semantics match bwt_inverse(). O(n+256) time/storage, no shared state.
    bwt_lf_mapping()Build a byte-consistent stable LF mapping and its actual occurrence provenance. Accepts any last-column bytes, including empty input; no primary row is needed. Every returned LF is a permutation, which does not by itself establish membership in the cyclic-transform image. O(n+256) time/storage; input is not mutated.
    bwt_transform()Transform a byte string by sorting cyclic rotations and retaining the last column. Preserves ASCII results, including banana -> (nnbaaa,3), and fixes signed-char ordering for arbitrary binary bytes by using unsigned order consistently with inversion. No sentinel is appended. Equal rotations use ascending start offsets. Sorts n indices, without allocating n full rotations. O(n^2 log(n+1)) worst-case time, O(n) auxiliary storage; does not compress or mutate input. Empty gives ("",0).
    bwt_transform_trace()Transform once and expose the actual sorted starts and comparator work. Shares the ordinary transform kernel; no sort is replayed and no matrix is stored. Counters include byte equality tests preceding a mismatch or a full-rotation tie. std::sort call counts may differ between toolchains. A positive byte budget throws without returning partial output. O(n) trace storage, O(n^2 log(n+1)) worst-case time.

    datamunge/algorithms/burstsort.hpp

    Classes

    BurstSortBurstOne actual overflow and redistribution into a newly created child. At creation, strings=bucket_capacity+1; later subtree sizes may be larger. trigger_input_index is the item being processed, including during redistribution from an earlier burst. No string values or full prefixes are copied into events.
    BurstSortNodeOne actual trie node, identified by its index in BurstSortTrace::nodes. Root zero has parent=depth=0 and no incoming byte. Every other parent precedes its child in creation order. Strings ending here precede all byte slots; their original input indices retain encounter order. Compact parent links avoid storing every full prefix, which could otherwise take quadratic space.
    BurstSortOptionsPositive leaf capacity and optional whole-call trie-node limit. A bucket bursts only when its size becomes greater than bucket_capacity. max_nodes=0 means unlimited; a positive cap includes the root and throws before an additional node would exceed it. Empty/singleton inputs build no trie.
    BurstSortSlotOne occupied byte slot observed during actual ordered collection. child=0 means a leaf bucket; a positive child names a real trie node (root is never a child). Child slots own no bucket records. Leaf snapshots preserve actual encounter order and actual sorted order; full string comparisons use unsigned byte ordering, with original input id as the equality tie break. Slots appear in collection preorder, with ascending byte slots within a node.
    BurstSortTraceOwned sorted strings, stable original ids, actual bursts and final trie metadata. Equal strings keep original-id order. Empty/singleton inputs take the historical shortcut: nodes/slots/bursts are empty and all work counters are zero. Otherwise snapshots come from the shared insertion/collection kernel, never a replay or a first-byte reconstruction. Parent links represent deep prefixes without quadratic prefix copies. Actual counters throw on size_t overflow. Calls share no mutable state.

    Functions

    burstsort()Sort strings with the original eight-item burst threshold and byte order. Signature and default threshold are preserved. Empty/singleton vectors return immediately. Flat node ownership and explicit insertion/collection stacks avoid recursive depth in insertion, traversal and destruction. Buckets hold indices into the unchanged input; full strings are copied once into output before a final swap. On allocation failure the caller's vector remains unchanged. Equal values retain input-id order; no collation, Unicode normalization or cache-speed guarantee is implied. Ordinary calls allocate no topology/event snapshots.
    burstsort_prefix()Materialize one actual node prefix from compact parent links, in O(depth) work. The generated trace stores no quadratic collection of full prefixes. This helper checks root, strictly earlier parents and depth increments along the selected path. A shortcut trace has no root. Result owns its bytes, including possible NULs.
    burstsort_trace()Sort once and own actual burst events, final slot/node records and sorted input ids. Uses the ordinary sort's kernel without replay or inferred first-byte counts. No full prefix is stored per node; use burstsort_prefix() for selected nodes. If D is input byte volume, Q node count, and n string count, algorithm storage is O(D+n+256Q), with O(D+n+Q) additional owned trace storage. Routing/collection work is O(D+n+256Q) plus actual full-string leaf comparisons. Long common prefixes can produce deep one-child chains; the trie is not guaranteed shallow.
    burstsort_with_options()Sort with a chosen positive bucket capacity and optional complete-call node cap. Same kernel, byte order, stable identity ties and strong input preservation as burstsort(). A node cap includes root; max_nodes=0 means unlimited. Exceeding a positive cap throws without swapping any partially sorted data into a.

    datamunge/algorithms/byte_histogram.hpp

    Functions

    byte_histogram()Count binary byte values in equal-width contiguous groups over [0,255]. Group width is 256/bins; embedded NULs and signed-char high bits are counted as unsigned bytes. Empty input gives bins zero counts after validating bins. Sum of counts is exactly bytes.size(); no statistical test or uniformity inference is performed. O(n+bins) work and O(bins) owned output, input unchanged, no shared state.

    datamunge/algorithms/cannon.hpp

    Classes

    CannonRoundOne actual round's source-block ownership and accumulated global output. Arrays a_sources/b_sources have q*q row-major cells. Each entry identifies the original input block by row*q+column, not a scalar offset. partial has n*n row-major values after this round's block products, before the next shifts. Values/indices are owned and independent of inputs and later rounds.
    CannonTraceOwned product, actual carried source ids, snapshots and loop work counters. The shared ordinary/traced kernel records without replaying multiplication or deriving source ids from a closed-form round formula. Source ids travel through the same source-cell selection as numeric shift buffers. Inputs are borrowed only during the call and never mutated; input values are not copied into this result. With q rounds, snapshots use O(q*(n*n+q*q)) storage. Empty input has no rounds.
    CannonWorkCounts of scalar arithmetic and buffer assignments in this Cannon implementation. A multiply-add counts one multiply-and-accumulate expression, not two measured machine instructions. Copies count double assignments, including the final closing shift and self-copies when the mesh has one cell. These are not network messages, bytes, timings, allocations or hardware performance counters.

    Functions

    cannon_block_matmul()Multiply with square blocks on a q-by-q logical toroidal processor mesh. Block side b=n/q. Initial direct copies skew A block row i left by i and B block column j up by j. Each of q rounds accumulates a block product, then copies A left and B up one block, including a redundant final closing shift. Local inner coordinates run in ascending k order; block order is cyclic and can change floating-point rounding. NaN/infinity propagate without rejection. No actual processors, messages or parallel execution are created. O(n^3+q*n^2) sequential work, O(n^2) temporary storage. Inputs are borrowed, never mutated; ordinary calls store no source ids or snapshots. Empty shape is n=q=0 only.
    cannon_matmul()Multiply square row-major matrices using the original scalar-cell Cannon API. Equivalent to cannon_block_matmul(A,B,n,n): n-by-n logical cells, one scalar per cell, n rounds and a closing shift after every round including the last. The cyclic summation order is retained. Floating-point results can differ from ascending-k multiplication; NaN/infinity and overflow propagate through ordinary double arithmetic. This is a sequential simulation, with no MPI/network execution. Inputs are checked for exact shape, borrowed and unchanged; output owns storage. Empty n=0 requires empty inputs and returns empty. O(n^3) work, O(n^2) extra storage excluding inputs; ordinary calls allocate no ownership/snapshot records.
    cannon_matmul_trace()Execute Cannon once, retaining actual round ownership, partials and work. Uses the same numeric kernel as cannon_block_matmul(), with carried original block ids and owned C snapshots. No multiplication or shifting is replayed to construct the trace. Final ownership follows the last closing shift and equals initial skew ownership, even though numerical C is complete before that shift. Tracing adds O(q*(n*n+q*q)) storage; shape, arithmetic, mutation and empty rules match cannon_block_matmul(). Snapshot allocations can fail without changing inputs.
    cannon_work()Predict exact loop counts without allocating matrices or running the kernel. The empty shape is n=q=0. Otherwise n>0 and q is a positive divisor of n. Counts include the final closing shift and one-cell self-copies; they do not model initial-skew network hops, messages, latency or execution time. O(1) work and storage, no shared mutable state. Shape/count checks precede kernel allocation.

    datamunge/algorithms/canopy_clustering.hpp

    Classes

    CanopyOwned canopy centre index and loose-radius member indices. Members generated by canopy_clustering() are unique, ascending original indices. Overlap is permitted. Removing a point from seed eligibility does not remove it from subsequent membership searches. The default centre is zero, without points.
    CanopyCoverageOwned inverted memberships and unique unordered candidate pairs. point_canopies[i] contains ascending canopy ids that include point i. shared_pairs is lexicographically sorted with each first id smaller than its second id. pair_visits counts all within-canopy pairs before deduplication, so it may exceed shared_pairs.size(). These describe candidate retention, not a clustering accuracy or speed guarantee. Copies are independent and own all indices.
    CanopyStepActual seed-pool transition for one complete canopy construction. Vector position is the corresponding canopy id. newly_removed is ascending and includes the selected seed, so every step consumes at least one point even at t2=0. Visit offsets delimit this step's full original-index-order distance scan.
    CanopyTraceOwned result and actual Euclidean canopy construction provenance. Inputs are not retained. Each of m seeds scans all n original points, including previously consumed seeds: distance_evaluations=n*m, coordinate_differences=n*m*d. Ordinary canopy_clustering() omits visits/steps. A trace needs O(n*m) additional storage, with no replay or shared mutable state. Empty points give empty records.
    CanopyVisitOne actual seed-to-point distance evaluation and its resulting decisions. already_removed describes eligibility before this canopy started, not membership. newly_removed includes the selected seed itself even when tight radius is zero. Flags are from the shared kernel; they are not reconstructed from final canopies.

    Functions

    canopy_centers()Copy selected centre coordinates, checking only centre indices. The helper does not compute distances or validate member lists, rectangularity or finiteness. Arbitrary coordinate rows are copied in canopy order, including repeats; copies own their storage independently of points/canopies. Work/storage is proportional to the copied coordinates; inputs are borrowed and unchanged, no shared state.
    canopy_clustering()Deterministic Euclidean canopies with separate membership and seed eligibility. Select the lowest eligible input index. Scan all original points, adding those with distance<t1; selecting the seed and distance<t2 make points ineligible for later seeding. Previously ineligible points still join later canopies. Both tests are strict, equality is outside; t1=t2 is allowed, and t2=0 makes every point a seed. Zero-width points have zero distance. Empty points return no canopies after radius validation. Finite rectangular inputs are checked before accessing coordinates. Hypot accumulation avoids squared-distance overflow/underflow, but not norm rounding. This all-points Euclidean variant supplies no approximate metric/index or downstream clustering. Nearby pairs are not universally retained merely because t1>=t2. Inputs are borrowed, unchanged; result owns indices, no shared mutable state. Work O(n*m*d+n*m), m<=n seeds and d coordinates; storage O(n+sum memberships).
    canopy_clustering_trace()Construct Euclidean canopies once and retain actual distances and pool transitions. Same shared kernel and result as canopy_clustering(), without replay. A positive whole-call budget throws before the excess distance evaluation; no partial result is returned. Recording adds O(n*m) storage. Source coordinates are not retained. Seed selection itself consumes a point, even when its tight-radius test is false at t2=0; this distinction is visible in visit and step records.
    canopy_coverage()Invert canopy memberships and enumerate unique unordered shared-canopy pairs. Checks centre/member bounds and rejects duplicate members within a canopy, while allowing unsorted members, repeated centres and overlap across canopies. Empty canopies may leave points uncovered. Pair visits count each within-canopy unordered pair before deduplication; a positive cap throws before an excess visit. Owned inputs are never modified and no partial coverage is returned on exception. For M memberships, V pair visits and U unique pairs, ordered-set insertion costs O(V*log(U+1)); add per-canopy member sorting and O(point_count+M+U) output storage. This is an explicit diagnostic enumeration, not a scalable spatial index.

    datamunge/algorithms/chacha20.hpp

    Classes

    ChaChaBlockTraceOwned actual state setup, 80 quarter rounds, 20 round states and serialization. Trace factories populate the record in the same kernel used by ordinary blocks; no round is replayed. initial contains the key, and later fields contain key-derived state/keystream. Use public test material for exposed diagnostics; records do not erase their memory. Default construction alone does not execute a block.
    ChaChaEncryptTraceOwned one-shot output and actual block/counter/offset/keystream records. Contains sensitive keystream and output material; no erasure/authentication is performed. Source input/key/nonce are borrowed only during the call. O(n+64*b) storage for n bytes and b=ceil(n/64) blocks; empty input has no block records.
    ChaChaQuarterStepOne actual quarter-round application inside a full block. before/after use the indices order; round zero is the first column round. Owned values and indices remain independent of the live working state.
    ChaChaQuarterTraceOwned four-word input, four actual compound ARX stages and final quarter round. Each stage follows an add/xor/rotate group, with rotation amounts 16,12,8,7. Arithmetic is modulo 2^32. No replay or shared state; this record may contain key-derived material. It performs no memory erasure or security certification.
    ChaChaXorBlockOne actual block used by one-shot XOR, retaining the full keystream. bytes may be less than 64 for the final block; unused tail bytes are retained here but discarded by the one-shot stream position. No source-data reference is held.

    Functions

    chacha20_block()Produce one RFC 8439 64-byte ChaCha20 block with the original signature. Byte-oriented 256-bit key and 96-bit nonce, both loaded little-endian; one exact 32-bit counter. Executes 20 rounds/80 quarter rounds, adds the original state and serializes little-endian. Stateless deterministic output; inputs unchanged, owned result, constant work/storage and no trace allocation. No authentication, nonce reuse tracking, memory erasure or audited constant-time guarantee is supplied.
    chacha20_block_trace()Execute a complete block once and retain actual states, selections and serialization. Same kernel as chacha20_block(); no permutation is replayed. Fixed state snapshots plus 80 quarter-round records use O(1) storage per block. initial exposes the key; all state/keystream records own their data and have no automatic erasure.
    chacha20_blocks_required()Validate a complete byte range and return its required block count without allocation. Checks before any counter addition or message copy. Empty input needs zero blocks even at the final counter. Ceiling division avoids overflowing bytes+63.
    chacha20_capacity_bytes()Number of bytes available before a 32-bit counter would repeat. Includes the starting counter and UINT32_MAX. Raw counter zero permits 2^32 blocks, or 2^38 bytes. This is a per-call range limit, not nonce management or a check for reuse across separate calls. Constant work/storage, no mutation.
    chacha20_encrypt()One-shot RFC 8439 XOR encryption/decryption, rejecting complete-call counter wrap. Original signature and valid-range bytes are preserved. Each call starts at byte zero of counter; an unused final-block tail is discarded. Arbitrary chunk splits therefore do not automatically preserve stream position. Binary strings retain embedded NUL/high-bit bytes. Empty returns empty without a block. Checks the whole range before copying/processing; no partial result on failure and inputs unchanged. O(n) work/output storage, O(1) block scratch; ordinary calls allocate no trace records. This raw cipher supplies no authentication, nonce tracking, erasure or audited constant-time guarantee. The same operation decrypts by XOR cancellation.
    chacha20_encrypt_trace()Execute checked one-shot XOR once and retain actual block-use records. Same kernel and binary output as chacha20_encrypt(), without replay. A positive max_blocks cap rejects the whole call before allocation/block work. Records own full keystreams, including unused tails, and output; do not erase themselves. O(n) work and O(n+64*ceil(n/64)) owned trace storage, no shared mutable state.
    chacha20_quarter_round()Apply the RFC 8439 quarter round to four owned unsigned words. Four add/xor/rotate groups use rotations 16,12,8,7 and addition modulo 2^32. All inputs are valid. Constant work/storage, no allocation or shared state; returned words own their values and input is unchanged.
    chacha20_quarter_trace()Execute one quarter round and retain each actual compound ARX stage. Same numeric kernel as ordinary quarter rounds, without replay. Owns input, four intermediate states and output; no allocation/shared state or erasure.

    datamunge/algorithms/chakravala.hpp

    Classes

    ChakravalaChoiceActual congruence class, bracketing candidates and minimum-norm multiplier. Admissible positive m satisfy m=residue mod modulus, with modulus=abs(k). below is the largest such m<=floor(sqrt(N)), or zero when none exists; above is the smallest such m>floor(sqrt(N)). Errors are abs(m*m-N), computed exactly in unsigned 128-bit arithmetic. A missing below has error zero but is never eligible. Equal errors select the smaller positive m.
    ChakravalaStateOwned auxiliary triple satisfying a*a-N*b*b=k in an executed cyclic solve. The kernel keeps positive a,b and a signed nonzero k for nonsquare N. Default construction is only a record, with no invariant validation.
    ChakravalaStepOwned before, multiplier decision and after records from one actual cyclic update. The ordinary and traced solver share arithmetic. Records are captured during execution; neither multiplier choices nor coordinate updates are replayed.
    ChakravalaTraceOwned initial triple, chronological cyclic steps and final Pell solution. Square inputs have initial={floor(sqrt(N)),1,0}, no steps and found=false. Nonsquares begin at the legacy floor-root triple and stop at k=+1, without the historical shortcuts for norms -1, +/-2 or +/-4. Their path therefore differs from variants starting at the nearest square or stopping at |k|=1.
    PellSolutionOwned positive solution of x*x-N*y*y=1, retaining the legacy field layout. A successful solver returns the fundamental positive solution. Default or square-input results are {0,0,false}; arithmetic/budget failures throw rather than returning a partial pair. Manually constructed records are not validated. Fields use the compiler's signed __int128 extension, not arbitrary precision.

    Functions

    chakravala()Solve positive Pell's equation using checked cyclic Chakravala arithmetic. Preserves the original signature and result layout. Every uint64 N is accepted; squares (including zero/one) return {0,0,false}. Nonsquares start with a=floor(sqrt(N)), b=1 and minimise abs(m*m-N) over positive admissible m, choosing the smaller m on ties. Corrects the old k=-1 floor-only choice. Uses no floating arithmetic. Quotient/remainder decomposition avoids forming oversized composition numerators when the reduced coordinates still fit. Coordinates are limited to 2^127-1; oversized reduced triples throw. At most 100000 cyclic updates, with no partial result on failure. Ordinary calls keep no provenance records; O(S log N) fixed-word arithmetic for S updates and constant auxiliary storage, not an arbitrary-precision bit-complexity bound. Independent calls share no mutable state and inputs are passed by value.
    chakravala_trace()Run the same checked solver while retaining every actual decision and reduced triple. Same square, tie, overflow and fixed-width semantics as chakravala(). The explicit budget counts complete cyclic updates; zero allows no updates, hence only square inputs return with a zero budget. An exceeded budget or allocation failure returns no partial trace. No caller-owned state is changed. O(S) owned trace storage in addition to the ordinary fixed-word solver work.
    pell_is_solution()Check a positive Pell pair exactly without squaring either signed-128 coordinate. Requires found=true, N>=2, x>1 and y>0. Cancels gcd factors between (x-1)*(x+1) and N*y*y, avoiding every large product. Accepts nonfundamental solutions too; equation satisfaction alone does not establish minimality. All manually supplied signed-128 values are handled without overflow. No allocation or mutation; a constant number of Euclidean gcd computations.

    datamunge/algorithms/checksums.hpp

    Functions

    adler32()Adler-32 (zlib), the checksum of RFC 1950: \((B \ll 16) \mid A\) with \(A = 1 + \sum_i x_i\) and \(B = n + \sum_i (n-i+1)\,x_i\), both modulo 65521.
    adler32_collision_probability()Approximate probability that two independent random messages of length bytes (each byte with variance byte_variance) have the same Adler-32.
    adler32_combine()The Adler-32 of the concatenation of two messages, from their checksums alone.
    adler32_roll()Slides the Adler-32 of a window byte window one byte along: drops out from the front and appends in at the back.
    adler32_update()Continues an Adler-32 checksum over data: adler32_update(adler32(x), y) == adler32(x + y).
    adler32_windows()The Adler-32 of every window byte window of data, in order of start position, computed with adler32_roll().

    Types and constants

    adler32_modulusvariable The Adler-32 modulus 65521, the largest prime below \(2^{16}\).
    adler32_nmaxvariable The longest run of bytes that adler32_update() sums before reducing modulo 65521.

    datamunge/algorithms/cheney.hpp

    Classes

    CheneyCopyOwned symbolic evacuated heap with rewritten slots and packed integral size offsets. heap ids are new slots; its roots and fields are rewritten during the actual traversal, preserving duplicate fields, duplicate roots, cycles and sharing. heap.sizes contains one positive size per survivor, including default ones. offsets[new] is the prefix sum of those sizes, in caller-chosen units, without alignment/header padding. This models layout and references, not raw allocation, object payload copying, deallocation, mutator suspension or an arena swap.
    CheneyEventOwned actual forward or scan-completion record, without replay or queue snapshots. For Root, source=-1 and field is the root-slot index. For Reference, source is the scanned old id and field its original reference-slot index. For Scan, source=target is the scanned old id, field=0, destination=scan, copied=false. scan is the current object-slot head; completed scans cover [0,scan) before the event. free_before/free_after count allocated object slots. At scan events they span that entire object's field processing; at forwards they span only that request. used_before/after measure packed units with the same convention. After Scan, [scan+1,free_after) is the pending queue. Records own all values.
    CheneyResultOwned breadth-first old-id order and dense old-to-new slot map, retaining the legacy layout. Each reachable object occurs once, ordered by first discovery from the ordered roots and reference fields. Unreachable old ids have forwarding=-1. Slots are object indices, not byte addresses; sizes are ignored by cheney_copy().
    CheneyTraceOwned evacuated heap plus every actual forward and scan-completion event. Uses the ordinary kernel; no discovery, forwarding or rewriting is replayed. There are R+E_live+L events on success. Input graphs are unchanged, and copied trace records can be modified independently. Trace memory is additional to the dense forwarding table and evacuated graph; it is not constant workspace.
    CheneyWorkActual validation, forward requests, completed scans and forwarding outcomes. root_probes includes duplicate root slots; reference_probes includes every live field, including repeated/shared/cyclic edges. Each forward request is either one copy or one reuse, so root_probes+reference_probes=copies+reuses. Validation visits the entire input, including garbage fields and supplied sizes.

    Functions

    cheney_copy()Compute the legacy checked breadth-first forwarding layout in object slots. Keeps the original call shape, inline availability and CheneyResult layout. Validates every graph row/id before copying; sizes is entirely ignored. Roots are forwarded in order, then fields in order while scan chases the append-only to-space vector. No separate traversal queue or recursion is used. Empty roots copy nothing; cycles/shared/duplicate edges copy each live object once. Does not rewrite roots/fields, copy payload bytes or reclaim memory. Total work is O(N+E+R), including dense map initialisation and full validation; O(N+L) owned storage. This graph model does not provide constant auxiliary space.
    cheney_copy_trace()Retain every actual root/field forwarding and scan completion from the shared evacuation. Same checked capacity and rewritten-heap semantics as cheney_evacuate(). A positive max_events caps the total retained records (R+E_live+L); zero adds no explicit cap. Reaching the cap throws before the next corresponding action or completed-scan record. Failed calls expose no partial heap or trace and leave input unchanged. Event storage adds O(R+E_live+L), with no queue snapshot copies.
    cheney_evacuate()Evacuate a symbolic heap, rewriting all live roots/fields and packing positive sizes. Same discovery order as cheney_copy(), with full size-prefix validation and default size one for omitted entries. Checks each first copy against capacity before adding units; exactly full heaps succeed, zero capacity allows no live objects. No input mutation or partial result on any failure. Ordinary calls retain scalar work counts but allocate no provenance records. Validation plus copying costs O(N+E+R); owns O(N+L+E_live+R) metadata. No alignment, payload copying, allocator lifecycle or mutator protocol is simulated.

    Types and constants

    CheneyPhaseenum Kind of actual chronological event in a symbolic Cheney evacuation. Root/reference events describe a forward request; scan events close one object scan after all its reference events have been recorded.

    datamunge/algorithms/chinese_remainder.hpp

    Classes

    CrtMergeOwned actual certificate and wide candidate for one sequential CRT merge. before is the last representable compatible prefix. Bezout coefficients obey before.modulus*bezout_first+input_modulus*bezout_second=gcd. difference is the normalized input residue minus before.remainder. Inconsistency leaves the correction/candidate fields zero and emits no hypothetical merged pair. Compatible attempts retain the actual signed correction product, normalized multiplier and wide candidate, even when the period cannot fit int64.
    CrtOptionsNamed complete-call limits for attempted merges and actual Euclidean divisions. Zero means unlimited. Limits count operations until the first inconsistency or period overflow, not the unvisited suffix. All moduli are validated before these limits apply. No partial result/trace escapes when a work cap is reached.
    CrtSolutionOwned representable generalized CRT result, retaining the legacy field order and defaults. A successful solve has 0<=remainder<modulus, with modulus the lcm of the processed input moduli. Inconsistency returns {false,0,0}; the default record {false,0,1} is merely unverified storage. Empty input solves to {true,0,1}. Period overflow throws in chinese_remainder(), rather than masquerading as mathematical inconsistency. Manually constructed records are not validated.
    CrtTraceOwned actual sequential CRT path with an optional complete int64 verdict. Complete and Inconsistent runs fill solution with their legacy result; Overflow leaves solution empty. prefix always retains the last representable compatible prefix, including on failure. steps includes the first rejected attempt and omits the unvisited suffix. Inconsistency/overflow are actual mathematical/range outcomes; work caps and allocation failures still throw, exposing no partial trace. Default construction alone performs no solve. Ordinary and traced entry points share the executing kernel without replay.
    CrtWorkActual validation visits, attempted merges and named arithmetic operations. Euclidean steps include an initial zero quotient when the first modulus is smaller. Products count the correction product, period product and residue product separately, including compatible overflow attempts and redundant/unit congruences. Validation covers every modulus even if arithmetic stops early. These are fixed-word counts, not elapsed time or arbitrary-precision bit cost.

    Functions

    chinese_remainder()Solve generalized CRT by checked sequential merging, permitting shared factors. Keeps the legacy call and CrtSolution layout. Equal-length inputs and every positive modulus are validated before merging. Residues may be any int64. Starts at 0 modulo 1; empty inputs return {true,0,1}. A failed gcd divisibility test returns {false,0,0}. Compatible merges use signed-128 products/Bezout arithmetic and check the new lcm before narrowing. A consistent prefix whose period exceeds INT64_MAX throws; later constraints are not examined, so this is not a verdict on that suffix's mathematical consistency. Duplicate and unit moduli are supported. Ordinary calls allocate no provenance and mutate no input. O(n) validation plus Euclidean division work per attempted merge; constant auxiliary storage, not an arbitrary-precision bit-complexity claim.
    chinese_remainder_trace()Retain actual sequential merges, Bezout certificates and wide range-failure diagnostics. Uses the same executing kernel, without replay. A compatible wide period is retained as status=Overflow with solution empty and prefix unchanged; unlike the ordinary solver this range outcome does not throw. Inconsistency fills solution with {false,0,0}. Stops at the first arithmetic outcome and records no suffix merges, although all moduli were validated first. Budget/allocation failures still throw and return no partial trace. O(k) owned records for k attempted merges, plus constant numeric state; no caller input is mutated.
    chinese_remainder_with_options()Solve with the same checked kernel and explicit attempted-merge/division caps. Same result, validation, range and sequential-stop semantics as chinese_remainder(). Positive caps count actual operations; zero is unlimited. Inconsistency before a cap returns its verdict even if more inputs remain. Cap failures expose no partial result; ordinary calls retain no provenance.
    crt_normalize()Normalize a signed residue into [0,modulus) without overflowing value+modulus. Handles INT64_MIN and every positive int64 modulus, including one. No allocation or mutation; constant fixed-word work and no shared state.
    crt_residue_satisfies()Check whether one signed integer satisfies every supplied congruence. Validates vector lengths and all positive moduli before comparing values, even if an earlier comparison would fail. Empty inputs return true. This checks a representative, not a claimed solution period or a uniqueness proof. No input mutation/allocation; O(n) modular comparisons, constant storage.

    Types and constants

    CrtStatusenum Actual outcome of a whole CRT run or one attempted merge. Overflow means a compatible prefix's period exceeds INT64_MAX, without a mathematical verdict on unprocessed constraints. Complete means a compatible, representable merge or a fully solved system, according to its record context.

    datamunge/algorithms/christofides.hpp

    Classes

    ChristofidesOptionsComplete-call storage limits for the exact odd-vertex matching subproblem. max_odd_vertices may be 0..22, defaults to the legacy limit 22, and is a hard vertex cap (zero permits only an empty odd set). max_matching_states counts allocated table entries, including odd masks; zero is unlimited. Limits are checked after the actual MST and before matching-table allocation. No partial result escapes a cap failure. These do not bound the complete graph's storage.
    ChristofidesTraceOwned actual tree, exact-matching choices, Euler circuit and shortcut result. All stages come from one execution without replay. tree edges are in Kruskal acceptance order, odd_vertices in ascending order, and matching in bitmask reconstruction order. Euler edge ids index tree followed by matching, retaining parallel copies as distinct identities. kept_positions indexes each first visit in euler_vertices; the final closing start is appended separately to result. Costs use long double accumulation for diagnostics and double for the legacy result. They describe rounded arithmetic, not an exact-real certificate.
    ChristofidesWorkActual named construction counts, distinct from timing or bit complexity. Every nonempty even mask is evaluated once; matching_candidates counts partner relaxations for its least set bit. Odd masks occupy table storage but are never evaluated. An empty odd set needs one table entry and no relaxations. Empty input bypasses all graph/matching work. No sort comparisons are counted.

    Functions

    christofides_trace()Retain actual Christofides stages and stable multigraph edge identities without replay. Same kernel, validation and caps as the ordinary APIs. Records own their values and do not borrow inputs. No partial trace escapes a failure. Trace recording adds O(n) stage/identity storage; no full DP table is retained in the result. The metric guarantee is conditional, not inferred from a successful return.
    christofides_tsp()Construct a closed TSP tour using an MST, exact bounded matching and Euler shortcutting. Preserves the legacy call/result layout and finite nonnegative square-matrix acceptance. The 3/2 theorem requires symmetric zero-diagonal triangle costs; these assumptions are NOT checked here (use is_tsp_metric()). Upper-triangle weights choose the undirected tree/matching even for asymmetric inputs; final cost uses directed input entries. Empty input ignores start and returns {}; singleton returns [start,start] with its diagonal cost. Tree ties now prefer (weight,u,v); matching ties prefer the smallest partner of the least set bit. Euler traversal consumes reverse insertion adjacency order. This makes ties explicit; a previously unspecified tied tour can change. Nonempty odd sets above 22 reject before matching allocation. Exact combinatorial matching uses long-double sums, not a polynomial weighted-blossom implementation or exact real arithmetic. No input mutation or shared state. For k odd vertices: O(n^2 log(n+1)+k*2^k) work, O(n^2+2^k) storage.
    christofides_tsp_with_options()Execute the same Christofides construction with explicit matching storage caps. Same validation, deterministic ties, numerical limits and conditional metric guarantee as christofides_tsp(). Cap failure returns no partial tour.
    euclidean_tsp_distances()Build a symmetric complete Euclidean distance matrix from finite planar points. Diagonal is exactly zero; repeated points are allowed. Coordinate differences and hypot use long double before checked conversion to double. O(n^2) work and owned storage. Floating-point rounding may require a small tolerance when checking triangle inequalities; this does not assert exact-real certification.
    hub_tsp_distances()Build controlled complete costs with one hub and interchangeable leaves. Vertex zero is the hub; leaves are 1..leaves. Hub/leaf distances are spoke, distinct leaf/leaf distances are rim, and the diagonal is zero. For at least two leaves this is a pseudometric iff rim<=2*spoke; rim<spoke may change the MST away from a star. These are synthetic costs, not necessarily planar Euclidean distances. O((leaves+1)^2) work and owned storage.
    is_tsp_metric()Test symmetry, zero diagonal and all triangle inequalities within an absolute tolerance. First validates the whole square finite nonnegative matrix and tolerance. Empty input is metric by convention; off-diagonal zeros are allowed, so the accepted class includes pseudometrics. Tolerance applies independently to each comparison and is not a proof of an exact metric or an unchanged 3/2 bound. Long-double comparisons avoid overflow in d(i,k)+d(k,j). O(n^3) worst-case checks, constant auxiliary space, no input mutation or shared state.

    datamunge/algorithms/chu_liu_edmonds.hpp

    Classes

    BranchingArcOwned actual working arc with wide reduced weight and stable original identity. All input arcs remain in input order through every contraction, even when mapped to irrelevant self loops. weight is an actual long-double working cost, not necessarily representable as double or equal to the original cost.
    BranchingOptionsWhole-call phase and named edge-visit limits for the iterative construction. Zero means unlimited. Every input edge validates before either cap applies. Edge visits count incoming-choice scans and contraction reweighting, including ignored self loops and root-entering arcs. Recovery/map copies are not edge visits. Failure throws with no partial tree/trace. These are work limits, not complete memory limits; a phase cap also limits retained expansion levels.
    BranchingPhaseOwned actual incoming choices, cycle partition and costs of one round. Root choice uses the sentinel and weight zero; missing choices use the sentinel and positive infinity. missing_vertices is nonempty only on failure, before any baseline addition or cycle search. cycles lists vertices in predecessor-following order, opposite to the directed edge traversal order. On contraction, cycle components come first in discovery order, then singleton components in vertex order. component is empty on acyclic/failed rounds. original_to_vertex maps every original vertex into this round's graph.
    BranchingTraceOwned actual contraction rounds, recovered original tree and operation counts. One executing kernel serves legacy, tree and trace calls without replay. reduced_total retains the actual sum of round baselines, including a prefix on failure. The returned cost instead sums the recovered original edges in original destination order; floating roundoff can distinguish those totals. A missing incoming choice proves nonexistence, including after a closed cycle is contracted. Failure returns no partial tree, but retains the actual rounds. All storage is independent of caller inputs and other calls.
    BranchingWorkActual named validation, scan, cycle and expansion counts. Counters describe executed work, not seconds or a bit-complexity model. Saved vertex entries count compact incoming-choice and original-map copies for contraction recovery; full trace snapshots and final output are excluded.
    DirectedArborescenceOwned original-vertex parent and input-edge identities of an optimum arborescence. Success has one entry per original vertex: the root parents itself and has kNoBranchingEdge; every other entry names its selected original incoming edge. Failure leaves both arrays empty and result={0,false}, with no partial tree. Parallel edges retain distinct input identities. Calls own all returned data.
    DirectedBranchingResultLegacy owned minimum rooted-arborescence cost and existence verdict. Field types/order/defaults are retained. Success spans all vertices from the prescribed root with outgoing paths; finite negative weights are supported. Failure returns {0,false}; default storage alone has not solved a graph. Manually assigned values are not validated or optimality certificates.

    Functions

    chu_liu_edmonds()Find the minimum-cost spanning directed out-arborescence rooted at root. Preserves the legacy call/result layout. Vertices are 0..vertex_count-1 and every vertex must be reachable from root in the returned tree. Finite negative weights and parallel edges are supported. Self loops and edges entering the root validate but never become choices. Equal working costs prefer the first original edge. Nonempty input graphs are required; a singleton costs zero. Original edge recovery now occurs before summing the final cost. Working differences and sums use checked long double, with checked final conversion to double. This is rounded arithmetic, not exact-real optimality certification. No vertex ids narrow to int, recursion, input mutation or shared state is used. For P rounds, O(P*(V+E)) work and O(E+P*V) auxiliary storage, plus owned output; P<=V. Compact expansion history is retained even by this cost-returning call.
    chu_liu_edmonds_trace()Retain actual selection, contraction and original-edge expansion evidence without replay. Uses the same kernel as chu_liu_edmonds_tree(). Records include stable original edge identities, wide reduced costs, current partitions, predecessor cycles, missing vertices and baseline additions. Full trace storage is O(P*(V+E)); no partial trace escapes work-cap/allocation failure. Mathematical nonexistence returns its failed round and an empty tree. Numerical overflow still throws.
    chu_liu_edmonds_tree()Recover the selected original input edges and parents with optional whole-call caps. Same executing kernel, cost, validation and deterministic tie rules as chu_liu_edmonds(). No partial tree escapes a failure or exhausted cap. Root parents itself on success; its incoming id is kNoBranchingEdge. O(E+P*V) auxiliary storage for iterative compact expansion history, plus owned output.
    rooted_cycle_edges()Generate root-entry arcs and a directed cycle for controlled contraction studies. Vertices are root 0 and cycle vertices 1..cycle_vertices. Root-entry arcs come first in ascending target order, followed by 1->2,...,k->1. With entry_cost> cycle_cost, each initial cheapest incoming choice is a cycle edge; ties can instead favour earlier root edges. Costs are synthetic, not observed data.

    Types and constants

    kNoBranchingEdgevariable No incoming edge for the root or for a missing phase choice. This is a storage sentinel, never an original input edge index.

    datamunge/algorithms/chudnovsky.hpp

    Classes

    ChudnovskyStepOwned actual term, accumulation and estimate from the executing double kernel. term is a_k=(-1)^k(6k)!(A+Bk)/((3k)!(k!)^3 C^(3k)), with A=13591409, B=545140134 and C=640320. The estimate is K/sum_after, K=426880*sqrt(10005), in double arithmetic. ratio_to_previous is zero at index zero, where no ratio was evaluated. sum_changed tests actual equality, not mathematical convergence; term can remain nonzero after additions stall.
    ChudnovskyTraceOwned actual Chudnovsky prefix records, stop reason and operation counts. Ordinary and traced calls share one kernel without replay. Positive requested counts are honoured through the first underflowed term; stagnation alone does not stop the loop. The first underflowed zero is included and suffix terms are skipped. first_unchanged_index is -1 if every addition changed the sum. No input or shared mutable state is retained. Default construction performs no evaluation. Trace records add O(m) storage for m actual evaluated terms.

    Functions

    chudnovsky_digits_per_term()Return the asymptotic exact-series decimal gain log10(640320^3/1728). Approximately 14.1816474627 digits per added term when arithmetic precision is sufficient. This is not a measured gain or accuracy guarantee for a double result. Constant floating work; no allocation, mutation or shared state.
    chudnovsky_log10_truncation_bound()Evaluate the log10 of a geometric bound for the exact N-term truncation error in pi. Let K=426880*sqrt(10005), A=13591409, b1=120*(A+545140134)/640320^3, rho=1728/640320^3 and L=A-b1. Exact arithmetic gives |K/S_N-pi| <= K*b1*rho^(N-1)/L^2 for N>=1. The bound uses alternating, decreasing terms and |a_(k+1)/a_k|<=rho for k>=1. Evaluation uses logarithms directly, so the bound does not underflow for large positive int counts. This is a rounded evaluation of a theoretical bound, not an outward-rounded interval or a bound on floating-point evaluation/normalizer/division error. O(1) floating work, no allocation or mutation.
    chudnovsky_pi()Approximate pi with a stable double Chudnovsky term recurrence. Replaces direct factorial/power evaluation while retaining the call signature. Uses K/S_N with K=426880*sqrt(10005); the rounding path can change the last bits of the old implementation. Requires terms>=1 (previous nonpositive requests divided by zero). Every requested term is added through the first underflowed zero; later terms stay zero and are skipped. Stagnation alone does not stop evaluation. No factorial overflow, arbitrary-precision arithmetic or binary splitting is used. On ordinary binary64, accuracy plateaus after about two terms; larger counts cannot guarantee more correct digits. O(m) floating work, O(1) auxiliary storage for m actual terms through underflow; no allocation, input mutation or shared state. Normal floating-point rounding and underflow are assumed, without fast-math reassociation or trapping modes.
    chudnovsky_pi_trace()Record each actual Chudnovsky term, addition and rounded prefix estimate without replay. Same recurrence, operation order and final estimate as chudnovsky_pi(). Records include nonzero terms whose sum no longer changes and the first underflowed zero; no huge reservation is made from the requested count. Underflow and unchanged additions do not certify real accuracy. O(m) work and owned storage for m actual evaluated terms. No partial trace escapes allocation failure.
    chudnovsky_term_ratio()Compute the signed ratio a_(k+1)/a_k without forming factorials or large powers. Uses bounded rational factors, tending to -1728/640320^3. The linear factor A+Bk is evaluated after conversion to double, so index arithmetic does not overflow at INT_MAX. Constant floating work, no allocation or mutation.

    Types and constants

    ChudnovskyStopenum Actual stopping reason for a Chudnovsky evaluation. RequestedTerms means all requested additions ran. TermUnderflow means the recurrence produced a signed zero term; that addition is recorded and every later requested term is skipped. Neither outcome certifies correctly rounded pi or a real-error tolerance. Default storage has not run an evaluation.

    datamunge/algorithms/cipolla.hpp

    Classes

    CipollaCandidateActual tested auxiliary value, difference and Euler residue. w=a^2-n modulo p. euler_value is w^((p-1)/2) modulo p, equal to zero, one or p-1; p-1 marks acceptance. Every rejected test is retained in a trace.
    CipollaElementOwned coefficients of x+y*s in one Cipolla call's quadratic extension. The call supplies p and s^2=w; this plain record stores neither and does not validate manually assigned coefficients. Returned coefficients are canonical uint64 residues. The basis symbol s is formal, not the complex number i.
    CipollaOptionsWhole-call actual-candidate and extension-product limits; zero is unlimited. Candidate order is 1,2,...,p-1,0, fixing the missing-zero case while retaining previous successful nonzero choices. Validation precedes limits and shortcuts. Products count result multiplications plus every base square, including the final unused square retained from the legacy loop. Primality and scalar Euler powers are outside the extension-product cap. No partial result escapes a cap.
    CipollaPowerStepOwned actual state transition of one right-to-left exponent bit. If remaining_exponent is odd, result is multiplied by base; otherwise result stays unchanged. Base is always squared, including the final unused square. Captures the executing arithmetic, not a recomputed explanation.
    CipollaResultOwned exact modular-root verdict and both unsigned root representatives. root follows deterministic auxiliary search/powering order, not size order. other_root is -root modulo p. They are distinct for nonzero residues at odd primes; zero and p=2 have one distinct root. Failure has exists=false, root=other_root=0 and legacy_root=-1. Default storage is not a completed solve. legacy_root equals root when it fits long long; otherwise it uses other_root, which fits because one of two complementary uint64 roots is at most p/2.
    CipollaTraceOwned actual prime-field path, candidate tests, bit states and full-range root result. The ordinary, unsigned-result and traced calls share a kernel without replay. input_n is the caller's uint64; normalized_n is input_n modulo the validated prime. residue_euler is zero when the p=2/zero paths skip its computation. a,w,final_element and both record arrays stay zero/empty off the extension path. No shared state or input mutation. Trace storage is O(T+log p) for T actual candidates; no allocation is reserved from the modulus magnitude.
    CipollaWorkActual named operation counts, excluding arithmetic inside primality validation. Scalar Euler powers retain a square in every bit iteration, including the closing unused square. Each extension product performs exactly five modular scalar products and two reduced additions, even for zero coefficients. Counts are executed operations, not timing, secret-independent work or bit complexity.

    Functions

    cipolla_root_satisfies()Check one unsigned candidate root with widened modular multiplication. Validates p first, including on zero inputs, then compares root^2 modulo p with n modulo p. Arbitrary uint64 n/root representatives are permitted. Empty/no-root result records must be checked via exists before using fields. This verifies the equation, not root ordering or a timing/security property. No allocation or mutation; prime validation plus one scalar modular product.
    cipolla_sqrt()Find a modular square root with the legacy signed result and full uint64 prime validation. Validates p with the existing deterministic 64-bit Miller-Rabin API before reducing n, avoiding modulo-by-zero and invalid zero shortcuts. Supports p=2 and n=0. Nonresidues return -1. The deterministic auxiliary order is 1,2,...,p-1,0; including zero fixes sqrt(1) modulo 3. Previously successful nonzero auxiliary choices remain. Products use unsigned-128 intermediates; sums reduce components before adding, and differences never form a+p-n. Returns the actual computed root when it fits long long, otherwise its complementary root, which fits. This avoids returning a negative value for a valid root. The algorithm is variable-time; sequential auxiliary search has no constant expected-trial guarantee. O((T+1)*log p) named fixed-word products including bounded prime validation, O(1) auxiliary storage; no allocation or shared state.
    cipolla_sqrt_result()Return both unsigned roots and the compatible legacy root with optional work caps. Same actual arithmetic/search as cipolla_sqrt(); the raw extension root keeps its uint64 range even when above LLONG_MAX. Zero/p=2 have one distinct root. Caps cover actual candidates and pair products; zero is unlimited. Validation and mathematical nonresidue/shortcut paths precede unused limits. No partial result escapes a cap failure. No input mutation, allocation or shared state.
    cipolla_sqrt_trace()Retain actual candidate rejections and every extension exponent bit without replay. Same kernel and final result as cipolla_sqrt_result(). Includes the closing unused base square, and counts all five scalar products per pair operation. Validation happens before shortcuts/caps. No partial trace escapes a cap or allocation failure. O(T+log p) owned records for T actual candidates, with no giant reservation based on p. Calls share no mutable state.

    Types and constants

    CipollaPathenum Actual route through the checked Cipolla solver. Shortcuts still validate primality first. NonResidue is a mathematical Euler verdict, while malformed moduli and exhausted work caps throw. Unprocessed describes default storage, without a solved input.

    datamunge/algorithms/circle_packing.hpp

    Classes

    CirclePackingFrameOwned actual unnormalised working disks and measured relaxation energy at one snapshot. Working disks have radius one. Raw edge target is two; nonedge repulsion uses clearance target 2.15. energy=(edge_stress+nonedge_penalty)/2, where the latter squares only positive clearance deficits. These are diagnostic measurements of the captured state, not a replay or a promised decreasing objective. The force distance floor 1e-9 can modify the gradient interpretation near coincidence. max_displacement is the largest actual committed vertex movement in the last sweep, zero for the initial snapshot. Postprocessed disks are stored separately.
    CirclePackingMetricsOwned tolerance-based contact, overlap and edge-error diagnostics for supplied disks. For each pair, gap=distance-radius_i-radius_j. Overlap means gap<-tolerance; contact means |gap|<=tolerance. Contacts can therefore include tiny tolerated overlaps. Edge stress is the sum of squared gaps on distinct nonloop edges; overlap penalty is the sum of squared negative gaps on every pair, independent of the overlap-count tolerance. Empty/singleton min_gap is zero; no-edge maximum error/stress is zero. Zero radii are counted separately and are not disk-packing certificates. These measurements do not establish planarity, optimality or an exact-real contact representation. All numeric aggregates use long double.
    CirclePackingOptionsExplicit fixed-sweep controls and preflight work/record limits for the legacy relaxation. Finite nonnegative step_size scales simultaneous pair displacements. There is no adaptive step, line search or early convergence test. Empty/singleton inputs execute no sweeps. snapshot_stride is positive and applies only to traced calls: record the initial state, every stride, and the final state without duplication. Zero caps mean unlimited. Positive caps reject the complete forecast before adjacency/snapshot allocation; validation precedes those caps. Snapshot controls do not limit untraced storage. The dense adjacency matrix remains O(V^2).
    CirclePackingTraceOwned actual relaxation snapshots, normalization map and returned fixed-radius disks. Ordinary and traced entry points share the executing kernel without replay. Raw snapshots precede postprocessing: subtract normalization_center, divide by normalization_scale, then RESET every radius to 0.45. The radius is not scaled with the centres. This can destroy tangencies or produce overlapping disks. The name is legacy: no Koebe packing, planarity test or convergence guarantee is supplied. Default storage alone performs no layout. Calls share no state.
    CirclePackingWorkActual named validation, relaxation and diagnostic work, excluding sort/allocator costs. Pair visits count all unordered pairs in every requested sweep for V>=2, even when their force is zero. Position updates count actual vertex commits, including unchanged values. Diagnostic scans are separate from the relaxation work cap. Graph input is validated in full; loops are ignored and duplicate/reversed edges collapse to one unweighted adjacency. Counts are not elapsed time.

    Functions

    circle_packing_layout()Run the legacy equal-centre pair relaxation and return normalized radius-0.45 disks. Preserves the call/default controls and Point2D/Circle2D layouts. Initializes unit working disks on a radius-three ring; each simultaneous sweep attracts edge centre distances toward two and repels nonedges below 2.15, with fixed factor 0.08 and force-distance floor 1e-9. Loops are ignored, duplicates collapse. Then subtract the mean, scale centre extent to one, and RESET radii to 0.45. This is a heuristic drawing, not a construction of a tangency packing: overlaps, missed edge contacts, extra contacts and nondecreasing stress are possible. No planarity test, adaptive step or convergence certificate is supplied. Empty input returns empty; a singleton returns centre zero/radius 0.45 without sweeps. Zero iterations returns postprocessed initial positions. Working arithmetic is checked/widened, so last bits can differ from the old unchecked double path. O(E+V^2+T*V^2) work and O(V^2) auxiliary storage, with actual T=0 for V<2. No input mutation or shared state; returned disks own their values.
    circle_packing_layout_with_options()Run the same checked heuristic with a configurable fixed step and preflight pair cap. Same geometry/postprocessing as circle_packing_layout(); a zero step still executes every requested sweep for V>=2. Pair/position-count forecasts are checked before adjacency allocation. Snapshot controls are validated but the positive snapshot cap applies only to traced calls. No partial output escapes a cap/range/allocation failure. O(V^2) auxiliary storage, no shared state.
    circle_packing_metrics()Measure supplied disks' overlaps and graph contacts with an absolute distance tolerance. Validates every finite centre, finite nonnegative radius, endpoint and tolerance before measuring. Negative radii/nonfinite data reject; zero radii are allowed and reported separately. Undirected loops are ignored; duplicate/reversed edges count once. Empty input is supported if edges are empty. O(V^2+E) work and O(V^2) dense adjacency storage. Widened distances/squares are checked for range. No input mutation or shared state; results own all values.
    circle_packing_trace()Capture actual unnormalised relaxation states and measure the returned disk geometry. Uses the same kernel without replay. Includes initial, every positive stride and final raw frames; the final frame is not duplicated on a stride boundary. Snapshot energy scans and final disk diagnostics are counted separately from relaxation visits. Complete frame/visit caps preflight after validation, before graph/state allocation. For F frames, adds O(F*V) owned storage and O(F*V^2) measurement work to the ordinary dense relaxation. No partial trace escapes.

    datamunge/algorithms/clarke_wright.hpp

    Classes

    ClarkeWrightOptionsComplete-call preflight limits for savings storage, endpoint scans and optional recording. With m customers there are C=m(m-1)/2 candidate pairs and exactly C*m route-slot inspections. All input validation precedes forecast/cap checks, which precede route/candidate allocation. Zero means unlimited. max_decisions applies only to traced calls; no partial routes or trace escape a failure. These logical counts exclude sorting comparisons, geometric arithmetic and allocator work.
    ClarkeWrightStepOwned actual sorted-pair decision, endpoint lookup and accepted concatenation. Stable route slots refer to the initial ascending customer order, excluding the depot. A merge retains route_i and clears route_j. Missing optional slots mean an interior customer. Loads are meaningful only for present slots. Reversal flags indicate executed reverse calls, even on singleton routes. merged_customers excludes depot visits and is empty on rejection. No replay.
    ClarkeWrightTraceOwned actual parallel-savings decisions, final routes, loads and distance accounting. Ordinary/traced entry points share the executing kernel without replay. initial_star_distance is twice the sum of cached depot distances. Accepted savings telescope in exact arithmetic; accounting_residual measures the actual widened final distance minus (initial_star_distance-accepted_savings). Rounded sums need not cancel exactly. No optimality, fleet-count or approximation guarantee follows. Calls share no state; no borrowed input references survive.
    ClarkeWrightWorkActual named routing operations, not elapsed time or a complete instruction count. Every sorted pair scans all initial route slots, including cleared slots. Geometric evaluations include cached depot distances, customer-pair distances and final output edges. Comparator counts depend on the standard library sort. Appended customers count elements copied into surviving routes, not reversals.
    VehicleRouteEvaluationOwned independent route-feasibility and widened distance measurements. Every nondepot occurrence contributes demand, including repeated customers or customer endpoints of malformed routes. repeated_visits counts extra visits, not the number of multiply visited customers. Missing customers count once. A malformed route has fewer than three vertices or wrong depot endpoints. Interior depot visits are reported separately. No capacity tolerance applies. This record certifies no optimality and validates no manually assigned fields.
    VehicleRoutesOwned depot-closed vehicle routes and their measured total Euclidean length. Each nonempty generated route begins and ends at the chosen depot, with every customer served exactly once. Depot-only input returns no routes and zero distance. This plain record validates nothing and certifies no optimality. The original field order and types are retained. Values own their storage.

    Functions

    clarke_wright_savings()Construct capacity-feasible Euclidean routes by deterministic parallel Clarke-Wright savings. Starts one route per customer, sorts all customer pairs by descending widened saving d(depot,i)+d(depot,j)-d(i,j), breaking ties by ascending (i,j), then joins distinct endpoint routes whose widened loads fit capacity. Zero-saving pairs are processed too. No improvement phase, fixed fleet size, time windows, split deliveries, optimality or approximation guarantee is supplied. Nonempty points and matching finite nonnegative demands are required; finite capacity is positive, each customer demand is at most capacity, and all coordinates are finite. Depot demand is validated but ignored; depot-only input returns empty routes. No capacity tolerance is applied: literal floating loads can straddle a boundary. Widened checked geometry/loads and deterministic ties can change last-bit costs or earlier unspecified tie choices. The old call/result layout remains. For m customers, O(m^3+m^2 log m) work and O(m^2) auxiliary storage, due to full route-slot lookup for each pair. Input is not mutated; outputs own all storage.
    clarke_wright_savings_with_options()Execute the same savings kernel with complete preflight work limits. All input validation precedes caps and allocations. Positive pair and endpoint caps apply; the decision-record cap applies only when tracing. No partial result escapes failure. Same geometry, ties, ownership and complexity as the ordinary call; zero caps are unlimited and inputs remain unchanged.
    clarke_wright_trace()Retain actual savings decisions, accepted route orders, loads and named work. Uses the same kernel without replay. Records all C=m(m-1)/2 candidate decisions and owned accepted concatenations, adding O(m^2) trace storage; no full route partition is copied on rejection. Positive record limits preflight C after input validation and before allocation. Ordinary work remains O(m^3+m^2 log m).
    evaluate_vehicle_routes()Independently measure supplied routes' closure, coverage, capacity and Euclidean distance. Validates the full point/demand/capacity input and every route vertex before measuring. Invalid vertex ids throw; structural/coverage/capacity defects are returned as counts with feasible=false. Empty route collections are feasible only for a depot-only problem. An empty route itself is malformed. Loads and geometry follow clarke_wright_savings(); final length remains long double. O(points+route vertices) work and O(points+routes) auxiliary storage; no input mutation/shared state, and the returned record owns its measurements.

    Types and constants

    ClarkeWrightDecisionenum Actual ordered reason for accepting or rejecting a sorted savings pair. Missing endpoint is checked first, then same route, then capacity. A customer in a route interior has no endpoint slot. Merged records include the committed customer order; rejected records never mutate routes. This is not a proof that another global routing could not use the rejected edge.

    Classes

    CocktailSortPassOwned state after one actual directional pass of cocktail shaker sort. Bounds are inclusive before/after the pass. A forward pass with swaps lowers hi by one; every backward pass raises lo by one, including a stopping pass. A zero-swap forward pass keeps both bounds. next_lo>next_hi means an empty remaining window. A final zero-comparison pass is retained, matching the legacy kernel. Only strict adjacent inversions swap; equal keys keep identity.
    CocktailSortTraceOwned input/output, stable original identities and actual directional passes. Empty/singleton inputs have no passes and zero work. Larger inputs include the final zero-swap pass even if its window has one item and no comparisons. Counts exclude copying, index initialization and loop control. Swaps equal strict inversions in the original input. No input references or shared state survive. Snapshot storage is O(n*p), where p<=n is the actual pass count; output-only sorting uses constant auxiliary state beyond its owned input copy.

    Functions

    cocktail_shaker_sort_trace()Sort integers and record the executing cocktail-shaker passes without replay. Same strict comparisons, alternating directions, early exits and one-position bound updates as cocktail_shaker_sort(). Signed extremes require no arithmetic on values. Equal keys retain ascending original positions. The by-value input leaves lvalue callers unchanged. All records own their data; concurrent calls use independent state. Time O(n^2), best O(n), with O(n*p) snapshot storage. The positive pass cap is checked before each pass, including an empty final pass: exceeding it throws without returning a partial trace. No cap applies to the output-only legacy call. Counts are checked before addition.

These are floating computations, not exact predicates: near-corner decisions can differ from real arithmetic. Counts exclude validation, coordinate comparisons and presentation.     Functions

    cohen_sutherland_clip()Clip a directed segment to a closed finite rectangle with checked widened arithmetic. Fully validates all eight coordinates and ordered bounds before trivial acceptance/rejection. Empty-area rectangles, corner tangency, axis-parallel and zero-length segments are valid. Endpoint zero is replaced when outside, otherwise endpoint one; edge priority is top,bottom,right,left. Free coordinates use the original supporting segment and a widened line determinant before division, preserving small integer corner cancellations and avoiding drift from earlier rounded cuts; unrepresentable products fall back to std::lerp. Current-endpoint-range projection retains already satisfied half-planes. The selected edge coordinate is pinned exactly. Output converts to double only at acceptance. Input direction and the historical result layout are retained. Intersections can differ in last bits from the former double product-before-division; widening is not an exact-real guarantee near corners or extreme scales. At most four cuts/five decisions, O(1) work/storage, no allocation/shared state.
    cohen_sutherland_clip_trace()Record actual outcodes, selected boundaries and terminal decision without replay. Uses exactly the same checked kernel, validation, priority, boundary inclusion and numerical behavior as cohen_sutherland_clip(). Trace coordinates retain the long-double working values, before the visible result's double conversion. Vector storage owns at most five records, so work/storage are O(1). Concurrent calls use independent state. See CohenSutherlandTrace for named counters.
    cohen_sutherland_outcode()Return a validated point's four-bit code relative to a closed ordered rectangle. Left=1, right=2, bottom=4, top=8; corner regions combine bits. Equality to an edge is inside. Zero-width/height rectangles are valid. All six coordinates are checked before classification, with no tolerance or allocation. O(1) work/storage, no mutation or shared state.

    Types and constants

    ClipActionenum Terminal or edge-replacement decision of one Cohen-Sutherland iteration. Edge priority is Top, Bottom, Right, Left, after the accept/reject tests. The first outside endpoint is selected; otherwise the second is selected.

    datamunge/algorithms/comb_sort.hpp

    Classes

    CombSortPassOwned state and work after one actual comb-sort gap pass. Pair indices increase from zero; each pair is (i,i+gap). One pass costs n-gap key comparisons. A zero-swap scan stops only at gap one. Original positions follow actual exchanges: their equal-value order need not remain stable.
    CombSortTraceOwned original values, final work and actual comb-sort pass states. work is identical to comb_sort_work() for the same input. Empty/singleton inputs have no records and identity final indices. Each record owns two length-n snapshots; p passes require O(np) snapshot work/storage. Output-only and work-only calls use constant auxiliary storage beyond their owned input. Equal-value identities may cross indirectly during a gapped exchange.
    ExchangeSortWorkOwned sorted values and actual key-operation counts for exchange sorts. Key comparisons count evaluations of left>right, excluding loop control, copying, index initialization and gap arithmetic. Passes include the final zero-swap scan. Empty/singleton inputs perform no passes. Counters are checked before increment. No references or shared state are retained.

    Functions

    bubble_sort_work()Sort and count the original report's full-width forward bubble baseline. Repeatedly scans all n-1 adjacent pairs, without shrinking a boundary, until an entire scan has no swaps. This preserves the report's comparator baseline; it is not a boundary-shrinking optimization. Empty/singleton inputs return without scans. Adjacent strict swaps are stable and their count equals strict input inversions. Comparisons=(n-1)*pass_count for n>=2, including the terminal scan. Worst O(n^2), sorted O(n), constant auxiliary state beyond owned input.
    comb_sort_next_gap()Compute max(1,floor(10*gap/13)) exactly without overflowing size_t. Quotient/remainder decomposition avoids forming 10*gap. Zero and one both return one. For gap>1 the result is strictly smaller than gap. No allocation, mutation, exceptions or shared state; O(1) work/storage.
    comb_sort_trace()Record actual comb-sort passes and carried original identities without replay. Same sorting/counter semantics as comb_sort_work(). The positive online pass cap is checked before each pass, including the final zero-swap pass. Exceeding it throws without returning a partial trace; it does not limit the work-only or legacy call. Records own their values and identities independently. Time includes O(np) snapshot copying; storage is O(np) for p passes.
    comb_sort_work()Sort and count actual comb-sort operations using the legacy executing kernel. Starts gap=n, shrinks before every pass by exact floor(10*gap/13), bounded below by one, and stops only after a zero-swap gap-one scan. No special gap adjustment is used. Signed extremes are valid; comparisons do not subtract keys. Strict swaps do not make this nonadjacent method stable. Worst-case upper bound O(n^2), sorted-input Theta(n log n); measured random behavior is not a universal linearithmic guarantee. No snapshots or shared state are used.

    datamunge/algorithms/computus.hpp

    Classes

    ComputusGregorianTraceOwned actual Meeus/Jones/Butcher integer steps and the resulting date. All divisions are floors of nonnegative integers for supported positive years. a is a zero-based Metonic index; the golden number is a+1. h is a nominal lunar offset, not an unconditional observed or corrected full-moon date. l+1 is the nominal following-Sunday offset. m subtracts one week in the two exceptional Sunday cases. No iteration, replay, allocation or shared state.
    EasterDateOwned Gregorian Easter month/day with the historical field order and types. Computed dates lie from March 22 through April 25. Value-initialized zeros are a placeholder, not a computed date. No year, timezone, input reference or historical calendar-adoption information is retained.
    EasterRangeSummaryOwned first-tie extrema and 35 date counts for an inclusive year range. Bins zero through 34 mean March 22 through April 25 on a fixed March axis. Counts describe deterministic Gregorian ecclesiastical rules over the selected years, not an astronomical forecast or a random-sampling probability model. Earliest/latest compare month/day, not chronology; equal dates keep the first ascending year. Storage is constant, with no per-year records or allocation. Default storage alone is not a valid summary.

    Functions

    computus_gregorian()Calculate Gregorian ecclesiastical Easter for a positive int year. Uses the Anonymous Gregorian / Meeus-Jones-Butcher integer rule. Year one through INT_MAX are supported; zero/BCE numbering is rejected. Before local Gregorian adoption the answer is a proleptic rule projection, not a historical observance claim. The moon/equinox are ecclesiastical tables and fixed March 21, not measured astronomical events. Results range March 22 through April 25. All intermediate int expressions are bounded for positive int input. Constant fixed-width work/storage, no allocation, mutation or shared state.
    computus_gregorian_summary()Summarize an inclusive positive-year interval using the canonical Easter kernel. Fully validates both positive endpoints and their order, then preflights the complete inclusive count against the positive cap before evaluating any year. Scans ascending years once, accumulates all 35 bins and retains first ties for date extrema. Loop termination is safe even when last_year=INT_MAX. Time O(last-first+1), constant 35-bin storage, no allocation or shared state. One complete 5,700,000-year rule period needs an explicit sufficient cap.
    computus_gregorian_trace()Return actual nonnegative integer steps without replaying the Easter calculation. Uses exactly the same positive-year validation and Gregorian rule as computus_gregorian(). Retains standard symbols a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h,i,k,l,m so the result can be checked against the published equations. In particular, m=1 exactly when l=6 and either h=29 or h=28 with a>=11. The uncorrected March coordinate may be 57 (April 26); the final date always lies in [22,56]. Constant work/storage; owned scalar data, no heap or shared state.

    datamunge/algorithms/conjugate_gradient.hpp

    Classes

    ConjugateGradientOptionsAbsolute stopping and optional actual-snapshot storage controls for CG. Zero iterations is valid; zero max_trace_values means unlimited. Positive trace caps count four vector entries per unknown per completed step, checked online before completing the next step. A failing call can already have requested A p. Solve-only calls ignore this storage cap.
    ConjugateGradientRunCG output with honest stop reason, counted products and optional owned steps. solution.residual is the recomputed absolute norm; solution.converged is true exactly for stop == CGStop::converged. Starting point is zero. There is one A p product and one diagnostic A x product per completed step, with no replay. A curvature failure also counts its attempted A p. Initial zero needs no call. No initial snapshot is stored; initial_residual is ||b||. Returns own storage.
    ConjugateGradientStepOwned actual CG step, including its used direction and resulting iterate. x and r are the resulting iterate and recursively updated residual; p and ap are the direction and A p actually used. beta is the next-direction coefficient only when has_next_direction is true. Norms/coefficients use long double; vector storage and each recurrence assignment use checked double rounding.
    GaussSeidelTraceOwned actual residual history for the forward in-place Gauss-Seidel baseline. residuals[0] is ||b|| and each subsequent entry follows a completed sweep. Empty and zero RHS converge initially. The legacy result layout is preserved.

    Functions

    conjugate_gradient_solve() ×2Solve dense SPD Ax=b from zero with checked true-residual stopping. Validates every entry, square shape, b length, exact stored symmetry and controls before work. Positive definiteness is a precondition: no Cholesky certification is performed; only encountered nonpositive curvature is caught. Empty/zero RHS can converge initially. Inclusive absolute tolerance; floating CG need not finish in n steps. Dot products/norms use long double, vector updates round to double. Nonfinite arithmetic cannot silently converge. Time O(n² + k n²), scratch O(n); two dense products per completed step. No input mutation or global state; concurrent calls are independent.
    conjugate_gradient_trace() ×2Execute dense checked CG and retain actual steps without replay. Same arithmetic, validation and stopping as conjugate_gradient_solve().
