Stores four n-vectors per completed step, O(kn) extra storage. The actual storage cap is checked after positive curvature, before updating; failure returns no partial trace. It does not precharge the requested maximum number of iterations.
    gauss_seidel_trace()Execute forward Gauss-Seidel while recording actual recomputed residuals. Validates finite square shape, matching RHS, nonzero diagonal, nonnegative controls before any sweep. Symmetry is not required; convergence is not guaranteed for a general matrix. Inclusive absolute stopping. Uses widened sums with checked double assignments. O(kn²) work, O(n+k) storage.
    laplacian_1d_apply()Apply the unscaled Dirichlet tridiagonal in O(n) time and storage. Full finite-input validation precedes arithmetic; zero boundary values are implicit. Widened sums narrow with range checks. Empty input returns empty.
    laplacian_1d_matrix()Build the dense n-by-n unscaled Dirichlet tridiagonal (-1,2,-1) matrix. n=0 returns empty. Complete n² storage is checked before allocation. No dataset or global state is used. O(n²) time/storage; prefer laplacian_1d_apply for sparse work.
    laplacian_1d_unit_solution()Closed-form unit-RHS solution x_i = (i+1)(n-i)/2, zero-based i. This is a fixture/oracle, not a CG solve. Complete dimension caps precede allocation; widened arithmetic avoids integer products. n=0 returns empty. O(n) time/storage; returned values round to double.

    Types and constants

    CGStopenum Why a checked conjugate-gradient run stopped. Values describe computed arithmetic, not a positive-definiteness certificate.

    datamunge/algorithms/connected_components.hpp

    Classes

    ComponentLabelAnalysisOwned final labelling and work, without history allocation. count equals labels_created minus successful_unions. Only foreground cells query representatives during renumbering; both scans visit background too.
    ComponentLabelCellOwned actual first-pass foreground decision with its union-record range. earlier_labels[0..earlier_count) follows up, left, upper-left, upper-right, omitting background/out-of-bounds positions and retaining duplicate labels. assigned is their minimum or a newly created ID. The union range is half-open.
    ComponentLabelOptionsComplete-image and actual-history budgets; zero means unlimited. Full shape validation precedes the complete max_cells cap and allocation. max_events counts foreground-cell plus union-attempt records online; analysis and output-only calls ignore the event cap.
    ComponentLabelTraceOwned actual two-pass history, without prefix reruns or synthetic decisions. provisional is the map after scan one. parents is the actual forest after scan two, including dummy zero; halving need not flatten it fully. root_to_dense is the actual remap, zero at non-root/unused entries. Input, snapshots and results own independent storage.
    ComponentLabelUnionActual union operands, pre-attachment roots and resulting attachment. Rank determines attachment; equal ranks choose the smaller root and increment its rank. Redundant attempts have merged=false, winner=root_a and loser=0. Internal root IDs are distinct from the final dense component labels.
    ComponentLabelWorkActual two-scan and balanced disjoint-set operation counts. Neighbor probes count in-bounds earlier positions for foreground cells only; admitted labels retain duplicates. find_steps counts path-halving iterations, not original edges. parent_writes counts union/halving assignments, including idempotent halving writes, excluding initial set creation. Snapshots and later measurements perform no counted operations. All counters are checked.
    ConnectedComponentsOwned dense component IDs, ordered by first row-major component occurrence. Zero is background; IDs are independent of internal union-find roots. Original fields and layout are preserved. All nonzero input ints mean foreground.
    ConnectedComponentStatsPixel-index area, bounds, centroid and exposed-edge measurements for one label. Bounds are inclusive; centroids average zero-based pixel-centre indices. perimeter4 counts exposed orthogonal edges including holes/image edges, regardless of label connectivity; it is not a smooth Euclidean perimeter.

    Functions

    component_blobs_example()Original deterministic 12-by-12 fixture with four disjoint inclusive rectangles. Rectangles (row,col): (1,1)-(3,3), (1,7)-(2,10), (6,2)-(9,3), (7,7)-(10,10). Areas 9,8,8,16; both connectivity choices retain four blobs. No RNG, download or global state; returned storage is owned.
    component_checkerboard()Generate a bounded checkerboard with foreground at (0,0), no RNG/global state. Dimensions must be positive. Complete checked rows*cols cap precedes allocation. O(rows*cols) time/storage; parity avoids adding row and column indices.
    connected_component_stats()Measure dense positive labels with checked integer counts and widened centroid sums. Validates rectangular shape, nonnegative count, IDs in 0..count and that every positive ID occurs. Does not certify connectivity: a supplied disconnected ID is measured as one group. Full label-range validation and count<=foreground preflight precede count-sized allocations. Empty/all-background count=0 returns empty. O(R+N+count) time and O(count) additional storage; no input mutation/global state.
    connected_components()Label rectangular nonzero foreground with orthogonal or diagonal adjacency. Full shape validation precedes allocation, including zero-width inputs. Empty and rectangular zero-width images retain shape and have zero components. Two row-major scans use union by rank and path halving. IDs follow first component occurrence, independently of root numbers. No input mutation/global state. O(R+N alpha(N)) time, O(R+N) storage for R rows and N cells. No optional cap.
    connected_components_analyze()Run the same kernel with actual work and no history allocation. Same foreground/order/complexity contract as connected_components(). Full rectangular validation precedes complete cell-cap preflight; event cap ignored.
    connected_components_trace()Retain actual decisions and the forest from the executing kernel without replay. Same work/validation as analyze plus O(R+N) owned history. Positive max_events counts actual foreground-cell plus union-attempt records online, never background; zero is unlimited. Failure returns no partial trace.

    datamunge/algorithms/context_free_grammar.hpp

    Classes

    ContextFreeGrammarA context-free grammar: a list of productions plus a start symbol.
    ProductionOne grammar rule: lhs -> rhs (empty rhs means the epsilon production).

    datamunge/algorithms/cordic.hpp

    Classes

    CordicAnalysisOwned actual approximation and final folded-frame recurrence state. result includes half-turn restoration; raw_x/raw_y and residual refer to the folded frame, initially (1,0,reduction.reduced). inverse_gain is the product actually accumulated for exactly iterations stages, initially one. No field certifies error to the true original angle. Zero stages is a valid unrotated approximation. The model uses double arithmetic, including multiplications.
    CordicConstantOne actual cached circular-stage constant, copied on request. shift=2^-index, angle=atan(shift), inverse_gain_step=1/sqrt(1+shift²), all rounded doubles. The shared immutable table is lazily built with libm calls; the subsequent recurrence performs lookups and floating multiplications.
    CordicErrorRowMeasured worst errors for one requested iteration count against the host libm. Empty angle inputs set has_samples=false and leave zero placeholders for errors/worst_angle. Positive samples select the first input with the largest max(abs(sine error),abs(cosine error)); norms measure abs(hypot(result)-1). Values are diagnostics against std::sin/cos, not certified mathematical bounds.
    CordicReductionOwned actual rounded-period reduction and optional half-turn fold. principal is remainder(theta,period), with period=2*pi_double. reduced lies within [-pi_double/2,pi_double/2]; flipped means a half turn was removed and both final coordinates must be negated. This does not perform high-precision reduction modulo mathematical 2*pi: large input angles can have large phase error.
    CordicStepOwned actual circular update, including before/after state and normalized direction. Constants are copied from the producing table. direction is +1 at residual >=0 (including either zero), otherwise -1. Before/after coordinates are raw; unit_x/unit_y divide the actual after-state by hypot and remain in the folded frame, without half-turn restoration. They reproduce the former report's plotted normalization; they are not a rerun or a compensated-output snapshot.
    CordicTraceOwned actual rotation sequence and the result it produced, without replay. Exactly one constant-size record per completed stage; zero stages is empty. Caller inputs, constants returned elsewhere, steps and result own independent values. Theta(1+N) work and O(N) extra trace storage for N<=1075.
    CordicWorkBounded actual per-call operations, excluding one-time shared table construction. These are algorithmic evaluations, not machine-instruction/throughput counts. Every requested stage executes even at zero residual. Trace normalization calls are additional diagnostics and do not change the producing recurrence.

    Functions

    cordic_error_sweep()Measure native CORDIC on supplied angles/counts with a complete evaluation budget. Full angle/count validation precedes checked angles.size()*counts.size() preflight and allocation. Repeated counts retain order; empty counts return empty and empty angles return absent rows. References use host std::sin/cos of the original angles, exposing both iteration and range-reduction error. O(S+C+S*sum(N+1)) time and O(S+C) storage for S angles/C counts, after the one-time table setup. No global RNG or input mutation.
    cordic_reduce()Expose the checked rounded-period reduction used by the CORDIC kernel. Uses remainder with the double constant 2*pi_double and a half-turn fold. Accepts every finite angle, but reduction accuracy to mathematical 2*pi can deteriorate severely for large magnitudes. No mutation or shared work state.
    cordic_sincos_analyze()Execute the canonical floating circular recurrence and expose its actual final state. Same result as cordic_sincos(). Validates finite theta and N in [0,1075] before reduction/table access. Uses actual cached atan/compensation constants, raw initial (1,0), N residual-sign updates, accumulated K_N and final sign fold. No early stop at zero residual, no forced exact identities or error certificate. Theta(1+N) work, O(1) per-call scratch after shared table construction. Large angles retain the documented rounded-period limitation. No input mutation.
    cordic_sincos_trace()Retain the producing CORDIC kernel's actual before/after steps without replay. Same recurrence/result as analyze; normalization of each actual raw step is an additional trace diagnostic. Full finite/count validation and the complete one-record-per-stage cap precede allocation, reduction and table access.
    cordic_stage_constants()Copy the actual immutable constants used by the recurrence, in stage order. The shared table is initialized thread-safely with atan/sqrt under the normal floating environment and then read only. Returned storage is independent. Count zero returns empty without constructing the table. O(N) copying.

    Types and constants

    cordic_rotation_limitvariable Number of nonzero scales 2^-i available in IEEE binary64, i=0..1074. Iteration counts are in [0,1075]. Further zero-scale iterations would not alter the recurrence. This is a work/domain limit, not an accuracy promise.

    datamunge/algorithms/counting_sort.hpp

    Classes

    CountingSortAnalysisOwned sorted values, stable original identities and bucket boundaries. For nonempty input, bucket b denotes min_value+b. Its output interval is [starts[b],ends[b]); counts[b] is its length. original_indices[j] identifies the input item copied to output[j], and increases within each equal-key block. Empty calls allocate no buckets: automatic bounds are both zero, explicit bounds retain the supplied values. No references or shared mutable state survive.
    CountingSortPlacementOne actual right-to-left assignment using a predecremented end cursor. Events appear in execution order, with input_index descending. The chosen output slot is cursor_before-1. No snapshot or report-side replay is needed.
    CountingSortTraceComplete owned counting-sort analysis and actual placement events. The same kernel drives legacy sorting, analysis and tracing. Storage and time are O(n+k), including n events; no partial trace is returned on failure.
    CountingSortWorkLogical operations actually performed by the counting-sort kernel. Excludes validation, allocation/zeroing, copies, cursor decrements, loop tests and hardware timings. Range discovery examines n items only in automatic calls; count/prefix/place work is n,k,n for nonempty accepted input.

    Functions

    counting_sort() ×2Stably sort signed 64-bit keys ascending, discovering their range. Replaces data only after successful completion; empty input is unchanged. O(n+k) time/space, k=max-min+1, with the legacy billion-bucket ceiling. Equal-key placement is shared with the diagnostic permutation kernel. Calls on independent inputs are thread-safe; no state is retained.
    counting_sort_analyze() ×2Sort keys with owned stable identities and an automatically discovered histogram. Leaves input untouched. Uses the same reverse-placement kernel as counting_sort. O(n+k) time/space; range discovery visits n items. Empty input returns zero bounds and empty arrays. Thread-safe for independent calls; all storage is owned.
    counting_sort_trace()Capture complete actual reverse placements without replay or packed keys. Explicit-range analysis plus n owned events, O(n+k) time/space. Input remains unchanged and the result retains no references. Full bounds/key validation precedes budget checks and allocation. Independent calls are thread-safe.

    Types and constants

    kCountingSortMaxRangevariable Inclusive maximum bucket count retained by the legacy sorting overloads. One billion size_t counters alone occupy about 8 GB on a 64-bit platform; this compatibility ceiling is not a promise that allocation is practical. Diagnostic calls additionally default to a one-million-bucket budget.

    datamunge/algorithms/cpu_schedule_types.hpp

    Classes

    GanttSegmentOne owned half-open contiguous busy interval.
    SchedMetricsOwned per-process completion and derived timing quantities.
    SchedProcessOne integral arrival/burst request with an opaque external id. Scheduling methods specify validation; checked round-robin requires unique ids and nonnegative arrival/burst.
    ScheduleResultOwned per-input outcomes, merged busy intervals and sample average timing.

    datamunge/algorithms/crank_nicolson.hpp

    Classes

    CrankNicolsonHeatTraceComplete owned initial/step states and actual reusable Thomas factors. One kernel drives final-only and traced calls. Factors are prepared once when steps>0; pivots are the actual eliminated diagonal and multipliers[0]=0. States include the initial sample plus all requested steps, never a partial history. Work/storage is O(nx*(steps+1)); final-only storage is O(nx). All vectors are owned and no callbacks/references survive. Independent calls are thread-safe subject to the supplied callback's own behavior.
    HeatGridValidated uniform heat-grid configuration with homogeneous Dirichlet boundaries. nx interior points lie at rounded i*dx for i=1,...,nx; endpoints are exactly 0,L. Rounded interior coordinates must remain strictly inside the domain. r=D*dt/(2*dx*dx). Coefficients and final time must fit finite double storage.
    HeatSineModeOwned unit sine-mode controls separating continuous, spatial and time errors. For mode m=1,...,nx, initial[i]=sin(m*pi*i/(nx+1)). continuous solves the continuous heat equation at the grid points; semidiscrete uses the exact central-difference eigenvalue; discrete applies the ideal CN amplification factor steps times. These are floating evaluations of modal formulas, independent of the Thomas recurrence, not arbitrary-precision certificates. Boundary values are set to exact zero. Negative amplification alternates sign.
    HeatStepOwned actual state and uneliminated right-hand side at one heat time level. Initial state has index/time zero, an empty rhs and zero scaled_residual. profiles include both exact zero endpoints; rhs holds nx interior entries. RMS uses the nx interior values. scaled_residual is the maximum rowwise |A*u-rhs|/(|rhs|+|A|*|u|), with zero/zero defined as zero. It is a backward-error diagnostic of the stored tridiagonal solve, not a PDE error.

    Functions

    crank_nicolson_heat()Advance u_t=D*u_xx on [0,L] with exact zero boundary values. Samples u0 once at each ascending interior grid point, never at endpoints. One shared CN/Thomas kernel averages old/new spatial stencils and factors the constant matrix once. Returns nx+2 owned values; zero steps returns the sampled initial values with zero endpoints. D=0 or dt=0 gives identity steps. O(nx*(nsteps+1)) time and O(nx) auxiliary storage. Ideal l2 stability does not imply positivity, strong stiff-mode damping, or immunity to rounding. Coefficients and arithmetic are checked; no implicit precision guarantee.
    crank_nicolson_heat_trace()Retain every actual heat state, RHS and reusable Thomas factor without replay. Same checked kernel and sample order as crank_nicolson_heat(). Validates scalar parameters/coefficient arithmetic before the complete storage budget; budget failure occurs before allocating profiles or invoking u0. Callback results are then fully checked during initial sampling. No partial result is returned. History scalar count is (nx+2)*(nsteps+1)+nx*nsteps; the cap excludes coordinates, factors and metadata. No state is retained after return.
    heat_profile_error()Return the largest absolute difference between two finite equal-length profiles. Empty matching profiles have zero error. Inputs are read-only, no references are retained, and O(n) work uses widened differences before checked conversion.
    heat_sine_mode()Evaluate independent sine-mode reference profiles for the heat discretization. Uses the same validated grid, with lambda_h=-4*D*sin²(m*pi/(2*(nx+1)))/dx² and g=(1+dt*lambda_h/2)/(1-dt*lambda_h/2). O(nx) time/storage, no Thomas calls or callbacks. Eigenvalue must fit finite double storage; analytic decay may underflow to zero. The ideal formula does not include solve rounding.

    datamunge/algorithms/crc32.hpp

    Classes

    Crc32ByteStepOne actual byte-at-a-time reflected CRC register update. raw_before precedes byte injection; lookup_index=(raw_before XOR byte)&255; raw_after=(raw_before>>8) XOR table_value. Raw registers exclude final XOR.
    Crc32FlipOne independent single-input-bit corruption and its finalized CRC difference. Bit numbering is byte-major, least-significant bit first inside each byte: bit b toggles byte b/8 with mask 1<<(b%8). syndrome is changed XOR baseline.
    Crc32FlipScanOwned complete census of each independent one-bit corruption of one message. For fixed length, CRC differences are linear in the error pattern and independent of payload. Output-bit counts are not collision probabilities or cryptographic avalanche guarantees. Empty input has no flips, false has_flips and zero summary placeholders. Independent calls share no mutable state.
    Crc32TraceOwned complete actual byte folds from the same kernel as crc32(). Input bytes are consumed in order; no view/reference survives. Initialization is FFFFFFFF and final XOR is FFFFFFFF. Empty input has raw FFFFFFFF, checksum zero and no events. O(n) time/storage for n bytes.

    Functions

    crc32()Compute reflected IEEE CRC-32, also called CRC-32/ISO-HDLC. Polynomial 04C11DB7 (reflected EDB88320), initial register FFFFFFFF, reflected input/output and final XOR FFFFFFFF. Accepts arbitrary bytes, including zeros; empty input returns zero. O(n) time, O(1) storage, one lookup per byte. No allocation, mutation, retained views or shared mutable state. This is an accidental-error checksum, not an authentication tag.
    crc32_flip_bits()Flip specified input-bit addresses into an owned binary string. Fully validates every address before copying or mutation. Repeated addresses toggle repeatedly, so duplicates cancel in pairs. Empty bit lists simply copy the message; the original input/view remains untouched. O(n+m) time and O(n) storage for n bytes and m requested toggles; no references survive.
    crc32_flip_scan()Census all independent single-bit corruptions using the same full-message CRC kernel. Computes one baseline and 8n corrupted CRCs, each over n bytes. Exact scan work is n*(8n+1) byte folds; copies/toggles/popcounts are additional work. O(n+8n²) time and O(n+8n) storage. One scratch message is toggled/restored rather than copied for each bit. Whole-call budget/size checks precede allocation and checksum evaluation; results never silently truncate.
    crc32_trace()Retain every actual lookup and raw register from the production CRC kernel. Owned complete byte history in O(n) time/storage. Valid empty input returns the conventional checksum zero and no events. Independent calls are thread-safe.

    datamunge/algorithms/cristian.hpp

    Classes

    CristianAnalysisOwned nominal receipt-time estimate and admissible return-delay interval. network_round_trip=RTT-processing; return delay lies in [minimum,network-minimum] in the ideal model. The interval midpoint is minimax for absolute error. All fields are double evaluations, not outward-rounded certificates. Large epochs can collapse absolute endpoints; the separate delay fields retain information that an absolute timestamp addition may round away. No clock is read/set and no references or shared mutable state are retained.
    CristianExchangeOwned controlled exchange separating actual path asymmetry from an uncertainty bound. The generated RTT includes both network legs and known processing. The server timestamp is at reply departure. model_error=(outbound-return)/2 is calculated from durations, rather than subtracting rounded epoch timestamps. It describes ideal midpoint error; fields are floating approximations, not certificates.
    CristianProbeOne ideal-rate request/reply observation using one consistent time unit. server_time is stamped at reply departure, after server_processing has elapsed. RTT includes outbound delay, processing and return delay. The common one-way lower bound applies to both network legs, not processing. All quantities are finite; durations are nonnegative. The server is assumed accurate and elapsed client durations calibrated to the same ideal rate.
    CristianSelectionOwned complete per-probe analyses and the first smallest stored error radius. Empty input has has_probe=false and index zero as an unused placeholder. Selection is by stored error_bound, not raw RTT when assumptions/processing differ. The chosen estimate refers to that probe's own receipt instant; it is not extrapolated to a later present and does not set an operating-system clock.

    Functions

    cristian_analyze()Analyze the admissible return delay after removing known server processing. All durations share one unit. Requires RTT-processing>=2*minimum. Reply departure is the timestamp point; request-arrival stamps need a different processing correction. Ideal-rate/server-accuracy assumptions are inputs, not measurements certified by this calculator. O(1) time/storage; owned result. Absolute values are rounded independently; use relative delay fields when epoch resolution is coarse. No outward rounding or drift/error propagation.
    cristian_error_bound()Return the ideal-rate midpoint uncertainty RTT/2 minus a common delay minimum. This is a model interval radius, not a statistical confidence interval or a floating-point enclosure. If known server processing is available, call cristian_analyze() to remove it first. Contradictory RTT<2*minimum now throws instead of silently returning a misleading zero. O(1) time/storage, no state.
    cristian_estimate()Estimate receipt time from a reply-departure timestamp and an uncorrected RTT. Same server_time+RTT/2 arithmetic as the original helper for accepted inputs. Assumes negligible server processing or treats it conservatively as part of the outbound leg. O(1) time/storage; no clock mutation or shared state. A symmetric network alone does not remove bias from nonzero processing.
    cristian_exchange()Generate a controlled asymmetric request/reply exchange in the ideal timing model. Both network legs must meet the supplied common lower bound. RTT is their sum plus processing; the timestamp is at reply departure. Known processing is removed by cristian_analyze(). If rounding hides all positive network time behind processing or invalidates the generated delay interval, the exchange is rejected. O(1), no I/O/clock mutation.
    cristian_select()Select the first probe with the smallest stored uncertainty after complete validation. All probes must use the same duration unit. Validates every probe including all derived output arithmetic before the optional count cap and allocation, then owns complete analyses in input order. Two linear passes, O(n) time/storage; no partial selection/history. A smaller radius can select a different probe than minimum raw RTT when residence/minimum assumptions differ. Estimates remain at their own receipt instants: no aging, drift compensation or clock-setting policy is supplied.

    datamunge/algorithms/cubic_spline.hpp

    Classes

    CubicSplineOwned local-power coefficients S_i(x)=a_i+t*(b_i+t*(c_i+t*d_i)), t=x-xs[i]. Preserves the original five-vector layout. For n>=2, xs contains n finite increasing knots and each coefficient vector has n-1 finite entries. Empty models have all vectors empty; singleton models have one xs/a entry and no b/c/d entries. Public mutation is permitted; evaluators validate the shape. A manually supplied model need not be natural or C2 merely because it is structurally valid. Coefficient units are y, y/x, y/x² and y/x³.
    InterpolationErrorScanOwned finite-query error census for two scalar functions, with sampled extrema only. Predictions and references are evaluated once each per query, in that order. Empty input has has_samples=false and zero max/RMS/index placeholders. Worst index is the first maximum absolute error, including first-zero ties. A grid maximum is not a certified supremum between queries. RMS uses scaled differences to avoid squaring large errors directly. All arrays are owned.
    NaturalCubicSplineTraceComplete owned moments and actual Thomas-system records from one natural fit. For k=max(n-2,0) interior unknowns, system vectors have length k. lower[0] and upper[k-1] are structural zeros; pivots/reduced_rhs are the actual post-elimination arrays, and multipliers[0]=0. Moments include both zero natural endpoints; degenerate empty/singleton fits use zero/one zero moments. All arrays own storage, with no prefix reruns or shared mutable state. Counts are logical loop iterations, not timings or all memory operations.
    PreparedCubicSplineOwned validated local-power spline for repeated value/derivative evaluation. Comparable to a scalar SciPy PPoly with endpoint-piece extrapolation. Construction checks/copies a public record once; evaluations never re-scan all coefficients. No references to the input survive. Empty/singleton models use the same zero/constant conventions as cubic_spline_eval(). Const methods are safe for independent concurrent reads. Finite arithmetic is checked, without a numerical error bound or a shape-preservation guarantee.

    Functions

    cubic_spline_eval()Evaluate a mutable public spline record after complete structural validation. Retains the original signature, zero/constant conventions and endpoint-piece extrapolation: the interval index is clamped, the query itself is not. Interior knots choose the right interval; the final knot uses the last. Validation is O(n), then lookup O(log n), with O(1) auxiliary storage. For repeated O(log n) evaluations, validate/copy once into PreparedCubicSpline. A structurally valid manually supplied record is not a C2/natural certificate.
    interpolation_error_scan()Evaluate and summarize a complete finite-query interpolation error census. Checks callback presence and all query finiteness before the optional cap, allocation or callback invocation. Then calls model and reference exactly once per query in order; callback exceptions propagate unchanged. O(q) work plus callback costs and O(q) owned storage, no input mutation/shared state.
    natural_cubic_spline()Fit a natural C2 cubic interpolant using a checked linear-time moment system. Finite strictly increasing knots and finite equally sized ordinates are validated before allocation. Empty input yields the empty zero evaluator; a singleton yields a constant, and two knots yield a line. For n>=2 the ideal interpolant has zero endpoint second derivatives, not zero endpoint slopes or globally linear extrapolation. It can overshoot monotone data. O(n) time/storage, owned result, no input mutation or shared state.
    natural_cubic_spline_trace()Capture complete actual widths, secants, moments and elimination arrays from the fit. Same canonical kernel and coefficients as natural_cubic_spline(). Full knot/ordinate validation precedes the optional complete knot cap and all size-dependent allocation. O(n) time/storage; results never truncate.

    datamunge/algorithms/cuthill_mckee.hpp

    Classes

    CuthillMcKeeStepOne actual CM queue removal and the neighbours it discovers. Owned values; steps are in forward BFS order even for a reversed result. Newly enqueued vertices use increasing (degree, original id), separately for each removed vertex, rather than sorting a whole BFS level.
    CuthillMcKeeTraceOwned complete output and actual queue history of one CM traversal. No input references survive. Arrays degree, parent and level use original ids; roots parent themselves at level zero. Each new component resets its level. Steps and forward_order always describe the forward run; order and position describe the requested final direction. Empty graphs have empty arrays and zero work. Adjacency scans count normalized directed entries, not raw duplicates.
    SymmetricPatternCoordinatesOwned row/column coordinates of a normalized symmetric sparsity pattern. Zero-based integral coordinates stored exactly as doubles (ids fit int). Row-major order, sorted columns; the optional diagonal is included once. No numeric matrix values or references to inputs are retained.
    SymmetricPatternMetricsSymmetric-pattern bandwidth and lower/upper envelope widths under an ordering. Width arrays use new row positions. The diagonal is treated as structurally present: isolated rows have zero widths. Profiles exclude diagonal entries; n+lower_profile counts lower skyline slots, not actual factor nonzeros. All values are owned; metrics describe the input pattern, not numeric values, Cholesky fill, optimality or a speed guarantee.

    Functions

    cuthill_mckee()Return a deterministic minimum-degree-start Cuthill–McKee ordering. Input is an undirected adjacency list; duplicate entries and diagonal loops are ignored. Off-diagonal symmetry is required after normalization. Components start at the smallest (degree,id) unvisited vertex. Each removed vertex's undiscovered neighbours are enqueued in that same order and marked immediately. Ties are explicit, independent of input row order. This is a heuristic: it may increase bandwidth. Reversing the whole result preserves bandwidth exactly; it can change profile and fill. No pseudo-peripheral-root search is performed. Read-only inputs, owned output, no shared mutable state. Empty input returns empty. Normalization and traversal take O(n log(n+1)+sum r_i log(r_i+1)) time and O(n+m_raw) auxiliary storage, including a sorted component-start list; duplicate-free row sizes are bounded by raw sizes r_i. No optional size cap.
    cuthill_mckee_trace()Capture the complete actual canonical CM traversal without replay. Same input, tie, component and reverse semantics as cuthill_mckee(). All endpoint ids and raw size sums are checked before optional limits and before normalized graph/history allocation. Symmetry is checked after normalization. Limits count raw vertices/entries (including loops/duplicates); zero disables only that optional cap. No silent truncation. Trace storage is O(n+m_raw).
    inverse_ordering()Validate and invert a new-position-to-original permutation. Empty input returns empty. Read-only input, owned result, O(n) time/storage.
    permute_symmetric_pattern()Normalize and symmetrically permute a graph pattern to new row/column ids. B[k,l]=A[order[k],order[l]] structurally, with loops removed and duplicate entries collapsed. Sorted output rows; inputs are unchanged, output owned. Empty graph/order return empty. Normalization as cuthill_mckee(); sorting output takes O(sum d_i log(d_i+1)), auxiliary storage O(n+m_raw).
    symmetric_band_pattern()Generate the simple symmetric pattern joining all ids at distance at most a width. n zero or one gives empty rows; width zero gives n isolated vertices. Width beyond n-1 is clamped, giving a complete graph. Counts are checked before graph allocation; optional limit counts directed entries and zero disables it. O(n+m) time/storage, read-only arguments, owned output, no random state.
    symmetric_pattern_coordinates()Extract sorted structural plotting coordinates after symmetric permutation. Uses permute_symmetric_pattern() and emits each directed off-diagonal entry once; optionally emits all n diagonal entries regardless of raw loops. No external plotting state or numeric matrix data. Time as permutation plus O(n+m) extraction; storage O(n+m_raw). Empty graph yields empty coordinates.
    symmetric_pattern_metrics()Measure bandwidth and both row-envelope profiles of a symmetric pattern. Normalizes as cuthill_mckee(), validates the full permutation, then scans every distinct directed edge once. Profiles use checked size_t sums. No numerical factorization; metrics do not count fill. Inputs read-only, output owned. O(n+m_raw) storage; normalization plus linear edge scan time.

    datamunge/algorithms/cycle_detection.hpp

    Classes

    BrentCycleStepOne actual Brent state after movement, phase entry or checkpoint reset. A checkpoint copies runner to reference without calling f; their equality at that row is not a detected collision, since movement precedes the next test. Indices identify positions in the original orbit, independent of equal state labels.
    BrentCycleTraceOwned actual Brent states and summary from the same kernel as ordinary detection. Records add O(mu+lambda) storage; they do not cache the function's state space or trigger extra transition calls. Callback storage is borrowed only during the call.
    CycleOptionsOptional completed-transition-call limit for diagnostic cycle finding. Zero means no caller limit. A positive limit stops before the next call that would exceed it; completed callback calls are not undone. It is not a timeout.
    CycleResultOwned least positive period lambda and least cycle-entry index mu. The historical layout/types are unchanged. Successful detection has lambda>=1; a default zero record is a placeholder, not a detected cycle.
    CycleWorkOwned cycle, its entry state and exact completed-call/equality counts. Evaluations are the sum of the four phase counters, including initial calls. Comparisons count only state-equality tests, excluding loop/limit checks. Entry is obtained by the canonical recovery phase without replaying the orbit.
    FloydCycleStepOne actual Floyd pair after a complete movement or a no-call phase reset. Detection pairs are x_t and x_(2t), with t starting at one. Locate resets tortoise to x0; measure holds tortoise at the recovered entry. Original-orbit indices distinguish equal labels reached at different times. Each row precedes that pair's equality test; phase resets are not callback evaluations.
    FloydCycleTraceOwned actual Floyd pairs and work from the ordinary detector kernel. Recording adds O(mu+lambda) storage and no callback calls or orbit replay. No retained callback/input views. Failure returns no partial trace.

    Functions

    brent_cycle_detection()Find an eventual period and entry by Brent's power-of-two block method. The deterministic callback is borrowed and may close over a larger state model. Reference indices are 0,1,3,7,..., with block lengths 1,2,4,8,... . After period detection, align a second pointer lambda ahead and move both to recover mu. O(mu+lambda) transition/equality work and O(1) auxiliary storage, excluding the callback's own cost/storage. No trace allocation; only caller-supplied callback effects can mutate external state. This legacy overload has no caller limit; arithmetic counters are checked.
    brent_cycle_trace()Record actual Brent checkpoints and all three phases without changing callback calls. Work/result match brent_cycle_work(); state recording adds O(mu+lambda) owned storage. Each row is a movement, checkpoint or phase entry, not necessarily a function call. In particular, checkpoint equality is followed by an advance.
    brent_cycle_work()Return Brent's entry state and actual counts from the ordinary detection kernel. Uses O(1) auxiliary storage, with no trace records or orbit replay. Costs and deterministic-callback requirements match brent_cycle_detection(). Limits count completed calls across every phase; exceptions do not undo callback effects.
    floyd_cycle_detection()Find an eventual cycle by Floyd's meeting, entry-location and period-measurement phases. Preserves the legacy transition-call order, including the repeated initial f(x0). Deterministic callbacks and ownership/mutation rules match Brent's overload. O(mu+lambda) transition/equality work and O(1) auxiliary storage, excluding f. No caller limit; counts are checked. Call counts alone are not elapsed-time claims.
    floyd_cycle_trace()Record actual Floyd pairs in all three phases without extra callback calls. Shares the ordinary/work kernel and preserves the repeated initial f(x0). O(mu+lambda) transition work and owned record storage, excluding callback cost. Global evaluation limits use CycleOptions; max_records is a separate online row cap, default one million, zero unlimited. Checks each next row's admission before its movement/reset, including phase-entry rows. Complete trace size cannot be known without traversing; this is not an upfront whole-orbit cap. Allocation failures or callback/evaluation limits can occur after earlier callback effects; those effects are not undone. No partial trace is returned. Empty callbacks reject before any movement. Independent calls share no state.
    floyd_cycle_work()Return Floyd's actual phase counts and entry without extra transition calls. The shared ordinary kernel uses O(1) storage and O(mu+lambda) work; callback lifetime, determinism, limits and mutation rules match brent_cycle_work().
    is_happy_number()Whether a positive integer reaches one under repeated decimal digit-square summation. Uses the canonical Brent kernel's recovered entry; zero is not happy. No orbit is stored and no caller/shared data are changed. The first transition is <=1620, making the subsequent finite search independent of the magnitude of the input.
    iterate_states()Materialise count successive states x0,f(x0),..., making exactly count-1 calls for count>0. Zero count returns empty, one returns only x0; these cases do not invoke f. Costs O(count) work/storage; inputs/shared state are unchanged except for callback effects. Returned values own their storage. This is an orbit renderer, not a detector.
    quadratic_cycle_step()Compute the mathematical quadratic residue (state squared plus constant) modulo m. Uses widened unsigned arithmetic, without uint64 square/add wrap. State and constant need not already be residues; modulus one returns zero. O(1) machine arithmetic, no allocation, no mutation/shared state. This is a transition, not a factorization algorithm or a random-map guarantee.
    rho_successors()Build a labelled rho map with the requested tail and cycle lengths. States 0..mu+lambda-1 advance consecutively; the last returns to mu. Starting from zero therefore has precisely the supplied lengths. O(mu+lambda) work/storage. Output owns its entries; no randomness or shared state is used.
    sum_squared_decimal_digits()Sum squares of decimal digits, with zero mapping to zero. O(number of decimal digits) work and O(1) storage; every uint64 input maps to at most 20*81=1620, so accumulation cannot overflow. No shared/input mutation.

    Types and constants

    CycleFunctiontype Deterministic uint64 transition; repeated equal inputs must have equal outputs. Callback exceptions propagate; a detector never owns or rewinds caller state.
    CyclePhaseenum Actual detector phase; counters separate discovery from recovering entry/period.

    datamunge/algorithms/cycle_sort.hpp

    Classes

    CycleSortPlacementOne actual final-cell placement in a cycle rotation. Each target occurs once in the complete trace. A placement stores the held value and its displaced value/identity before the value-cell write. The displaced item becomes the next held item until target==cycle_start closes the cycle; that final displaced duplicate of the original start is discarded. rank_begin is the first destination for this key in the remaining suffix; equal values may advance target. No full array snapshot is stored.
    CycleSortTraceOwned input, actual aggregate work and complete ordered placement records. Original identities travel with the same moves as values, exposing instability on equal keys. Final original_indices is output-to-input; intermediate array states must be interpreted with the held item because a cycle's start remains unchanged until closure. Empty/singleton traces have no placements and identity final indices. At most n records and O(n) extra storage, with no snapshots.
    CycleSortWorkOwned sorted values and actual operations from the canonical cycle-sort kernel. array_writes counts assignments to working value-array cells only. It excludes argument/output copying, the held item, counters, trace identities, allocation and physical device writes. Rank comparisons count strict less-than tests; equality comparisons include the final false duplicate-skip test. Loop/index tests are excluded. Empty/singleton inputs have zero counts. Values and counts are owned; no input references or shared mutable state survive.

    Functions

    cycle_sort()Return a sorted integer vector using write-minimal rank-scan cycle rotations. Retains the legacy by-value signature. The working vector is sorted in place with O(1) auxiliary storage; an lvalue argument is copied by the call. Every changed value-cell is written once, already-correct value-cells remain intact, and writes equal the Hamming distance to the unique nondecreasing key sequence. Equal-key records need not be stable. Signed extremes are valid; keys are compared without subtraction. For n>=2, even sorted/all-equal inputs require Theta(n^2) rank comparisons. No random/shared state or input size cap. The cycle-placement idea is related to Haddon, but repeated rank scans here are quadratic, rather than the paper's conditional linear-time variants.
    cycle_sort_trace()Capture the complete actual canonical cycle sort without replay or snapshots. Same integer/key/tie semantics as cycle_sort(). Owns two value vectors, final identities and at most n placement records: O(n) storage and Theta(n^2) time. No references survive. A complete element cap is checked before any copy, identity allocation or sorting; it bounds both history and quadratic work. Default 4096; zero disables only this optional cap. Even a sorted oversized input rejects. Results never silently truncate. Identity bookkeeping and result copies are deliberately excluded from the logical array-write count.
    cycle_sort_work()Sort and count the actual canonical cycle-sort operations without replay. Same placements and by-value ownership as cycle_sort(), with O(1) auxiliary storage beyond the working vector. No sorted reference, instrumentation copy of the algorithm or trace snapshots are used. Counts distinguish suffix less-than tests from duplicate equality tests and logical value-cell writes. A held-item swap counts one array write. All aggregate increments are checked.
    cycle_sort_write_lower_bound()Compute the minimum logical value-cell writes needed for nondecreasing keys. Makes a private std::sort reference, then counts positions whose input key differs from the sorted key. Every such cell must change; cycle_sort attains this bound, including duplicate keys, by leaving correct equal-value cells alone. The bound does not impose stable record identities and excludes argument copies, temporaries, allocation and device erase/write granularity. O(n log(n+1)) time and O(n) owned temporary storage; input read-only, no shared state. This independent reference computation is not part of the sorting kernel's measured work. Empty/singleton/already-sorted inputs return zero.

    datamunge/algorithms/cyk_parser.hpp

    Classes

    CNFGrammarEpsilon-free binary-normal-form grammar with arbitrary integer nonterminal ids. The original three-field layout is retained. unary maps one terminal byte to the ids A with A->byte; it does not represent nonterminal unit rules. binary entries {A,B,C} mean A->BC. Negative and sparse ids, including signed extremes, are valid. Repeated productions are semantically idempotent for recognition. No epsilon, unit-production or general-CFG conversion is supplied. The start may appear on a right-hand side because no epsilon rule exists. Public containers own their data; subsequent analyses own their results.
    CykAnalysisComplete owned CYK result, triangular chart and actual work. cells is ordered by increasing length, then begin; all cells, including empty ones, are retained. nonterminals lists all grammar ids, including unreachable ids and start, in ascending order. First witnesses try increasing left length then original binary-rule order. Duplicate terminal/binary rules do not create duplicate memberships. No input/grammar views or shared mutable state remain. Empty input rejects and has an empty chart; no epsilon convention is inferred. Public edits are possible; helper access/reconstruction checks local structure rather than certifying an edited result against the original grammar.
    CykCellOwned membership and first witnesses for a nonempty half-open byte span. entries is sorted by original nonterminal id and contains at most one entry per id. Empty entries means no nonterminal derives the span. Storage contains no references into grammar/input; begin is zero-based and length is positive.
    CykEntryFirst actual derivation establishing one nonterminal in a chart cell. left_length=0 denotes a length-one terminal rule; terminal is then the input byte, left/right are unused zero placeholders and binary_rule is SIZE_MAX. Otherwise the children have original ids left/right, with lengths left_length and cell.length-left_length. binary_rule indexes the original ordered binary vector. Length, start and input live in the containing cell/analysis. A first witness does not count or exclude alternative parses.
    CykParseNodeOne node of an owned first-witness parse in preorder. A leaf has length one, terminal equal to its input byte and both child indices SIZE_MAX. A binary node's children partition its half-open span and follow their parent in preorder; terminal is unused zero. Nodes contain original ids. The returned vector's indices remain valid until the caller mutates it.
    CykShapeChecked CYK geometry and worst-case dense-state/rule-loop sizes. cells=n(n+1)/2, splits=n(n-1)(n+1)/6, state_slots=cells*m, max_rule_tests=splits*r. These are potential capacities/work, not counts of successful derivations. Empty input has all four counts zero. No ownership beyond scalar values and no shared state.
    CykWorkChecked actual operations from the same CYK kernel that recognizes the input. Terminal candidates count raw matching unary-list entries, including duplicates. split_points includes every split, even when an empty child skips the binary rule loop. binary_rule_tests counts rules entered; matching_rules counts those whose two children are present, including repeated/already-known conclusions. new_states counts distinct (span,nonterminal) insertions. No replay or timing estimates; empty input has zero work. Counters exclude grammar preparation, dense initialization, chart extraction, allocation and witness reconstruction.

    Functions

    cyk_analyze()Analyze every substring with the canonical byte-oriented CYK kernel. Grammar semantics are those of CNFGrammar. Ids are compressed by sorting, never by max id; compiled byte/rule memberships use dense indices. Complexity is O(G log(G+1)+n*G+n^2*m+n^3*(r+1)) time and O(G+n^2*m) storage, including dense initialization, first choices and chart extraction; G counts raw grammar ids. For a fixed grammar the usual cubic bound applies. This computes membership and one witness, not ambiguity counts, probabilities, all parses or CFG conversion. Grammar preparation precedes the complete potential-capacity checks; those checks precede input/chart/choice allocation and parsing. Budgets bound possible state slots cells*m and binary-rule tests splits*r, rather than actual successes or actual tests after empty-child skips. Zero disables only the corresponding optional budget. No truncation. Empty input rejects with no chart/work.
    cyk_cell()Borrow one checked cell of a native or locally edited CYK analysis. O(1) checked triangular indexing. Validates requested bounds, full cell-vector length and selected cell coordinates; it does not validate every membership or certify grammar derivability. Borrow ends when the owner/cells are mutated or destroyed. Empty input has no valid cell. No allocation or shared state.
    cyk_first_parse()Recover one complete parse using the stored first witnesses, without rerunning CYK. Returns empty for a native rejected/empty result; accepted n-byte inputs give exactly 2n-1 nodes in preorder. Iterative traversal avoids recursive stack depth. Validates full chart length, root acceptance consistency and visited local witness uniqueness, terminal bytes, rule-index bounds and proper child spans. Public edits are not certified against the original grammar (which is not retained). Native reconstruction takes O(n*m) entry-search time and O(n) extra storage. The complete node cap is checked before node/task allocation; zero disables only this optional cap. No caller mutation or retained references.
    cyk_recognize()Recognize a byte string using the canonical CYK kernel and the original inline API. Same grammar and integer-id semantics as cyk_analyze(), without chart/witness output or optional budgets. Checked geometry/container limits still apply. Empty input always rejects; an unknown byte rejects any complete derivation. No caller mutation, retained references or shared state. Time is O(G log(G+1)+n*G+n^2*m+n^3*(r+1)); storage O(G+n^2*m). No grammar conversion, epsilon rules, Unicode tokenization, ambiguity counting or parse enumeration.
    cyk_shape()Compute exact CYK span, split and dense-state capacities without allocating. Cancels factors before multiplying, so representable results are not rejected merely because an uncancelled product overflows. All returned counts must fit size_t, even with zero binary rules. No mutation/shared state, O(1) time/storage.

    datamunge/algorithms/d_star.hpp

    Classes

    DStarLiteGridPersistent D* Lite for a rectangular four-neighbor unit-cost occupancy grid. Owns g/rhs labels and an indexed binary heap with at most one entry per vertex. Planning runs backward from a fixed goal; Manhattan priorities and a checked movement modifier let changed edges/new starts reuse prior state. Cell bounds must fit int and total cells<=INT_MAX. A shortest simple route has at most N-1 edges; backups at N or more are saturated to infinity, retaining every possible optimum and bounding integer labels. Priorities use exact uint64_t arithmetic; modifier headroom of4*N is reserved before moving the start. Blocked goal has rhs=infinity; unblocking restores its zero boundary. Blocked endpoints yield no route. No diagonals, weighted terrain, moving goal, sensor inference or automatic movement are included. Copying owns an independent full planner. Concurrent mutation of one instance needs synchronization. Each repair can touch the whole grid; there is no guaranteed speedup over fresh search. Heap operations are O(log N), backup degree<=4, persistent storage O(N), plus caller-requested trace.
    DStarRepairOwned route and actual interval work from one successful repair call. Default fields are an uncomputed placeholder. All caller data remain owned by the planner or this return value; no borrowed references are retained here.
    DStarStepOwned scalar operands/results of one actual popped vertex, without replay. rhs_after includes any self update; predecessor backups may affect other vertices.
    DStarTraceOwned initial/final labels, original live queue and actual repair pops. Entry accounting is5*N+initial_open.size()+steps.size(): grid cells,four label arrays,one per initial queue record and one per pop record. Scalar metadata, planner working storage, paths and allocator bytes are excluded. The complete base cost is checked before copies; each new pop entry before queue/label mutation. On a trace cap exception completed earlier pops remain in the planner; a later repair resumes correctly. work_before distinguishes already pending work from pops captured in this call. Initial/final labels outside the needed frontier can remain stale/infinite; only current-start optimality is guaranteed at termination.
    DStarWorkLogical work since construction or the previous successful repair. Includes pending map/start updates and current repair. Counts exclude input validation, heap comparisons/swaps, snapshots and final route extraction. Neighbor checks count actual Bellman backup neighbors, including blocked ones. Work is not elapsed time; a resumed capped repair may include prior completed pops.
    GridCellUpdateOne validated occupancy change, applied in input order by update_cells(). Repeated coordinates are allowed; the last value wins. Default is an unblocked origin update, not a request to initialize a planner.
    GridPathResultOwned grid route preserving the historical field order and failure convention. Coordinates are(row,column), endpoints included, four-neighbor unit steps. On failure path is empty,cost zero,found false; cost is meaningful only if found.

    Functions

    d_star_replan()One-shot optimal grid route using a newly constructed D* Lite planner. Preserves the original function signature, result shape and blocked/outside- terminal false/empty/zero convenience. Each call starts fresh; persistent reuse requires DStarLiteGrid. Empty/ragged grids throw. No optional cell cap is imposed, but the implementation count bound INT_MAX remains. Unit four-neighbor movement.
    grid_obstacle_mask()Build a validated owned occupancy grid from obstacle coordinates. All dimensions/counts/coordinates are validated before allocation. Repeated obstacles are harmless; coordinates use(row,column), zero-based.
    plot_grid_route()Render a checked grid route with native polygons and actual cell coordinates. Uses columns to the right and rows downward. Black cells are blocked, blue is the route, green/orange terminals are S/G(or S=G). Validates every supplied path step, occupancy, endpoint and cost before creating a plot; supports single cells. This is a renderer/feasibility check, not an independent optimality certificate.

    Types and constants

    d_star_infinityvariable Exact infinity sentinel for D* Lite labels and both components of an empty queue key. All finite labels are at most cell_count-1; priorities include a checked integer moving-start modifier. This value is not a finite path cost.
    DStarActionenum Actual D* Lite pop classification. A key refresh requeues an old moving-start key; lower sets g=rhs; raise sets g=infinity and recomputes this vertex and its predecessors.
    DStarKeytype Lexicographic integer priority(min(g,rhs)+Manhattan(start,u)+km,min(g,rhs)). Both components use d_star_infinity for an infinite minimum. Remaining heap ties use flattened cell id, which is not part of the mathematical key.

    datamunge/algorithms/dag_longest_path.hpp

    Classes

    DagLongestPathTraceOwned input edges, actual topological order, final paths and every reachable-edge attempt. topological_order covers all n vertices. Initial zero-indegree vertices are queued in ascending id; newly ready vertices are appended in original outgoing edge order. This FIFO policy is deterministic for fixed input, not a global smallest-id order. Original edge order and ready timing determine first ties. predecessor_edge uses m as the source/unreachable sentinel; result's vertex sentinel remains n. No input references or shared mutable state survive. Public edits are possible; witness recovery validates local chains rather than certifying arbitrary edited graphs for optimality or acyclicity.
    DagLongestPathWorkActual operation counts for the canonical DAG ordering and relaxation phases. Topological work includes the entire graph, even unreachable components. Relaxation work includes only edges leaving source-reachable vertices. Counts exclude input validation, adjacency construction, output copying, allocation and later path recovery. They count logical visits, not elapsed instructions or wall time. No shared state or borrowed storage.
    DagPathOwned source-to-target vertex/edge witness with its stored rounded total. Unreachable paths have found=false, empty arrays and negative-infinite weight. The source's empty-edge path has one vertex and weight zero. Edge indices select the exact original parallel edges. No input references survive.
    DagRelaxationOne actual candidate evaluated from a finalized reachable vertex. edge_index identifies the original directed edge. from_distance is final at evaluation; previous_distance may be negative infinity on first discovery. candidate is its checked finite double sum. improved uses strict > without a tolerance, so equal stored values preserve the earlier witness.
    LongestPathResultOwned single-source longest distances and predecessor vertices, retaining the original layout. distance[source]=0 uses the empty path; unreachable vertices have negative infinity. predecessor is n at source and unreachable vertices, otherwise an original vertex id. Finite negative distances are reachable, not missing. Values are ordinary rounded double sums; equal stored candidates keep the first improvement. The record alone cannot identify parallel-edge choices. Public arrays own their data and contain no caller references.

    Functions

    dag_forward_band_edges()Generate a forward DAG band, joining u to u+d for 1<=d<=width. Output is ordered by ascending u then positive offset d. Width beyond n-1 is clamped, yielding the complete forward DAG; width zero or n<=1 yields no edges. Finite weights of either sign are valid, even for empty output. Checked edge count w*(n-w)+w*(w-1)/2 precedes allocation, with factors cancelled before multiplication. Optional complete edge cap defaults to 1000000; zero disables it. No random/shared state, caller mutation or borrowed storage. O(n+m) time and O(m) owned output, with an immediate empty return.
    dag_longest_path_to()Recover the stored source-to-target path without rerunning the graph algorithm. Checks array sizes, source/sentinels and the visited predecessor chain, its original edge endpoints, finite weights and exact stored double recurrence. Unreachable target markers must be consistent. A length guard rejects edited cycles without recursion. Checks do not certify an edited graph's global acyclicity or optimality. O(n) worst-case time and O(path length) owned output space; no caller mutation or retained views. Unrelated trace events/order are not required for local recovery. The returned weight is the stored distance.
    dag_longest_paths()Find longest paths from one source by whole-graph topological dynamic programming. Vertices are [0,n). All finite negative/zero/positive weights and parallel directed edges are allowed; any cycle, including an unreachable cycle or self-loop, rejects. The original signature and two-vector result layout are retained. Full endpoint/weight/source validation precedes allocation. Kahn's FIFO order starts with ascending zero-indegree ids, and scans outgoing edges in input order. Strict stored > keeps the first tied candidate. No optional size cap, mutation of inputs or shared mutable state; O(n+m) time/storage. In exact arithmetic the DAG recurrence is exact. Ordinary double additions and comparisons can collapse distinct real path totals into ties; no exact- real, interval or compensated-summation guarantee is made. Any reachable candidate addition producing infinity rejects, even if it would lose to an existing route. Unreachable edges are validated but never added.
    dag_longest_paths_trace()Capture the complete actual longest-path run using the same canonical kernel. Same directed graph, numeric, tie, cycle and sentinel semantics as dag_longest_paths(). Full endpoint/weight/source validation precedes complete optional n/m caps and graph/order/trace allocation. Cycle detection follows graph allocation, so an oversized cyclic graph can hit a size cap first. Acyclicity is established before numerical relaxation. At most m events are captured, including unsuccessful reachable candidates, without replay or per- vertex snapshots. O(n+m) time/storage. Zero disables only its corresponding optional cap. Results never silently truncate and own all inputs/results.

    datamunge/algorithms/damerau_levenshtein.hpp

    Classes

    ByteEditOne checked edit at a position in the current evolving byte string. before/after own literal payloads: insert 0/1 bytes, erase 1/0, substitute 1/1 different bytes, transpose 2/2 reversed bytes, match 1/1 equal bytes. Native shortest scripts omit matches, so their vector length equals cost. No references into the trace or source survive. Positions are current-state offsets, not original source offsets.
    DamerauCellAll actual candidates and the selected move at one positive-prefix cell. Prefixes i,j are one-based lengths. last_source is the previous source row holding the current target byte; last_target is the earlier column of this row matching its source byte, captured before the current equality update. Candidate costs are clipped to bound=n+m; an unavailable bridge has bound. This cannot change an interior minimum, which is at most max(i,j)<n+m.
    DamerauShapeChecked rectangular capacities and finite sentinel for Lowrance–Wagner. rows=n+2, columns=m+2, cells=rows*columns, interior_cells=n*m, bound=n+m. Empty inputs still have the sentinel/prefix borders. Values are capacities, not operation counts or allocated bytes; no references or shared state.
    DamerauTraceOwned inputs, full sentinel table and actual Lowrance–Wagner cell records. table is row-major with shape.columns columns. Ordinary prefix distance D(i,j) is table[(i+1)*columns+j+1]. cells is row-major over positive prefixes, at index (i-1)*target.size()+j-1. Every cell is retained; no replay or snapshots. Strings are literal bytes, including NUL/high bytes, without Unicode decoding, normalization or case folding. Public edits are possible; helper checks are local consistency checks, not a certificate of edited-table optimality.
    DamerauWorkActual checked operations of the shared unrestricted-distance kernel. Byte matches count all equal-byte cells, not matches in one recovered script. Eligible bridges have both earlier occurrence indices positive. Selected bridges count winning DP cells, not necessarily edits on the final traceback. Counts exclude initialization, allocation, input copying and script recovery.

    Functions

    apply_byte_edits()Replay literal byte edits against an owned evolving string, checking each operation. Validates each kind's payload lengths/content, current position and exact expected before bytes before that operation. Native scripts omit matches; explicit equal one-byte match records are accepted as checked no-ops. A failure discards this call's local state, leaving an lvalue caller unchanged. No decoding/normalization or retained references. With k edits and maximum evolving length L, std::string replacement costs O(k*L+n) worst-case time, O(L) output storage; payload validation is constant per valid unit operation.
    damerau_edit_script()Expand the stored native optimal traceback into literal executable unit edits. Diagonal/insert/erase moves give direct operations. A transposition bridge deletes source-interior bytes, swaps its now-adjacent endpoints and inserts target-interior bytes between them. This yields current-state positions and exactly distance instructions; matches are omitted. Checks input-derived table/record shapes, endpoint distance and visited local coordinates, chosen recurrences and crossed bytes. Does not certify arbitrary edited tables as globally minimal. The distance cap is checked after basic shape/endpoint validation and before traceback/output allocation; zero disables it. Local validation may allocate O(n+m) temporary blocks. Native time/storage is O(n+m+distance), without rerunning the DP; outputs own their byte payloads.
    damerau_levenshtein_distance()Compute unrestricted unit-cost Damerau–Levenshtein distance between byte strings. Retains the original signature and Lowrance–Wagner semantics: insertion, deletion, substitution and adjacent transposition cost one, equality zero; characters/substrings can participate in further edits. Empty inputs give the other byte length. The result is a metric on literal byte strings and does not exceed Levenshtein distance. Uses the same executing kernel as the trace, a full checked (n+2)*(m+2) table and 256 last-row entries. Time/storage O((n+1)*(m+1)+256), including borders/empty cases; no optional size cap, caller mutation, retained references, decoding, normalization or shared state. Candidate arithmetic clips safely at checked n+m, without changing minima.
    damerau_levenshtein_trace()Capture every actual unrestricted-distance cell and first-minimum choice without replay. Same byte/unit-cost semantics as damerau_levenshtein_distance(). The complete border-inclusive cell cap is checked before input copying, table/record allocation or evaluation; zero disables only this optional cap. Empty cases still need their full border table and can exceed the cap. At most one cell record per n*m update, with checked counters and no array snapshots. Time and owned storage O((n+1)*(m+1)+256). Results never silently truncate.
    damerau_prefix_distance()Read one ordinary prefix distance from a checked trace table in O(1). Validates prefix bounds and input-derived flat table size, not optimality or every public record. No allocation, mutation, borrowed return or shared state.
    damerau_shape()Compute checked Lowrance–Wagner table dimensions without allocating. O(1) time/storage, no caller mutation or shared state. All five counts must fit size_t, including border dimensions and the finite n+m marker.
    optimal_string_alignment_distance()Compute the restricted optimal-string-alignment (OSA) byte distance. Unit Levenshtein moves plus a local crossed-byte D(i-2,j-2)+1 candidate. Unlike unrestricted distance this cannot reuse an aligned substring in a later edit; CA->ABC costs 3 and triangle inequality can fail. Symmetric, byte-exact and nonnegative, but not a metric. Three rolling rows give O((n+1)*(m+1)) time and O(min(n,m)+1) storage, including empty inputs. No size cap, caller mutation, retained references or shared state.

    Types and constants

    DamerauMoveenum Selected prefix-DP move, also identifying a literal byte-edit instruction. Native scripts omit matches. Candidate ties prefer diagonal (match/substitute), insert, erase, then transpose. A DP transpose can bridge deleted/inserted interior bytes; a ByteEdit transpose always swaps exactly two adjacent current bytes.

    datamunge/algorithms/davis_putnam.hpp

    Classes

    DpStepOwned result of one actual unit, pure or resolution elimination. after is the complete normalized formula: ascending distinct literals per clause, lexicographically ordered distinct clauses, no tautologies. Empty after means true; a contained empty clause means false. No subsumption is performed. Adjacent snapshots are related by existential elimination of abs(literal), not equivalence with that variable left free. All counts refer to this transition; positive/negative/pairs/tautologies/duplicates are zero for unit/pure steps. No views into the caller or previous states remain.
    DpTraceComplete owned normalized input, eliminating history and SAT verdict. Native ordering is deterministic: check empty clauses/sets first, then first unit, then smallest signed pure literal, then smallest absolute variable. All formulas are canonical as in DpStep. num_vars is a domain bound, not an array allocation: unused and very large sparse ids cost no dense storage. Every step eliminates at least one occurring variable; at most that many steps exist. No satisfying assignment or independent proof certificate is returned. Independent calls share no mutable state; public edits are unchecked.
    DpWorkActual rule applications and parent-pair work from one eliminating solve. Pair counts include tautological and duplicate conclusions. Peak counts distinct non-tautological clauses in normalized input or any completed state; excludes old/new coexistence, temporary unions and retained history. Counters exclude validation, sorting, normalization, scans, allocation and snapshot copies. Owned scalar values have no shared state; they are not elapsed-time estimates.

    Functions

    davis_putnam()Decide propositional CNF satisfiability by Davis-Putnam elimination. Literal +v/-v denotes variable v true/false, for 1<=v<=num_vars. Empty CNF is true; any empty clause makes it false. Duplicate literals and clauses are idempotent; tautological clauses are removed. Complete domain validation precedes all verdicts, including trivially true/false inputs. Uses the same executing kernel as davis_putnam_trace(), without retaining history or optional limits. Each step removes a variable. With C active clauses, width W and p/q pivot parents, a resolution step visits pq pairs, with sorted-set unions and ordered-clause insertion costing conservatively O(pq W log(W+1) log(C+pq+1)); scans/normalization and allocation are additional. Time and memory can grow exponentially in occurring variables; no polynomial or resource guarantee is implied. Caller input is unchanged; calls are independent.
    davis_putnam_grid_formula()Construct a square parent-grid CNF exposing one resolution growth step. For k=order, x=1, a_i=2+i and b_j=2+k+j (zero-based), returns k clauses (x OR a_i), k clauses (NOT x OR b_j), and the two clauses (NOT a_0 OR ... OR NOT a_(k-1)), (NOT b_0 OR ... OR NOT b_(k-1)). Uses variables 1..2k+1 and returns 2k+2 clauses, in that construction order, without normalization. Always UNSAT: x=false forces every a true; x=true forces every b true; each contradicts a negative tail. At k>=2 no initial unit/pure exists; eliminating x yields k*k distinct two-literal resolvents plus the two tails. At k=1 unit propagation takes priority. Owned output, O(k) clauses/literals/time/storage; no randomness, shared state or solver call.
    davis_putnam_trace()Trace the actual Davis-Putnam kernel with complete owned formula snapshots. Same normalization, rules and verdict as davis_putnam(), without replay. The optional clause cap bounds each distinct normalized set during construction. The cumulative pair cap is checked before an entire p*q resolution loop. Snapshot entries count one per snapshot plus one per clause plus one per literal, including initial and every after state; checked before copying that snapshot. Complete domain validation precedes these limits. Zero disables only an optional limit; overflow/container checks remain. On exceeding a limit, throws with no partial result or SAT/UNSAT verdict. Caps do not bound caller memory, input clause width, temporary unions, allocator bytes or time. Live old/new formulas and all snapshots may coexist. Trace overhead is linear in retained entries; kernel costs are documented on davis_putnam().

    Types and constants

    DpRuleenum One satisfiability-preserving variable-removal rule. Unit and pure record the signed true literal; resolution records a positive variable id. Each native step removes that variable entirely. No branching assignment or first-order quantifier procedure is represented.

    datamunge/algorithms/dda_line.hpp

    Classes

    DdaSampleActual pre-rounding accumulator and its exact-rational sample comparison. index is the zero-based major-axis sample. point rounds the stored double coordinates halfway away from zero; exact_point rounds the exact rational endpoint interpolation using the same tie rule. Drift and pixel errors are double diagnostics computed against integer quotient/remainder pieces of the exact sample, avoiding subtraction of two large nearly equal coordinates. They are approximations to real errors, not directed interval bounds. Owned values have no caller lifetime dependency or shared mutable state.
    DdaTraceOwned ordinary DDA points, actual accumulators and checked work diagnostics. The floating kernel is exactly the repeated-addition implementation, without endpoint snapping, clamping or replacement by the rational reference. One record per returned centre; no replay. Counts exclude final unused additions: coordinate_additions=2*steps and roundings=2*(steps+1), including the coincident case with zero additions and two rounds. Counters exclude reference/diagnostic arithmetic, allocation and copying. Storage and work are O(steps+1), with O(1) kernel state. Calls are independent and returned containers own all data.

    Functions

    dda_exact_sample()Round one exact rational endpoint interpolation to its nearest centre. At N=max(abs(dx),abs(dy)), sample i is (x0+i*dx/N,y0+i*dy/N). Uses unsigned 64-bit products, integer quotient/remainder and signed halfway-away-from-zero rounding, with no floating selection or accumulation. The largest product is (2^32-1)^2, which fits uint64 for 32-bit int. Coincident endpoints accept only index zero. O(1) work/storage, no allocation, input mutation or shared state. The result lies within the endpoint rectangle.
    dda_line()Rasterise integer endpoints using the original repeated-double-addition DDA. Retains the four-argument signature, DDAPoint and accumulator output on safe original inputs. Uses N=max(abs(dx),abs(dy)), initial exact integer doubles, increments double(dx)/N and double(dy)/N, then rounds each current coordinate halfway away from zero. Coincident endpoints return their single centre. Both coordinate differences and loop/count arithmetic are widened. No clipping, endpoint snapping or tie repair is performed: small floating drift may select the other side of a rational tie, and sufficiently large drift may miss the final minor endpoint. Returned centres need not equal dda_line_exact(). O(N+1) time and owned output storage, O(1) auxiliary state; no trace/reference arithmetic or input/shared mutation. No optional allocation cap; large requests can exhaust memory. Floating results assume ordinary non-fast-math evaluation; the current floating environment is neither changed nor restored.
    dda_line_exact()Rasterise exact rational major-axis samples with signed nearest-centre ties. Calls the same integer quantizer as dda_exact_sample() at every index. Both endpoints are included; for distinct endpoints the centres are 8-connected, with one unique centre per major-axis coordinate. Coordinate error relative to each exact sample is at most one half; minor rounding also bounds distance to the geometric segment by one half. Reversal returns the reversed sequence. This is a mathematical comparison API, not a replacement for the repeated double accumulator. It is not a cell supercover or antialiased raster. O(N+1) time/output storage and O(1) auxiliary state; integer products fit uint64 for all supported endpoints. Independent calls own results and share no state.
    dda_line_trace()Record actual DDA accumulators, rounding and rational-reference differences. Uses the same executing kernel as dda_line(), without replay. Retains every original accumulator choice and adds exact integer nearest-centre comparisons plus approximate drift/coordinate-error diagnostics. A positive complete-point limit is checked before all allocation; zero disables only that optional cap. No truncated raster or partial trace is returned on failure. O(N+1) time and storage; reference work is additional to the recorded floating operation counts.
    dda_point_count()Count inclusive DDA samples without allocating or walking the line. Widened differences cover all int coordinates up to 32 bits. No mutation, shared state or allocation; O(1) time/storage. Includes one coincident point.

    Types and constants

    DDAPointtype Owned integer pixel-centre pair (x,y), retaining the original DDA alias. Centres do not imply cell-area coverage, clipping, antialiasing or intensity.

    datamunge/algorithms/de_casteljau.hpp

    Classes

    BezierSubdivisionOwned degree-preserving left/right Bezier control nets from one triangle. At split s in [0,1], left(u)=original(s*u) and right(u)=original(s+(1-s)*u) in exact arithmetic. Both nets have the original control count and share a copied meeting point; no views remain. At s=0 the left net is constant; at s=1 the right is constant. Degree-zero input gives one identical point in each net. No tessellation or tolerance- based adaptive stopping is performed. Floating identities hold approximately.
    DeCasteljauShapeChecked complete interpolation-triangle geometry for m control points. Empty input has zero counts. For m>0, there are m levels, m(m+1)/2 stored points including the controls, m(m-1)/2 point blends and twice that many coordinate blends. These are potential exact loop counts, not elapsed time or counts of individual machine arithmetic instructions.
    DeCasteljauTraceOwned actual interpolation levels and final value from one kernel execution. levels[0] copies the controls; subsequent rows contain actual increasing-index updates, with sizes m-1 down to one. Empty input retains the legacy zero-point sentinel and has no levels. point_blends increments inside the actual loop, excluding copies, validation and allocation. No triangle is reconstructed by replay. Finite t outside [0,1] extrapolates and has no convex-hull guarantee. Fields own their values; public edits are unchecked and calls share no state.
