    PlanarPointOwned two-double planar point, retaining the original interpolation API layout. Coordinates are unvalidated plain values; curve functions require finite x/y. Default construction gives (0,0). No ownership outside these two scalar fields.

    Functions

    de_casteljau()Evaluate a planar Bezier by the original repeated weighted-blend recurrence. Uses (1-t)*left+t*right in increasing index order on a copied work vector. Preserves the original name/signature, PlanarPoint layout, interpolation.hpp include and empty-control result (0,0). A singleton is constant. All controls and t must be finite, including the empty-input parameter. Finite parameters outside [0,1] retain polynomial extrapolation, subject to finite intermediate arithmetic. In exact arithmetic, t=0/1 interpolates endpoints and [0,1] yields convex combinations; ordinary rounding is not an exact hull certificate or a universal small relative-error guarantee near cancellation. Nonfinite intermediates reject even when another algebraic arrangement could be finite. O(m^2+1) time and O(m) owned temporary storage; input unchanged, no shared state.
    de_casteljau_sample()Sample uniform parameter intervals with both requested endpoints included. Returns segments+1 points. Parameters use std::lerp(first,last,i/segments), with first and last assigned directly; no repeatedly added parameter step. Equal or descending endpoints are valid, as is finite extrapolation. Distinct grid parameters may round to duplicates in tiny intervals. All controls and parameter bounds are validated once, before complete output/work caps and allocation. Empty controls return the legacy zero sentinel at every parameter; this is not a curve. A singleton is constant. Output count and prospective total point blends (segments+1)*m(m-1)/2 use checked arithmetic. Zero disables either optional cap independently, not arithmetic/capacity checks. O(m+k(m^2+1)) work for k=segments+1, O(k+m) output/temporary storage, no shared/input mutation.
    de_casteljau_shape()Count a complete de Casteljau triangle without allocating or evaluating it. Products are cancelled before multiplication. O(1) time/storage, no mutation or shared state. Zero controls has all zero counts; one has one stored point.
    de_casteljau_subdivide()Extract both exact-subcurve control diagonals during a single evaluation. Only O(m) work/output storage is used; no full triangle is retained. Left diagonal runs from the original first control to B(t); reversed right diagonal runs from that same computed B(t) to the original last control. The exact reparameterization identities are documented on BezierSubdivision. Validation precedes output-count caps, and the inclusive count is 2m including both copies of the meeting point. At most m(m-1)/2 actual point blends; no curve replay.
    de_casteljau_trace()Capture complete actual rows from the same evaluator as de_casteljau(). No replay or independent reconstruction. Empty input has zero stored points; its sentinel does not define a Bezier curve. The complete triangle cap includes initial controls and is checked after full finite validation, before copying or allocating rows. Zero disables only the optional cap; count/capacity checks remain. O(m^2+1) time and O(m^2) owned history, with O(m) temporary work.

    datamunge/algorithms/decision_tree_induction.hpp

    Classes

    C45CandidateOne actually evaluated continuous threshold, with entropy in bits. Candidates appear in node preorder, then increasing feature and distinct-value boundary order. Threshold is a finite separating midpoint, falling back to the lower value if rounding reaches the upper value. selected marks the first strict positive maximum ratio at this node. The records belong to their owning trace.
    C45NodeTraceActual selected rows, depth, entropy and stopping reason of one node. Vector position equals the corresponding DecisionTree node id. rows preserves original input order, with owned indices; labels and feature values are not copied. candidate_begin/count delimit this node's records in C45Trace::candidates.
    C45OptionsGrowth controls for the restricted continuous gain-ratio learner. Root depth is zero. A zero depth cap is unlimited; min_samples is a node-size stopping rule, not a minimum child size. Zero/one both allow any impure node. max_candidates bounds the whole call before an excess candidate is partitioned; zero means unlimited. No partial model is returned on any exception.
    C45TraceOwned continuous model and actual training provenance from a shared kernel. No training is replayed. Ordinary c45_train() omits row/candidate records. Input values/labels are borrowed only during the call and are never mutated. Empty aligned inputs give empty vectors. Trace storage includes O(n*h) row indices and one record per evaluated candidate, h the largest reached depth.
    DecisionTreeOwned flat node array, with root zero and an empty array for empty training data. Copies are independent; prediction borrows the tree without mutation. Do not mix categorical and continuous prediction functions: no runtime model-kind tag is stored.
    DecisionTreeNodeOne owned node of a categorical ID3 or continuous C4.5-style tree. Internal nodes keep the local majority label for unseen categorical values. Class ties choose the smallest integer label. Indices refer to DecisionTree::nodes.

    Functions

    c45_predict()Follow checked continuous threshold tests to a leaf without mutating inputs. O(visited depth) work, O(1) extra storage. Validate only the visited path: bad indices, nonfinite thresholds/tested query values, categorical internal nodes, short queries and cycles throw. Unvisited malformed branches and unused query values are ignored; a leaf accepts an empty query. No runtime model-kind tag exists for leaf-only models.
    c45_train()Continuous binary tree using maximum information-gain ratio, inspired by C4.5. Restricted unpruned threshold variant: no average-gain filter, MDL penalty, categorical tests or missing-value inference. Each feature considers all adjacent sorted distinct boundaries. Midpoints avoid overflow; if rounding reaches the upper value, the lower value is used so both children are nonempty. First strict positive maximum wins (lowest feature, then earliest boundary); no tolerance is applied. Label ties choose the smallest integer. Purity, min_samples, max_depth or no positive computed ratio stop growth. Root depth is zero; min_samples limits the parent size, not child size. Empty aligned inputs return no nodes; width-zero rows give a majority leaf. Inputs are checked, borrowed and unchanged; result owns storage, no shared state. Construction uses an explicit stack. Work at a searched node of m rows and d features is O(d*m*m*log(m)) with current ordered-map entropy calculations; sum this over nodes. Temporary partition storage is O(n) excluding sorting/maps and the O(n)-node model.
    c45_train_trace()Train the restricted gain-ratio variant and retain actual candidates and rows. Uses the same kernel as c45_train(); no candidate search or model is replayed. The whole-call budget counts only thresholds actually evaluated, including zero- gain candidates. It is checked before excess partition work; exceptions return no partial model. Trace records own indices and scalar statistics, not copies of inputs. Recording adds O(n*h+c) storage for row memberships and c candidates, with h reached depth; training complexity and finite-input rules match c45_train(). No pruning, average-gain eligibility filter or MDL threshold penalty is added by tracing.
    id3_predict()Predict a class by categorical traversal, falling back on an unseen value. Reads only visited features; extra query values are ignored. A leaf-only tree accepts an empty query. Checks visited indices and limits visits to the node count, rejecting cycles; unvisited malformed branches are not inspected. Work O(h*log(b)), b the largest visited branch count, with O(1) extra storage.
    id3_train()Greedy multiway ID3 induction over integer-coded categorical attributes. Features are categories, never ordered thresholds. Each path uses a feature at most once. Stop at purity, exhaustion of features, the depth cap, or nonpositive best information gain. Root depth is zero; max_depth=1 permits only a root split. Equal computed gains choose the lowest feature index; majority ties choose the smallest class label. No pruning, missing-value inference or gain-ratio correction is performed. Empty aligned inputs return an empty tree; rows of width zero give a majority leaf. Borrows inputs, owns result, no shared mutable state. Work is O(n*d*h*log(n)) as an upper bound with ordered maps, h<=d; recursive row partitions can use O(n*h) storage in addition to the returned nodes.

    Types and constants

    C45StopReasonenum Reason a continuous-tree node stopped, or confirmation that it split. Reasons are checked in declaration order; no-positive-gain includes no features or no distinct feature values. This is training provenance, not a prediction.

    datamunge/algorithms/depth_first_search.hpp

    Classes

    DepthFirstEventOwned scalar data for one transition from the executing DFS kernel. vertex is the current/new/finished vertex. neighbor exists only for examine; otherwise it is n. edge_index is the scanned original id for examine, incoming tree-edge id for discover, and m for the root or finish/goal events. depth counts tree arcs from start. stack_size is after push/pop for discover/finish and current size for examine/goal. neighbor_state is sampled before examination descent, and is the unused unseen placeholder for every other event kind.
    DepthFirstOptionsInclusive limits on complete graph storage and actual retained event count. Complete terminal/endpoint validation precedes all caps and allocation. Original edges count loops, duplicates and unreachable components. Event caps are checked online before appending each actual event. Zero disables an optional cap; arithmetic/capacity checks remain. Failures return no partial trace.
    DepthFirstTraceOwned goal-search or complete source-component DFS state and actual events. n is the parent/depth sentinel; edges.size() is the absent parent-edge marker; 2*n is the discovery/finish-time sentinel, checked representable before graph allocation. Times tick only at discoveries and genuine finishes, starting zero. Seen-but-unfinished vertices therefore have a valid discovery and missing finish. Parent/edge/depth are set on first entry only. preorder contains all entries, postorder only actual finishes. Successful goal search keeps its path active; it does not fabricate unwinding. Full traversal sets goal_requested=false, goal=n, result.path empty and result.found=false, while expanded/preorder exhaust all source-reachable vertices. Unseen after an early stop need not mean unreachable. Every container owns data, including original edges; no shared mutable state.
    DepthFirstWorkActual vertex entries/exits, adjacency scans and maximum live frame count. Each vertex is discovered at most once. Every examined arc has exactly one target-state category; unseen arcs cause discovery, active arcs close a directed ancestor cycle (including self-loops), finished arcs need no descent. Counters exclude domain validation, adjacency construction, allocation/copies, result-path extraction and timestamp/event bookkeeping. They are not timings.

    Functions

    depth_first_search()Find the first directed source-to-goal path in recursive DFS adjacency order. Preserves the original four-argument signature, BasicPathResult layout and search_more.hpp include. Uses heap-stored {vertex,next-successor} frames instead of recursive calls, preserving descent and resume order without a C++ call-stack depth limit. Vertices are marked globally on first entry and never entered again. Outgoing arcs retain input order; parallel arcs/self-loops are accepted but cannot rediscover a marked vertex. Stop immediately on first entering the goal, before examining its outgoing arcs. Start=goal returns one vertex; failure an empty path. expanded counts distinct first entries including the goal, not edge scans. The selected simple path need not be shortest and may change with edge order. All terminals/edges are validated before allocation, even for start=goal or unreachable bad arcs. O(n+m) total worst-case time/storage including adjacency; the traversal alone uses O(reached vertices+scanned arcs) work and at most n active frames. No trace/history allocation, input mutation or shared state.
    depth_first_search_trace()Record actual entry, edge-target state, finish and goal events from the same DFS. No replay, full stack copies or synthetic early-stop finishes. Returns the same path/entry count as depth_first_search(), plus state and timing described by DepthFirstTrace. Retains O(n+m) input/state/event storage: at most two events per reached vertex, one per scanned arc and one goal event. A successful early stop may leave vertices unseen or active. Complete graph validation precedes all optional caps; timestamp 2*n and container capacities remain checked when caps are disabled. Graph preparation remains O(n+m), even for an immediate goal.
    depth_first_traversal()Exhaust the source-reachable directed component and record genuine finishes. Uses the same explicit continuation kernel without a goal stop. Discovery and finish intervals are complete for every reachable vertex; isolated/unreachable vertices remain unseen. This is one source tree, not a forest over all n vertices. The path/success fields are intentionally empty/false; expanded counts all entries. Work, caps, timestamps, ownership and O(n+m) storage match the traced goal call.
    rooted_tree_edges()Generate a labelled forward rooted tree with fixed maximum branching. For child i=1..n-1, emit ((i-1)/branching,i) in increasing child order. Root is zero. Branching one gives a chain, two a heap-indexed binary tree, and branching>=n gives a star. Zero/one vertices give no edges, but branching must still be positive. O(n) work/output storage, owned deterministic arcs, no randomness/shared state. Complete n-1 output count is capped before allocation.

    Types and constants

    DepthFirstEventKindenum One actual directed DFS transition, with no synthetic early-stop finishes. Discover occurs after marking/pushing a new vertex; examine before deciding whether to descend; finish after a frame pop; goal after its discovery.
    DepthFirstStateenum DFS state at the stopping time or immediately before a scanned arc. Active vertices are exactly the current frame path. Finished vertices have genuinely exhausted adjacency; unseen vertices have never been entered. A successful early stop leaves the goal and its ancestors active.

    datamunge/algorithms/deutsch_jozsa.hpp

    Classes

    DeutschJozsaClassicalResultSequential classical promised decision and actual callback count. Agreement of 2^(n-1)+1 values implies constant only under the promise. n=0 needs one observation. The full table is not certified.
    DeutschJozsaResultOriginal two-field numerical Deutsch–Jozsa decision. constant is the compatibility threshold p0>0.5, not a promise certificate. Probabilities are unclipped and may slightly exceed one through rounding.
    DeutschJozsaTraceOwned executing-circuit snapshots and observed promise evidence. No replay or repeated oracle evaluation. Basis bit q is qubit q, with q=0 least significant. mean_phase is count-derived (zeros-ones)/2^n in binary64, independently of gate accumulation. No shared mutable state; all arrays own their data. Stateful callbacks describe an observed table, whereas a physical Boolean oracle must describe a fixed function.
    DeutschJozsaWorkCircuit oracle, callback, gate and amplitude-pair counts. Excludes allocation, copying, probability extraction and callback internals. A butterfly updates one pair per single-qubit Hadamard.

    Functions

    deutsch_jozsa()Simulate one phase-oracle query, returning the original result type. Applies n initial Hadamards, f(x)&1 once per ascending x, then n final Hadamards. No promise verification or random measurement is performed. n=0 calls f(0) once and returns constant. O(2^n) storage; O((n+1)*2^n) work plus callback cost. Exceptions do not undo callback side effects. Separate calls share only f.
    deutsch_jozsa_classical()Decide the promised problem by querying distinct ascending inputs. Stops at the first differing low bit or 2^(n-1)+1 agreeing outputs. n=0 queries its single input once. O(1) storage, work proportional to queries plus callback cost. No promise verification or random sampling occurs.
    deutsch_jozsa_trace()Record actual gate-boundary states, promise counts and simulator work. Same kernel and gate order as deutsch_jozsa(); no replay. Stores three complex arrays and one integer table, each of length 2^n: O(2^n) total storage. Complete state-count cap is checked before allocation/calls. Zero disables only this cap; dimension, capacity and counter-overflow guards remain. Exceptions return no partial trace; earlier callback side effects remain.

    Types and constants

    DeutschJozsaPromiseenum Promise category determined from every observed effective bit. Constant includes n=0; balanced requires exactly half ones in an even domain. Neither explicitly identifies a table outside the promise.

    datamunge/algorithms/dfa_minimization.hpp

    Classes

    HopcroftOptionsComplete projected graph and online logical history policies, each zero disabling its cap. Counts include a materialized sink and unreachable states. Trace units count records and retained state IDs, not bytes/capacity/peak memory. Input validation precedes caps and completed graph/predecessor allocations.
    HopcroftPassOwned actual preimage and splits from one producing splitter/symbol pass. Empty preimages retain an empty split list; a zero-symbol machine has no passes despite actual splitter pops. Splitter labels refer to the copied set popped at this pop index, even if later passes refine its original block.
    HopcroftRunOwned reachable quotient, completed-state partition labels and selected producing work. blocks index completed states, including any sink and unreachable input states. Their IDs describe the final internal partition, not the quotient's reachable BFS numbering. result starts at0 and retains only reachable quotient blocks.
    HopcroftSplitOwned actual block split and its producing worklist branch. Every vector is ascending in original completed-state labels. inside and outside partition parent exactly. Both means an existing pending parent was replaced; it does not mean two additional pushes.
    HopcroftTraceOwned actual initial partition, chronological producing passes and final run. Initial units are one per block plus one per retained state ID. Each pass adds 1+|splitter|+|predecessors|; each proper split adds 1+|parent|+|inside|+|outside|. Counts are admitted before history copies, after their triggering sets are known. Working sets and ordinary output are outside this capture policy. No truncation, replay, partial result or retained input references.
    HopcroftWorkSelected producing visits of the ordered-set worklist implementation. These exclude validation, completion, set insertion/comparison internals, copying, allocation, quotient construction and history; not timing or FLOPs.
    MooreOptionsComplete projected-input and actual history policies for Moore refinement. States/transitions include unreachable states and any materialized rejecting sink. Zero disables each independent cap. Ordinary moore_minimize() disables policies, preserving its legacy uncapped entry point.
    MooreRoundActual before/after labels and per-state signatures in one synchronous round. Each signature begins with its state's old block, then destination old-block IDs in symbol order. New IDs follow first state encounter, not map key order. Stable means block count unchanged; numeric labels can still be renamed.
    MooreRunOwned completed graph, final partition and reachable minimal quotient. Completed graph/partition include unreachable states; result removes unreachable quotient blocks in ascending-symbol BFS order. Acceptance bytes retain the first state's original nonzero representation, rather than normalizing to one.
    MooreTraceOwned actual initial labels, complete round histories and producing run. Initial capture units count one label per completed state. Each full round adds one record, before/after labels, signature row records and their integers: 1+3n+n*(k+1). Working maps and ordinary run output are excluded from this logical capture policy. Admission precedes complete history copies; no replay.
    MooreWorkActual Moore rounds, state/signature work and ordered-map comparisons. Signature components count examined integer pairs, not individual less-than instructions. Map counts depend on the standard-library tree implementation. Completion, quotient construction, allocations and copying are excluded.

    Functions

    hopcroft_minimize()Minimize a possibly partial DFA using preserved ordered-set worklist refinement. Validates the entire input, materializes an implicit rejecting sink if needed, then refines accepting/rejecting blocks. Splitters use LIFO order, symbols ascend, and nonpending ties append the intersection half. Pending parents become both halves. The reachable quotient uses symbol-order BFS numbering and retains representative acceptance bytes. Empty language yields one rejecting state, including zero input states; zero symbols permits only epsilon. The set-based implementation scans every partition state for every nonempty preimage and linearly searches pending sets. It does not claim the optimized textbook O(k*n*log(n)) implementation bound. A conservative bound is O((k+1)*n*n*log(n+1)) time and O(n*(k+1)) ordinary working/output storage for completed n and alphabet k, excluding borrowed input and optional history. Legacy has no optional graph/capture policies; all inputs/outputs own their storage and no references/shared mutable state are retained.
    hopcroft_minimize_run()Execute the shared refinement with complete projected-input caps and selected work. Same algorithm/order/domains as hopcroft_minimize(). Caps include unreachable states and any added sink before graph copies/predecessor allocation. Capture cap ignored. Selected counters exclude set internals, copying and quotient work.
    hopcroft_minimize_trace()Capture actual initial blocks, preimages and proper splits during producing refinement. Same contracts as hopcroft_minimize_run(). Whole known capture records are admitted before history copies after computing their triggering sets. No truncation/replay/partial history. Capture units count records/state IDs, excluding ordinary working sets, output, metadata and capacity; not peak RAM.
    moore_chain_dfa()Construct a unary acceptance-distance chain for refinement scaling. State i moves to min(i+1,n−1); only the final state accepts. All states are reachable from0 and pairwise distinguishable by distance to acceptance.
    moore_demo_dfa()Return the original reachable six-state, two-symbol demonstration DFA. Rows(1,2),(0,3),(4,5),(4,5),(4,5),(5,5); start0, accepting2,3,4.
    moore_minimize()Minimize a possibly partial DFA by actual ordered-map Moore signature refinement. Complete rejecting moves/start with a sink, refine all states synchronously, then return reachable quotient blocks in symbol-order BFS numbering. No input mutation/references retained. Empty-language zero-state input yields one rejecting state; zero alphabet allows epsilon only. Ordinary call disables optional policies. At most n rounds; vector-key maps give a conservative O((k+1)*n^2*log(n+1)) work bound and O(n*(k+1)) driver/output storage.
    moore_minimize_run()Return actual completed graph, final partition and selected Moore work. Same producer/ordinary numbering; complete projected caps precede graph copies. Capture cap is ignored. No input/shared-state mutation. Ordinary complexity applies; completed and quotient outputs are owned independently.
    moore_minimize_trace()Capture actual old/new partitions and every produced signature per round. Same producer and complete caps as moore_minimize_run(). Admit initial labels then each whole known round before history copies; no replay/truncation or partial result. Storage adds the actual retained units described by MooreTrace.

    Types and constants

    HopcroftScheduleenum Actual worklist action for a proper split of one current block.

    datamunge/algorithms/dfa_minimization_analysis.hpp

    Functions

    dfa_unary_threshold()Build the minimal unary DFA accepting words of length at least a threshold. States 0..minimum_length advance on symbol0, and the last state accepts and self-loops. Every state is reachable; any pair is distinguished by reaching the accepting threshold from the later one first. Threshold 0 accepts epsilon and every unary word. Full state/count policy admitted before allocation. O(minimum_length+1) time and owned storage, no randomness/shared state.
    hopcroft_example_dfa()Return the original six-state, two-symbol Hopcroft report fixture. Accepting states 2,3,4 have identical future behavior; states 0,1 are equivalent and state 5 is a rejecting sink. All six input states are reachable from 0. The reachable minimal quotient has three states. Fixed owned storage; no shared/input state, randomness or retained references.

    datamunge/algorithms/dice_coefficient.hpp

    Classes

    DiceBigramCountOne unsigned-byte bigram and its actual left/right/shared multiplicities. key=(first_byte<<8)|second_byte. All 65,536 byte pairs are distinct, including NUL and bytes 128–255. Native trace rows are sorted by this unsigned key.
    DiceConsumeEventActual remaining-count transition for one right-hand bigram occurrence. One record per ascending right byte offset, including failed matches. Before and after refer only to this key's unconsumed left count. A miss has both zero.
    DiceOverlapChecked multiset sizes, intersection/union counts and normalized overlap. Counts are occurrence counts, not numbers of distinct keys. For a nonempty combined multiset, Dice=2*shared/total and Jaccard=shared/union_count. For two empty multisets both values use the caller's explicit empty-equality convention. Scores use binary64 rounding; integer fields retain exact checked counts.
    DiceTraceOwned actual bigram counts, consumed occurrences, inputs and scores. No replay or independent reconstruction: sorted rows and events come from the executing dictionary kernel. Rows include keys seen on either side. The rich trace scans even identical/short inputs, unlike the scalar early-return paths. Containers own their values, including byte strings; no shared mutable state. There is no case folding, trimming, padding, UTF-8 decoding or normalization.
    DiceWorkActual occurrence-level operations of the shared consuming kernel. One left dictionary update per left bigram and one right lookup per right bigram. Counts exclude hash collisions/probes, reserve/rehash, equality checks, copies, trace-only row insertion/counting, sorting and score arithmetic.

    Functions

    dice_coefficient()Compute the original literal byte-bigram multiset Dice coefficient. Identical strings give 1; any other pair with a length below two gives 0. Otherwise uses 2*sum(min(count_a,count_b))/((a.size()-1)+(b.size()-1)). Equal bigram bags can belong to different strings: score one does not prove equality. Bytes, case, whitespace and embedded NULs are literal; there is no Unicode decoding, normalization or padding. Inputs are borrowed and unchanged. A size_t-count dictionary packs each key into 16 bits, without substring keys. Expected O(|a|+|b|) work; O(min(|a|,65536)) auxiliary storage. Hash collision behavior can increase work; the identity/short early paths allocate no table. Calls share no state. Scores use binary64 rounding, not a semantic probability.
    dice_coefficient_trace()Record actual byte-bigram consumption and sorted multiplicity rows. Uses the same consuming kernel as the nontrivial scalar path, without replay. Scans both inputs even if equal/short. Complete A+B cap is checked before any copying/allocation/scanning; zero disables only the optional cap, not checked arithmetic. Expected O(|a|+|b|+K*log(K+1)) work including the final row sort, K<=65536 distinct union keys. Owned inputs/events require O(|a|+|b|+K) storage.
    dice_overlap_counts()Normalize supplied multiset overlap counts without constructing strings. Validates shared<=min(left,right), then checks the total sum. No allocation, mutation or shared state; O(1) work. Does not verify that counts came from actual strings. The empty convention is supplied separately from bag sizes.

    datamunge/algorithms/difference_map.hpp

    Classes

    DifferenceMapResultOriginal result layout with a decoded B-side cross-projection estimate. After positive iterations solution is P_B(f_A(x_before)), not P_B(x_after). At a true fixed point it equals P_A(f_B(x_before)) and lies in both sets if callbacks are actual projections. converged retains only the strict numerical step<tol rule: small beta can hide a large projection gap. It is not a feasibility certificate. With zero iterations, solution=P_B(x0), residual=0 is an unevaluated historical sentinel, and converged=false. Containers own data; defaults are empty/zero.
    DifferenceMapStepOwned vectors from one actual four-projection difference-map update. Calls occur in order A(x), B(x), A(f_B), B(f_A). f_A=(1-1/beta)A(x)+x/beta; f_B=(1+1/beta)B(x)-x/beta. estimate_a and estimate_b are the cross projections; x_after=x_before+beta*(estimate_a-estimate_b). Eight n-vectors are retained.
    DifferenceMapTraceOwned initial/final iterates, actual steps, decoded result and stop metadata. No replay or independent reconstruction. Callback side effects occur only during the recorded execution; a thrown call returns no partial trace but prior external effects remain. The iterate, B-side estimate and cross-projection gap are distinct. No shared mutable state except what callbacks capture. Empty vectors are valid zero-dimensional states if both callbacks return empty vectors.
    DifferenceMapWorkActual callback/update counts and retained-history entry count. Each completed update calls A and B twice and updates n coordinates. A zero budget calls only B once. Counts exclude callback internals, validation, norm arithmetic, copying and allocation. History entries count one per record plus its eight n-vectors, excluding initial/final/result vectors and transient buffers.

    Functions

    difference_map()Run the difference map with validated vectors and corrected solution decoding. Preserves callable-by-value parameters, defaults and the original result layout. Inputs/outputs must be finite; each output must keep x0's dimension. beta must have a finite reciprocal. Updates preserve A(x),B(x),A(f_B),B(f_A) order; the last B cross-projection is returned without an extra final projection call. With max_iter=0 only B(x0) is evaluated, and the historical zero residual is unevaluated. tol=0 disables strict stopping. O(n) driver storage and O(kn) vector work for k updates, plus four projection costs per update. No general nonconvex convergence or arbitrary-beta guarantee is made. Genuine projectors are a caller responsibility; step<tol is not a membership certificate.
    difference_map_history_cost()Checked entry cost of one actual retained n-dimensional update: 1+8n. One entry counts the record, eight n entries count its vectors. Does not include initial/final/result vectors, vector metadata or transient work. O(1), no allocation.
    difference_map_trace()Record actual eight-vector steps, stable norms and projection calls without replay. Same compiled kernel and decoder as difference_map(). Online entry caps are checked before each new iteration's callbacks/retained snapshots; early stopping therefore needs space only for actual records. One record costs 1+8n entries. Initial/final/result vectors and temporary work are excluded from this history cap. Zero disables only the optional cap; checked arithmetic remains. O(kn) history in addition to driver storage/callback costs. Prior callback side effects remain if a later iteration or cap throws; no partial trace is returned.
    project_affine_hyperplane()Euclidean projection onto the affine hyperplane normal dot x = offset. Scales the normal by its largest component, accumulates in long double, and checks intermediates/results; wider arithmetic depends on the platform. No exact or universal full-range guarantee. O(n) work/storage; inputs borrowed unchanged, output owned, no shared state. Zero-dimensional/zero normals are invalid.
    project_finite_set()Return the closest listed finite point, using earliest input on a numerical tie. Validates every point before searching, including unreachable/nonwinning entries. Empty-dimensional points are allowed, but the point set must be nonempty. Uses long-double hypot distances with checked intermediates; no exact tie predicate. O(M*n) validation/search work and O(n) owned output, ignoring borrowed set storage. No input mutation or shared state. Represents a generally nonconvex constraint.

    Types and constants

    DifferenceMapStopenum Reason iteration stopped; neither value certifies constraint feasibility. Zero tolerance disables the strict step test, even at an exact fixed point.
    DifferenceProjectiontype Type-erased projection from a borrowed vector to an owned vector of the same size. Outputs must be finite. Callbacks may hold external state; the algorithm validates shape/finiteness but cannot establish nearest-point or set-membership properties.

    datamunge/algorithms/diffie_hellman.hpp

    Classes

    DhExchangePublic values and raw shared residues from one deterministic toy exchange. Retains supplied g/p and four computed residues, not private exponents. Does not certify a group or protocol. No shared state; raw residues are exposed.
    DhPowerCycleComplete cyclic subgroup generated by a validated nonzero prime-field element. values[x]=g^x mod p for x=0..order-1, starting at1. The next product closes back to1; exactly order products are performed. Values are distinct, owned and ordered by exponent. This small-cycle enumeration is not a strength estimate.

    Functions

    dh_exchange()Execute four arithmetic exponentiations and retain both parties' raw results. Deterministic toy transcript; private exponents are inputs but are not stored. Preserves all legacy arithmetic conventions, including p=1 and zero exponents. Agreement holds algebraically and does not prove secrecy, primality, subgroup strength or peer identity. O(log(a)+log(b)+1) word operations, O(1) storage; all operations are variable-time and no randomness/KDF is performed.
    dh_power_cycle()Enumerate an exact generated subgroup until the first return to the identity. Checks p>=2 prime with the existing deterministic uint64 primality API and 1<=g<p before any cap/enumeration. Performs one product per emitted residue, including the closing product; order divides p-1. The cap is online because order is unknown. Failure returns no partial cycle. O(order) storage/work plus the primality check. Not suitable for enumerating large production groups.
    dh_public_key()Compute g^secret modulo p, preserving the original arithmetic-only API. Delegates to exact mod_pow(); p may be prime, composite or one. Exponent zero, zero/nonunit bases and unreduced g are accepted. Does not sample/validate keys, groups or public values. Variable work exposes exponent properties.
    dh_shared_secret()Compute peer_public^secret modulo p without protocol or peer validation. Same exact arithmetic/edge conventions as dh_public_key(). Zero/one/p-1 peers are accepted and can collapse the output; callers must not infer safe agreement from matching residues. No authentication, key derivation or constant-time work.

    datamunge/algorithms/dijkstra.hpp

    Classes

    DijkstraPopOwned state of one actual heap removal, fresh or stale. A fresh removal settles the vertex before its outgoing arcs are inspected. Its relaxation_begin/count index this pop's contiguous range in DijkstraTrace::relaxations. A stale pop has zero relaxations. Heap_after is the size after the whole expansion.
    DijkstraRelaxationOwned operands and outcome of one actual outgoing-edge inspection. Original edge identity is retained for multigraphs. Equal candidates do not update either the predecessor or heap; no decrease-key or hidden replay occurs.
    DijkstraTraceOwned actual removals, relaxations, chosen edge identities and logical work. No input views survive. Histories use O(V+E) storage without full distance/heap snapshots. The trace cap counts pops plus edge inspections, not result arrays or adjacency storage.
    DijkstraWorkLogical operation counts of the actual lazy binary-heap execution. Counts exclude validation, adjacency construction and binary-heap comparator calls. Heap pushes include the source; every pushed entry is eventually popped, including stale ones.
    ShortestPathResultOwned shortest distances and one strict-improvement predecessor per vertex. The original two-field layout is retained. Unreachable distances are positive infinity; source/unreachable parents are kNoPredecessor. This public record can also be constructed manually; reconstruct_path() validates the shape and visited chain before indexing it.

    Functions

    dijkstra()Computes all source distances with Dijkstra's nonnegative directed shortest-path algorithm. Uses a lazy binary min-heap of (distance,vertex); equal keys choose smaller vertex id. Adjacency preserves input order and only strict improvements update parents. Self-loops, zero weights and parallel arcs are accepted. Encode an undirected edge twice. All input arcs, including unreachable ones, are validated before adjacency allocation. Rejects nonfinite/negative weights and any nonfinite examined candidate sum, even when that candidate would not improve a known shorter route. Distances use rounded double sums, not exact-real arithmetic. No input mutation/shared state; no trace allocation. Work O(V+E+(E+1)log(E+2)), storage O(V+E); for simple graphs the usual bound is O((V+E)log V). The lazy heap may hold O(E) entries in a multigraph.
    dijkstra_parallel_workload()Generates a two-vertex stress graph with strictly improving parallel arcs 0->1. Returns weights count,count-1,...,1 in that order. At positive count m the actual lazy heap peaks at m entries, has m+1 pushes/pops and m-1 stale removals, despite V=2. Zero count returns no edges. Complete output guards precede allocation. No random or shared state; O(count) work/storage. Intended for operation-count checks, not timing claims.
    dijkstra_trace()Records actual lazy-heap pops and outgoing relaxations without replay. Uses the exact ordinary dijkstra() kernel, validation and tie rules. Caps are checked online before the corresponding event is performed; failures return no partial trace. A zero cap disables only the optional history budget, not capacity checks. No full heap or distance snapshots; capture adds O(V+E) work/storage to the base bound.
    reconstruct_path() ×2Recovers a finite predecessor chain, safely rejecting malformed public records. For an out-of-range or positive-infinity target returns empty before examining other fields, preserving the original convenience behavior. A reachable target requires equal vector lengths and a visited chain of finite nonnegative distances, valid parents and no cycle; an early sentinel is a root. Only the visited chain is checked. Without edges or a stored source this does not certify that a manually supplied root is the source or that parent distances satisfy edge recurrences. No mutation/shared state; O(path length) work/storage with a length bound n, avoiding unchecked indexing and infinite loops.

    DinicAugmentationOwned actual path push, with residual operands copied before mutation.

Each level, phase, augmentation and path-arc record counts one entry; owned original edges/results/work arrays are outside this optional history budget. No input views survive.
    DinicWorkLogical operations in one actual Dinic execution, excluding validation/allocation. BFS scans include zero-capacity, reverse and self arcs of reached vertices.     FlowCertificateNumerical primal/dual checks for a public maximum-flow result. Feasibility and cut equality are tested separately. A nonzero tolerance gives numerical agreement, not an exact proof; every error and the signed gap remain visible.
    FlowNetworkOwned directed capacitated fixture, with explicit terminals and isolated vertices. Generators validate capacities and checked output counts before allocation.

    Functions

    dinic_disjoint_paths()Generates equally long internally disjoint source-to-sink paths for one blocking phase. Source=0, sink=1; paths are emitted in order, each with fresh internal vertices. With p paths of length l>=1, E=p*l and V=2+p*(l-1). Zero paths yields two isolated terminals. For length one the paths are distinct parallel arcs. Counts/capacity guards precede allocation; no shared state or randomness. Work/storage O(V+E).
    dinic_max_flow()Computes directed maximum flow using BFS levels and iterative current-arc blocking flow. Preserves the original four-argument API and MaxFlowResult layout. Adjacency follows input order, including separate forward/reverse pairs for parallel/antiparallel arcs and self-loops. Uses strictly positive residuals, replacing the former absolute 1e-12 cutoff; tiny positive capacities are not discarded. No recursive DFS or history storage. Complete terminal/finite-capacity validation precedes adjacency allocation. Returned per-edge flows come from each pair's cancellation residual, retaining small represented flows. Every residual subtraction/addition and total flow must remain finite and make positive representable progress; otherwise the fit fails explicitly, with no partial result. This is double arithmetic, not an exact-real or arbitrary-precision solver. Calls borrow inputs unchanged and share no mutable state. Exact-arithmetic bound O(V^2 E) after graph initialization, O(V+E) storage; the terminal BFS adds O(V+E) for empty/disconnected cases.
    dinic_max_flow_trace()Captures actual BFS levels and residual path updates in the same Dinic kernel. The history budget is reserved before each BFS or path update, including the terminal failed BFS. Exceeding it returns no partial trace. Storage/work for capture adds O(C) to the base algorithm, with C defined in DinicTrace. Zero disables only the optional cap.
    dinic_staircase_paths()Generates disjoint unit-capacity paths of lengths one through paths. Exactly one path augments in each successive phase. E=p*(p+1)/2 and V=2+p*(p-1)/2; checked factors are divided before multiplication. Zero paths gives isolated terminals. Counts/optional cap precede allocation; O(V+E) work/storage, no random/shared state.
    max_flow_certificate()Checks edge bounds, conservation, reported value and a supplied cut independently of the solver. Uses long-double sums followed by checked finite-double conversion. Does not run Dinic, infer a different cut or silently adjust flows. Work O(V+E), owned work/output O(V+E). Default absolute tolerance is zero, in capacity units; a positive tolerance explicitly relaxes every scalar check. Inputs are unchanged and calls share no state.

    CapacityEdgetype Directed (tail,head,capacity) input arc; each parallel/antiparallel arc has its own identity.

    Functions

    pohlig_hellman_log()Solve by prime-power digits and CRT using the native linear digit search. Requires prime p and exact base order in [1,LLONG_MAX], dividing p-1; validates all prime factors by g^(order/q)!=1. Target must lie in that subgroup. Trial factoring can take O(sqrt(order)) checks; each native digit search scans q candidates linearly, not sqrt(q) and not a prebuilt lookup table. Selected work is capped by default. Fixed-width products and CRT merges are widened; modular inverse delegates to the canonical checked extended-Euclidean API.
    pohlig_hellman_run()Run the shared linear-digit Pohlig-Hellman producer with actual selected counts.
    pohlig_hellman_trace()Capture the actual factor decomposition, digit searches and CRT merges.
    pollard_rho_log()Solve g^x=h in a prime field using the native deterministic-seeded rho walk. Reduces g,h modulo p; requires both nonzero, prime p, and declared order in [1,LLONG_MAX] dividing p-1 with g^order=h^order=1. The order may be a multiple of the exact base order; candidates are individually verified. A collision implies an exponent congruence modulo the exact ord(g). Solving that congruence modulo a larger declared annihilator is a stronger condition and can discard useful collisions. Uses the historical seed, three-way branch and up to40 restarts, with a default selected-operation cap. An unresolved return is not proof no logarithm exists. O(1) producer storage; restart iteration bounds are checked without wrap. Heuristic square-root collision behavior is not a per-run work guarantee.
    pollard_rho_log_collision_study()Execute the original six-prime/fixed-start first-collision experiment through the shared walk. Uses forty starts per prime, original targets and a0/b0 schedule; reports actual completed iterations separately from the legacy zero-based index. Does not refit a scaling law or count a collision as a successful logarithm.
    pollard_rho_log_first_collision()Run the shared native walk from explicit exponent state until first collision/cap. This stops before congruence solving; a collision alone is not a logarithm.
    pollard_rho_log_run()Run the shared rho solver with actual work and configurable selected policies.
    pollard_rho_log_trace()Capture each actual cursor update and collision from the shared rho solver.

    datamunge/algorithms/dixon.hpp

    Classes

    DixonCollectionOwned positive smooth relations and actual scan progress for a fixed modulus. Input candidates are consecutive integers from floor(sqrt(n))+1, even for perfect squares. Only accepted relations are retained; zero residues are counted separately. This is a deterministic scan, not uniform random sampling.
    DixonDependencyAn actual zero row of the eliminated parity matrix and its square congruence. Owns original relation indices and full exponent sums, all even. Both GCDs are retained; the solver selects a proper minus factor first, then plus. A factor need not itself be prime. No combinations of different zero rows are searched, and a trivial congruence can therefore leave the run unsuccessful.
    DixonRelationOne positive factor-base-smooth square residue from the actual scan. Owns exponents in the collection's prime order. The empty product is one; residue zero is excluded. No references into solver storage survive return.
    DixonTraceOwned actual collection, tested dependencies and logical elimination work. No replay: the same kernel implements dixon_factor(). Collection stops at base_size+1 relations or the candidate budget. All-row GF(2) elimination uses dynamic 64-bit word vectors, so bases and relation sets can exceed 64 bits. Only dependencies visited up to the first proper factor are captured. Captured scalar cells equal base.size()+sum(exponents.size()+3) over relations +sum(relation_indices.size()+exponent_sums.size()+4) over dependencies. The optional cap excludes vector objects and transient elimination storage. Scratch space is O(k*k), in addition to captured output; no shared mutation.

    Functions

    dixon_collect()Collect a fixed window of positive smooth square residues for Dixon analysis. Scans exactly candidates integers unless the capture cap or an allocation fails. Supports all uint64_t moduli at least two, including primes/even inputs; no primality classification or factorisation is promised. Zero residues are skipped before trial division, so division of zero cannot loop forever. Each candidate costs O(k+log(n)) trial/modular operations, with k=base_size; base construction uses trial division. Returned vectors own their storage.
    dixon_factor()Return a proper divisor from the shared deterministic Dixon kernel. Preserves the original two-argument API and first k+1-relation batch strategy. Tests at most 2000000 consecutive candidates, from floor(sqrt(n))+1. Dynamic parity and combination vectors support bases beyond the former machine-word boundary; singleton dependencies are eligible. See dixon_factor_trace() for ordering, complexity and the limits of this bounded deterministic method. Retains no dependency history and imposes no optional capture cap.
    dixon_factor_trace()Factor by deterministic smooth squares with owned actual GF(2) evidence. Same scan, relation target, pivot/row order and arithmetic as dixon_factor(), with a configurable candidate budget. Computes both GCDs for each visited dependency. A zero result means only that this bounded run did not find a factor; neither primality nor irreducibility follows. Rank-nullity guarantees a dependency for k+1 rows but does not guarantee a nontrivial factor. Uses 128-bit products for exact uint64_t modular arithmetic. Search is a sequential teaching variant; Dixon's random-sampling expected-time theorem does not establish a subexponential bound for this scan. For R<=k+1 rows, elimination costs O(k*R*ceil((k+R)/64)) word operations and O(k*R) storage.

    datamunge/algorithms/doomsday.hpp

    Classes

    DoomsdayAnchorOwned monthly anchor with its one-based day of year and computed weekday. All twelve anchors for one year share its doomsday; differences between their ordinal days are multiples of seven. All fields are values, without references.
    DoomsdayTraceOwned actual year terms and signed monthly offset for a validated date. No replay: doomsday_weekday() calls this same executing kernel. The monthly reference is January3/4, February28/29, March14, April4, May9, June6, July11, August8, September5, October10, November7 or December12. All fields are values; no allocation or references into caller storage.
    DoomsdayYearOwned actual year terms of Conway's Doomsday rule. Uses astronomical year numbering, including zero and negative years, and floor division for centuries. All weekday codes are Sunday=0 through Saturday=6. The dozen decomposition is an equivalent mental-arithmetic identity evaluated alongside the direct offset, not a second weekday solver. Default fields are an uncomputed placeholder, not the terms of year zero. O(1), no allocation, input references or shared mutable state.

    Functions

    doomsday_date_trace()Evaluate a validated date through actual Doomsday year and month terms. Reuses gregorian_month_days() for complete date validation before reference lookup or offset arithmetic. Negative offsets are normalized mathematically. Supports every int year, with the same proleptic/astronomical conventions as doomsday_year_trace(). O(1), no allocation or shared mutation.
    doomsday_day_name()Name a Sunday-first weekday code, normalizing arbitrary signed integers. No locale/timezone is consulted; the returned English name owns its string.
    doomsday_is_leap()Test whether an astronomical year is a proleptic Gregorian leap year. Year zero and negative years use the same divisibility rule. No historical adoption cutover, allocation, mutation or timezone; O(1).
    doomsday_month_anchors()List all twelve canonical monthly Doomsday anchors for an astronomical year. Retains the original March14 convention; January3/4 and February28/29 adjust for leap years. Weekdays come from the shared date kernel, ordinal days from existing Gregorian month lengths. O(12) fixed work/storage, no allocation.
    doomsday_of_year()Weekday of the last day of February, using the shared Doomsday year kernel. Supports every astronomical int year, with zero denoting1 BCE. All dates use the proleptic Gregorian calendar, without historical adoption cutovers. O(1) time/storage, no allocation or shared mutable state.
    doomsday_weekday()Weekday of a valid proleptic Gregorian date by Conway's Doomsday rule. The original three-argument function now validates complete dates and uses floor-based negative-century terms through doomsday_date_trace(). No timezone, locale or historical cutover is inferred. O(1), no shared mutation/allocation.
    doomsday_year_trace()Compute a year's Doomsday weekday with actual integer terms. Supports every int year with floor-based century decomposition. Applies the Gregorian rules proleptically, with astronomical year zero and no historical Julian/Gregorian cutover. No allocation, replay or shared mutation; O(1).

    datamunge/algorithms/double_dabble.hpp

    Classes

    DoubleDabbleStepOne owned actual correction-and-shift stage, with padded most-significant-first nibbles. before and after contain decimal digits0..9. corrected can contain8..12 and is an intermediate binary nibble field, not decimal text. carry_out[i] moves from nibble i toward i-1; the rightmost nibble receives input_bit. All four vectors have trace.capacity entries. Default fields are an uncomputed placeholder.
    DoubleDabbleTraceOwned actual binary-to-BCD result, steps and logical work from the shared kernel. Captures at most64 stages of at most20 nibbles, without replay. Four nibble snapshots per stage use O(B*D) storage; ordinary conversion/work calls keep O(D) scratch. This finite uint64_t domain needs no optional history cap. Default fields form an uncomputed placeholder, not a computed zero-width result. Caller inputs are unchanged, no borrowed references or shared mutable state.
    DoubleDabbleWorkLogical work of the shared fixed-capacity shift-and-add-three kernel. Counts nibble-level operations, excluding validation, allocation, zero trimming, output formatting and trace copies. With B requested bits and D capacity, digit_checks=nibble_shifts=B*D. Corrections and decimal carries depend on the selected value and are equal; these are not CPU timings or hardware cycles.

    Functions

    bcd_to_uint64()Decode an unpacked most-significant-first BCD digit vector with checked uint64_t arithmetic. This inverse is ordinary decimal Horner evaluation using multiply-ten/add, not a reverse shift/subtract-three algorithm. Leading zeros are accepted. Complete digit-domain validation precedes overflow checking. O(n) time, O(1) storage, no mutation/allocation or shared state.
    double_dabble()Convert the low requested bits of a uint64_t into decimal BCD digits. Preserves the original function/return ordering and deliberate high-bit truncation. Width zero selects no bits and returns{0}. Width64 uses every input bit without a shift by64. Leading output zeros are removed, retaining one zero. The shared conversion loop uses comparisons, add-three corrections, shifts, OR and masks; capacity is an exact fixed lookup. O(B*D) logical work and O(D) scratch, B=num_bits and D=capacity. No mutation/shared state.
    double_dabble_capacity()Minimum BCD digit capacity sufficient for every value of a requested binary width. Exact fixed integer lookup for widths0..64; no floating logarithm or runtime division. Capacity is one for width zero and20 for width64. O(1), no allocation.
    double_dabble_string()Decimal string of the selected low bits through the same Double Dabble kernel. Returns ordinary decimal text, not a packed BCD byte string. Width-zero, truncation, validation and complexity follow double_dabble(); no shared state.
    double_dabble_trace()Capture actual Double Dabble nibble states without replay. The executing kernel is shared with ordinary conversion. Snapshots retain requested-width padding, while final digits remove leading zeros. Every after state decodes to the selected input prefix. Captured storage is bounded by64 stages times four20-nibble vectors plus scalar fields; O(B*D) work/storage.
    double_dabble_work()Measure actual nibble work while converting, without retaining stage snapshots. Same conversion, masking and validation as double_dabble(); O(B*D) logical work and O(D) scratch. Includes all allocated leading-zero nibbles.

    datamunge/algorithms/dpll.hpp

    Classes

    DpllEventOwned actual partial assignment at a search event, with original clause identities. assignment has num_vars+1 values: index0=0; other values0(unassigned),+1,-1. node ids start at0 in entry order. Root parent uses SIZE_MAX. Unit/conflict clause is the original zero-based index; all other kinds use clauses.size(). No formula normalization, assignment replay or borrowed state is represented.
    DpllMeasurementOwned actual model/verdict and work without search-history capture. Carries no borrowed input references. Defaults are an uncomputed placeholder.
    DpllTraceOwned original CNF, actual search events, total result and work from one solve. No replay: the same executing iterative kernel implements ordinary/work calls. Trace entries count1 per formula plus1 per clause plus1 per input literal, then1 per event plus1 per captured assignment element. The cap excludes scalar metadata, working stack, allocator bytes and elapsed time. Root/event capacity is checked before the affected capture; all input validation precedes limits. Zero disables only the optional cap. A cap exception returns no partial verdict.
    DpllWorkChecked logical work of the shared DPLL kernel, excluding validation/copies/allocation. nodes counts root and branch entries. decisions counts split points, branches counts attempted children; nodes=branches+1. Clause visits count outer clause-loop iterations of status/unit/pure scans. Literal visits count each inspected occurrence, including both passes over unsatisfied clauses in the pure scan; a second literal pass does not add another outer clause visit. Counters are operations for this implementation, not CPU timings or CDCL work.
    SatResultOriginal SAT verdict and owned total model, preserving the historical two-field layout. On SAT, assignment has num_vars+1 entries, index0 is zero and every variable is +1 or -1; don't-cares are filled true. On UNSAT, assignment is empty. Default construction is an uncomputed false/empty placeholder. No borrowed views.

    Functions

    cnf_assignment_satisfies()Check a supplied total signed model against every original CNF clause. Fully validates clauses and model domain first. Index0 is ignored; positions 1..n must be +/-1. Empty CNF is satisfied, a contained empty clause is not. O(n+L) time, O(1) scratch, no allocation/mutation or shared state.
    dpll_sat()Decide validated propositional CNF satisfiability by deterministic DPLL. Keeps the original signature, SatResult layout and search order: first raw unit occurrence, then smallest-id pure variable, then first unassigned variable true before false. Original clause/literal order, repetitions and tautologies remain; duplicate occurrences can delay unit detection without changing SAT. Empty CNF is true; an empty clause is false. Complete domain validation precedes any verdict or dense allocation. Uses a heap-backed iterative frame stack, avoiding C++ recursion by decision depth. Dense assignments use O(n) space each, up to O(n^2+L) live storage for n variables and L input literals. Search can visit O(2^n) nodes, with repeated polynomial scans per node; no learning/restarts, watched literals, timeout or polynomial/resource guarantee is provided. Input is unchanged; calls share no mutable state.
    dpll_sat_trace()Capture actual DPLL nodes, propagation, conflicts and restored backtracks. Same executing kernel as dpll_sat(); snapshots store raw original-clause ids and partial states, not a replay or clause-learning proof. UNSAT is justified by completed search, with explicit exhausted events for both-failed splits. See DpllTrace for entry accounting and exclusions. Capture adds O(events*n) copying/storage to the ordinary kernel; default cap is one million entries.
    dpll_sat_work()Solve with actual logical work and no retained event/input history. Same validation, search order, model, complexity and ownership as dpll_sat().
    random_3sat_formula()Generate the original report's reproducible three-distinct-variable random CNF stream. Each clause samples rng()n ids, rejects duplicate ids before drawing its sign, then uses rng()&1 for polarity. Clause duplicates are allowed; no tautological clause can occur. This preserves the original mt19937 draw order; modulo bias means it is not an exactly uniform mathematical3-SAT sampler. O(m) expected generation work for n>=3; rejection has no deterministic draw-count bound. The full literal count/cap/domain are checked before allocation or engine mutation.

    Types and constants

    DpllEventKindenum Kind of an actual iterative DPLL transition or terminal node. Enter records root/branch arrival; unit/pure record post-assignment states; conflict identifies a falsified original clause; exhausted means both children failed, not that its own partial state falsifies a clause. Backtrack restores the parent state. Satisfied records a partial state already satisfying every clause, before filling don't-cares in the separate final total model.

    datamunge/algorithms/earley_parser.hpp

    Classes

    EarleyItemOne dotted original production and its origin column. In chart column k, prod names an original production, dot counts matched RHS symbols and 0<=origin<=k. Equal triples in a column are deduplicated; duplicate input productions retain distinct prod ids. Standalone default fields are a placeholder, not a claim that a production exists. Copies own their scalars.
    EarleyLocationNumeric location of an item in an owned Earley chart. Both default coordinates are earley_no_item, denoting no parent. Validity depends on the containing trace; copying does not retain a pointer into it.
    EarleyReasonOwned first-insertion evidence attached to one actual chart item. Parents are numeric chart locations, always lexicographically earlier than the target. This gives an acyclic first-witness deduction graph even for nullable cycles. Duplicate attempts do not replace the first reason. It is not a packed parse forest and does not enumerate all derivations. Default is a placeholder.
    EarleyResultOwned recognition verdict, legacy-compatible column sizes and actual work. The temporary chart/indexes are discarded; no input or provenance is retained. Default is an uncomputed placeholder. A computed chart_sizes has N+1 entries, including empty columns, even for an undefined start or rejected input.
    EarleyTraceOwned actual chart and first-insertion reasons from one Earley recognition run. Copies own independent grammar/token/chart buffers. Items keep insertion order and original production ids; reasons[k][i] explains chart[k][i]. Full chart closure supports epsilon, unit cycles, left recursion and ambiguity, but returns no parse forest or count of parses. Empty RHS means epsilon; symbol strings, including empty strings and embedded NUL, are opaque atomic names. A symbol is nonterminal exactly when it occurs on a LHS. A missing start production rejects. Logical capture cost is base+2I, where base=2N+P+sum(rhs lengths)+2 and I is the number of unique items. Base counts start/LHS/RHS/token strings and one column metadata record per boundary; each item and its reason count once. String bytes, runtime indexes, scalar fields and allocator overhead are excluded. Editing returned records may invalidate numeric references; no automatic repair occurs.
    EarleyWorkActual logical recognition work, excluding compilation, hashes, allocation and capture copies. Every item is processed once. Predictions run once per requested nonterminal per column; completion joins each waiter with each distinct completed span once. Counts are not execution time and checked uint64 arithmetic cannot wrap.

    Functions

    earley_chart_sizes()Preserve original unique-item counts at boundaries zero through N. Same semantics, validation, ownership and complexity as earley_recognize_work(). These count dotted items, not parse trees. One grammar's bounded per-column counts do not establish a general complexity bound. No optional capture quota.
    earley_item_text()Format one selected actual item with escaped symbols, a dot and its origin. Validates the selected location, production, dot and origin, not the whole mutable trace or its proof. Debug-quoted strings distinguish an empty named token from an empty RHS and escape embedded control bytes. No mutation or I/O.
    earley_recognize()Preserve the original boolean Earley recognition interface. Same grammar semantics, ownership, closure, complexity and errors as earley_recognize_work(); discards only its summary. No optional capture quota.
    earley_recognize_work()Recognize a general CFG with indexed prediction/completion and checked logical work. Supports epsilon and late waiters without iterating a vector while extending it. All raw index/count validation precedes allocation. Inputs are borrowed unchanged; temporary charts/indexes are discarded after preparing an owned summary. Duplicate productions retain original ids. Missing start rejects, including a default empty grammar. For fixed grammar, expected O(N^3) time and O(N^2) chart/index storage assume ordinary constant expected hash access; string preparation is additional. This implementation promises no unconditional worst-case hash bound, all-parses enumeration, lookahead, LR(0) precomputation or Leo optimization. Calls share no mutable state; borrowed inputs must not be concurrently modified.
    earley_trace()Capture actual unique items and first-insertion parents from the shared recognizer. Complete raw input/count validation and the base-budget check precede copies and column allocation. Each unique item reserves two logical records before insertion; duplicate attempts consume none. Same closure/order as ordinary recognition. Reasons are captured on insertion, without replay. No partial result escapes on failure. Returned copies own all buffers; concurrent calls share no mutable state when inputs are not modified concurrently.
    earley_trace_base_entries()Check input geometry and compute capture cost before any item is inserted. No allocation. Symbols are opaque strings, not validated as source-code names. Token/production/RHS lengths and each eventual column item count must fit int; base arithmetic must fit size_t. This count does not promise enough memory.

    Types and constants

    earley_no_itemvariable Sentinel used in both coordinates of an absent Earley provenance reference.
    EarleyActionenum First successful insertion cause of one unique Earley item. Seed has no parents; prediction/scanning use first; completion uses first as the waiter and second as the completed item, including a late nullable join.
