    datamunge/algorithms/edmonds_karp.hpp

    Classes

    EdmondsKarpAugmentationOne actual bottleneck push along a recorded BFS parent path. path runs from source to sink. search identifies its complete pre-push BFS; amount is the minimum positive residual on that path. Copies own all records.
    EdmondsKarpPathArcBefore/after values of an actual oriented residual pair on a pushed path. Input edge i owns arc ids 2*i (forward) and 2*i+1 (cancellation). Reverse use decreases that edge's original flow, preserving independent identities for parallel, antiparallel and self edges. Values are copied during the actual push.
    EdmondsKarpResultOrdinary owned flow result and work, without retained search/path history. Inputs remain unchanged and independent calls share no mutable state. No optional capture quota applies; ordinary working storage is O(V+E).
    EdmondsKarpSearchFull actual BFS levels and first-discovery parents before a path push. Unreachable level is vertex_count; source and unreachable parent ids are SIZE_MAX. Every successful search has exactly one augmentation at the same vector index. The last search fails to reach the sink and supplies the returned source cut.
    EdmondsKarpTraceOwned original network and search/path evidence captured without replay. Logical capture C=E+1+P*(1+2V)+A+L: E input records, one network header, P full BFS headers/levels/parents (including failure), A augmentation headers and L path-arc records. Result copies, runtime arrays, scalars, vector capacity and allocator bytes are excluded; this is not a peak-RAM limit. Histories add O(C) work/storage. Mutable records are inspectable data, not self-certifying proofs.
    EdmondsKarpWorkChecked logical operations from the actual complete-BFS Edmonds-Karp run. Counts exclude validation, allocation, copying, certificate checks and CPU time. Each BFS scans every outgoing residual arc of every reached vertex, including zero, reverse and self arcs. The final failed search is included.
    MaxFlowResultOwned flow value, per-input-edge flows and a source-side cut witness. Shared by maximum-flow algorithms; the original three-field layout is retained. Flow/cut agreement is numerical for double solvers, rather than an exact-real guarantee. Default construction is an uncomputed placeholder. No input views survive.

    Functions

    edmonds_karp()Compute maximum flow by shortest residual augmenting paths.
    edmonds_karp_trace()Capture complete actual BFS parents/levels and oriented path updates.
    edmonds_karp_trace_base_entries()Calculate minimum trace entries including input and the first complete BFS.
    edmonds_karp_work()Return the ordinary flow and checked actual BFS/path work.

    datamunge/algorithms/elementary.hpp

    Classes

    AlphaBetaCoefficientsCoefficients of an alpha-max-plus-beta-min estimate alpha·hi + beta·lo.
    AlphaBetaErrorRangeThe range of estimate/true over every direction for a coefficient pair.

    Functions

    alpha_max_beta_min() ×3The alpha max plus beta min algorithm: a fast, division- and square-root-free approximation of the Euclidean magnitude sqrt(x^2+y^2), as alpha·max(|x|,|y|) + beta·min(|x|,|y|). With the peak-error-minimizing coefficients alpha≈0.96043, beta≈0.39782 the worst-case relative error is about 3.96%. It is a classic DSP/embedded trick for estimating vector magnitude (or complex modulus) where a true hypot is too expensive.
    alpha_max_beta_min_error()Exact error range of a coefficient pair over all directions.
    alpha_max_beta_min_least_squares()The pair minimizing the mean squared relative error over directions uniform in angle, \(\int_0^{\pi/4}(\alpha\cos\theta+\beta\sin\theta-1)^2\,d\theta\), from its 2x2 normal equations.
    alpha_max_beta_min_minimax()The pair minimizing the worst relative error, in closed form: \(\alpha=2\cos(\pi/8)/(1+\cos(\pi/8))\), \(\beta=2\sin(\pi/8)/(1+\cos(\pi/8))\), with peak error \(\tan^2(\pi/16)\approx3.96\%\).
    alpha_max_beta_min_no_underestimate()The pair with the smallest worst error among those that never underestimate: \(\alpha=1\), \(\beta=\tan(\pi/8)\), peak error \(1/\cos(\pi/8)-1\approx8.24\%\).
    alpha_max_beta_min_polygon()The minimax k-line generalisation: the octant [0, pi/4] is split into lines equal sectors, each with its own minimax pair, and the estimate is the largest of the lines linear forms (a regular polygon around the circle).

    datamunge/algorithms/elias_gamma.hpp

    Classes

    GammaDecodedOwned strictly decoded positive values and actual parse work, without history. Every input character must belong to one complete representable codeword; trailing zeros are not padding. Empty input yields no values. No input views survive.
    GammaEncodedOwned encoded characters and actual emission work, with no optional history. bits uses one char per bit, not packed bytes. No input view survives; ordinary work calls have no optional capture quota. Empty input gives empty bits and zero work.
    GammaSizeSummaryExact gamma and minimal common fixed-width payload sizes for positive values. Empty input has zero sizes and maximum zero. Fixed width is the binary width of the largest value; it does not include framing or a transmitted width/count. These are theoretical bit counts. The string codec stores one char per bit.
    GammaTraceOwned values, bit characters and spans captured during the actual codec run. Retained logical entries C=B+2N count B bit characters, N values and N word records. Scalar fields, result/runtime temporaries, string/vector capacity and allocator bytes are excluded: this is not a peak-memory bound. Encoding knows complete C before copies/emission; decoding knows B first and reserves two entries per complete word online. Copies own independent buffers, with no input views.
    GammaWordActual half-open bit spans of one emitted or parsed gamma codeword. The prefix occupies [begin,payload_begin), and the binary payload including its leading one occupies [payload_begin,end). Spans refer to GammaTrace::bits, which owns its data; numbers are indices, not borrowed iterators or views.
    GammaWorkLogical value and bit counts from actual gamma emission or parsing. Each successful codeword contributes its zero-prefix and full binary payload lengths. bit_visits counts emitted characters for encoding or consumed characters for decoding; validation, preflight, allocation/copying and CPU instructions are excluded. Full input validation is an additional pass, not hidden in this count.

    Functions

    elias_gamma_code_length()Return the exact Elias gamma length of one positive uint64 value.
    elias_gamma_decode()Decode complete gamma words, retaining the original inline entry point.
    elias_gamma_decode_trace()Capture actual strict parse spans and values with an online retained-history cap.
    elias_gamma_decode_work()Strictly parse an entire gamma bit string with actual work counters.
    elias_gamma_encode()Concatenate positive gamma words, retaining the original inline entry point.
    elias_gamma_encode_one()Encode one positive integer, retaining the original inline entry point.
    elias_gamma_encode_trace()Capture actual emission spans after complete positive-input and quota preflight.
    elias_gamma_encode_work()Emit positive uint64 gamma words with actual logical work counters.
    elias_gamma_size_summary()Summarize gamma payload and minimal common fixed-width bit counts.

    datamunge/algorithms/ellipsoid.hpp

    Classes

    EllipsoidCutOne actual factored central cut, without an objective or convergence claim. support_bound=||lower^T*g|| is computed at the input state. Log volumes are measured from the input/output positive diagonals. center_changed is false if rounding left every coordinate unchanged; an optimizer treats that as stagnation.
    EllipsoidIterationActual subgradient query at one recorded sample, with its accepted-cut decision. No callbacks are retained and no explanation is replayed. A terminal iteration has updated=false. state_index identifies the pre-cut objective sample.
    EllipsoidOutcomeDetailed finite outcome with best point, last state and an explicit stop reason. last_support_bound belongs to the most recent subgradient query, which can precede the final state if the last allowed iteration performed an update. has_support_bound is false when max_iter=0. Ordinary/work calls retain no input or iteration history, have no optional capture quota, and own their output.
    EllipsoidResultBest evaluated point, its objective and attempted oracle iterations. Retains the original three-field layout. iterations counts subgradient calls, including a terminal zero/tolerance/stagnation check; it is not the number of successful cuts. A best point alone does not certify convergence. Copies own x.
    EllipsoidSampleActual objective evaluation at an owned ellipsoid state. Initial sample is followed by exactly one sample for each committed cut. objective is the center value; best_value is the smallest evaluated value so far. The ellipsoid algorithm need not decrease the current center objective.
    EllipsoidStateOwned ellipsoid E={center+lower*u : ||u||<=1} with a triangular shape factor. The lower matrix is n by n, finite, exactly zero above the diagonal, with positive diagonal. Thus P=lower*lower^T is positive definite mathematically; forming P explicitly may lose this property through floating cancellation. Public values are mutable; entry points validate shape before access.
    EllipsoidTraceOwned actual objective samples and subgradient attempts from the same optimizer run. For dimension n, each sample costs S=1+n+n*n entries (record, center and all stored factor entries) and each iteration I=1+n (record and gradient). Thus C=samples*S+iterations*I. The returned outcome, callbacks, runtime buffers, row/container metadata, capacities and allocator bytes are excluded; quota is retained history, not peak RAM. No input/callback views survive.
    EllipsoidWorkChecked logical counts from the actual callback/cut execution. Counts exclude validation, geometry preparation, allocations, copying, logs, candidate arithmetic and CPU time. support_products counts lower-factor terms in L^T*g for nonzero oracle gradients, including terminal tolerance attempts. factor_entries_updated counts committed lower-triangle entries, not all writes.

    Functions

    ellipsoid_ball()Construct an owned ball using a positive triangular factor, without squaring radius.
    ellipsoid_central_cut()Enclose a central half ellipsoid using a positive triangular shape update.
    ellipsoid_log_volume()Measure log volume from the actual positive factor diagonal.
    ellipsoid_log_volume_ratio()Return the exact-arithmetic central-cut log-volume ratio as a stable numeric value.
    ellipsoid_minimize()Return the best evaluated point through the original six-argument interface.
    ellipsoid_minimize_trace()Capture actual objective states and subgradient decisions without replay.
    ellipsoid_minimize_work()Minimize with factored central cuts and an explicit finite stopping outcome.
    ellipsoid_outline()Sample a two-dimensional factored ellipsoid boundary in native diagram coordinates.

    Types and constants

    EllipsoidStopenum Why the finite optimizer stopped; only two reasons are conditional optimality checks. Valid convex subgradients and an initial enclosing ellipsoid are caller assumptions, not verified by the implementation. Iteration limit and rounded center stagnation do not certify an optimum or the requested tolerance.

    datamunge/algorithms/euclidean_mst.hpp

    Classes

    EuclideanMstOutcomeOwned planar minimum spanning tree and actual complete-graph work. Point indices are preserved, including separate vertices at identical coordinates. The output owns its edge records; no inputs or optional trajectory are retained.
    EuclideanMstTraceOwned points and actual Kruskal trace on their complete Euclidean graph. Pair edges are generated lexicographically (i,j), i<j, with stable ties in that order. Captured entries C=N+M+S count N point records plus the nested M input-edge and S actual scan records. N+M is checked before any generated graph/copy; nested steps reserve online before scanning. Default one million; zero disables only quota. Output tree, runtime graph/sort/DSU state, capacities and allocator bytes are excluded, so this is not a peak-memory bound. Points, nested trace and output are all owned; exceptions expose no partial result. No independent optimization replay is performed.
    EuclideanMstWorkActual distance and stable Kruskal work from a complete planar graph. Each unordered point pair is measured once with hypot, before sorting. Logical counts exclude coordinate validation, allocation, sorting and CPU time.

    Functions

    euclidean_minimum_spanning_tree()Return the complete-graph Euclidean minimum spanning tree of planar points. Constructs every unordered pair in lexicographic input-index order, weighted by Euclidean hypot distance; then calls the shared stable Kruskal kernel. Equal weights retain pair order. Coincident points remain distinct vertices joined by zero edges. Empty/singleton input is connected with zero total. Coordinates are arbitrary Cartesian units and outputs use those same units; this is not geographic distance, a tour or a Steiner tree. The complete graph always connects finite valid inputs. O(n² log(n+1)) time and O(n²+n) runtime memory; no Delaunay sparsification is used. All coordinates and pair/container geometry are checked before generated allocation. Independent calls share no mutable state; concurrent caller mutation is unsafe. Ordinary/work calls retain no optional history or capture quota. The original function remains available through advanced_graph.hpp.
    euclidean_minimum_spanning_tree_trace()Capture the actual complete-graph Euclidean Kruskal execution with a record quota. Constructs every unordered pair in lexicographic input-index order, weighted by Euclidean hypot distance; then calls the shared stable Kruskal kernel. Equal weights retain pair order. Coincident points remain distinct vertices joined by zero edges. Empty/singleton input is connected with zero total. Coordinates are arbitrary Cartesian units and outputs use those same units; this is not geographic distance, a tour or a Steiner tree. The complete graph always connects finite valid inputs. O(n² log(n+1)) time and O(n²+n) runtime memory; no Delaunay sparsification is used. All coordinates and pair/container geometry are checked before generated allocation. Independent calls share no mutable state; concurrent caller mutation is unsafe. C=N+M+S follows EuclideanMstTrace. Known N+M capture is checked before coordinate copies/edge generation; each actual scan is checked before capture. The nested result is the result of the shared kernel, not reconstructed from steps.
    euclidean_minimum_spanning_tree_work()Return a planar minimum tree and actual pair-distance/union-find work. Constructs every unordered pair in lexicographic input-index order, weighted by Euclidean hypot distance; then calls the shared stable Kruskal kernel. Equal weights retain pair order. Coincident points remain distinct vertices joined by zero edges. Empty/singleton input is connected with zero total. Coordinates are arbitrary Cartesian units and outputs use those same units; this is not geographic distance, a tour or a Steiner tree. The complete graph always connects finite valid inputs. O(n² log(n+1)) time and O(n²+n) runtime memory; no Delaunay sparsification is used. All coordinates and pair/container geometry are checked before generated allocation. Independent calls share no mutable state; concurrent caller mutation is unsafe.
    euclidean_mst_pair_count()Check complete-pair geometry without allocating a graph. Computes n(n-1)/2 by dividing an even factor before checked multiplication. Also checks the point, edge and DSU container geometries required by these APIs. Zero and one yield zero; this is a count check, not a promise of available RAM.

    datamunge/algorithms/euler_method.hpp

    Classes

    EulerOutcomeOwned intrinsic trajectory, nominal step size and actual work. Every Euler call returns N+1 samples, including both endpoints. Ordinary/work calls keep the intrinsic trajectory but no optional derivative history or capture quota. step_size is the finite rounded nominal h; sample times follow euler_method()'s documented grid rounding. A successful run is not an error estimate or a guarantee of stability/accuracy for the supplied ODE.
    EulerTraceOwned actual derivative vectors alongside the same execution's intrinsic trajectory. derivatives[i] is the exact callback vector at solution.t[i], solution.y[i]. The final sample has no derivative query. No callbacks are retained or replayed. Logical capture C=(2N+1)(d+1) counts N+1 sample slots with d state entries and N derivative slots with d derivative entries. All C is checked before history copies or callbacks. Default one million; zero disables only that quota. Other outcome metadata, runtime state/callback storage, vector headers, capacities and allocator bytes are excluded: C is not peak RAM. Copies own all samples/derivatives. Failures return no partial trace; callback side effects before a later callback/arithmetic failure remain the caller's responsibility.
    EulerWorkLogical work from the actual fixed-step Euler execution. Counts exclude validation, time-grid construction, allocation, history copying and CPU time. rhs_calls counts actual callback invocations; scalar_updates counts committed component updates, not floating instructions. Complete results have steps=rhs_calls=N and scalar_updates=N*d. Exceptions expose no partial result.

    Functions

    euler_method()Integrate a first-order vector ODE using checked fixed-step forward Euler. Uses one actual derivative per step: y_next=y+h*f(t,y). Under suitable C2 solution and Lipschitz assumptions, one-step defect is O(h^2) and global error over a fixed finite interval is O(h); neither stability nor an error estimate is provided by the API. Runtime/callback storage aside, time is O(N*d+N*cost(f)) and the intrinsic returned history uses O((N+1)*d) entries. Nominal h is converted from an extended-precision endpoint difference/N. Interior times use extended t0+i*h; the last time is exactly t1. Rounded grid differences need not equal h exactly; state updates always use nominal h. For a nonzero interval every stored time must advance strictly in its direction, checked before any callback. Reverse integration is supported. A zero interval preserves N callbacks and N+1 repeated-time states with h=0. Inputs and every returned derivative are checked before indexing. Each double product h*f_i and subsequent double sum must be finite; callback exceptions propagate unchanged. No callback or input storage is retained. Concurrent calls are independent if the caller's callback/captured state is safe for concurrency.
    euler_method_trace()Capture the exact derivatives from the actual Euler trajectory with a checked quota. Same numerical kernel, validation, intrinsic storage and grid rounding as euler_method(). Optional capture C=(2N+1)(d+1) follows EulerTrace; the full known quota is checked before copies or callbacks. A quota failure therefore performs no callback. Other later failures can follow earlier callback side effects and expose no partial output. Capture adds O(N*d) derivative storage and copies.
    euler_method_work()Return the intrinsic Euler trajectory, nominal h and actual logical work. Uses the same checked kernel and grid rounding as euler_method(), including reverse/zero intervals and full derivative validation. Keeps no optional derivative history or capture quota. Intrinsic output uses O((N+1)*d) memory; runtime is O(N*d+N*cost(f)). Caller callback exceptions propagate unchanged.
    euler_trace_size()Check Euler state/history geometry and return the complete logical trace size. Computes (2N+1)(d+1) with checked counts. Also checks intrinsic state cells and required per-vector/container limits before allocation. This is a geometric count check, not a promise of available memory. It allocates no trajectory.

    datamunge/algorithms/exact_cover.hpp

    Classes

    DominoCoverProblemOwned exact-cover encoding of adjacent domino placements on a rectangular board. Cells use row-major IDs r*board_columns+c with row zero at the top. Each placement has exactly two orthogonally adjacent cells. The canonical builder visits cells row-major, adding horizontal then vertical placements. Identical dominoes need no piece-identity column. Public mutable fields are validated by domino_tiling_diagram(); exact_cover() separately validates general incidence.
    ExactCoverNodeOwned snapshot of one actual index-linked dancing-links node. Node IDs are indices into a trace mesh. Root is zero; required-column headers are 1..C and data nodes follow input row/entry order. column is a HEADER NODE ID, not a zero-based problem column. Root column/row are -1; header column points to itself and row is -1. Data row is the original input row ID and size is zero. Header size is its current vertical list length. Mutable records do not validate their own links; they own integers rather than pointers into another object.
    ExactCoverOutcomeOwned first-cover result and actual search/restoration work. Uses the same deterministic search as exact_cover(). The runtime mesh is fully restored even after success; the first selected-row result is retained separately. Ordinary/work calls retain no optional input, event or mesh-snapshot history.
    ExactCoverResultFirst exact-cover verdict and selected original row indices. Preserves the original bool/vector field layout. A solved result covers every required column exactly once; an unsolved result has an empty row vector. Empty universes are solved by the empty selection. Row order is actual search order, not sorted order. Copies own rows; default construction is unsolved.
    ExactCoverStepOwned actual residual-column and selected-row state at a search event. column_sizes has C entries: -1 for a covered column and actual nonnegative vertical-list size for an active column. partial_rows is the actual selected-row stack at this event; depth equals its length. column/row use zero-based problem IDs, or -1 when inapplicable. At unselect_row, the pivot column is still covered even though that candidate has been popped. These are live captures, not replay.
    ExactCoverTraceOwned actual search states and initial/final dancing-links meshes. All inputs, nodes, events and output rows are owned. Initial/final nodes are copied from the actual runtime mesh; every successful/failed search unwinds fully, so those arrays agree exactly. No explanation is reconstructed by another solver. Let R be input row count, I total incidences and K=1+C+I nodes. Known base capture B=R+I+2K counts row records/incidences plus two NODE RECORD snapshots (each entire seven-field node counts as one record). Each event costs 1+C+depth: event record, column sizes and selected-row IDs. B is reserved before graph/copy allocation; events are reserved before snapshot copies. Default one million; zero disables only quota. Ordinary output/work, runtime mesh/stack/validation, vector headers, capacities and allocator bytes are excluded: this is not peak RAM. Any failure returns no partial trace; caller input is never mutated.
    ExactCoverWorkChecked logical operations from the actual iterative dancing-links execution. Initialization, validation, allocations, snapshots, copying and CPU time are excluded. Column scans count every active header visited by the minimum-size heuristic. Link writes count assignments even if their value is unchanged. Every completed successful or failed search restores its mesh: covers=uncovers and row_attempts=row_restorations. Search remains exponential in the worst case.

    Functions

    domino_exact_cover()Build every horizontal/vertical adjacent domino placement for a rectangular board. Rows/columns are nonnegative; a zero-area board has zero cells/placements. For positive dimensions, placement count is h(w-1)+(h-1)w. Cell/pair/node/count geometry is checked before allocation. Construction and owned storage are linear in cells+placements. Canonical row-major, horizontal-before-vertical order retains the original report encoding and therefore its stable first tiling choice.
    domino_tiling_diagram()Draw a validated selected domino cover as an owned native C++ diagram. Uses actual placement cell IDs; row zero is drawn at the top. Selected rows get coloured rectangles and original row-ID labels. A solved result must cover every cell exactly once. An unsolved result must have no selected rows and is labelled reported unsolved, without independently proving nonexistence. Mutable problem shape, every adjacent pair and selected ID are checked before access. Zero area returns an informative empty-board diagram. Time/storage O(cells+placements). The diagram owns primitives/text and borrows no input. Primitive mutation follows Diagram thread-safety; concurrent calls are independent for unmodified inputs.
    exact_cover()Find the first required-column exact cover using checked iterative dancing links. Every column is required exactly once (no secondary columns). Each row must contain distinct in-range column IDs; unsorted order is allowed and preserved. Duplicate whole rows are separate alternatives; empty rows are ignored. The empty universe is solved by no rows. All inputs are checked before early success/access. Minimum-size active column ties use the first column in ascending header order; its row candidates keep input order. Iterative depth-first search follows Algorithm X without recursive call-stack growth. It stops at the first cover and restores the complete mesh afterwards on both success/failure. Work remains exponential in general; runtime mesh/stack storage is O(columns+rows+incidences), excluding output. Independent calls share no mutable state; concurrent caller mutation is unsafe. The original compiled signature/result field layout are retained. Ordinary/work calls have no optional history or capture quota and never mutate input.
    exact_cover_node_count()Check exact-cover index/container geometry without allocating a mesh. Requires root+column headers+nonzeros to fit positive int node IDs and all node containers; row IDs must fit int. This is a count check, not available-memory validation, and does not examine individual incidence lists.
    exact_cover_trace()Capture the same actual exact-cover search and its restored mesh with a quota. Every column is required exactly once (no secondary columns). Each row must contain distinct in-range column IDs; unsorted order is allowed and preserved. Duplicate whole rows are separate alternatives; empty rows are ignored. The empty universe is solved by no rows. All inputs are checked before early success/access. Minimum-size active column ties use the first column in ascending header order; its row candidates keep input order. Iterative depth-first search follows Algorithm X without recursive call-stack growth. It stops at the first cover and restores the complete mesh afterwards on both success/failure. Work remains exponential in general; runtime mesh/stack storage is O(columns+rows+incidences), excluding output. Independent calls share no mutable state; concurrent caller mutation is unsafe. Capture B=R+I+2K plus sum(1+C+depth) follows ExactCoverTrace. The known base is checked before optional input/mesh copies or runtime graph allocation; each event is checked before its state snapshot. Quota failure exposes no partial trace. Optional history can be much larger than the sparse runtime mesh.
    exact_cover_work()Return the first exact cover and actual search/restoration operations. Every column is required exactly once (no secondary columns). Each row must contain distinct in-range column IDs; unsorted order is allowed and preserved. Duplicate whole rows are separate alternatives; empty rows are ignored. The empty universe is solved by no rows. All inputs are checked before early success/access. Minimum-size active column ties use the first column in ascending header order; its row candidates keep input order. Iterative depth-first search follows Algorithm X without recursive call-stack growth. It stops at the first cover and restores the complete mesh afterwards on both success/failure. Work remains exponential in general; runtime mesh/stack storage is O(columns+rows+incidences), excluding output. Independent calls share no mutable state; concurrent caller mutation is unsafe. Retains no optional input/events/mesh snapshots or capture quota. Counters include restoring all selected rows and columns after the first cover has been retained.

    Types and constants

    ExactCoverEventenum Kinds of actual search events, including restoration after a found solution. choose_column and dead_end are recorded before covering the chosen column. select_row follows covering all its columns. unselect_row follows restoring its other columns and popping its row; the pivot column remains covered until its frame exits. Thus unselect_row can be cleanup after success as well as a failed branch. solution precedes cleanup; finished follows complete mesh restoration.

    datamunge/algorithms/exchange_sorts.hpp

    Classes

    PancakeResultOwned sorted integers and actual prefix lengths reversed by pancake_sort(). Applying flips to the original input reproduces sorted; no optimal-flip claim.
    PancakeStepOne actual greedy maximum search, including any resulting reversals.
    PancakeTraceSame-producer greedy decisions and post-reversal states, with owned output.

    Functions

    cocktail_shaker_sort()Return a stable nondecreasing integer copy using alternating adjacent exchanges. Forward passes fix the rightmost remaining maximum, backward passes the leftmost minimum. Strict greater-than comparisons preserve equal-key order; signed extremes are valid. Stops at the first zero-swap directional pass. Each successful pass shrinks one bound by one: reversing direction does not guarantee half the directional passes or comparisons of bubble sort. Empty/singleton inputs return immediately. Worst-case time O(n^2), best O(n); constant working state beyond the by-value input/output buffer. Lvalue callers retain their original vector; no shared state is used. See the trace API for actual pass states, identity labels and work counters from this same kernel.
    pancake_sort()Greedily sort integers using only prefix reversals. First maximum wins ties; no stability guarantee. At most 2(n-1) reversals for n>=1, O(n^2) comparisons and element swaps, O(n) owned output/flip storage. Lvalue input is copied, never mutated. Empty/singleton returns without flips.
    pancake_sort_trace()Retain actual prefix searches and reversal snapshots from pancake_sort's kernel. O(n^2) history entries in the worst case. No replay or second sort is used.

    datamunge/algorithms/exp_golomb.hpp

    Classes

    ExpGolombDecodedOwned complete decoded values, consumed prefix length and actual work. The count argument is an upper limit. A complete frame ending earlier returns fewer values; hitting the limit leaves any tail unread. consumed_bits identifies that exact boundary. A malformed attempted word throws instead of returning partial output. No input, optional span history or capture quota is retained.
    ExpGolombEncodedOwned bit-vector payload and actual encoding work. bits follows vector<bool> specialised storage, with no byte serialization or endianness format defined. Order k and outer framing are supplied by the caller. Empty input produces empty bits and zero work. No optional history/quota is kept.
    ExpGolombSizeExact coded bits and a positive-common-width binary payload comparison. For nonempty input fixed_width=max(1,bit_width(maximum)); all-zero values thus use one bit per field by this convention. Empty input has zero width/counts and maximum zero. fixed_bits=values*fixed_width. Order/count/width framing and storage overhead are excluded. Computing a count does not promise available output memory.
    ExpGolombTraceOwned actual bit vector, values and spans from the shared Exp-Golomb execution. Encoding owns the complete output bits and copied input values. Decoding owns the entire input vector, including unread tails, plus actual complete values. There is no explanatory replay. consumed_bits equals output size for encoding and actual prefix length for decoding. Logical C=B+2N counts retained bit positions, value entries and whole word records. Encoding reserves known C before copies or emission; decoding reserves whole input B before copying, then two entries online before each value/span append. Default one million; zero disables only quota. Other metadata, runtime/capacity/container headers/allocator bytes are excluded: C is not peak RAM and is not a byte-packing format. Exceptions expose no partial trace; every returned container owns its values. Caller mutation is independent.
    ExpGolombWordActual emitted/parsed word with zero-run, quotient and low-bit boundaries. All half-open indices address the trace bit vector. [begin,payload_begin) is the zero run; [payload_begin,suffix_begin) is binary(q+1), including its leading one; [suffix_begin,end) contains k raw low bits. At UINT64_MAX,k=0 the quotient payload is a real 65-bit sequence, not a wrapped uint64 value. Records own scalars.
    ExpGolombWorkLogical values and emitted/consumed bits from the actual Exp-Golomb kernel. zero_prefix_bits counts only leading zeros; quotient_bits includes the leading one and remaining quotient-plus-one binary digits. suffix_bits counts the k raw low bits per value. bit_visits is their sum, excluding preflight, allocation, copies, validation and CPU instructions. Unread input tails are not visits.

    Functions

    exp_golomb0_encode_value()Append the order-zero word through the shared checked compiled emitter. Retains the original inline entry point. Every uint64 is valid, including zero and UINT64_MAX. Existing prefix bits are unchanged; complete geometry is checked and reserved before appending. Exceptions preserve original logical contents/size; reallocation may invalidate proxy references. Runtime O(word length), no history.
    exp_golomb_append_work()Append one actual order-k word and return counts for the appended word only. Keeps arbitrary existing prefix bits unchanged and does not parse that prefix. Validates order and complete output geometry, then reserves before any write. Exceptions leave the original logical contents/size unchanged. Reallocation may invalidate existing vector<bool> proxy references/iterators. Runtime O(word bits), no optional history/quota; out must not be concurrently accessed during mutation.
    exp_golomb_bit_string()Render a bool bit sequence as owned literal zero/one debug characters. Does not encode, decode or define byte packing. Allocates one char per input bit, with O(B) time/storage. Empty input returns empty text. No view or input mutation survives; independent calls are safe for unmodified borrowed input.
    exp_golomb_code_length()Return the exact Exp-Golomb word length of any uint64 value. Let q=n>>k and m=floor(log2(q+1)) mathematically. Length is 2m+1+k; UINT64_MAX,k=0 uses m=64 and length129. Native arithmetic avoids forming unrepresentable q+1 or shifting by64. Every uint64 including zero is supported.
    exp_golomb_decode()Decode up to count complete values, preserving original bounded-prefix behavior. Parses complete words until count values are returned or the input ends at a word boundary. count is an UPPER LIMIT: a shorter complete frame returns fewer values; count0 reads nothing. Hitting the limit leaves any tail unread, without validating that tail. consumed_bits reports the exact boundary. Any incomplete attempted zero run, quotient payload or k-bit suffix throws; no partial result is returned on that error. Wider-than-uint64 values fail instead of wrapping. Runtime O(consumed bits), output O(actual values); input is borrowed unchanged, without optional history/quota. Order must match the sender. Independent calls are safe for stable inputs; input mutation during a call is unsafe. Retains the original inline entry point. Use the work/trace result to obtain consumed_bits; exact-count or whole-frame callers check their own framing.

Any incomplete attempted zero run, quotient payload or k-bit suffix throws; no partial result is returned on that error. Wider-than-uint64 values fail instead of wrapping. Parsing takes O(consumed bits); input is borrowed unchanged. Order must match the sender. Independent calls are safe for stable inputs; input mutation during a call is unsafe. The trace owns whole input B, including unread tails, and reserves B before copying. It reserves two additional entries online before each complete value and word record is appended.     datamunge/algorithms/exponential_backoff.hpp

    Classes

    BackoffScheduleOwned actual steps and cumulative idle waits, excluding request durations. steps and retry_times have equal length N; retry_times[i] is the ordinary floating sum of delays through i, starting at zero. They are idle-wait offsets, not wall-clock deadlines or a simulation of request success/latency. Zero waits can give equal offsets. Addition rejects delay>DBL_MAX-current before summing; thus no cumulative infinity escapes, though ordinary rounding still applies. total_delay is the final offset, or zero when empty. Intrinsic output owns O(N) records/values; no optional replay/history quota is imposed. Caller data is copied as scalars and independent results share no mutable RNG state.
    BackoffStepOne actual checked retry window, applied unit variate and finite delay. Attempt k is the zero-based wait before retry k+1. Parameters base/cap use one caller-chosen common time unit, must be finite and nonnegative, and can be zero. The window is min(base*2^k,cap) mathematically, including immediate clamping when base>=cap. Exponent/mantissa comparison precedes ldexp, so no intermediate infinity or retry-index loop is needed. Scalar work uses a fixed number of math operations even at INT_MAX; this is not a CPU-time or real-clock guarantee. u is finite in [0,1], including the legacy endpoint one. delay=u*window is finite in [0,window]; underflow/rounding can erase tiny waits or round them to a window endpoint. capped/scaled describe the actual scalar branch, not instruction counts. No sleeping, networking, random draws or optional history is involved.

    Functions

Parameters base/cap use one caller-chosen common time unit, must be finite and nonnegative, and can be zero. The window is min(base*2^k,cap) mathematically, including immediate clamping when base>=cap. Exponent/mantissa comparison precedes ldexp, so no intermediate infinity or retry-index loop is needed. Scalar work uses a fixed number of math operations even at INT_MAX; this is not a CPU-time or real-clock guarantee. Retains the original inline name/signature. Returns a window only, with no randomness or cumulative idle sum; separate calls share no mutable state.

Returns u*min(base*2^k,cap) with checked finite nonnegative base/cap and k>=0. u is finite in inclusive [0,1], preserving the originally tested u=1 endpoint. The caller provides randomness; a single supplied u does not establish a uniform law. Product rounding/underflow follows double arithmetic; output stays within [0,window]. Pure scalar output, no sleeping, cumulative sum or global RNG.
    exponential_backoff_schedule()Emit actual windows/delays and their checked cumulative idle waits. Attempt k is the zero-based wait before retry k+1. Parameters base/cap use one caller-chosen common time unit, must be finite and nonnegative, and can be zero. The window is min(base*2^k,cap) mathematically, including immediate clamping when base>=cap. Exponent/mantissa comparison precedes ldexp, so no intermediate infinity or retry-index loop is needed. Scalar work uses a fixed number of math operations even at INT_MAX; this is not a CPU-time or real-clock guarantee. Empty uniforms selects deterministic full windows (u=1). Otherwise exactly N finite values in [0,1] are required and all are checked before output allocation. The shared emitter creates each record and prefix offset once, without replay. Known vector geometry is checked before reserve. O(N) work/owned storage; no sleeping, callbacks, request durations, clock operations or random draws. Cumulative overflow throws without exposing a partial result; ordinary windows remain available independently when no representable timeline exists.
    exponential_backoff_seeded()Emit a reproducible jitter schedule from the original local xorshift64 stream. Attempt k is the zero-based wait before retry k+1. Parameters base/cap use one caller-chosen common time unit, must be finite and nonnegative, and can be zero. The window is min(base*2^k,cap) mathematically, including immediate clamping when base>=cap. Exponent/mantissa comparison precedes ldexp, so no intermediate infinity or retry-index loop is needed. Scalar work uses a fixed number of math operations even at INT_MAX; this is not a CPU-time or real-clock guarantee. Starting from a nonzero uint64 seed, each actual step applies x^=x<<13, x^=x>>7, x^=x<<17 modulo2^64, then u=(x>>11)*2^-53. This preserves the original report stream. It is deterministic, noncryptographic and not a proof of independence across clients. Reusing a seed reproduces the same waits; use a suitable seeding source, such as random::SplitMix64, for distinct fixtures. Unit outputs lie in [0,1); floating delay products can round to an endpoint. The shared emitter records the actual draw/window/wait and cumulative offset. All scalar/seed/geometry validation precedes allocation or draws. O(N) time and owned storage, no global RNG, borrowed state, optional history or partial result.
    exponential_backoff_sequence()Return the original sequence API with O(N) shared-kernel work. Validates nonnegative count and finite nonnegative base/cap even for an empty sequence. Retains original inline name/signature.
    exponential_backoff_step()Compute one finite capped backoff window and apply an explicit unit variate. Attempt k is the zero-based wait before retry k+1. Parameters base/cap use one caller-chosen common time unit, must be finite and nonnegative, and can be zero. The window is min(base*2^k,cap) mathematically, including immediate clamping when base>=cap. Exponent/mantissa comparison precedes ldexp, so no intermediate infinity or retry-index loop is needed. Scalar work uses a fixed number of math operations even at INT_MAX; this is not a CPU-time or real-clock guarantee. u is a caller-supplied finite number in inclusive [0,1]; one is retained for legacy endpoint callers, not a uniform-generator output. The function does not sample a distribution. Calls are pure, own scalars and share no mutable state.
    exponential_backoff_windows()Return N pure capped windows without requiring a cumulative timeline. Attempt k is the zero-based wait before retry k+1. Parameters base/cap use one caller-chosen common time unit, must be finite and nonnegative, and can be zero. The window is min(base*2^k,cap) mathematically, including immediate clamping when base>=cap. Exponent/mantissa comparison precedes ldexp, so no intermediate infinity or retry-index loop is needed. Scalar work uses a fixed number of math operations even at INT_MAX; this is not a CPU-time or real-clock guarantee. Validates count/base/cap even for empty output. Uses the shared scalar kernel once per output, O(N) work/owned storage. Does not sum windows, apply jitter, retain step records or fail merely because a hypothetical sum would overflow. Borrowed/global state is not mutated; independent calls are safe.

    datamunge/algorithms/extended_euclidean.hpp

    Classes

    EuclidOutcomeOwned unsigned-range Bezout certificate and work from one actual kernel execution. Ordinary/work calls keep only running scalar states and this result; they do not allocate optional row history or apply a capture quota. Certificate follows the same signed-truncation ordering as the legacy API, with exact widened intermediates. No borrowed input, shared mutable state or explanatory replay.
    EuclidRowOne actual raw Euclidean remainder and its signed-wide Bezout row. remainder=s*a+t*b holds mathematically for the trace inputs. Initial rows are (a,1,0) and (b,0,1), with divided=false and quotient=0 unused. Each derived row has divided=true and the actual truncation-toward-zero quotient that produced it. The terminal zero row is retained. Signed compiler-supported128-bit fields allow quotient2^63 and terminal coefficients beyond int64 without wrapping. These raw rows are not rewritten by the separately reported final sign normalization.
    EuclidTraceOwned actual raw rows and unsigned-range outcome from the shared extended-Euclid loop. For D actual divisions, rows/captured_entries=2+D WHOLE ROW RECORDS, including two initial rows and the terminal zero row when a division occurs. Input scalars, result/work metadata, vector capacity, runtime and allocator bytes are excluded; this is not peak RAM. Initial two records are quota-checked before allocation; each next record is admitted before its division and append. Default max_rows one million; zero disables only quota. Arithmetic/container checks remain. Exceptions expose no partial trace. Every returned container owns its values; ordinary calls retain no optional history. Final sign normalization lives in outcome, while raw rows preserve the actual signed-truncation computation.
    EuclidWorkActual Euclidean divisions, coefficient updates and final normalization flag. Each quotient/remainder iteration counts one division and two coefficient updates, including an initial zero quotient when input magnitudes are reversed and the terminal zero-remainder update. sign_normalized records the actual final three-value sign flip. Counts exclude validation, copies, allocation, CPU time and arbitrary-precision bit cost; native input width bounds these counters.
    ExtendedGcdLegacy signed gcd and Bezout coefficients, preserving the three-int64 field layout. For returned results, gcd>=0 and the mathematical identity a*x+b*y=gcd holds. Evaluate products in a wider type: int64 products can overflow even when the identity is small. Actual legacy gcd(0,0) returns {0,1,0}; this corrects the old comment claiming zero coefficients. A gcd of2^63 cannot fit this record and extended_gcd() throws instead. Manually constructed records are not validated.
    ExtendedGcdCertificateUnsigned gcd and signed canonical Bezout coefficients for the entire int64 input range. gcd is at most2^63, so INT64_MIN magnitudes are representable. Actual final coefficients fit signed int64; intermediate/terminal-zero coefficients need wider arithmetic. Mathematical a*x+b*y=gcd requires widened evaluation, not unchecked int64 multiplication. The returned zero-pair certificate is {0,1,0}. Default or manually assigned fields do not prove a solve; bezout_certificate_valid checks both the identity and common-divisor conditions without overflowing.
    ModularInverseTraceCanonical modular inverse and the actual same-pass Euclid certificate history. value and positive modulus are the original inputs; inverse lies in [0,modulus). euclid captures the actual computation on (value,modulus), followed by reduction of its coefficient of value. No explanatory rerun occurs. Modulus one returns zero, retaining the original degenerate-residue convention. Nonunits or invalid moduli throw instead of returning this record. All fields own their values.

A zero gcd is valid exactly for two zero inputs.     datamunge/algorithms/fft.hpp

    Functions

    fft()Forward or inverse complex DFT using iterative radix-2 butterflies. The forward uses exp(-2*pi*i*k*t/N) with no scaling. Inverse uses the positive exponent and divides by N. Bit reversal followed by log2(N) passes costs O(N log N) time; the by-value working vector uses O(N) storage. Input lvalues are copied and unchanged, rvalues can donate storage; no shared mutable state. Empty returns empty and a singleton is identity. Finite arithmetic has roundoff; nonfinite values or overflow are propagated, not validated by this low-level transform.
    fft_real()Forward FFT of real samples, returning the full N-bin complex transform. Unlike a packed rfft, this does not discard the conjugate negative-frequency half. Empty input returns empty. Samples are borrowed unchanged; output owns its storage. Work O(N log N), storage O(N); no shared mutable state or nonfinite-value validation.
    is_power_of_two()Tests the nonzero power-of-two domain accepted by the radix-2 transform.

    datamunge/algorithms/fft_diagnostics.hpp

    Functions

    dft_reference()Evaluates the defining complex DFT directly with extended-precision accumulation. An O(N^2) small-signal reference, not a fast transform. Unlike fft(), arbitrary lengths are accepted. Input is borrowed unchanged; result owns its values; no shared state.
    fft_diagnostics()Checks FFT coefficients, full complex inverse residual and Parseval energy against a direct DFT. Quadratic work O(N^2) is intentional; output is numerical evidence, not a timing benchmark or a guarantee for every dynamic range. Empty input gives a single zero row. No mutation/shared state; auxiliary storage O(N). Ratios with zero scale are zero.
    fft_linear_convolution()Full linear convolution via zero padding, spectral multiplication and normalized inverse FFT. Pads to the smallest power of two >= a.size()+b.size()-1, preventing circular wrap. Discards the inverse's roundoff imaginary residual and returns real coefficients. Work O(N log N), storage O(N); inputs borrowed unchanged, owned result, no shared state.
    fft_spectrum()One-sided real-input spectrum with explicit sample rate, window and padding normalization. Window M observed samples, append zeros to N, then call the full radix-2 FFT. Define W=sum(w), U=sum(w^2), a_k=1 at DC and even-N Nyquist, 2 elsewhere. Returned amplitude is a_k*abs(X_k)/W: coherent-tone magnitude calibration, not an exact off-bin amplitude estimate. Returned mean_square is a_k*abs(X_k)^2/(N*U); its sum is sum(w^2*x^2)/U. It is a mean-square contribution per bin, not a spectral density per Hz. Padding changes bin spacing, not observed duration or intrinsic resolving power; W/U exclude padded zeros. Borrows input unchanged; owns columns; no shared state. Work O(N log N), storage O(N).

    Types and constants

    FftWindowenum Window applied to M observed samples before any zero padding. Both windows are deterministic and nonnegative. Periodic Hann uses denominator M, as in scipy.signal.windows.hann(M,sym=False), not the symmetric M-1 convention.

Empty inputs give zero counts; scalars are owned without shared state.

    datamunge/algorithms/filtered_back_projection.hpp

    Functions

    back_projection()Gather projection rows linearly onto a centered image with the original pi/M scale. Uses the same detector weights as radon_transform, so in real arithmetic this is(pi/M) times that finite splat operator's transpose. Floating sums round. No filter is applied here. Fixed pi/M angular weights are appropriate to the ordinary uniform full-half-turn grid; arbitrary finite angle lists are accepted but not reweighted or certified as valid quadrature. Outside detector support contributes zero. Validates all shapes/finite data before allocation/gather. O(MN²+MD) work, O(N²) output and constant scratch, no shared state or input alias.
    disk_phantom()Create an owned centered disk on a square unit-spaced pixel grid. Pixel(r,c) uses x=c-(N-1)/2,y=r-(N-1)/2. Includes pixels with hypot(x,y)<=radius; others are zero. Radius zero selects the center pixel only for odd N. Uses hypot rather than squared-radius arithmetic, accepting every finite nonnegative radius and finite signed/zero intensity. O(N²) work/output, constant scratch; no input aliases or shared state. This is a numerical phantom, not medical data.
    filtered_back_projection()Reconstruct using the original finite Ram-Lak filter followed by shared backprojection. Retains the original callable signature and valid arithmetic/summation order. All dimensions/shapes/finite values are validated before filtering/allocation. Delegates to the same kernels exposed by ram_lak_filter and back_projection; in real arithmetic output is(pi/M)A-transpose H sinogram. This finite operator is not the inverse of its pixel-splat A. Accuracy depends on pixel/detector/view sampling, support and object; correlation alone does not certify amplitude or pointwise accuracy. Unit spacing and fixed pi/M weights, as back_projection. O(MD²+MN²) work; output O(N²), temporary filtered O(MD) and kernel O(D). No history quota, input mutation, retained references or shared mutable state.
    parallel_projection_angles()Generate rounded uniform half-turn projection angles in radians. Computes pi*i/count in the original report's arithmetic order, for i=0..count-1. Values are clamped below pi if final rounding reaches it; extremely large counts need not produce distinct doubles. Count1 gives only zero. O(count) work/output, constant scratch, no shared state. Supplies ordinary pi/count angular quadrature; arbitrary caller angle lists do not gain adaptive weights.
    radon_transform()Splat square-image pixel values linearly into a parallel-beam sinogram. Retains the original callable signature and valid arithmetic order. Pixel coordinates are centered with unit spacing. For each angle, detector coordinate is s=x*cos(theta)+y*sin(theta)+(num_detectors-1)/2. Two adjacent bins receive weights1-frac(s) and frac(s); out-of-range bins receive nothing. This finite pixel-splat operator is not exact continuous line integration. Clipping can lose projected mass. Empty angles, shape mismatch and nonfinite data reject before output allocation. Floor is cast only inside supported detector bounds. O(MN²+MD) work, O(MD) output and constant scratch, M=angles.size(). Owned output/input unchanged; concurrent reads require unchanged inputs; no shared state.
    ram_lak_filter()Filter each finite projection row by the original unit-spacing finite Ram-Lak convolution. Uses h[0]=1/4,h[k]=-1/(pi²k²) for odd k,zero for nonzero even k. For row width D, retains lags-(D-1)..D-1 with zero extension and direct convolution, preserving the original summation order. This is not circular FFT convolution; the finite kernel does not annihilate all finite constant rows. Empty sinogram returns empty; nonempty rows must have equal positive width and finite entries. O(MD²) work, O(MD) output plus O(D) kernel storage; no input mutation or aliases.

    datamunge/algorithms/fisher_yates.hpp

    Classes

    ShuffleCensusOwned complete integer counts of labelled permutations and all position marginals. Labels are the original positions 0..n-1, so repeated caller values cannot merge distinguishable labels. by_position[p][v] counts original label v at output position p. permutation_counts contains only observed outputs in lexicographic order. Empty trials yield an empty map and zero marginal counts.
    ShuffleOutcomeOwned seeded shuffle output with actual swap-stage and raw-generator work counts. stages counts n-1 swap attempts (zero for empty/singleton), including self-swaps; nontrivial_swaps counts i!=j, even when the two values are equal. random_words includes rejected range-sampler words. Copying owns the values; no shared state.
    ShuffleStepOne actual descending Fisher–Yates swap, with values read before mutation. Stores no whole-array snapshot or post-hoc replay; i is finalized by this stage.
    ShuffleTraceOwned initial input, seeded output and actual ordered swap records. Complete capture units are C=2*n+max(n-1,0): two value arrays plus one entry per stage. This counts entries, not bytes or peak RAM. No replay or shared state.

    Functions

    fisher_yates_from_choices()Apply one completely validated descending Fisher–Yates choice sequence without a generator. The choices correspond in order to i=n-1..1 and each must lie in [0,i]. Validates all choices before copying/mutation. Shares the seeded swap kernel; O(n) work/storage, caller inputs unchanged and no shared state.
    fisher_yates_seed_census()Count whole labelled permutations and every position marginal over a contiguous seed interval. Uses the same seeded kernel, once per seed; this is deterministic enumeration, not independent random sampling. Zero trials are allowed, with empty permutation counts; n=0 still counts one empty output per trial. No seed wrapping is allowed. Checks C=n*n+trials*(n+1) before allocation or any shuffle. Matrix setup is O(n²); map updates add O(log distinct_outputs) comparisons of O(n)-length keys per run, plus O(n) shuffle work and actual rejection retries. Storage is bounded by C entries up to map/container overhead; the cap is not a byte or peak-RAM bound.
    fisher_yates_shuffle()Return an owned permutation using descending Fisher–Yates and the canonical SplitMix64 sampler. Preserves the seeded output convention: rng.uniform_u64(0,i) for i=n-1..1. The sampler uses multiply-and-reject, not modulo reduction. The ideal uniform permutation theorem assumes independent uniform bounded draws; a fixed uint64 seed gives a deterministic finite-state experiment, not that theorem's premise. No cryptographic unpredictability is promised. Duplicates are preserved; empty and singleton inputs consume no random words. Input is not mutated; separate calls share no state. O(n) copying/swaps and O(n) owned storage, plus rejection sampler retries (expected O(n) under ideal raw words, no fixed retry bound).
    fisher_yates_shuffle_trace()Capture one seeded shuffle's actual input, output, pre-swap values and accepted choices. Checks the whole C=2*n+max(n-1,0) capture before copying input or drawing randomness. O(n) stored entries and copying/swaps plus sampler retries; owned records are independent of later caller edits. No partial trace is returned on failure.
    fisher_yates_shuffle_work()Run the same seeded shuffle and count actual swap attempts and raw generator calls. Shares the ordinary kernel and canonical range sampler, without history or replay. O(n) output storage, O(n) copying/swaps plus retries; source values are unmodified. Counts are algorithmic work, not runtime measurements or a uniformity certificate.
    shuffle_choice_census()Enumerate every ideal finite choice sequence for a shuffle model, retaining exact counts. No pseudorandom generator is used. FisherYates has n! equally weighted choices; AllPositions has n^n ascending full-range choices; CyclicShift has n rotations. At n=0 every model has one empty outcome. Models do not assert actual seeded uniformity. Checks the whole C=n*n+outcomes*(n+1) before allocation/enumeration. Map/copy/storage costs follow fisher_yates_seed_census(), without random retries; complete count overflow and label/container limits still apply with the cap off.

    Types and constants

    ShuffleCensusRuleenum Exact choice-tree models for permutation-law comparisons, without a random generator. FisherYates is the descending shrinking-range algorithm. AllPositions is the deliberately biased model: visit i=0..n-1 and independently choose j=0..n-1. CyclicShift enumerates only the n rotations (one empty output when n=0).

    datamunge/algorithms/flashsort.hpp

    Classes

    FlashsortClassGroupConsecutive class-index range and its total original occupancy.
    FlashsortMoveOne actual carried-value exchange before the finishing insertion sort.
    FlashsortTraceOwned original, class-grouped and sorted states plus actual class/carry evidence. A nonshortcut capture admits C=5n+2m entries before copying: input, output, grouped values, original assignments, at most n carry records and two m-entry class arrays. Shortcut C=2n stores only input/output; other arrays are empty. Counts are entries, not bytes or peak RAM. No sorting/assembly is replayed.
    FlashsortWorkActual work and class occupancy from one native Flashsort, without a history. Min/max comparisons count two ordered tests per element after the first; classifications counts every actual value-to-class call, including leader searches. permutation_writes counts carried-value exchanges, including cycle closure. Insertion comparisons count predecessor>key evaluations (including false ones), shifts count successful predecessor moves, and placements count final key stores. Loop-bound/finite-validation tests and allocations are excluded. n<=INT_MAX keeps these whole-run uint64 counters representable. No timing claim.

    Functions

    flashsort()Sort an arithmetic vector in place by value classification, cycle carries and insertion. Uses max(2,int(0.43*n)) classes for nonconstant n>1 input; empty/singleton/ constant inputs return without classes. Requires finite floating values and n<=INT_MAX, checked before mutation/allocation. Integral spans are safe across the full type range; unsafe floating ranges use scaled classification. Historical safe classifications and carry/insertion order are retained; this variant does not first swap the maximum to index zero. It is not stable. O(n+m+sum(class_size²)) worst-case work, O(m) auxiliary metadata; m is Theta(n), so auxiliary memory is not constant. Expected linear work needs a suitable balanced-input model; all-equal data takes the shortcut. No shared state.
    flashsort_class_count()Return the historical nominal nonconstant-input class count without an array allocation. Gives zero for n<=1 and max(2,int(0.43*n)) otherwise. A constant actual input still takes the shortcut and allocates zero classes. O(1), no shared state.
    flashsort_class_groups()Aggregate actual original class counts into consecutive near-equal index ranges. Group g contains [floor(g*m/groups),floor((g+1)*m/groups)). Empty input or groups>m is allowed and can yield empty ranges. This sums actual class counts; it does not reclassify values using a different number of value bins. Validates the complete total and optional group cap before output allocation. O(m+groups) time and O(groups) owned output, no input mutation/shared state.
    flashsort_class_index()Evaluate the sort's safe value classifier without allocating or sorting an array. Preserves the historical rounded double coefficient/product when it is safe. Integral differences use exact nonnegative unsigned subtraction. Floating ranges that would overflow or make the coefficient nonfinite use a scaled long-double ratio. Clamps before conversion; rounding near a class boundary is part of the map and need not equal an arbitrary-precision floor formula. A constant range maps its sole valid value to zero. O(1), no shared state.
    flashsort_trace()Sort one owned copy and retain actual classes, carried exchanges and insertion work. Validates/scans the input once, then admits complete C=5n+2m (shortcut2n) before copying or sorting. Shared preparation and kernel avoid replay. Input remains unchanged; all snapshots/records own their values and copies are independent. O(n+m) output entries plus the ordinary sort's work; capture limits count entries, not bytes, timing or a peak-memory bound.
    flashsort_uniform_sample()Generate the original Flashsort report's local mt19937_64 integer-uniform sample. Uses std::uniform_int_distribution<int> on inclusive [lower,upper]. Repeated arguments reproduce on a given standard library; mappings across toolchains are not promised identical. O(count) time/storage, no global random state.
    flashsort_work()Sort in place with the same shared kernel and return actual class/primitive work. No snapshots or carry history are stored. Complexity, validation, mutation guarantees and distribution conditions are those of flashsort(). Counters describe this execution; they do not measure time or certify expected work.

    datamunge/algorithms/fletcher16.hpp

    Classes

    Fletcher16ByteStepOne actual modulo-255 byte fold from the production Fletcher-16 kernel. Residues use the canonical representation 0..254; byte 255 contributes zero modulo 255. Before/after values describe the actual sequential fold, not replay.
    Fletcher16FlipOne independent single-input-bit corruption, recomputed by the same full-message fold. Bit numbering is byte-major, least-significant-bit first within each octet. delta_a and delta_b are modular differences, not XOR popcounts or probabilities.
    Fletcher16FlipScanOwned complete one-bit census and its exact full-message byte-fold budget. Every candidate toggles/restores one owned scratch message. The original view is unchanged and never retained. Empty input has zero records and counters.
    Fletcher16ReplacementOne replacement candidate at a fixed byte position, including the unchanged control.
    Fletcher16ReplacementScanOwned exact 256-candidate single-position replacement census. There are 255 changed candidates and one unchanged control. A zero/255 original has one changed candidate that aliases; other originals have none. Records are complete actual folds, not an assumed detection theorem.
    Fletcher16TraceOwned complete actual byte states for zero-initialised raw Fletcher-16. No input view survives. Empty input has checksum/residues zero and no events. The packed raw tag is B in the high byte and A in the low byte; it is not a protocol-specific pair of complemented check bytes.

    Functions

    byte_sum32()Compute the original report's plain unsigned32-bit byte sum, with intentional modulo 2^32 wrap. Unsigned octets are added without positional weighting; reordering always keeps this sum. Includes embedded zeros/high bytes. O(n) time/O(1) storage, no allocation, input mutation or retained view. This is a checksum convention, not an exact unbounded integer sum or authentication tag.
    checksum_swap_bytes()Swap two validated byte positions in an owned binary copy without changing the source. Checks both indices before copying or mutation; equal valid indices return an unchanged owned copy. Empty input has no valid index. O(n) copy work/storage, constant swap work, arbitrary binary octets preserved and no retained view.
    fletcher16()Compute the original zero-initialised raw Fletcher-16, packed as (B<<8)|A. Processes every unsigned octet, including embedded zeros/255. Each byte updates A=(A+x)%255 and B=(B+A)%255, using canonical residues 0..254; empty input returns0. All single-input-bit errors change the raw tag when the original tag is held fixed. It does not detect every single-byte substitution:0 and255 alias. Transpositions can also alias. No authentication, collision probability or speed ranking follows. O(n) time, O(1) storage, two modulo reductions per byte, no allocation/mutation, retained input or shared mutable state. Preserves the existing const-string API.
    fletcher16_combine()Combine two zero-initialised raw tags without reading either message. For a right message of length m, A=A1+A2 and B=B1+B2+m*A1, modulo 255. Reduces m before multiplication, supporting every uint64 length. Both tags must have canonical lanes 0..254. Their consistency with the claimed message/length is the caller's responsibility. O(1) time/storage, no allocation/shared state.
    fletcher16_flip_scan()Census every independent one-input-bit toggle using complete production checksum folds. Computes one baseline and 8n changed tags, each over n bytes; exact fold work is n*(8n+1). One owned scratch message is toggled/restored, not copied per candidate. Whole bit/work/capacity checks precede allocation or checksum evaluation. O(n²) byte-fold work plus toggles, O(n) scratch/records; no partial/truncated scan. Empty input has no records and zero counters. No input mutation/shared state.
    fletcher16_replacement_scan()Recompute all 256 possible octet replacements at one validated input position. Includes one unchanged control and255 changed candidates; uses one owned scratch message and the ordinary complete checksum fold for each. Checks exact 257*n byte work, capacities and optional whole cap before allocation/evaluation. O(257n) time/O(n+256) output/scratch entries, no input mutation or retained view.
    fletcher16_trace()Capture every actual byte fold from the same zero-initialised production kernel. Checks the whole n-event cap and vector capacity before allocation/folding. Each record owns its byte and states; no source view or replay survives. O(n) time and O(n) history entries, with checksum0/no events for empty input.
    fletcher16_transposition_delta()Predict the modular second-residue change for exchanging two positions at a given distance. If the left byte a is replaced by b and the right b by a, deltaA=0 and deltaB=distance*(b-a) modulo 255. Uses reduced factors, supporting uint64MAX. Returns the exact arithmetic formula, not an actual message fold or probability. Zero distance or equal/congruent bytes gives zero. O(1), no allocation/state.
    fletcher16_update()Continue one canonical raw Fletcher-16 state over the next byte view. A is the low byte and B the high byte; both must be in 0..254. Empty input returns the same validated state. Shares the ordinary byte kernel, with two modulo 255 reductions per byte and no trace/allocation. O(n) time/O(1) storage, no retained views, mutation or shared state. Arbitrary packed lane255 states are rejected.

    Classes

    FloodFillNeighborOne ordered neighbor slot; invalid slots have zero row and column. Four directions are up/down/left/right; eight are NW/N/NE/W/E/SW/S/SE.
    FloodFillNeighborhoodFixed-capacity ordered neighborhood without allocation or grid storage. Unused slots are zero initialized; count is zero for an invalid center.
    FloodFillProbeOne actual direction attempt and its value before any discovery paint. Outside slots have value zero; accepted means an in-bounds target match.

    FloodFillVisitOne actual LIFO pop and its contiguous range of neighbor probes. Stack sizes exclude/include the current scan's discoveries respectively.
    FloodFillWorkOwned scalar measurements of one actual iterative fill. Each discovered cell is painted when pushed and popped once. Neighbor slots include outside probes; in_bounds_neighbors counts actual value reads. A preexisting replacement-valued cell is a barrier, not a traversal bridge.

    Functions

    flood_fill()Paint the seed component, preserving the original count-returning API. Uses flood_fill_work() and its validation, direction order, complexity and partial-mutation behavior on resource failure. Full signed int values are valid.
    flood_fill_example()Construct the original six-by-eight binary flood-fill report fixture. Upper-left and lower-right foreground components have eight and five cells. Returns fresh owned storage; no external dataset or random state.
    flood_fill_neighborhood()Enumerate the actual fill direction order using guarded size_t geometry. No product, narrowing, allocation or grid access; virtual SIZE_MAX dimensions are supported. Boundary guards precede coordinate subtraction/addition.
    flood_fill_trace()Copy a grid and record actual pop/probe evidence while painting its copy. Validates shape first. Before copying, admits the whole upper entry bound 2*rows+(D+3)*cells for an active fill (D=4 or 8), or 2*(rows+cells) for a no-op. Counts outer-row entries, cell entries, visits and probes, not bytes or peak RAM. Actual histories contain only K visits and D*K probes. Default cap is one million; zero disables only the optional cap. Checked arithmetic/container bounds remain. O(rows+cells+D*K) time/storage. Caller input is unchanged on success or failure; no partial result escapes.
    flood_fill_work()Paint the exact-value seed component and measure the actual traversal. Full rectangular validation and checked cell product precede all no-ops and mutation. Signed int values are unrestricted. Empty/outside/same-value fills change nothing. Marks on push, scans four directions U/D/L/R or eight NW/N/NE/W/E/SW/S/SE, then pops LIFO. O(rows+K) time and O(K) stack for K changed cells; no history quota. Independent calls have no shared mutable state.

    FloodFillStopenum Reason a validated flood-fill operation did or did not traverse. Empty includes zero-width rectangular grids. SameValue changes no cells.

    Classes

    AllPairsShortestPathsOwned native distance/next-hop matrices with the historical member layout. Native results have two n-by-n matrices. Unreachable distances are positive infinity. A zero-length diagonal path costs0 unless affected by a negative cycle. After negative-cycle detection, affected raw entries are not shortest distances; they are retained to preserve the actual in-place computation. Independent classification uses the matrices, not an externally supplied boolean flag.
    FloydWarshallOutcomeOwned ordinary matrices and actual work without history. Uses the same seeding and k/i/j kernel as the original API; no replay.
    FloydWarshallRelaxationOne actual strict improvement in k/i/j execution order. The left/right entries are read immediately before the update; in a negative cycle sweep they can change within that same k stage. A record is not a failed comparison or an edge seed. The selected hop is the actual next[from][k].
    FloydWarshallStageOwned actual matrices at one admitted-intermediate boundary. Admitted0 is the seeded state. Admitted k+1 follows the complete k sweep. Snapshots are raw execution states; affected negative-cycle entries do not have shortest-path meaning. No negative-cycle flag is fabricated before its final scan.
    FloydWarshallTraceOwned graph, raw matrices and evidence captured during the executing sweep. Contains seeded and every post-k matrix, plus only strict successful improvements. No input views, rerun or independent alternative algorithm is retained.
    FloydWarshallWorkActual seeding, guarded sweep and final diagonal-scan counts. Counts refer to the executing kernel, excluding input validation, allocations and optional snapshot copying. Each finite candidate costs one addition and one strict comparison; equal-cost candidates keep the existing next hop. All counts are checked by representable full sweep bounds before matrix allocation.

    Functions

    floyd_warshall()Compute all-pairs directed distances and next hops using Floyd's native recurrence. Validates all endpoints and finite edge weights before allocating. Keeps the lightest parallel edge using strict comparisons; equal weights retain the first hop. Diagonal initialization is zero, positive self-edges are ignored, and negative self-edges are retained. Sweep order is k/i/j with infinity guards. Every attempted finite sum must remain finite, including non-improving ones. Floating additions/comparisons and strict negative-diagonal tests follow double arithmetic; they do not certify exact-real shortest costs near rounding limits. After all sweeps, the first negative diagonal sets the global cycle flag. Raw matrices remain unchanged for affected pairs; use pair classification. No mutation of inputs or shared state. O(n squared+edges+n cubed) worst-case work and O(n squared) owned matrix storage. No ordinary history quota.
    floyd_warshall_example_edges()Return the original nine-edge five-vertex report graph with negative edges. Fresh owned data; no random state/dataset. No negative cycle, and0-to-2 has cost-3 along0,4,3,2. Vertex count is five, supplied separately to the detector.
    floyd_warshall_pair_status()Classify a pair as finite, unreachable or negative-cycle unbounded. Validates complete square distance/next matrices, finite-or-positive-infinity distances and every hop ID before querying. Unbounded means some k has a negative diagonal and finite i-to-k and k-to-j entries. The supplied global boolean is not trusted as a substitute. Unaffected pairs remain meaningful despite another component's cycle. External matrices are not certified shortest paths by shape/value validation. O(n squared) validation plus O(n) querying; no allocation, mutation or shared state.
    floyd_warshall_trace()Record actual seeded/post-k matrices and strict improvements without replay. Validates all endpoints and finite edge weights before allocating. Sweep order is k/i/j with infinity guards. Every attempted finite sum must remain finite, including non-improving ones. Floating additions/comparisons and strict negative-diagonal tests follow double arithmetic; they do not certify exact-real shortest costs near rounding limits. After all sweeps, the first negative diagonal sets the global cycle flag. Raw matrices remain unchanged for affected pairs; use pair classification. No mutation of inputs or shared state. O(n squared+edges+n cubed) worst-case work and O(n squared) owned matrix storage. No ordinary history quota. Full input validation and the complete upper bound from trace_entries() precede copies and kernel execution. Default cap is one million entries; zero disables only that cap. Checked arithmetic/container limits remain. This conservative bound can reject a graph with few actual improvements. Actual records contain every stage and only successful updates, without truncation or partial results. O(edges+n squared+n cubed) work/storage for owned full-stage evidence.
    floyd_warshall_trace_entries()Compute the complete upper entry bound of an owned full-stage trace. Keeps the lightest parallel edge using strict comparisons; equal weights retain the first hop. Diagonal initialization is zero, positive self-edges are ignored, and negative self-edges are retained. Sweep order is k/i/j with infinity guards. Every attempted finite sum must remain finite, including non-improving ones. Floating additions/comparisons and strict negative-diagonal tests follow double arithmetic; they do not certify exact-real shortest costs near rounding limits. After all sweeps, the first negative diagonal sets the global cycle flag. Raw matrices remain unchanged for affected pairs; use pair classification. No mutation of inputs or shared state. O(n squared+edges+n cubed) worst-case work and O(n squared) owned matrix storage. No ordinary history quota.
    reconstruct_path() ×2Follow validated next hops with a vertex-count bound and negative-cycle checks. Full matrix validation matches pair_status() before diagonal/no-path shortcuts. An affected pair throws even on the diagonal; unrelated negative cycles do not prevent finite/unreachable queries. Unreachable or a broken sentinel chain returns empty; a finite diagonal returns its single vertex. Cyclic malformed hop chains throw after at most n moves, preventing unbounded walks. Validation does not certify an external record's weights or optimality. O(n squared+path length) work due to full validation; O(path length) returned storage.
