    FloydWarshallPairStatusenum Meaning of one ordered pair after the negative-cycle reachability test. This classification does not rewrite raw matrices to negative infinity.
    kNoVertexvariable No-next-hop sentinel, equal to SIZE_MAX; normally used on diagonal/unreachable pairs. Native negative-cycle raw matrices may contain diagonal next hops.

    datamunge/algorithms/fnv_analysis.hpp

    Classes

    FNVBucketProfileCounted bucket occupancy and distinct-key integer-hash collisions. All fields own their values. Bucket pairs count unordered INPUT RECORD pairs sharing a bucket, including duplicates. Hash pairs count unordered DISTINCT byte-key pairs with equal full-width integer hashes. These are different events. Numeric dataframe columns convert counters to double, exact up to 2^53.

    Functions

    fnv_bit_flips()Flip each input bit separately and count changed output bits against the original hash. Input bit IDs are byte-major, least-significant bit first. This is a finite sensitivity experiment, not a cryptographic or distribution test. Cost O(n²) hashed bytes and O(n) result rows; no input mutation or retained string copies.
    fnv_bucket_profile()Form an owned bucket census using canonical full-width FNV hashes modulo B. Validates width and positive B before work/allocation. Duplicate strings stay separate bucket records, but are not distinct-key hash collisions. Uses ordered sets/maps, with O(B+n log n) dictionary operations plus byte hashing/comparisons and O(B+distinct-key bytes) storage. Pure, thread-safe; no input changes.
    fnv_byte_keys()Generate all one-byte keys with a chosen low-bit residue, in byte order.
    fnv_example_words()Original report's 32-word fixture in unchanged order.
    fnv_trace_table()Tabulate actual byte updates, keeping large hash words as exact hexadecimal strings.

    datamunge/algorithms/fnv_hash.hpp

    Classes

    FNVStepActual before/XOR/after state for one consumed byte, in integer hash order. Owns primitive values, not a view into the input. Unsigned word arithmetic wraps.
    FNVTraceOwned hash value and one complete actual record per consumed byte. Empty input retains zero records and its offset basis. Copying owns independent history; input and ordinary scalar state are excluded from the record quota. This is O(n) retained storage, unlike the ordinary hashes' O(1) state.

    Functions

    fnv1a_32()32-bit FNV-1a integer hash, with the same byte semantics as fnv1a_64(). Basis 2166136261, prime 16777619; unsigned narrowing after every multiplication implements modulo 2^32. Pure O(n) selected updates, O(1) auxiliary state.
    fnv1a_64()64-bit FNV-1a hash of a byte string, as RFC 9923's integer interface. Starts at 14695981039346656037 and uses prime 1099511628211. Processes every unsigned byte, including NUL, without Unicode decoding, normalization or an appended terminator. Empty input returns the basis. Pure, thread-safe, O(n) selected byte updates and O(1) auxiliary state; not a cryptographic hash. Integer return is distinct from the RFC's little-endian serialized byte vector.
    fnv1a_trace()Trace the same native FNV-1a loop, retaining one actual record per byte. The complete n-record quota is checked before allocation or hashing. Zero disables the policy quota; vector capacity is still checked. No replay, partial return, input copy, or peak-RAM interpretation of the quota. Calls ordinary and traced kernels with identical arithmetic; pure and thread-safe.

    Classes

    ForceDirectedFrameOwned state of one actual sweep. Repulsion is captured before attraction; displacement is the actual net accumulator after attraction. Positions follow all vertex moves. No replay or separately rounded force sums.
    ForceDirectedMetricsIndependent widened geometry and regularized force potential. Diagnostics use long double, O(n squared + m) work and O(1) auxiliary storage.     Functions

    force_directed_layout()Compute the historical seeded force-directed drawing. The direct unit-area variant uses k=1/sqrt(n), distance floor 1e-9, ordered u<v repulsion and input-order attraction (duplicates count; loops ignored). All forces precede all moves: F/s*min(s,t), s=max(1e-9,hypot(F)), t=0.1*(1-double(i)/T). Coincident points receive no jitter. There is no bounding box, convergence test, velocity or energy line search. For n>=2, final double centering and maximum-radius scaling run even for T=0. For n<2, return initialized positions unchanged and perform no sweeps. All endpoints and supplied finite coordinates are validated before allocation or optional capture admission. Actual nonfinite arithmetic throws without a partial result. No caller mutation or shared state. Counts and capacities are checked; ordinary auxiliary storage is O(n), time O(n+m+T*(n*n+m+n)) for n>=2. Seeded coordinates use a local mt19937_64 and two uniform(-.5,.5) variates per vertex; exact seeded bits also depend on the standard library.

    datamunge/algorithms/forward_backward.hpp

    Classes

    ForwardBackwardOutcomeOwned inference tables and actual work from the same kernel. All arrays own storage; caller edits are independent. There is no additional phase-history copy because the result already contains the actual tables.
    ForwardBackwardResultOwned actual scaled forward/backward tables and smoothed state marginals. Historical field layout retained. For positive representable evidence, alpha rows are filtering distributions; beta uses terminal beta[T-1]=scale[T-1] and is not a probability distribution. In exact arithmetic sum(alpha[t]*beta[t])=scale[t], so gamma is explicitly normalized. Impossible sequences have log_likelihood=-infinity and zero gamma placeholders, not defined posteriors. Empty observations have empty arrays and log likelihood0.
    ForwardBackwardWorkActual once-only inference counts, excluding validation and allocations. Transition terms count pair visits: one product plus accumulation in the forward pass, two products plus accumulation in the backward pass. Support probes run only on the first zero predictive mass to distinguish a mathematically impossible prefix from numeric underflow. No replay or diagnostic arithmetic is included.
    HiddenMarkovModelOwned finite-alphabet hidden Markov model parameters in state-major order. Initial has N entries, transition N rows of N entries, emission N equal rows of M>0 entries. Forward-backward and path-query APIs validate all shapes first, then finite weights in[0,1] and each distribution's long-double sum within absolute1e-12 of1. They never normalize caller parameters. The entirely empty model is accepted with empty observations. Other legacy consumers may assume valid parameters. State and symbol IDs are zero based; arrays own their storage.
    HmmPathEnumerationOwned widened path sum, state marginals and best joint path. A bounded small-model reference, not a fast inference method or exact arithmetic. Time0 is the least significant base-N digit; strict best-weight updates keep the first enumerated tie. Impossible evidence yields probability0, log_likelihood=-infinity, zero marginal placeholders and no best path. Empty observations enumerate one empty path of weight1. Long-double positive product underflow throws.

    Functions

    forward_backward()Compute validated scaled filtering, smoothing and log likelihood. Fully validate model shapes/finite stochastic rows and every observation before allocation, quotas or empty-input shortcuts. No caller mutation, RNG or shared state. The original double operation order and scaling convention are retained for representable positive evidence. Impossible evidence returns log likelihood -infinity and zero undefined-posterior placeholders. A zero predictive mass with a positive-probability support path throws underflow_error; nonfinite actual arithmetic or reciprocal scales throw overflow_error. Individual tiny terms can still round away: scaling is not an arbitrary-length/precision guarantee. Empty observations have likelihood1 and empty tables. Time O(N²+NM+T+TN²), owned storage O(TN+T), auxiliary scratch O(N) only for the exceptional support probe. Returned arrays already expose actual states. The historical two-argument call has no optional admission cap; representability checks remain.
    forward_backward_entries()Forecast whole owned inference entry records without allocation. For positive N,T, counts4T+3TN: three row records and one scale scalar per time plus three N-scalar rows. Otherwise0. Units are entry records, not bytes or peak RAM; container objects and exceptional support scratch are additional. Shape and probability validity cannot be checked from counts alone.

    forward_backward_work()Measure actual smoothing work with optional whole-result admission. Impossible evidence returns log likelihood -infinity and zero undefined-posterior placeholders. A zero predictive mass with a positive-probability support path throws underflow_error; nonfinite actual arithmetic or reciprocal scales throw overflow_error. Individual tiny terms can still round away: scaling is not an arbitrary-length/precision guarantee. Empty observations have likelihood1 and empty tables. Time O(N²+NM+T+TN²), owned storage O(TN+T), auxiliary scratch O(N) only for the exceptional support probe. Returned arrays already expose actual states.     datamunge/algorithms/fp_growth.hpp

    Classes

    FPGrowthHeaderOwned node-link indices for one observed item in a captured tree. Headers are returned by ascending item ID; each node-index list preserves actual creation order. It replaces a linked-chain view with independent owned indices. Sum the referenced node counts for item support in this conditional tree.
    FPGrowthNodeOne actual FP node in creation order, with a checked full-width parent ID. Node0 is the dummy root with item SIZE_MAX, count0 and parent SIZE_MAX. Other nodes may legitimately carry item SIZE_MAX; root identity comes from index0, never the item value. Counts are weighted prefix occurrence totals, not edge probabilities.
    FPGrowthResultOwned canonical frequent sets and actual work without history. Uses the same executing kernel as capture. The ordinary output is never counted as retained trace-history quota. No input mutation or shared state.
    FPGrowthStepOne actual DFS emission followed by its conditional pattern base. Step order is the original depth-first mining schedule. Pattern is the emitted unsorted suffix sequence. Empty ancestor paths are omitted from base. A nonempty base always builds a child tree, even if filtering leaves only its root. SIZE_MAX child means no nonempty base and no child build; no replay is used.
    FPGrowthTraceOwned raw baskets, actual trees, emissions and weighted conditional bases. Retained history is admitted online before each associated copy/move. Base entries are N+raw occurrences. Each tree costs1+prefix+nodes+order+sum(1+header node IDs); each step costs1+pattern+sum(1+path items). Node/step/tree/header aggregates count one record each; arrays add their item/index entries. Root nodes and pruned child trees count. This quota excludes ordinary canonical output, work, normalized input, active trees, conditional buffers and allocator bytes; it is not bytes or peak RAM. Working records may be formed before their size is known. No partial result escapes failure.
    FPGrowthTreeOwned actual fully built tree, including conditional trees pruned to a root. Trees occur in actual build order. Prefix stores the current DFS suffix sequence, not sorted canonical output. Order is frequency descending with ID-ascending ties; header rows are ID ascending. Nodes/headers own storage. Only the frequent-item projection is compressed; raw rows, infrequent items and empty projections are not recoverable from this tree alone.
    FPGrowthWeightedPathOne actual nonempty conditional prefix path with its target-node count. Items run from the nearest ancestor toward the root, excluding the target and root. The child builder sorts them again using its own conditional frequency order. Weight is the target node count, not an ancestor count or number of path records.
    FPGrowthWorkActual build, insertion, header, parent-walk and DFS counts. Counts exclude validation, allocation, sort comparisons, hashing internals and capture copies. Weighted counts contribute one visit per stored item, not weight visits. Root creation is counted through trees_built; nodes_created excludes roots. Peak node records include only trees resident in active DFS frames, excluding temporary child/conditional buffers and retained history.

    datamunge/algorithms/gabow_scc.hpp

    Classes

    GabowEventOwned actual state after one traversal primitive, without replay. Kinds are enter,edge,collapse,close-root,assign,finish. Enter follows first preorder/S/B pushes; edge follows neighbor-index increment before edge action; collapse/close-root follow one B pop; assign follows one S pop and component write; finish follows frame pop and any component counter increment. Intermediate assignment states need not satisfy quiescent boundary invariants. S contains every discovered-unassigned vertex, including finished DFS calls, and can exceed the active DFS path.
    GabowResultRaw component IDs and actual work from one SCC execution. IDs are contiguous0..C-1, assigned in sink-first closure order. For a cross-component edge u->v, id[u]>id[v]. Neighbor order can change labels for incomparable components; equality of partitions is the stable meaning.
    GabowTraceOwned graph and actual primitive snapshots from one kernel execution. Whole-request conservative admission precedes graph copy and state allocation. No replay, shared state, caller mutation, truncation or partial output. Captured entry accounting excludes ordinary final labels/work/scalar root metadata, working state and allocator bytes.
    GabowWorkActual traversal operations and peak stack lengths. Excludes validation, history copies, allocation, rendering and partition summaries. Each vertex enters/finishes once, is assigned once and is pushed/popped once on each stack. Individual edges can collapse many boundaries; total root pops is N. Event count is E+4N, including root-close pops and collapse pops.
    SccComponentOne labeled partition group with ascending member vertex IDs. Groups are sorted by nonnegative raw label, which need not be contiguous. Vertex IDs are original row positions. This container does not itself certify strong connectivity.
    SccSummaryOwned groups and the deduplicated quotient graph for supplied labels. Dense quotient indices follow ascending raw labels, distinct from those labels. Internal edges are omitted from adjacency; cross edges are sorted/deduplicated. For arbitrary labels the quotient may contain cycles: no SCC correctness certificate is computed. Gabow labels make reverse_topological true, which proves acyclicity by strict label decrease.

    Functions

    gabow_scc()Find strong components with validated iterative path-based DFS. Validate n, exact row count and every endpoint before empty returns, state allocation or capture admission. Preserve loops, duplicate entries, neighbor order and ascending start-vertex order. Empty(0,{}) returns empty. One explicit heap DFS avoids call-stack recursion. S holds all discovered-unassigned vertices, not only active frames. Raw labels follow component closure order, with cross edges strictly decreasing IDs. Ordinary traversal is O(N+E) time/O(N) auxiliary state excluding input/result; no mutation or shared state.
    gabow_scc_example_graph()Construct the original eight-vertex cycle-chain fixture. Owned fixed graph: cycles0<->1,2->3->4->2,5<->6 and sink7, linked by1->2,4->5,6->7. No shared state.
    gabow_scc_trace()Capture actual S/B/DFS states with whole-request admission. Validate n, exact row count and every endpoint before empty returns, state allocation or capture admission. Preserve loops, duplicate entries, neighbor order and ascending start-vertex order. Empty(0,{}) returns empty. One explicit heap DFS avoids call-stack recursion. S holds all discovered-unassigned vertices, not only active frames. Raw labels follow component closure order, with cross edges strictly decreasing IDs. Ordinary traversal is O(N+E) time/O(N) auxiliary state excluding input/result; no mutation or shared state. Uses gabow_scc_trace_entries() before graph copies and state allocation. Default quota1m;0 disables only optional cap. Count/container checks remain. Snapshots are actual primitive states with owned storage; no partial trace or truncation. Snapshot copies add O((N+E)*N) time and retained storage in the worst case.
    gabow_scc_trace_entries()Forecast whole retained-history entries from virtual graph dimensions. Require n>=0; n0 permits only edges0. Actual transition count is E+4N. Input rows+neighbors cost N+E; each snapshot has one metadata record plus full comp/preorder arrays and up to N entries in each S, B and active-frame vector. Return (N+E)+(E+4N)*(1+5N), not bytes or peak RAM. Each DFS frame pair counts as one record. Excludes ordinary final labels/work/scalar root metadata/working state/allocator bytes. Bound all snapshots conservatively; check count/vector capacities without allocation.
    gabow_scc_work()Find strong components and count actual traversal operations. Validate n, exact row count and every endpoint before empty returns, state allocation or capture admission. Preserve loops, duplicate entries, neighbor order and ascending start-vertex order. Empty(0,{}) returns empty. One explicit heap DFS avoids call-stack recursion. S holds all discovered-unassigned vertices, not only active frames. Raw labels follow component closure order, with cross edges strictly decreasing IDs. Ordinary traversal is O(N+E) time/O(N) auxiliary state excluding input/result; no mutation or shared state. Counts exclude history, validation and summary work; no replay.
    scc_same_partition()Compare labeled partitions independently of their numeric IDs. Validate every nonnegative label before a length mismatch returns false. Labels may be noncontiguous or INT_MAX. Two directional maps establish a label bijection in O(N log C) time/O(C) state; empty partitions agree. No mutation, relabeling or connectivity test.
    scc_summary()Group supplied labels and form a sorted deduplicated quotient graph. Validate every adjacency row/endpoint and nonnegative label, with labels.size()==adj.size(), before grouping. Groups sort by raw label; quotient IDs index groups. This summarizes a supplied partition without proving its classes are SCCs; an arbitrary quotient may be cyclic. Costs O(N log C+E log C+sum degree*log degree), with O(N+E) owned/scratch storage. Input loops/duplicates count in raw metrics, but internal arcs are omitted and cross arcs deduplicated. No input mutation.

    Types and constants

    GabowDfsFrametype One actual suspended DFS frame: vertex and next neighbor index. The first field is the vertex ID; the second is the next size_t adjacency position. Frames are bottom-to-top. No call-stack recursion.
    SccAdjacencytype Directed adjacency rows with full-width neighbor positions. Rows correspond to vertex IDs0..n-1. Endpoint IDs are int; duplicate edges, loops and neighbor order are retained. No symmetry or simple-graph condition.

    datamunge/algorithms/game_search.hpp

    Classes

    GameNodeA node of a two-player game tree: a leaf carrying a heuristic value, or an internal node with children. Levels alternate between the maximizing and minimizing player.
    GameResultThe outcome of a game-tree search: the minimax value of the root and the number of leaves_evaluated to obtain it (the work done).

    Functions

    alpha_beta() ×2Alpha-beta pruning: minimax that carries a window [alpha,beta] of values still relevant and prunes a subtree as soon as it cannot affect the result (a max node whose value already exceeds beta, or a min node below alpha). It returns the identical value as minimax but can skip large parts of the tree; with good move ordering it roughly halves the effective depth, examining O(b^{d/2}) leaves instead of O(b^d).
    alpha_beta_branching_factor()Pearl's asymptotic branching factor of alpha-beta on random uniform trees, \(\xi_b/(1-\xi_b)\) where \(\xi_b\) is the positive root of \(x^b+x-1=0\).
    minimal_tree_leaves()Leaves in the Knuth-Moore minimal tree of a uniform tree: \(b^{\lceil d/2\rceil}+b^{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}-1\).
    minimax()Minimax: the value of a game position under optimal play. The maximizing player picks the child of greatest value, the minimizing player the child of least value, alternating down the tree; leaf values propagate up. Plain minimax evaluates every leaf.
    order_moves()Copy of root with every node's children sorted by their minimax values.
    random_game_tree()A complete game tree with branching children per internal node and independent Uniform(0,1) leaf values at depth depth (the model of Knuth-Moore and Pearl).

    Types and constants

    MoveOrderenum The order in which order_moves() arranges each node's children.

    datamunge/algorithms/gauss_jordan.hpp

    Classes

    GaussJordanEventOwned actual accepted/rejected pivot, normalization or completed other-row update. kind is pivot/reject/normalize/eliminate. column is the current zero-based pivot column; row is selected pivot row before swapping, normalized pivot row or updated row. value is selected pivot, normalization divisor or raw f. A pivot event follows all row swaps; reject precedes any rejected swap. transform starts as I and undergoes exactly the same row operations as matrix and rhs: it is a partial row transformation, not yet an inverse certificate. Every full matrix/RHS/permutation snapshot is independently owned.
    GaussJordanRunOwned final reduction state and legacy result from a single checked execution. result.inverse and result.x exist only on success; no duplicate final inverse is stored. reduced/rhs are the actual final coefficient/RHS state on success or cutoff failure. Partial transformation matrices on failure are available through trace events, not result.inverse. accepted_pivots is n on success or the rejected zero-based column. row_order records cumulative row interchanges (row combinations mean rows no longer equal the original equations). max_clear_factor is the largest raw f used against a normalized pivot row; it is not the Gaussian pre-normalization ratio and need not be at most1. Empty valid input succeeds with empty outputs. No accuracy/rank certificate.
    GaussJordanTraceOwned original system, actual-time events and final run, without replay. captured_entries counts input matrix row records/cells and RHS plus one metadata record and all matrix row records/cells/RHS/permutation per event. Ordinary final outputs, root/work metadata, working storage and allocator bytes are excluded. Entries are not bytes or peak RAM. Successful full histories attain their admission bound; early rejection may retain much less. O(n^4) worst-case history/copy cost versus O(n³) ordinary arithmetic/O(n²) storage.
    GaussJordanWorkActual full-block Gauss–Jordan work, excluding validation, allocation and snapshots. A block update counts one stored multiply-subtract, not one floating operation. Zero factors and already-processed columns are still updated, preserving the legacy recurrence. Identity zero-fill is allocation; diagonal writes count.
    InverseResidualSummaryOwned unsnapped products and infinity-norm residuals of a supplied inverse candidate. left_product=A*V and right_product=V*A use checked long-double arithmetic; each error norm is max_i sum_j |product_ij-I_ij|. a_inf/candidate_inf are max absolute row sums. norm_product is their product, not a certified condition number unless V is the true inverse. Even small residuals are computed evidence, not interval certificates of accuracy. Empty products/norms are0.

    Functions

    gauss_jordan_solve()Checked full [A|I|b] reduction with earliest-tie partial pivoting. Validates ALL finite square A, matching finite b and positive finite cutoff before input copies or inverse/state allocation. Preserves legacy ordered double divisions and full-column updates of both blocks, even for zero factors. Rejects strictly below the absolute cutoff; equality is accepted. Failure is not a rank certificate or a distinction between inconsistent, underdetermined and ill-scaled nonsingular systems. Empty succeeds. Stored assignments are checked for nonfinite arithmetic; rounding/underflow and inaccurate inverses remain possible. O(n³) time/O(n²) owned storage, no caller mutation/shared state. Computing the inverse has explicit arithmetic cost.
    gauss_jordan_trace()Capture actual full reduction after whole admission and complete validation. Full input/control validation precedes admission, which precedes input copies and inverse/state allocation. Zero max_entries disables only the optional cap; arithmetic/container/work-counter checks remain. Uses the same kernel as ordinary/legacy calls, without replay, truncation or partial returned traces. Failed pivots produce a normal reject event and an empty legacy inverse; their event transform is a partial row transformation. Successful history reaches its conservative bound, unlike early-rejected runs. O(n^4) history and copying in the worst case. No caller mutation or shared state.
    gauss_jordan_trace_entries()Conservative whole-trace entry bound for a virtual n-by-n reduction. Returns n²+2n+(n²+n)*(1+2n²+4n), including matrix row records. Zero gives0. Successful histories attain this count; no early-stop discount is given to rejected pivots. Checks arithmetic/container/work-counter capacities without allocation. Ordinary output/root/work metadata, working state and allocator bytes are excluded; entries are not bytes or peak RAM.
    inverse_residual_summary()Independently multiply and assess both sides of a supplied inverse candidate. Validates both complete finite square matrices and equal order before quota or allocation. Computes products and residual norms without solving, snapping small entries or assuming V is an inverse. O(n³) time/O(n²) owned output. Optional cap counts 2n+2n² product row records/cells; zero disables only the optional cap. Checked container/count arithmetic remains. No caller mutation. This is a numerical diagnostic, not a rigorous rank/conditioning certificate.

    datamunge/algorithms/gauss_legendre_pi.hpp

    Classes

    GaussLegendreRunOwned fixed-count analysis result and actual initial/final states. Executes exactly iterations stages, without replay or early stopping. Flags record first equality of successive computed estimates and of (a,b,t), not exact convergence or correct rounding; p is deliberately excluded from that mean-state comparison. a and b can stall one ULP apart. Final unused p may be infinite at the maximum iteration, while the estimate remains finite. O(iterations) work/O(1) result storage; no shared mutable state.
    GaussLegendreStateActual arithmetic-geometric means, correction accumulator and doubling weight. Default values are inert storage, not the initialized pi system. Produced states start at a1,b1/sqrt2,t1/4,p1. At the maximal supported iteration the final unused p overflows to infinity; no subsequent stage may use it.
    GaussLegendreStepOwned actual stage, including the used correction and before/after states. correction is the actual left-associated (p*delta)*delta used in t-=correction; it need not equal the subsequently rounded difference t_before-t_after. estimate_changed compares rounded estimates; mean_state_changed compares actual a,b,t, excluding p. Neither flag certifies mathematical accuracy.
    GaussLegendreTraceOwned actual fixed-count history and final run, admitted as complete records. captured_records counts one initial-state record plus each fixed-schema stage record, not scalar entries or bytes. Ordinary final output, root/work metadata, working state and allocator bytes are excluded; this is not a peak RAM limit. All state copies are independent. O(N) history/copy cost, no numerical replay.
    GaussLegendreWorkActual arithmetic counts, excluding diagnostics, allocation and snapshots. Initial sqrt is included in square_roots. Each stage executes both means, left-associated p*delta*delta subtraction and p*=2. Legacy scalar calls evaluate only the final estimate; run/trace evaluate the initial estimate and every stage to observe changes. One estimate is one quotient expression, not one floating operation. No early stop is triggered by stagnation.
    PiReferenceAccuracyComputed comparison with rounded double and long-double pi references. These are reference differences, not certified errors against mathematical pi. rounded_ulp_offset uses spacing at the double reference, not a bit-distance metric for distant candidates. Wider precision is platform-dependent. Log fields have zero placeholders when the corresponding difference is zero, with explicit has-log flags. -log10(error) is an accuracy measure, not a certified count of correct decimal digits. No shared state or allocation.

    Functions

    gauss_legendre_pi_limit()Largest fixed stage count whose doubling weight is never used after overflow. This model requires radix-two double at build time. The limit is its maximum exponent (1024 for binary64). The last unused p*=2 can overflow, but every used weight and mean/correction/estimate remains finite in this model.
    gauss_legendre_pi_run()Execute exactly N ordered double AGM stages and inspect actual changes. Initialized at (1,1/sqrt2,1/4,1); preserves original expression order, including left-associated p*delta*delta, rather than widening or using pow. No early stop or a==b forcing. Initial and per-stage estimates are computed to measure stagnation, unlike the legacy scalar API's single final estimate. Negative or excessive counts are rejected before work. Zero gives the initialized estimate. The final unused p can overflow at the format limit; a future use is forbidden. An unchanged estimate is not correctly rounded pi or an error certificate.
    gauss_legendre_pi_trace()Capture actual AGM stages after complete count validation and whole admission. Admission precedes initialization and history allocation. Zero max_records disables only the optional cap; count-domain/container checks remain. Units are one complete initial record plus N fixed-schema stage records, not scalar entries/bytes or peak RAM. No replay, truncation, partial output or mutation. The final unused p overflow at the maximum count is retained transparently; it is never used by another stage. Executes all requested admitted stages.
    gauss_legendre_pi_trace_records()Whole-history record admission for a checked fixed stage count. Counts one initial-state record plus N fixed-schema stage records; zero stages still require one record. No early-stop discount, scalar-entry or byte claim. Checks the complete count domain and vector capacity without allocating.
    pi_reference_accuracy()Compare any finite candidate with both rounded pi references, without clipping errors. Retains the original double reference subtraction and separately computes a checked widened difference and local-reference ULP offset. No solver is called. Zero differences get explicit unavailable-log flags, not a fabricated floor. A wider reference can itself round and may add no bits on some platforms.

    datamunge/algorithms/gauss_newton.hpp

    Classes

    GaussNewtonIterationOne evaluated parameter state, including its proposed next step. The initial state is iteration zero. step_norm is the norm of the incoming completed update (zero initially), while next_step_norm and linearized_sse describe the proposed outgoing update. Diagnostics are calculated at these params, not the preceding state.
    GaussNewtonLinearizationOne local residual/Jacobian least-squares problem and its undamped step. All values are owned. J is observations by parameters, r=model-y, and step minimizes ||r+J*step||_2. Columns are scaled to unit norm internally, then the solution is restored to parameter units; no normal equations, regularization or bounds are used. A numerically rank-deficient Jacobian is rejected, not assigned an arbitrary solution.
    GaussNewtonResultOwned full-step Gauss-Newton fit and its evaluated parameter trajectory. The original params/iterations/sse fields remain first for aggregate compatibility. iterations counts completed updates, including on budget exhaustion. sse and residuals always describe the returned params. step_tolerance_met only certifies that the next proposed step has norm <= tol: it does not prove stationarity, a minimum, global optimality or parameter identification. Check the gradient and model assumptions too. No early rejection or line search hides an increase in the objective.

    Functions

    gauss_newton() ×2Fits unweighted nonlinear least squares with analytic derivatives and full QR steps. Solves min_delta ||r+J*delta|| without forming normal equations, updates params by the entire step, and reevaluates residuals/Jacobian. Stops when the proposed next step has Euclidean norm <= tol or max_iter updates are complete. This absolute parameter-unit test is not invariant to reparameterization and is not a minimum certificate. Objective increases are allowed; no globalization, constraints or automatic scaling of the stopping rule is applied. Column scaling only stabilizes the local linear solve. history includes the initial and every completed state. Inputs remain unchanged; callback state/thread safety belongs to the caller.
    gauss_newton_linearize() ×2Linearizes model-minus-y residuals with a caller-supplied analytic Jacobian. Computes residuals, full-rank scaled-QR step, current SSE, infinity norm of J^T*r, and predicted linearized SSE. Model and derivative see identical params and x. Inputs remain unchanged; callbacks must be deterministic for fixed inputs. Callback state/thread safety is the caller's responsibility.

    gauss_seidel_history()Execute the shared Gauss-Seidel kernel while capturing its actual states. Same arithmetic, validation and stopping as gauss_seidel_solve; no replay. Checks the complete worst-case entry bound and vector capacities before initialization or history allocation. A positive cap admits the full requested budget even when the RHS would converge initially; zero disables only the optional quota. No truncation, partial returned trace, or caller mutation. Existing gauss_seidel_trace keeps its separate online residual-entry policy.
    gauss_seidel_history_entries()Count a complete worst-case Gauss-Seidel history before execution. No early success discount for a nonempty system, no allocation or work is performed.
    gauss_seidel_solve()Execute checked forward in-place Gauss-Seidel with actual work counts. Validates all inputs before initial convergence. Uses the legacy zero start, ordered widened sums, checked double assignments and recomputed residual from rounded dense A x. Stops when residual<=tol or max_iter sweeps complete. Nonzero diagonal is required; no dominance, symmetry or convergence claim is inferred. Empty and zero RHS converge initially. No input mutation or shared state. Dense O(kn²) work/O(n) extra space; zeros are still visited.

    datamunge/algorithms/gaussian_elimination.hpp

    Classes

    GaussianEliminationEventOne actual accepted/rejected pivot, completed elimination or back-substitution step. kind is pivot, reject, eliminate or back. column is zero-based; row is selected current pivot row (before swapping), eliminated row or solved coordinate. value is selected pivot, actual factor or assigned solution coordinate. matrix/rhs/row_order are post-event owned copies, except reject precedes any rejected swap. x is empty before back substitution and a full n-vector after each back step; unsolved earlier coordinates are zero placeholders.
    GaussianEliminationRunOwned ordinary solve output, actual upper state, row order and element-growth evidence. solution preserves the legacy LinearSolution layout. A rejected pivot leaves solution.x empty and accepted_pivots identifies its zero-based column. This is a computed cutoff failure, not a rank/conditioning certificate. upper/rhs are actual stored doubles, including cancellation residues; row_order[i] is the original row now at i. They remain available on rejection. Successful empty input has accepted_pivots0 and solved=true. max_coefficient includes the input and every stored coefficient assignment; RHS is excluded. growth is max_coefficient/initial_max, or the placeholder1 for all-zero/empty A. The scalar double recurrence is not widened; finite stored assignments are checked, while rounding and underflow remain possible. No shared state.
    GaussianEliminationTraceOwned inputs, actual elimination history and ordinary run from one shared execution. Inputs and all event vectors are independent of caller and other snapshots. captured_entries counts input rows/cells/RHS, plus each event's one metadata record and matrix rows/cells/RHS/x/row_order. Ordinary final outputs, root/work metadata, working storage and allocator bytes are excluded. Entries are not bytes or peak RAM. Worst-case history costs O(n^4), ordinary work O(n^3).
    GaussianEliminationWorkActual arithmetic work in one partial-pivot solve, excluding validation and copies. Counts record executed comparisons, nontrivial swaps and stored updates, even on a pivot rejection. A coefficient update is one multiply-subtract, not one floating operation. Checks, allocation, diagnostics and history are excluded.
    GaussianResidualSummaryWidened infinity-norm residual and normwise backward error for a supplied candidate. These describe the candidate, not solver success, conditioning or forward accuracy. residual is b-Ax in long double. backward_error is its infinity norm divided by matrix_inf*x_inf+b_inf, with0/0defined0; empty givesallzeros. Units differ from linalg::backward_error(), which uses Frobenius/2-norms.
    GaussianSystemOriginal report's fixed finite coefficient matrix and RHS, returned by value. Deterministic owned rows and RHS; exact mathematical solution(2,3,-1). Floating arithmetic yields an approximation. No RNG or external dataset.

    Functions

    gaussian_elimination_example()Return the original three-equation report fixture without solving it. Owned copies; exact mathematical solution(2,3,-1), no random state.
    gaussian_elimination_growth_matrix()Wilkinson partial-pivot growth family with last column one and strict earliest ties. Diagonal and last column are1, strict lower triangle-1, other entries0. For n>0 and exact arithmetic, this solver's earliest-tie pivoting has no swaps, |multiplier|=1 and coefficient growth2^(n-1). This is not the symmetric eigenvalue Wilkinson matrix, nor a claim that every RHS has large error. O(n²) owned storage/time. Empty n0 returns empty. Checks n+n² row/cell entries and capacities before allocation; zero max_entries disables only optional cap.
    gaussian_elimination_solve()Checked scalar Gaussian elimination with absolute-cutoff partial pivoting. Validates ALL square row lengths, matching RHS, finite input and positive finite cutoff before input copies or state allocation. Uses earliest maximal absolute pivot ties and the legacy double recurrence/order. Rejects strictly below cutoff; equality is accepted. Failure does not distinguish inconsistent from underdetermined or ill-scaled nonsingular systems. No rank/conditioning certificate, relative scaling, iterative refinement or stored L factor. Empty square input succeeds. O(n³) work/O(n²) storage, no caller mutation.
    gaussian_elimination_trace()Capture actual partial-pivot elimination without replay, truncation or partial results. Full input/control validation precedes conservative quota admission, which precedes input copies and state allocation. Zero max_entries disables only the optional cap; count/container/counter checks remain. Uses the same kernel and recurrence as solve-only/legacy calls. Rejecting a small pivot is a normal run result and its actual rejection event is retained. A thrown quota/domain/ arithmetic/allocation exception returns no partial trace or caller mutation. O(n^4) worst-case history/time in addition to O(n³) arithmetic.
    gaussian_elimination_trace_entries()Conservative whole-history entry admission for a virtual n-by-n solve. With E=n(n-1)/2+2n, returns n²+2n+E*(1+n²+4n). Zero gives0. Counts owned input and worst-case event vectors including matrix row records; not bytes or peak RAM. Excludes ordinary output, work/root metadata, working state and allocator bytes. Rejects arithmetic/container/counter capacities even without allocation. No early-stop discount: a singular input can need fewer events than admitted.
    gaussian_residual_summary()Recompute widened residual and infinity-norm backward error independently of elimination. Validates full finite square A, matching b/x before any allocation. No caller mutation or solver invocation; O(n²) time/O(n) output. Long double arithmetic is checked for nonfinite results (it may have the same range as double). A small residual/backward error alone does not bound forward solution error.

    Types and constants

    GaussianMatrixtype Owned square coefficient rows for the checked direct solver. No implicit symmetry, scaling, sparsity or matrix-factorization metadata.

    datamunge/algorithms/general_problem_solver.hpp

    Classes

    PlanningActionOne grounded positive-precondition operator on a 64-bit fact state. Applicable when all require bits hold. Transition is (state & ~remove) | add; overlapping add/remove bits end present. No negative preconditions, variables, theorem prover or external action is executed. All 64 bits are valid, including bit 63. Names may be empty, duplicated or arbitrary byte strings; identity is position in the operator vector. Legacy field order and types are preserved.
    PlanningCertificateOwned finite certificate from independently executing operator indices. Validates the entire index vector before any transition. If a precondition fails, stops before that action: applicable=false, applied is its zero-based failing position, states retains the valid prefix including initial. A goal miss after a fully applicable sequence is reported by reaches_goals=false. Empty sequences are applicable; goals may already hold. O(p) transition work and O(p) owned states for p indices; no search, shortest-path or budget claim.
    PlanningEventOne actual fixed-schema search event; state masks are constant-width values. state/depth identify the current frame. apply has the actual successor in next_state; other kinds use next_state=state. action_index is meaningful for test/apply/backtrack/finish, otherwise size_t maximum. applicable is meaningful only for test. repeat/reopen expose the previous expansion depth and set has_previous_depth; other events leave it false. No vector/path is replayed.
    PlanningResultOwned legacy planning outcome with operator names in application order. Success contains an executable plan no longer than the requested budget, not necessarily shortest. Initially satisfied goals give an empty successful plan and final_state=initial. Failure has empty actions/final_state0/found=false; its final_state is a placeholder, not a reached failure witness. Names alone can be ambiguous; PlanningRun also retains operator indices. Stable layout.
    PlanningRunOwned ordinary planning result, unambiguous operator indices and actual work. action_indices and result.actions describe the same successful sequence; both are empty on failure. No replay or history is performed by this result. Indices refer to the caller's original operator order; no shared state or caller mutation. DFS frame storage is on the heap, not the C++ call stack.
    PlanningTraceOwned inputs, ordinary result and ordered actual search events from one execution. Every event is one fixed-schema record, not one numeric entry or byte. The online event quota excludes owned input operators/names, root and work metadata, final ordinary output, working stack/map and allocator storage; it is not a peak RAM limit. No partial or truncated trace is returned when a quota is exceeded. Inputs, labels and snapshots are independent owned copies.
    PlanningWorkActual node, operator and pruning work from one ordered forward DFS. Visits include root, goal, depth-cutoff and repeated-state entries. Expanded states pass all three terminal/pruning checks and can be expanded again after a shallower arrival. Goal/depth checks precede the best-depth map. Counters exclude copies, allocation, hashing internals and trace capture; not timings.

    Functions

    check_planning_plan()Independently execute a selected operator-index sequence without searching. Full index validation and complete p+1 state capacity/quota checks precede transitions/allocation, even if an early precondition would fail. Positive preconditions/add-wins semantics match the planner, but this is an independent checker. Captures every successful prefix; no caller mutation or shared state. This does not validate a claimed found flag or prove shortestness/budget; inspect applicable/reaches_goals/final_state/length for those comparisons.
    general_problem_solver()Find a bounded positive-fact plan using ordered DFS with shallower-state reopening. Preserves legacy signature/default 32/layouts, operator order, add-wins effects, initial-goal success and failure placeholders. Corrects old depth-insensitive visited-state false negatives. Goal testing precedes the depth limit; states are pruned only if expanded at equal/smaller depth. Returns the first DFS plan, not necessarily shortest; it is complete within max_steps for this finite grounded model if execution returns normally. Heap frames remove recursive call-stack depth limits. Names may be empty or duplicated; all 64 bits valid. No external action, negative preconditions, theorem prover or GPS means-ends heuristic. Expected O(m*S*min(K+1,S)) checks for m operators, S reachable states and budget K, O(S+min(K,S)) working records plus output/name bytes; hashing is expected constant time. No allocation for an entire theoretical 2^64 space.
    general_problem_solver_run()Execute the same bounded planner while returning actual work and operator indices. Same search, effects, order, correctness and complexity as general_problem_solver. No trace capture or hidden plan replay. Safe with arbitrary operator labels; inputs are never changed and no global state is used.
    general_problem_solver_trace()Capture primitive events directly from the same executing forward planner. Online capture checks each next actual record before retaining it; it does not reserve an exponential worst-case tree or discount/truncate future events. The ordinary search/arithmetic is unchanged. Root/input/final/working storage exclusions are specified in PlanningTrace; the quota is not bytes or peakRAM. Initially successful and zero-budget searches still produce actual events. O(E) extra event storage for E captured records, in addition to ordinary search state and owned input/name bytes. No partial return, replay or caller mutation.
    planning_binary_counter()Construct low-bit-first carry operators for a finite binary-counter planning family. Operator k requires every lower bit, clears those lower bits and sets bit k. No negative preconditions: operations with bit k already set may move backward; best-depth pruning handles those cycles. From zero to bit(bits-1), this input ordering has a successful DFS plan of 2^(bits-1) applications when admitted by the step budget; no shortestness claim is made for arbitrary domains. This family allocates only bits operators; executing it can be exponential.
    planning_event_name()Return the stable lower-case label for a primitive planning event. No global state or input mutation. O(1) fixed-length output.

    Types and constants

    PlanningEventKindenum Primitive event kinds recorded at the actual search control-flow points. test precedes apply; visit precedes goal/cutoff/repeat/reopen. finish follows successful recursive-return-equivalent propagation, while backtrack follows a failed child. exhausted means all operators of that frame were tested.

    datamunge/algorithms/generational.hpp

    Classes

    GenerationalEventOne primitive collector event with actual object, decision and stack size. kind is root/old_field/remember/seed/mark/visit/young_field/promote/free or full_root/full_mark/full_visit/full_field. object is source/current id; target is the referenced id or the same id, except remember uses -1. accepted records young membership for root/old_field, a newly marked candidate for seed/young_field/full_root/full_field, false for free, true otherwise. stack_size is actual current size (after mark-push or visit-pop); discovery and classification events use zero. No per-event vector or path is replayed.
    GenerationalHeapOwned fixed-age graph with an exact maintained set of old-to-young reference slots. Construction validates once and indexes young ids and every boundary slot. Only checked existing-field replacement is permitted; ages, roots, object ids and field counts stay fixed. set_reference maintains the slot invariant as a modeled write barrier. It is not a concurrent/runtime collector: collect only proposes retention/reclamation, with no age changes, copying or deallocation. Copies own all data. Concurrent collect calls are safe absent concurrent writes.
    GenerationalInputOwned graph and binary ages for a generated generational example. Sizes are absent and references use dense slots; no real memory is allocated for modeled objects. Vectors are independent of later calls.
    GenerationalResultOwned legacy minor-analysis flags, candidates and full-trace comparison. promoted[i] names a retained young object proposed for promotion; young_freed names unretained young objects. No real objects, ages or references are changed. All old objects conservatively supply boundary references, including unreachable old garbage, so promoted need not imply full-root reachability. Counts are object visits, not total collector work. Legacy field order/types are stable.
    GenerationalRunOwned legacy result, actual full marks and work from one executing analysis. Full marks distinguish true root reachability from conservative minor retention. Same values as minor_gc; includes boundary discovery and a full comparison, O(N+E+R) work/storage bounds, with no caller mutation or hidden replay.
    GenerationalTraceOwned input graph/ages, ordinary run and chronological actual collector events. The online quota counts complete event records, not numeric entries or bytes. Owned input/name vectors, root/work/final output, working tables/stacks and allocator storage are excluded; it is not a peak RAM limit. Invalid inputs are rejected before copies/capture. No partial/truncated trace is returned.
    GenerationalWorkActual selected validation, discovery, tracing and output-loop work. Counts include stored duplicate fields/roots. They are visits, not timings or a complete instruction count; allocation, container internals, copies and trace capture are excluded. Full-comparison fields are zero for young-only collection. preparation_work() records construction only, not later writes.
    YoungCollectionSparse young-only outcome from a validated maintained heap model. survivors/freed partition its fixed young ids in ascending order. These are candidates only: collect() does not promote, deallocate or change the graph. No full traversal, dense old-object output or global age scan is performed. Work/storage per call is O(Y+R+W+E_y), for Y young objects, R root slots, W remembered old-to-young slots and E_y fields of retained young objects.

    Functions

    generational_chain_example()Build an old chain with a direct young root, an old-to-young boundary and garbage. Old ids 0..old_count-1 form a rooted chain; its last source points to young old_count+1. The second root is young old_count. Additional young ids are isolated/unrooted. old_count 4/unreachable_young 1 reproduces the original report. Complete object count is checked before allocation; O(N) construction/storage.
    minor_gc()Analyze the young generation and compute a separate full-root comparison. Validates complete graph shape/ids then exact binary ages before indexing. Rebuilds boundary roots from ALL old fields, including unreachable old sources; this conservatively retains every full-root-reachable young object, possibly more. Young roots precede old-source/field-order targets; all seeds are marked before ordered LIFO traversal. Duplicate fields/roots/cycles are allowed. Sizes are entirely ignored. No graph, generation or real object is changed. Discovery, dense outputs and full comparison make total work O(N+E+R), not merely proportional to young visits. O(N+E+R) worst-case auxiliary storage.
    minor_gc_run()Run the same checked collector with actual work and full-root marks. Same semantics, ordering, ownership and complexity as minor_gc; no replay. Every stored old field is visited for discovery and a separate full DFS runs.
    minor_gc_trace()Capture actual discovery, young traversal, classification and full-comparison events. Same execution as minor_gc_run. Complete validation precedes input copies and capture. Each next actual event is admitted online before append; zero quota disables only that optional cap, not capacity/counter checks. No replay, truncation, partial return or caller mutation. O(events) extra record storage plus owned input bytes and ordinary working/output storage.

    datamunge/algorithms/geohash.hpp

    Classes

    GeohashBitOne actual coordinate comparison and axis-endpoint update. bit_in_symbol is zero-based 0..4 before the group count increments. symbol_value is the actual accumulator after shifting in this bit. longitude=true selects the longitude interval. Exact equality to midpoint chooses upper. No input is borrowed and no event is reconstructed from a final key.
    GeohashBoundsOwned latitude/longitude bounds in degrees, initially the whole world rectangle. These are actual ordered double-bisection endpoints, not certified exact-real bounds at arbitrary precision. Long runs can stagnate or collapse an interval. Longitude is not normalized across the date line. No shared state or mutation.
    GeohashCellOwned decoded double cell bounds, unrounded center and actual angular spans. latitude_bits/longitude_bits count decoded bit positions, not significant coordinate bits. limited is true if any update stagnated or ended collapsed. Long keys may have degenerate/unchanged bounds; no physical-distance or exact real-cell certificate is implied. Center is (lo+hi)/2 without decimal rounding.
    GeohashEmissionOne actual base32 emission with endpoints at that control-flow point. Records the appended character before the executing kernel resets its group counter/accumulator. Owns its bounds; no prefix string is copied per record.
    GeohashResolutionIdeal dyadic angular resolution rounded to double, separate from actual endpoint arithmetic. Ideal widths use 360*2^-longitude_bits and 180*2^-latitude_bits. At high counts these rounded spans can underflow to zero; spans_positive reports both positive. This is neither a metric-distance estimate nor a guarantee the actual encoder endpoints retain that width beyond floating precision. No allocation or mutation.
    GeohashRunOwned encoded key, actual final bounds, work and first precision-limit flags. first_unchanged_bit/first_collapsed_bit are one-based actual bit indices, zero if absent. A repeated interval need not have zero width; these flags do not claim additional geographic accuracy, true convergence or unique ownership of a shared boundary. Ordinary result needs O(p) output bytes, O(1) other storage.
    GeohashTraceOwned initial-coordinate record, actual bit/emission records and final ordinary run. captured_records counts 1 initial fixed-schema coordinate/bounds record, one per GeohashBit and one per GeohashEmission. These are records, not numeric entries or bytes. Root/work/final ordinary output, working state and allocator storage are excluded; this is not a peak RAM limit. Vectors are independent.
    GeohashWorkActual bit and character operations from one ordered encoder execution. Counts include all requested steps even after interval stagnation. They are selected operations, not timings or total floating-operation counts. Allocation, copying, validation and trace capture are excluded.

    Functions

    geohash_common_prefix()Count the common leading characters of two fully validated geohash keys. Validates both complete alphabets before comparison, even if their first characters differ. Different lengths/empty strings are safe. Prefix agreement identifies nested angular cells; proximity does not imply prefix agreement. O(a.size()+b.size()) work, O(1) extra storage, no mutation or copies.
    geohash_decode()Decode a strict lowercase geohash by consuming longitude-first symbol bits. Validates the entire alphabet before arithmetic. Empty denotes world bounds, center(0,0) and zero consumed bits. Does not lowercase or decimal-round the center; any uppercase, embedded NUL or non-alphabet byte is invalid. O(p) work, O(1) owned result/working storage. High counts expose limited endpoint precision; center re-encoding need not round-trip a degenerate high-precision key.
    geohash_encode()Encode a finite latitude/longitude pair using the legacy ordered double bisections. Starts with longitude, takes upper on equality and appends the alphabet 0123456789bcdefghjkmnpqrstuvwxyz after every five bits. Coordinates include poles/end-meridians; +180 and -180 are not normalized to one key. Finite valid negative precision retains legacy zero-character compatibility, including INT_MIN; zero yields empty. Coordinates are validated even for zero/negative precision. No arbitrary positive precision cap or early stop is imposed; high-count intervals can stagnate/collapse while output continues. O(p) time and owned output bytes, O(1) additional working state; no caller/global mutation.
    geohash_encode_run()Execute the same encoder while returning actual bounds, counts and precision-limit flags. Same arithmetic/output as geohash_encode for nonnegative precision. Checked analysis rejects negative counts rather than applying the legacy clamp. No trace allocation or numerical replay, no early stop after stagnation.
    geohash_encode_trace()Capture actual encoder bisections and character emissions from the shared kernel. Validates coordinates/count before quota. Checks the whole 1+6p record bound, bit/emission vector capacities and positive quota before initialization/history allocation. Zero disables only optional quota; no early-stagnation discount, truncation, partial returned trace, numerical replay or caller mutation.
    geohash_resolution()Return ideal angular bit counts and dyadic spans without running the encoder. Longitude consumes ceil(5p/2) bits, latitude floor(5p/2). Each added character divides angular area by 32; individual axes alternate factors 4 and 8. Spans rounded to double may underflow to zero, exposed by spans_positive. O(1) work.
    geohash_trace_records()Count complete initial, bit and emission records without executing or allocating. Bound and actual count are 1+6p, including the initial coordinate/bounds record even when p=0. Does not include final ordinary run/work or working storage.

    Classes

    AdjacentSortInputsFour owned controlled inputs for integer adjacent-exchange sort experiments. All arrays contain 0 through n-1. ascending has no inversions; descending has n(n-1)/2; adjacent_inversion exchanges the middle adjacent pair when n>=2; last_minimum moves zero from first to last, giving n-1 inversions for n>=1. Empty/singleton arrays coincide. The whole generator retains exactly 4n integer entries, with no input aliases or shared state; copies own their vectors.
    GnomeSortEventOne owned fixed-size record from the executing pointer loop. Step ordinal is zero-based among loop bodies. Pair values and original ids describe the pair BEFORE the comparison/exchange, only when compared is true. Boundary visits have compared/swapped false and unused pair fields zero. Initial/stop metadata have unused ordinal/pair/flag fields zero. Metadata pointer fields are both zero for initial and both n for stop. Copies retain no references; unused fields are placeholders, not input observations.
    GnomeSortRunOwned sorted values, identities carried by the actual swaps and selected work. Original indices are zero-based positions in the supplied input. Equal keys retain increasing original indices, including repeated signed extremes. The identity output and its initialization cost O(n); sorting has constant other working state. Copies own both vectors and share no mutable state or aliases.
    GnomeSortTraceOwned ordinary result and every online fixed-size state record. No full array snapshots are retained per visit: history storage is O(H) complete records, in addition to O(n) owned values/identities. Inputs, root, ordinary output/identities, constant working state and allocator overhead are outside the record quota. It is not a numeric-entry, byte or peak RAM limit. No replay, truncation or partial trace is returned on quota failure. Copies own all storage; independent calls share no mutable state.
    GnomeSortWorkSelected actual operations of an executing gnome sort, initially zero. Counts exclude input copying, identity initialization, allocations, loop tests, FLOPs and wall time. A boundary visit at index zero advances without a key comparison. Every strict adjacent swap moves the pointer backwards once. Diagnostic counters are checked before increment and own no references.

    Functions

    adjacent_sort_inputs()Generate four owned adjacent-sort families with a checked whole output count. Validate n-1 fits int, 4n fits size_t and every vector capacity BEFORE allocation. The optional quota counts ALL four arrays together, default one million integer values; zero disables it. Root/vector objects and allocator overhead are not counted: this is not bytes or peak RAM. No partial result or shared mutation. O(n) time and 4n output values. Assignments avoid a final overflowing int increment.
    gnome_sort()Return a stable nondecreasing integer copy using the original one-pointer gnome loop. Start at index zero. A boundary visit or left<=right comparison advances; otherwise exchange the adjacent strict inversion and step backwards. Equal values never exchange. Empty input has no visits; a singleton has one boundary visit and no key comparisons. Signed extremes need no arithmetic on keys. For n values with I strict inversions, exactly n+2I loop visits occur: O(n+I) time, O(n) best and O(n^2) worst. The supplied owned buffer is sorted in place, with O(1) auxiliary state, but passing an lvalue makes an O(n) owned copy. Scalar output does not allocate identity/history vectors or update diagnostic counters. No caller lvalue mutation, retained aliases or shared mutable state.
    gnome_sort_run()Execute the shared gnome loop with actual stable identities and checked work. Semantics and pointer steps are those of gnome_sort(). Identities are created once and exchanged alongside actual values. They are output, not per-step snapshots. O(n+I) time and O(n) owned identity output/initialization, with O(1) other working state beyond the owned input/output buffers. No history quota, caller lvalue mutation, retained aliases or shared mutable state.
    gnome_sort_trace()Capture every actual gnome-loop visit and metadata online with a whole-record quota. Uses the same execution as gnome_sort_run(), not a second sorting loop or numerical replay. Before EACH complete append the optional max_records and container capacity are checked, including initial/stop metadata. Default one million complete records; zero turns off only that optional quota. Empty input needs two records (reject1/admit2); [2,1] needs six (reject5/admit6). No ordinary output is returned if a final metadata append exceeds the cap after sorting. No truncation, partial return or caller lvalue mutation. O(n+I+H) time and O(H) additional fixed-size records beyond owned value/identity output. Record count excludes inputs/root/ordinary outputs/working state/allocator; not scalar entries, bytes or peak RAM. Independent calls have no shared mutable state.

    Types and constants

    GnomeSortEventKindenum Metadata or an actual loop visit captured without replaying the sort. Initial and stop records count towards the same complete-record quota as step records, even for empty input. A trace with S loop visits has S+2 records if it completes; that expression is mathematical and is not precomputed.

    datamunge/algorithms/goertzel.hpp

    Classes

    DtmfPeaksOwned eight-frequency results and first-maximum keypad candidate, not a validated detection. In results from dtmf_peaks(), the first four targets are rows697/770/852/941Hz, then columns1209/1336/1477/1633Hz. Default construction leaves the target array zero-filled; dtmf_peaks() fills the grid and all responses. row/column index their own four-element groups. Equal powers retain the first index. Empty input and silence choose candidate '1' by ties. No energy, duration, frequency tolerance, level ratio, speech or noise validation is performed. Finite negative raw powers remain visible. All fixed-size results own scalars; no input aliases or mutable shared state survive.
    GoertzelEventOne owned fixed-size actual recurrence record, without numerical replay. For sample records index is zero based, input is x[index], before_s1/s2 are the actual prior states and value is the evaluated s0. State assignments then make s1=value and s2=before_s1. For stop, index=N, before fields are final states and value is raw power. For initial index/before/input are zero and value is the actual coefficient, or zero for empty input. Metadata input is unused zero.
    GoertzelRunOwned actual selection, terminal states and unnormalized raw squared-magnitude estimate. For bin_indexed calls bin holds the supplied size_t index, never reduced mod N; frequency_mode/selected_bin are then unused placeholders. For legacy frequency calls selected_bin is the actual signed int; for unrounded calls it is unused zero. Empty input has has_coefficient=false, zero omega/coefficient/states/power and zero updates; no frequency grid is evaluated. The supplied bin is still retained for empty bin-indexed calls. All unused fields are placeholders. power is not normalized by sample count, a PSD, calibrated watts or mean-square signal power. Cancellation can produce a FINITE NEGATIVE value, retained without clamping. Very long blocks, large unreduced angles and cancellation can lose accuracy even when all states are finite. Copies own every scalar.
    GoertzelTraceOwned ordinary result plus all fixed-size records captured online. Complete initial/sample/stop records are charged, not numeric entries, bytes or peak RAM. Input, root, ordinary result/selection metadata, constant working states and allocator overhead are excluded. No input aliases, replay, truncation or partial return survive. Copies own their history vectors.
    SinusoidOne finite sinusoid descriptor in Hz, sample-amplitude units and radians. Descriptors do not validate construction; sinusoid_signal() checks all fields. Negative amplitudes/frequencies and arbitrary finite phases are allowed. Copies own scalars and share no mutable state.

    Functions

    dtmf_peaks()Compute eight native Goertzel responses and return the first row/column power maxima. The fixed Q.23 grid and key mapping are shared with dtmf_signal(). Each response uses goertzel_run() in the requested mode. No receiver validation is added; empty/silent input gives candidate '1'. Complete finite sample/rate/mode checks precede evaluation. O(8N) work, including repeated validation, O(1) auxiliary storage and fixed-size owned output; input is neither modified nor referenced after return. No history is retained. Aggregate update counts are checked.
    dtmf_signal()Generate a unit-amplitude zero-phase DTMF row-plus-column illustration. Uses the Q.23 frequency grid for keys123A/456B/789C/*0#D. It is a synthetic finite block, not a telephone transmitter conformance claim. The key and rate are checked before whole output admission, including zero samples. Ordered two-sinusoid generation and sample/range/ownership costs are those of sinusoid_signal(). O(n) time and output, no shared mutable state.
    goertzel_bin_run()Execute the shared unsigned-bin kernel with owned actual metadata/states. Uses the unreduced-bin semantics and numerical limitations of goertzel_power_bin(). No history or optional input-size cap. O(N) validation/recurrence, O(1) working state, no caller mutation/retained aliases/shared mutable state.
    goertzel_bin_trace()Capture every actual unsigned-bin recurrence state with the same online quota. Raw signal processing semantics are those of goertzel_bin_run(). History, validation-before-quota, metadata count, failure, ownership and memory exclusions are those of goertzel_trace(). Empty retains two records, with no coefficient evaluation. O(N+H) time/O(H) extra fixed-size history; no replay.
    goertzel_power()Return the original ordered raw Goertzel power after historical frequency-to-bin selection. Nonempty input selects k=trunc(0.5+double(N)*target_freq/sample_rate), then uses omega=2*pi*k/N. This is NOT the response at the exact requested frequency. Negative-frequency selection is biased by offset-then-truncation; the old rule is retained. Bin conversion is checked after truncation, including fractional values just outside int bounds whose truncated integer still fits. No Nyquist range restriction or automatic modulo reduction is imposed. All samples and finite positive rate/finite target are validated BEFORE empty input handling. Empty returns zero without selecting a bin/coefficient. The shared recurrence keeps the original x+c*s1-s2 and terminal s1*s1+s2*s2-c*s1*s2 expressions. Evaluated nonfinite selection/state/output is rejected; finite underflow/cancellation and NEGATIVE raw power remain possible. Input is borrowed without mutation or retained aliases. O(N) validation plus O(N) recurrence, O(1) auxiliary state; no shared mutable state.
    goertzel_power_at_frequency()Return raw power at the supplied frequency without integer-bin quantization. Uses omega=2*pi*target_freq/sample_rate and the same ordered real recurrence. This means direct frequency selection, NOT exact floating arithmetic. No modulo-angle reduction is added. Full finite sample/parameter validation precedes empty zero. Raw negative/cancellation/range limitations, constant auxiliary state, O(N) time, borrowing and thread safety match goertzel_power().
    goertzel_power_bin()Return raw Goertzel power at the supplied unsigned DFT bin using its original unreduced angle. All size_t indices are accepted, including k>=N. The actual angle is computed as 2*pi*double(k)/double(N), WITHOUT k modulo N. Large indices can lose integer bits and angle accuracy; ideal DFT alias periodicity is not a bitwise numerical guarantee. Finite sample validation precedes empty return zero. Recurrence, raw negative-power limitations, O(N) time/O(1) auxiliary space, borrowing and independent-call safety are those of goertzel_power().
    goertzel_run()Execute the shared frequency-selected kernel and own its actual metadata/states. Selection and numeric contracts are those of goertzel_power() for legacy_bin, or goertzel_power_at_frequency() for unrounded. All parameters/samples are validated before empty handling; an unknown mode is rejected. No history or optional sample cap. sample_updates counts actual recurrence updates only, excluding validation, trig, selection, allocation, timing and hardware FLOPs. O(N) time, O(1) auxiliary state and owned scalar result; input is unchanged.
    goertzel_trace()Capture a complete actual frequency-selected recurrence online, without replay. Before EACH complete append, max_records and vector capacity are checked. Default one million records, zero disables only the optional quota. Initial and stop metadata count: N4 needs6 (reject5/admit6), empty needs2 (reject1/admit2). Full sample/parameter validation precedes selection and history admission. No partial history, truncation, input mutation or ordinary result on failure. O(N+H) time and O(H) extra complete records, excluding input/root/ordinary metadata and result/constant working states/allocator overhead. Not numeric entries, bytes or peak RAM. Records are from this same execution.
    sinusoid_signal()Generate an owned sum of sinusoids in descriptor order with whole output admission. Sample n sums amplitude*sin(2*pi*frequency_hz*double(n)/sample_rate+phase). All descriptors and the rate are checked before output quota/capacity/allocation, including empty output. Optional max_samples counts the WHOLE output samples, default one million; zero disables it. Computed phases and accumulated sample values are checked before retention. Empty descriptors produce zeros. Frequencies are not Nyquist-clipped or reduced. O(n*terms.size()) time plus O(n) output initialization, O(n) owned output. Inputs/root/allocator/unused capacity are not quota units; it is not bytes or peak RAM. No input mutation/retained aliases.

    Types and constants

    GoertzelEventKindenum Emission point in an online actual Goertzel execution. Initial and stop records count even for empty input; a completed N-sample history therefore contains N+2 complete records, not just N sample rows.
    GoertzelFrequencyModeenum Select the historical offset-truncated bin or evaluate the supplied frequency directly. legacy_bin uses trunc(0.5+double(N)*f/fs), with an int representability check. For nonnegative ordinary requests this chooses the nearest bin with upward half ties; negative requests are asymmetric. unrounded uses omega=2*pi*f/fs without integer quantization. Neither mode guarantees exact floating accuracy.
