    datamunge/algorithms/goldschmidt_division.hpp

    Classes

    GoldschmidtRunOwned scalar output, normalization states and selected loop-operation counts. No callbacks, input references or histories are retained. The ordinary double-returning API uses the same kernel with no record allocation.
    GoldschmidtStateActual normalized numerator and denominator, not a mathematical quotient certificate. Owns two doubles; a scaled numerator may underflow to zero or overflow to infinity.
    GoldschmidtStepOne complete actual before/factor/after update captured during execution. All values own primitive storage. The same rounded factor feeds both products.
    GoldschmidtTraceOwned run plus one whole record per actual update, without replay. Initial normalization lives in run.initial and is not a history record. Copying duplicates the vector. Ordinary state/output, allocation overhead, inputs and the initial/final scalar records are excluded from the quota. O(t) retained history; quota units are records, not bytes or peak RAM.

    Functions

    goldschmidt_division()Approximate finite-input n/d by the preserved Goldschmidt loop. Uses frexp(abs(d)) and ldexp(n,-exponent), then at most 60 updates with f=2-D, N*=f, D*=f, testing abs(D-1)<1e-16 AFTER each update. Returns the actual final signed numerator, not a substituted hardware division. Pure apart from ordinary floating-point flags/errno; uses the caller's rounding environment. The products have independent data dependencies after f exists; this implementation launches no threads and promises no hardware speedup. O(t) selected scalar work, O(1) auxiliary state. No correctly-rounded or all-magnitude accuracy guarantee: scaling can lose a subnormal numerator, overflow can yield infinity, and a denominator can stall until the cap.
    goldschmidt_run()Run the same actual arithmetic with an explicit update budget and work metadata. Same finite-input semantics and limitations as goldschmidt_division(). A zero budget still normalizes and applies the denominator sign, but makes no updates. No history allocation or input mutation. Maximum selected products are 2*max_updates.
    goldschmidt_stop_name()Name a native Goldschmidt stop without allocating storage.
    goldschmidt_trace()Record the shared native loop, admitting each whole update before its arithmetic. Same arithmetic and budget rules as goldschmidt_run(); no replay, truncation, partial result or retained input references. Initial normalization is not a history record and occurs before online update admission. Ordinary FP flags from work already performed are not rolled back if a later admission fails.

    Types and constants

    GoldschmidtStopenum Actual stopping condition, without a quotient-accuracy claim.

    datamunge/algorithms/golomb_analysis.hpp

    Functions

    golomb_geometric_expected()Expected Golomb bits for P(N=n)=(1-a)a^n on n=0,1,... . Uses b+ a^c/(1-a^M), where b=ceil(log2 M), c=2^b-M. Stable expm1 evaluates the denominator for a near one. Returns the complete infinite-source expectation, not a finite-window renormalization or measured codec timing. a=0 is a point mass at zero. No allocation or input mutation.
    golomb_geometric_table()Compare full and conditional finite-window Golomb expectations. Each row uses the same zero-based geometric source. The finite mean conditions on N<window; omitted_probability is a^window. Scalar length calls do not emit codewords. Empty parameters return an empty frame with all numeric columns. O(parameters*window) work, O(parameters) output. No source samples are generated.
    golomb_length_plot()Plot native logical word lengths on a shared numerical value axis. Lines connect the requested values in their supplied order; use a sorted grid for a curve. Output remains editable through the native plotting API.
    golomb_length_table()Build a native exact-length table, without emitting potentially huge unary strings. Counts are converted to double for presentation and are exact only through 2^53. O(values*parameters) work/output. No mutation, random data or retained references.

    datamunge/algorithms/golomb_coding.hpp

    Classes

    GolombTraceOwned actual bits, complete spans and selected bit-visit counts. Encoding owns emitted bits; decoding owns only the consumed prefix, excluding any unread tail. Each word owns its value; no input references survive. Unary counts include terminators. Remainder counts include actual short/long payload positions. These selected visits exclude preflight, copies and CPU costs. The quota counts words only, not bits, bytes, capacity or peak RAM.
    GolombWordActual complete codeword boundaries and decoded/emitted integer parts. Owns scalars; indices are half-open bit positions in the associated trace.

    Functions

    golomb_bit_string()Copy logical bits into a printable first-bit-first string. No wire format or byte packing is implied. O(bits) work and owned characters.
    golomb_code_length()Compute a Golomb word's exact logical bit size without emitting it. O(1) scalar work, no allocation; M=1 gives unary length n+1 when representable.
    golomb_decode()Decode at most count complete words using checked bounded input reads. Clean input exhaustion returns fewer values; a partial attempted word throws. Reaching count leaves any tail unread and unvalidated. M and count are external framing; byte-padding is not ignored automatically. No inputs are mutated. O(consumed bits+values) work and O(values) output; no trace allocation.
    golomb_decode_trace()Capture complete actual parsed words and own their consumed bit prefix. Online admission occurs before attempting each word. Unread tails are excluded from trace bits and all counters. Malformed/quota failures return no partial history. The quota limits word records, not input/output bit storage or bytes.
    golomb_encode()Encode a sequence with checked complete sizing and no retained word history. Same bit convention as golomb_encode_value(). Empty input returns empty after parameter validation. Input is borrowed only during the call. O(values+bits) selected work, O(bits) output storage. Output is not a byte serialization.
    golomb_encode_trace()Capture actual encoding words in the ordinary emitter, without replay. Known complete word quota and bit sizing are checked before emission/allocation. History has O(values) entries in addition to the ordinary O(bits) output. No input references survive. Zero max_words disables only the policy cap.
    golomb_encode_value()Append an actual Golomb word after complete size/capacity preflight. Writes q ones, one zero and an MSB-first truncated-binary remainder. M=1 has no remainder. Existing prefix bits are preserved. Parameter/length/allocation failures occur before mutation; work/storage are O(word bits), not O(1). No packed-byte wire format, parameter header or framing is supplied.
    rice_decode()Decode Rice words through the same checked native Golomb parser. Same clean exhaustion, attempted-word and unread-tail semantics as golomb_decode().
    rice_encode()Encode Rice words using the same native Golomb emitter with M=2^k. Same ownership, bit convention, complexity and failures as golomb_encode().

    datamunge/algorithms/gram_schmidt.hpp

    Classes

    GramSchmidtOptionsAbsolute residual acceptance and complete input/optional capture limits. The threshold is an order- and scale-dependent heuristic, not a numerical rank certificate. Pass two repeats the modified projection sweep before one final normalization; it does not change the threshold or promise exact orthogonality.
    GramSchmidtProjectionOne actual modified projection, with owned complete before/after residuals. coefficient is the dot of before with the current accepted basis row, not a replay from the original input. Pass indices are zero based. All vectors own their values; basis identifies a row in trace.run.basis.
    GramSchmidtRowActual final residual and acceptance decision for one original row. residual is stored before normalization. accepted_rows counts basis rows immediately after the decision, including this row if accepted.
    GramSchmidtRunOwned accepted row vectors, their original row identities and actual work. Rows are accepted when their computed residual norm is strictly above the absolute tolerance. They approximate an orthonormal set; one pass can lose orthogonality or accept dependent rounding noise. No exact span/rank guarantee. Empty input returns empty; rectangular zero-width rows are all skipped. No references to caller input survive. Copying owns all nested storage.
    GramSchmidtTraceOwned actual projections, row decisions and result from one shared execution. Capture performs no arithmetic replay. Floating-value quota units are 1+2d per projection (coefficient, before and after) and 1+d per row decision (norm and residual). Metadata, ordinary basis/output/work, capacities and allocation overhead are excluded: this is not a byte or peak-RAM budget. Online admission precedes each dot request and capture vector copies; zero disables the policy cap. Failure returns no partial trace. With full rank, O(k²d) retained history can be much larger than O(kd) ordinary working/output storage. Caller inputs are never retained or mutated.
    GramSchmidtWorkSelected operations in the producing native loop, not timings or all CPU work. Dot products count one request per projection plus one residual self-dot per input row. Products/additions count d terms per dot, including the initial zero addition. Updates count d products and d subtractions per projection; divisions count normalization coordinates of accepted rows only.

    Functions

    gram_schmidt()Apply the preserved one-pass modified ordering and absolute 1e-12 residual test. Rows are input vectors. Sequential double dot products, projection updates and sqrt(sum of squares) retain ordinary original results; scaling can change acceptance and rounding can lose orthogonality. No pivoting, relative rank test, robust scaled norm or exact-span certificate is supplied. Validates rectangular shape and finite inputs before internal copying/arithmetic; nonfinite intermediate arithmetic throws instead of returning invalid basis vectors. Empty/zero-width semantics follow GramSchmidtRun. Independent calls share no state; concurrent mutation of borrowed input is outside the contract. O(k²d) selected arithmetic, O(kd) working/output storage, no capture or caps.
    gram_schmidt_run()Execute the shared modified kernel with options, source rows and selected work. Same arithmetic/limitations as gram_schmidt(); options allow a second full projection sweep and a different absolute threshold. Complete rectangular and finite validation, plus option validation, precede input quota and arithmetic. The complete input cap counts k+kd entries, including zero-width row headers; zero disables it. Trace quota is ignored. No histories or input references.
    gram_schmidt_trace()Capture actual before/coefficient/after projections and final row decisions online. Same kernel, accepted basis, work and input rules as run; capture performs no extra dot products. Actual quota units and ownership follow GramSchmidtTrace. Row-decision admission occurs before the residual self-dot; projection admission before its coefficient dot and before copying state. No partial history is returned on failure; zero trace cap disables only that policy cap.

    datamunge/algorithms/gram_schmidt_analysis.hpp

    Functions

    gram_schmidt_columns()Copy selected numeric dataframe columns as optionally centered input vectors. Each selected variable becomes a row; original dataframe rows become vector coordinates. Column order is preserved, duplicates allowed. Centering subtracts the ordinary sequential arithmetic mean, without scaling variances. Finite complete numeric columns are required; no imputation or labels enter the basis. No dataframe storage is retained or mutated. Empty selection returns empty.
    gram_schmidt_near_parallel()Build three nearly parallel independent rows in four dimensions. Rows are (1,e,0,0), (1,0,e,0), (1,0,0,e). Small e isolates loss of orthogonality; absolute-threshold skipping is a separate effect.
    gram_schmidt_quality()Measure a supplied basis's Gram defect and direct orthogonal-projection residual. Computes max|q_i dot q_j - identity_ij| and ||V - sum_i(v dot q_i)q_i||F/||V||F with ordinary double dots and hypot norm accumulation. Rounded diagnostics can underreport a true stored-basis defect, especially below machine precision; they are not interval bounds or certified accuracy. For a nonorthogonal basis this is NOT a least-squares or best-span residual. Empty basis has vacuous zero Gram defect; a nonzero input then has projection residual one. Zero input norm defines relative residual zero. All rows must have a common width; inputs are unmodified, no references survive. O(r²d+krd) work.
    gram_schmidt_scores_plot()Plot the first two accepted basis rows as per-observation coordinates, grouped by labels. Requires at least two basis rows and a label per coordinate. This is an order-dependent orthogonal feature representation, not PCA, a fitted classifier or held-out prediction. All points are shown; labels affect colors only. Copies coordinates and grouping into an owned native plot.

    Classes

    ColoringAnalysisOwned producing result, actual degree ordering and selected work, without event history. order sorts multigraph degree descending, then vertex ID ascending. Degrees exclude self-loops. Inputs are not retained. Copying owns all vector storage.
    ColoringEventOne actual constant-size first-fit event, without marker-array snapshots. vertex is always the vertex being processed. For neighbor events, neighbor is the actual adjacent vertex; colored states whether its label exists, color is that label or zero placeholder, and flag states whether a true marker write occurred. For probes color is the tested label and flag its blocked value. For assignments color is the committed label. Other fields are placeholders.
    ColoringOptionsComplete input caps and online actual-event cap for analysis/capture. All endpoints are validated before caps or adjacency allocation. Vertices include isolates; edges count original records, including loops/duplicates. Event units are whole neighbor/probe/assignment records, not bytes or peak RAM.
    ColoringResultOwned legacy greedy labels and contiguous palette size. Empty graphs use no colors; each nonempty edgeless graph uses color zero. The output is proper for the graph after deleting loops, not an optimality certificate or a proper coloring of an original graph containing a loop.
    ColoringTraceOwned actual preparation, output and chronological constant-size sweep events. Capturing performs no replay or extra degree sorting. Online admission occurs before each neighbor read/marker write, availability read or assignment. Default cap is one million records; zero disables it. Preparation, ordinary output/work, capacities and allocation overhead are excluded. No truncation or partial trace escapes failure. History is O(n+m) records, not full marker arrays.
    ColoringWorkSelected actual preparation and first-fit work, excluding validation and CPU costs. Degrees and adjacency entries include parallel edges, but not loops. Marker initialization is measured in logical slots; writes count every actual assignment of true, including repeated writes from duplicate edges.

    Functions

    greedy_coloring()First-fit vertex coloring in descending-degree, ascending-ID order. Undirected adjacency preserves input edge order and parallel entries. Endpoints must be valid, including on ignored loops. Self-loops are deleted: the result is proper for that projected loopless multigraph, not the original looped graph. Duplicate edges do not add coloring constraints but CAN change the degree order, chosen labels and palette size. The heuristic is not optimal. Empty input uses zero colors; a nonempty isolate set uses one. Legacy signature and ordinary labels are preserved. Full endpoint validation precedes internal adjacency allocation. No optional caps, retained inputs or event history. O(n log n+m) selected work, O(n+m) working/output space, where m counts nonloop records; input validation also visits loops. Independent calls share no state.
    greedy_coloring_analyze()Execute the same native first-fit kernel with actual preparation and work. Same loop-deletion/parallel-edge/order/output contract as greedy_coloring(). Full endpoint validation precedes complete vertex/edge caps and adjacency allocation. Zero disables either cap. No events; max_events is ignored.
    greedy_coloring_trace()Capture shared-kernel actual neighbor, probe and assignment events online. Same result/work/preparation as analyze, with O(n+m) optional owned history. Whole-record admission and exclusions follow ColoringTrace. No replay, input retention, marker snapshots, truncation or partial result on failure.
    is_proper_coloring()Check unequal labels across nonloop edges, with the same loop-deletion policy. Returns false for wrong vector size, any invalid endpoint or a monochromatic nonloop edge. Any size_t labels are allowed, including gaps and SIZE_MAX; this does not certify contiguous labels, a palette count, optimality, or validity for an original graph containing loops.     datamunge/algorithms/graph_coloring_analysis.hpp

    Classes

    ColoringGraphOwned undirected graph fixture with explicit vertex count, including isolates. Edges retain their order and may be edited; family builders produce simple loopless graphs. No coloring or optimality certificate is implied by storage.

    Functions

    coloring_complete()Generate each unordered edge of the complete loopless graph once. Computes n(n−1)/2 without overflowing an intermediate when the result fits. Empty/singleton graphs have no edges. O(n²) output/work for n>=2.
    coloring_crown()Generate K(k,k) minus its matched pairs, in paired or grouped vertex numbering. Paired IDs are a_i=2i,b_i=2i+1; grouped IDs a_i=i,b_i=k+i. All degrees are k−1. For k>=2 the graph has an edge and is bipartite, hence chromatic number two. Paired ID ties make this native greedy use k colors; grouped ID ties use two. The underlying abstract graphs are isomorphic. O(k²) output/work, no random state or caller references.
    coloring_crown_witness()Return the explicit two-color bipartition for a generated crown numbering. This is a constructive feasible witness, not a general exact-coloring solver. Labels own their storage; both colors occur for every permitted k.
    coloring_cycle()Generate the simple cycle 0–1–...–(n−1)–0. No randomness or input references. O(n) output/work. n must be at least three.
    coloring_diagram()Draw a small supplied coloring on an equal-scale circular native graph diagram. Validates endpoints and label vector length; loops are omitted to match the library projection. Parallel records are drawn separately on coincident links. Does not certify properness or optimality. Node labels include vertex ID and actual color number, so palette reuse cannot hide distinct numeric labels. O(n+edges) retained geometry plus diagram node-lookup costs. Empty input gives a text-only diagram; at most 32 vertices are permitted for legibility.

    datamunge/algorithms/grasp.hpp

    Classes

    GraspCandidateActual scores and RCL membership for one unplaced candidate. Scores concern assigned neighbors only; side zero wins exact g0/g1 ties.
    GraspConstructionOne actual construction step, owning all candidate scores and chosen RNG state. pick is an index into candidates, not a vertex ID or RCL rank. Quota admission precedes scores, candidate snapshots and the one modulo RNG draw.
    GraspFlipOne actual vertex-flip test in a cyclic immediate-improvement scan. before_side is the label read before possible mutation; delta is the sequential signed incident-weight sum. Later tests in the same pass see earlier flips.
    GraspMaxCutResultLegacy owned feasible partition and producing final cut value. side contains zeros/ones by vertex; value sums u<v crossing adjacency entries once, including parallel entries. This is a feasible value, not an optimum certificate. Empty graphs return zero with an empty partition.
    GraspOptionsComplete input, local-pass and actual optional capture limits. Basic shape/endpoint/finite/no-loop/parameter validation precedes input caps; reciprocal-multiplicity validation allocates only after those input caps. A local pass includes a full cyclic scan, including the terminal no-flip scan.
    GraspRestartActual completed restart with owned pre/post-local partitions and best-so-far value. constructed_side is captured before local search, final_side after its terminal scan. No constructed objective is evaluated by the producing kernel.
    GraspRunOwned ordinary best result and actual selected work without retained histories. Copying owns the partition; no input references or callback state survive.
    GraspTraceOwned actual construction, flip and completed-restart histories from one execution. Logical capture units: 1 per construction step plus 1 per candidate record; 1 per flip test; 1 per restart plus 2n retained partition labels. A restart's whole 1+2n requirement is admitted before its construction; step and flip requirements are admitted online before their producing score/delta work. Excludes record fields, allocation overhead/capacities, validation and ordinary result/work. This is not a byte/peak-RAM bound. No replay or partial result. Histories own storage; ordinary/run calls allocate no optional histories.
    GraspWorkSelected actual construction, local-search and objective work, excluding validation/copies. Construction candidates are scored once per unplaced vertex per step. Neighbor visits count every inspected adjacency entry, even if unassigned or not crossing. RNG words count exactly one modulo draw per placement.

    Functions

    grasp_max_cut()Apply weighted MAX-CUT GRASP with the preserved xorshift/modulo construction and cyclic flips. Requires finite symmetric loopless weighted adjacency, preserving entry order. Parallel/signed/zero weights are supported; reciprocal multiplicities must match exactly by numeric weight (signed zeros compare equal). Alpha is finite in [0,1]; iterations is positive. Alpha zero still randomizes ties and gains within 1e-12 of the best; alpha one includes all candidates only in the ideal threshold model, subject to floating rounding. Modulo selection is biased in general. One continuing RNG stream spans restarts; seed zero uses a fixed nonzero fallback. Local scans test vertices 0..n-1 and immediately flip any computed delta>1e-12 until a no-flip scan. This is tolerance-local, not a global certificate. A finite partition space alone does not prove floating termination; the legacy call uses a one-million-pass per-restart cap. No input/capture caps or retained histories. Nonfinite score/range/delta/objective arithmetic throws. Ordinary finite valid arithmetic and strict best-restart tie behavior remain; initialization now uses infinities instead of arbitrary 1e300 sentinels. O(T(n²+nA+LA)) selected loop work for T restarts, A adjacency entries and at most L local passes per restart, plus O(A log A+n) reciprocal validation; O(n+A) working storage. Independent calls share no mutable state.
    grasp_max_cut_run()Execute the same producing kernel with actual work and explicit resource options. Same numeric/ordering/RNG semantics as grasp_max_cut(). Basic validation precedes complete input caps; reciprocal checking follows caps before search. Trace cap is ignored. Zero disables any selected policy cap, including the local-pass guard, so disabling it carries no floating termination guarantee.
    grasp_max_cut_trace()Capture actual candidates/RCL/RNG, immediate flips and completed restart prefixes. Same result and producing arithmetic work as run, with the capture units and admission points documented by GraspTrace. Inputs are borrowed only during the call. Failures return no partial best/history, even after completed earlier restarts; already executed floating flags/errno are not rolled back.

    Types and constants

    GraspAdjacencytype Owned weighted adjacency rows, each entry a neighbor ID and finite weight. Public calls validate outer size, endpoints, no loops and exact reciprocal weight multiplicities. Signed/zero weights and parallel entries are permitted. Original row/entry ordering is preserved and affects sequential sums.

    Classes

All storage is owned.
    GraspExactCutOwned exact-enumeration result and actual examined complement classes. Exact refers to exhaustive partitions, not exact arithmetic on arbitrary floating weights. Requires matching side length and labels zero or one.
    grasp_demo_graph()Return the original report's seeded fourteen-vertex integer-weight graph. Preserves the original seed12345, xorshift draw sequence, edge-presence modulo two and weight1+word%9 choices. Contains fifty undirected edges on this fixed unsigned generator. No download/global RNG or input references.
    grasp_exact_max_cut()Enumerate all small-graph cuts with vertex zero fixed to side zero. Hard limit24 vertices; complete partition count2^(n-1) (one if n=0) is checked against max_partitions before enumeration. Zero disables only the policy cap. Basic/symmetry graph validation occurs before this partition cap. Uses no GRASP search, RNG or local improvement. O(2^n(A+n)) work and O(A+n) storage; actual partition count is returned. This is a bounded verification tool.

    datamunge/algorithms/grover.hpp

    Classes

    GroverOptionsComplete state and full-phase-capture caps, each zero disabling its policy limit. State units are complex amplitudes, not bytes. Capture counts the initial N amplitudes and 2N+1 per iteration (oracle state, diffused state and oracle mean). Metadata, ordinary final state, capacities and allocation overhead are excluded.
    GroverResultLegacy deterministic summary, without sampling or state collapse. measured retains its historical name but is an argmax; success_prob is the actual squared target amplitude, unclamped and not renormalized. Roundoff can make the state norm differ from one. No quantum device or hidden-target search is performed: the simulator is given the marked index.
    GroverRunOwned final native state, deterministic summary and selected producing work. State preparation uses the existing Hadamard gate arithmetic; iterations use actual complex-vector reflection loops. No analytic probability substitution, normalization, probability clamping, sampling or input references.
    GroverStepActual oracle and diffusion states captured during one iteration. before is the preceding step's after_diffusion, or trace.initial on step one. oracle_mean is the actual sequential complex mean used by diffusion. Each vector owns storage; no second execution reconstructs these phase states.
    GroverTraceOwned initial state, actual full-phase snapshots and final producing result. Known complete requirement N+K(2N+1) is preflighted before state allocation or gates. No truncation, replay, partial result or retained references. Capture adds O(KN) owned complex values to ordinary O(N) working/output storage; units exclude metadata, final ordinary output, capacity and peak RAM. Copying is deep.
    GroverWorkSelected actual state-operator visits, excluding snapshots and probability extraction. One oracle call is one known-target phase flip in this simulator. It is not a gate synthesis, physical device timing or a classical black-box query count. Hadamard pairs count the actual two-amplitude gate pairs, not scalar FLOPs.

    Functions

    grover()Run the preserved legacy round(pi/4*sqrt(2^n)) iteration schedule. This schedule is an approximation, not an optimal integer stopping rule: for n=2 it uses two iterations while one succeeds with near-unit probability. measured is a first argmax, not measurement. Preserves ordinary legacy output and arithmetic; validates n/target before shifts/allocation. n=0 is supported. No optional state/history policy caps; container limits still apply. Floating state-vector work O(nN+KN), storage O(N); these are classical simulation costs.
    grover_first_peak_iterations()Estimate the first-lobe integer stopping point from the single-marked-state rotation model. Uses floor(pi/(4*asin(1/sqrt(N)))); returns zero for n=0 and n=1, where ideal success is constant across integer iterations. O(1) scalar theory calculation, not a native run, exhaustive window maximization or global-time optimum claim.
    grover_run()Execute a requested nonnegative count through the shared native state-vector kernel. Uniform preparation uses qstate_zero and h_gate, then actual oracle/diffusion loops. No analytic substitutions or sampling. Complete input/capture geometry validation precedes state allocation. Trace cap is ignored without capture.
    grover_success_trace()Return actual target probabilities at steps zero through max_iters, without full snapshots. Shared kernel arithmetic preserves legacy outputs. Negative max_iters now throws rather than silently returning only step zero. No sampling, clamping or normalization. O(nN+KN) work and O(N+K) working/output storage; no optional policy caps, but checked containers/counts. n=0 is valid.
    grover_trace()Capture the shared execution's initial, oracle and diffusion states without replay. Complete known complex-value requirement follows GroverTrace. Preflight checks policy/container/count limits before allocating states or invoking gates. Operator work equals the untraced run; probability extraction/copies are excluded.

Returns sin²((2k+1)asin(1/sqrt(2^n))) using ordinary scalar floating math. n=0 returns one; n=1 returns one half, avoiding artificial numerical differences in these constant ideal cases. This is a theoretical reference, not an actual state, oracle execution, sampled outcome, interval bound or high-precision result.

    datamunge/algorithms/halley.hpp

    Classes

    HalleyRunOwned final legacy summary, precise stopping reason and producing callback counts. No callback or input references survive. Legacy iterations count loop inspections, including the successful residual inspection, rather than updates; with cap zero the final callback is evaluated but iterations remains zero.
    HalleyStepOwned actual callback inspection and optional Halley update from one execution. Derivative and denominator fields are meaningful only when derivatives_evaluated; next is x unless updated. The final budget inspection evaluates only f, even if its residual is not accepted. No extra callback evaluations reconstruct records.
    HalleyTraceOwned chronological actual inspections and producing run; no replay or truncation. One record per f call, including final budget check, is admitted before that callback. Default cap one million records, zero disables it. Record counts are not bytes, capacities or peak RAM. Copying is deep; no retained callable state.
    HalleyWorkActual selected callback calls and applied updates, not FLOPs or elapsed time. Callback bodies can have arbitrary costs; no timing comparison follows from these counts.

    Functions

    halley()Solve f(x)=0 using the retained Halley update and strict residual stopping. Uses x-2*f*df/(2*df*df-f*d2f) in the original arithmetic order. Cubic local convergence assumes a sufficiently smooth simple root, consistent derivatives and a sufficiently close start; multiple roots and distant starts need not be cubic or converge. No bracket, step-size test or stagnation acceptance. tol=0 disables acceptance even at callback zero. A zero denominator returns failure. All controls/callables are checked before callbacks; nonfinite callback/update arithmetic throws. Callback exceptions propagate; their side effects persist. Calls are independent except for caller-owned callback state. O(K) scalar work plus callback costs; constant storage. max_iter=0 still evaluates f(x0).
    halley_run()Execute the same Halley kernel with explicit stop and actual selected work. Same domains, arithmetic, callback order, errors and stopping rules as halley(). No extra callback evaluations or trace storage. No input references retained.
    halley_trace()Capture actual Halley inspections from the producing execution without replay. Same contracts as halley_run(). Online whole-record admission precedes each callback; no partial trace returns on cap/error, but earlier callback side effects persist. O(K) owned records in addition to scalar working storage.

    Types and constants

    HalleyStopenum Distinguish residual acceptance, a zero update denominator and exhausted updates. These are numerical outcomes, not existence or uniqueness certificates.

    datamunge/algorithms/hamming_code.hpp

    Classes

    Hamming74DecodedOwned decoded data and the applied syndrome correction, without a recovery certificate. corrected means a flip was applied. Only an at-most-one-bit channel error assumption makes that flip correct; two errors are miscorrected. A zero syndrome can also hide three or more errors. No input references retained.
    Hamming74ParityOwned actual inputs and running XORs of one even-parity check. Positions are one-based. Prefix0 is the first input bit; prefix1..3 use exactly three producing XORs. No replay, heap storage or borrowed state.
    Hamming74TraceOwned fixed-size actual parity checks, syndrome and correction from one decoding. All arrays own values; copying is deep. No heap, optional history, replay or truncation is needed for this fixed7-bit/3-check trace. Work excludes snapshot copies, validation and weighted syndrome assembly. Input remains unchanged.
    Hamming74WorkSelected actual decoder visits and XORs, excluding validation/capture/assembly. Fixed-size input uses12 parity bit visits,9 parity XORs,0or1 correction flips and4 final data reads. These counts are not timing or total machine work.

    Functions

    hamming74_decode()Apply the syndrome flip and extract data, assuming at most one channel error for recovery. Every binary received word lies within one bit of exactly one codeword. The decoder always selects it; it cannot establish that it was transmitted. Nonzero syndrome detects any two flipped bits, but this correcting interface then miscorrects them. Zero syndrome only establishes code membership. Constant fixed work/storage, no heap, no retained references or shared state.
    hamming74_decode_trace()Capture actual parity prefixes and the applied flip from the shared decoder execution. Same binary domain and correction limits as hamming74_decode(). Fixed-size owned records require no history policy cap; no replay, callbacks or input mutation.
    hamming74_encode()Encode four binary data values in even-parity positions1..7. Layout is p1,p2,d1,p4,d2,d3,d4, with parity positions1,2,4. The array order is position order, independent of integer endianness. Six parity XORs; constant fixed work/storage, no heap or mutation. Independent calls share no state.
    hamming74_syndrome()Compute the three binary parity checks without applying a correction. Nonzero means nonmembership, not a count of errors. Zero permits undetected codeword-shaped errors of weights3,4or7. Actual12 parity visits/9XORs; no heap, mutation, retained references or shared state.

    datamunge/algorithms/hamming_code_analysis.hpp

    Classes

    Hamming74AuditFixed exhaustive codebook and decoder outcomes grouped by actual channel error weight. Totals include all16 transmitted codewords and128 masks (2048 decodings). Results describe this deterministic decoder, not an assumed real-channel law. No heap, random draws or caller references; weight arrays have indices0..7.

    Functions

    hamming74_audit()Exhaustively audit the actual fixed codec over its complete binary state space. Builds16 codewords, checks120pair distances, then decodes2048word/mask pairs. There is no sampled approximation or second hand-coded decoder. Constant bounded work/storage for this fixed code; no callbacks, heap or shared state.
    hamming74_bsc_recovery()Evaluate exact-model block recovery probability on an independent binary symmetric channel. Assumes each of seven bits flips independently with the same probability p, and this bounded-distance decoder: only weights0or1 recover the transmitted data. Evaluates (1-p)^7+7p(1-p)^6 in double; not simulation, confidence bounds or a statement about correlated/unequal real errors. p0and1 permitted.

    datamunge/algorithms/hamming_distance.hpp

    Functions

    hamming_bit_distance()Counts differing bits in two packed unsigned 64-bit words using XOR/popcount. The comparison includes all 64 positions, including leading zeros. Unlike the string hamming_distance(), the symbols here are individual bits, not bytes. Inputs are borrowed values, there is no mutation/shared state, and work/storage are O(1).
    hamming_code_summary()Minimum separation and universal detection/correction radii of a finite code. Enumerates unordered pairs in O(m^2*n) time with O(m) validation storage; does not run a decoder. Detectable_errors=d_min-1 assumes code-membership rejection; a hard nearest-codeword decoder can miscorrect outside its guaranteed correction radius.
    hamming_comparison()Per-byte positional comparisons and cumulative mismatch counts, without realignment. Strings may contain NUL and arbitrary bytes; byte values are reported as unsigned numbers, not interpreted as UTF-8 characters. Empty pairs give a zero-row typed table. This and the other helpers own their results, leave inputs unchanged and have no shared mutable state. Work and output storage O(n).
    hamming_distance_matrix()Symmetric byte-Hamming distances for fixed-width words, in caller order. Work O(m^2*n), result space O(m^2). Duplicates are allowed; an empty word list gives a zero-by-zero matrix. Empty words of a common width zero are also allowed.
    hamming_nearest()Every codeword's distance to a query, retaining all nearest-neighbour ties. No word is silently selected and no decoding guarantee is inferred from one query. Work/storage O(m*n)/O(m), with original codebook ordering preserved.
    hamming_shells()Sizes of q-ary Hamming shells/balls and uniform-word probabilities. Shell k has binomial(n,k)*(q-1)^k words; the ball is the cumulative shell sum. Counts are numerical double values (not exact integers beyond 2^53); positive probabilities may underflow to zero. No enumeration of q^n words is needed. Work/output storage O(n); overflow is rejected before allocating the table.
    plot_hamming_comparison()Aligned byte labels and agreement markers for a short Hamming comparison. Printable ASCII bytes display literally; other bytes use hexadecimal labels. Work and output size O(n). Call save_svg() to save a local image rather than printing XML.

    Functions

    heap_permutation_size()Compute checked n!, n*n! and recursive-call requirements without allocation. C0=C1=1 and Cn=1+n*C(n-1). Large n fails at the first overflowing recurrence; no loop over an unrepresentably large n completes. No container/policy checks or generation are performed; representable counts do not guarantee allocability.
    heap_permutations()Materialize every positional permutation in the preserved recursive Heap order. Even prefix k swaps i with k-1 after block i; odd k swaps0 with k-1. One swap separates outputs, n!-1 total. With distinct values the rows are unique; repeated values can produce identical consecutive rows. Empty input yields one empty row. No sorting, deduplication, input mutation or references. Checks exact counts/container sizes before copies. No optional policy caps; allocation failure remains possible. Total time/storage O(n*n!+n!) including row materialization, with O(n) working array and recursion for n>=1. Independent calls share no mutable state. This is not the heapsort algorithm.
    heap_permutations_run()Execute the shared Heap kernel with complete output caps and actual work counts. Same positional order and domains as heap_permutations(). Complete checked output limits precede working/output allocation. History cap is ignored here.
    heap_permutations_trace()Capture actual recursive swap events without a second execution or snapshots. Same output contracts as heap_permutations_run(), plus complete n!-1 history admission before any allocation/copy/swap. Failure returns no partial result. A history entry is one record, excluding ordinary output/fields/capacity/bytes.

All values/slopes/queries must be finite and widths finite positive. Failures in normalized coordinate/basis/weighted-term arithmetic throw instead of returning nonfinite values. Preserves ordinary legacy operation order. O(n) validation plus O(log n) lookup; constant auxiliary storage, no allocation, input mutation, retained references or shared mutable state. Exact-arithmetic C1 joins and cubic reproduction do not imply bit-exact floating behavior.

    Functions

    hirschberg()Align whole byte strings globally with the preserved legacy input orientation and ties. Splits first input at its midpoint and takes first maximizing column. Base traceback preserves diagonal/up/left preference without a dense DP table. Uses views, releases profiles before children and appends output once; no substring/reversal copies or recursive alignment concatenation. Time O(nm+n+m); auxiliary score values O(m), stack O(log(n+1)), owned output O(n+m). This legacy orientation does not promise O(min(n,m)) score rows. No optional input/work/history caps; representability checks still precede execution. Inputs must exclude literal '-' to make gap rows unambiguous. Other bytes, including NUL, compare literally. Conservative score admission requires (n+m)*max(abs(match),abs(mismatch),abs(gap))<=INT_MAX. Any integer scoring signs are otherwise supported. Tied alignment rows may differ from dense NW. Independent calls share no mutable state and retain no references.
    hirschberg_run()Execute checked Hirschberg with optional shorter score-row orientation and actual work. Same domains, base ties and producing kernel as hirschberg(). Default internal second input is shorter, giving O(min(n,m)) score values plus O(log(max(n,m)+1)) frames and O(n+m) output. Transposition can choose a different tied optimum, but output rows return to caller order. Complete input domain/caps precede output allocation; each full score sweep/base scan is admitted before it runs.
    hirschberg_trace()Capture the same execution's actual split profiles without replay or dense tables. Complete record units1+3*(subrange_b+1) admitted before profile capture/call work. Known row-work units also admitted before their producing sweeps. No truncation/partial result or caller mutation. Histories own copies and add their retained memory beyond untraced score rows, frames and ordinary output.

    hits()Apply preserved HITS authority-then-hub power updates with a strict change test. Uses each edge in input order, counting loops/duplicates as endorsements. Starts with both vectors1/sqrt(n), or empty for n0. Sequential sum-of-squares normalization divides only nonzero norms, otherwise retaining zeros. Stops when the largest absolute change in either vector is strictly below tolerance. Zero budget returns initialization without a test. With default small tolerance, a nonempty edgeless graph needs two paired zero updates; n0 takes one empty paired update when budget permits. Unit norms are not promised in these cases. No optional input/history caps; checked counts/container sizes still apply. O(n+K(n+m)) time/O(n) working/output storage, excluding borrowed input edges; no retained references or shared mutable state. Finite positive tolerance is required; an iteration cap or tiny change is not a uniqueness/residual proof.
    hits_run()Execute the shared HITS kernel with explicit stop/work and complete input policies. Same arithmetic, initialization, tie-free numeric order and domains as hits(). Complete graph validation precedes optional input caps and vector allocation. Capture cap ignored without tracing. No extra producing score sweeps.
    hits_trace()Capture actual raw/normalized paired updates from the producing execution without replay. Same contracts as hits_run(). Online whole iteration capture admits1+4n units before allocation or work; input and initial2n admission precede vectors. Failure returns no partial trace and never mutates input. Histories own all score vectors and add memory beyond the ordinary O(n) working/output bound.

    Types and constants

    HitsEdgetype Directed zero-based endorsement u->v, preserving loops, order and duplicate edges. Repeated pairs contribute repeatedly, equivalent to integer adjacency weights. The alias owns its two indices; validation belongs to the called algorithm.
    HitsStopenum Distinguish a strict max-component change test from exhausted update budget. Tolerance is not a spectral-residual or uniqueness certificate.

    datamunge/algorithms/hmac.hpp

    Classes

    HmacOptionsComplete combined key/message input policy before copying or hashing. The cap counts input bytes once, not allocations, bytes hashed or peak memory.
    HmacRunOwned tag and producing call-boundary diagnostics; no input references retained.
    HmacTraceFixed-size owned intermediates captured during the actual producing HMAC. This educational record contains key material; example keys are public fixtures. No replay, message-history copy or input references. Arrays occupy 256 byte values beyond run (three 64-byte blocks plus two 32-byte digests), excluding metadata/padding. key_digest is meaningful only when run.key_hashed; otherwise its zero initialization is a sentinel. This is not secure-erasing storage.
    HmacWorkSelected work recorded at actual SHA-256 invocation boundaries. Block counts use SHA-256 padding length, not a captured round/compression trace. Excludes pad generation, copying, allocation, hex formatting and trace copies.

    Functions

    hmac_sha256()Compute full HMAC-SHA-256 using the preserved one-shot SHA implementation. Arbitrary byte strings are accepted, including empty and embedded-NUL inputs. Keys longer than 64 bytes are hashed first; other keys are zero-padded to 64. The actual inner digest hashes (keyblock XOR0x36)||message; the final digest hashes (keyblock XOR0x5c)||inner_digest. No tag truncation or verification. O(k+m) time and O(k+m) additional storage for the one-shot copies and SHA padding, not streaming O(1) storage. No optional input policy; representable bit lengths, padded string sizes and counters are checked before hashing. No retained references, shared mutable state or constant-time/secure-erasure guarantee. Functional digest correctness is distinct from security certification.
    hmac_sha256_hex()Format the preserved complete HMAC tag as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Same byte-domain, complexity, ownership and non-streaming contract as hmac_sha256().
    hmac_sha256_run()Run the shared HMAC with complete input policy and actual call-boundary counts. Same byte/arithmetic/storage contracts as hmac_sha256(); no intermediate capture.
    hmac_sha256_trace()Capture actual key normalization, pads and inner digest from the producing HMAC. Same complete input policy/storage/domain as hmac_sha256_run(). Fixed owned intermediate arrays contain key material; no recomputation or round history.

    Types and constants

    HmacBlocktype Complete 64-byte SHA-256 key/pad block, in original byte order.
    HmacTagtype Complete 32-byte SHA-256 authentication tag, retaining embedded zero bytes.

    HmacReferenceCaseOwned public RFC4231 HMAC-SHA-256 input and expected full/prefix hex. expected_hex contains 64 characters except case 5's 32-character 128-bit prefix. The full-tag API remains 32 bytes for every case. No references are retained.

A failed limit throws; there is no sampling, truncation or partial result. Calls the shared HMAC kernel for one baseline and 8k changed keys. For k key bytes and m message bytes, time O((8k+1)(k+m)) and additional working/output storage O(k+m+8k), excluding borrowed input. Empty key still computes a baseline but returns no flips and has_flips=false. Values describe only this fixture; a mean near 128 does not prove PRF behavior or authentication security.

    Classes

    BipartiteMatchingResultOwned maximum-cardinality matching in both orientations, with preserved field order. Unmatched entries use kBipartiteUnmatched. A matching is not generally unique; left roots and supplied adjacency order determine deterministic choices.
    HopcroftKarpOptionsComplete graph and online logical-history policies, each zero disabling its cap. Input caps count all supplied vertices/edge entries, including isolated or repeated entries. Trace counts records and retained vertex/distance values, not bytes/capacity/peak memory. No sampling or truncation.
    HopcroftKarpPathOwned actual shortest augmenting path immediately before its producing flip. left[i]->right[i] are the path's forward unmatched edges. Before the flip, right[i] is matched to left[i+1] except for the final free right vertex. The root is free and all path vertices are distinct. k pairs mean2k-1 graph edges; flipping gains one matched pair. No replay or input references.
    HopcroftKarpPhaseOwned actual BFS labels and subsequent shortest-path flips, including terminal BFS. left_distance counts matched-right-to-left hops from free left roots, before DFS dead-end pruning; SIZE_MAX means undiscovered. BFS stops expanding labels at/above the shortest free-right distance, though already discovered frontier labels can remain. Every augmentation has shortest_pairs forward pairs. Terminal BFS has shortest_pairs=0 and no augmentations; its complete reachable sets produce the run's minimum cover. Records own all arrays.
    HopcroftKarpRunOwned actual matching, terminal-BFS minimum vertex cover and selected work. cover_left/cover_right use their own side indices in ascending order. They cover every supplied edge and their combined size equals matching size, certifying optimality independently of tie choices. No references retained.
    HopcroftKarpTraceOwned producing BFS/path history from an initially empty matching. Each BFS admits1+n_left record/distance units before its work; each known path admits1+2k record/vertex units before copies and flipping. Working buffers, ordinary output, metadata/capacity/byte peak memory are excluded. No partial result, truncation, post-hoc reconstruction or retained references.
    HopcroftKarpWorkSelected actual producing visits, excluding validation/copy/allocation/certificate/capture costs. Duplicate edges count repeatedly when visited. Pair writes count matched-pair assignments along paths, each of which writes both orientation arrays. These counters are not timing, FLOPs or complete memory traffic.

    Functions

    hopcroft_karp()Compute maximum-cardinality bipartite matching using shortest-layer blocking paths. Full endpoint validation precedes allocation. Duplicates/order are retained; roots ascend and adjacency follows supplied order. BFS bounds free-right distance, and an explicit DFS stack with phase-local edge cursors extracts shortest augmenting paths only, avoiding recursive stack exhaustion. Empty sides/edge lists are valid and leave unmatched sentinels. Tie choices can differ from older code that allowed longer paths in a shortest-layer phase; cardinality/validity and the original public signature/layout are preserved. For V>=1, O((E+V)*sqrt(V)) time and O(E+V) working/output storage, with supplied duplicate entries counted in E. No optional graph/history caps; count/container representation checks still apply. No input mutation, retained references or shared mutable state.
    hopcroft_karp_run()Run the shared shortest-layer kernel with graph policies and terminal minimum cover. Same domains/order/storage as hopcroft_karp(). Validates every endpoint before combined vertex/edge caps or adjacency allocation. Capture cap ignored. Cover extraction uses actual terminal BFS reachability with no extra edge walk.
    hopcroft_karp_trace()Capture actual BFS labels and shortest path stacks before their producing flips. Same contracts as hopcroft_karp_run(). Online complete BFS/path units are admitted before work/copy/flip as described in HopcroftKarpTrace, with no sampling, truncation or replay. Added storage is O(retained logical units) plus metadata, beyond ordinary O(E+V) buffers/output.

    Types and constants

    HopcroftKarpEdgetype Ordered left/right endpoint pair; repeated edges and input order are retained.
    kBipartiteUnmatchedvariable SIZE_MAX sentinel for an unmatched vertex; never a valid retained index.

Retains three extra random states before ten with-replacement probe toggles, preserving the original data RNG stream. Those ten draws need not change ten distinct positions. Stored weights, actual trace/trials and summaries are owned.

    hopfield_original_experiment()Run the original seeded100-neuron/three-memory experiment with complete trial admission. Uses MT19937-64(data_seed), std::bernoulli_distribution(.5) for three memories then three comparison states, then ten uniform0..99 toggle draws. Each noise level0,5,..50 creates new probes by testing uniform0..99 modulo100 at every neuron. Recall uses100 sweeps and seeds1..trials_per_level at every level. Standard-library distribution/shuffle mappings need not agree across vendors. Validates/admit full11*T calls before RNG work, training or result allocation. O(rows*columns+rows+columns) preparation/owned render storage.

    datamunge/algorithms/hopfield_network.hpp

    Classes

    HopfieldNetworkOwned symmetric zero-diagonal Hopfield weight matrix with its historical aggregate layout. Nonempty models require square finite weights, exact symmetry and zero diagonal when used by energy/recall. Hebbian storage does not guarantee every supplied pattern is stable, nor recall of the nearest stored pattern. No references or shared state are retained; do not mutate weights concurrently with a call.
    HopfieldOptionsComplete neuron/weight and online logical-history caps, each zero disabling policy. Input validation precedes these policies and internal working copies. History units count records/state/index values, not bytes/capacity/peak memory.
    HopfieldRecallRunOwned actual final state, completed sweeps, stop branch and selected work. No nearest-memory or stored-pattern guarantee. NoChange certifies only the computed local-field update rule, not an exact-arithmetic energy certificate.
    HopfieldRecallTraceOwned actual initialization and producing sweep/update history, without replay. Initial1+N units count one record and its state. Each sweep admits1+3N before shuffle/copies: one sweep record, N order IDs, N end-state values and N update records. Scalar record fields/metadata/capacity/working/output/byte peak memory excluded. Histories add O(S*N+1) storage; diagnostic energies add O((S+1)N*N) work beyond ordinary recall. No truncation/partial result/input references.
    HopfieldSweepOwned actual shuffled sweep and its end-state/energy observations. Energy observations are extra sequential full-matrix calculations at actual states, not replayed dynamics or exact/compensated arithmetic. They can round.
    HopfieldUpdateActual local field and sign decision at its producing asynchronous update. Later updates in the same sweep see this decision immediately. Exact zero, including negative zero, chooses+1, preserving historical code behavior.
    HopfieldWorkSelected actual recall and separate diagnostic-energy visits. Excludes validation, copies, RNG/shuffle, allocation and history bookkeeping. Fields include all diagonal zero terms. Counts are not timing or total traffic.

    Functions

    hopfield_energy()Evaluate E=-1/2 sum_ij W_ij*s_i*s_j with full matrix/state validation. Requires finite exact-symmetric square weights and zero diagonal, bipolar equal-size state. Empty gives zero. Preserves sequential double arithmetic; not an exact energy/sign certificate. O(N*N+1) work, no allocation on success or retained references/input mutation; nonfinite producing arithmetic throws.
    hopfield_hamming()Count differing positions of two complete equal-length bipolar states. Rejects unequal lengths instead of silently ignoring a suffix. Empty equals empty at distance0. O(N+1) time, O(1) storage; no allocation on success, input mutation, references retained or shared state.
    hopfield_recall()Recall with the historical by-value state interface and preserved sign/shuffle arithmetic. Zero local field selects+1 (it does not keep a negative sign). Initializes one index order, shuffles it in place each sweep with MT19937-64(seed), and updates asynchronously in that order until no change or budget exhaustion. Zero budget returns initialization; empty state takes one empty unchanged sweep when budget permits. Different standard-library shuffle mappings can differ. Complete matrix/state validation precedes internal copies; the historical by-value parameter itself may already copy at call entry. No optional caps. O(N*N+S*N*N+S*N+1) ordinary work and O(N+1) extra output/working storage, excluding the borrowed N*N matrix. No nearest-memory or universal convergence certificate for floating arithmetic; finite budget always bounds execution.
    hopfield_recall_run()Run shared recall with complete matrix policies and actual stop/work diagnostics. Same state/shuffle/arithmetic/budget semantics as hopfield_recall(). Validates borrowed input before internal copies or caps. Capture cap ignored.
    hopfield_recall_trace()Capture actual producing asynchronous decisions and extra sweep-boundary energies. Same contracts as hopfield_recall_run(), with online complete initial/sweep admission and owned histories, no replay. Diagnostic energies add work and can overflow even when untraced local fields would remain finite.
    hopfield_train()Store bipolar patterns with the historical interface and no optional matrix policies. Same complete validation, arithmetic, ownership and storage semantics as hopfield_train_checked(), with neuron/weight/capture caps disabled.
    hopfield_train_checked()Store complete bipolar patterns with checked Hebbian outer-product weights. W_ij=sum_p(pattern[p][i]*pattern[p][j])/N for i!=j; diagonal zero. Validates every row/sign before matrix admission/allocation; empty list or zero-length rectangular patterns produce an empty network. Pattern/order arithmetic is preserved; supplied memories need not be fixed points. O(P*N*N+P*N+1) work, O(N*N+1) owned output, borrowed input unchanged and not retained.

    Types and constants

    HopfieldStopenum Distinguish an actual unchanged sweep from exhaustion of the requested budget. A budget stop is not a fixed-point certificate; zero budget performs no updates.

    Classes

    AssignmentEventOwned actual state at one reprice or completed augmentation boundary. All vectors have n entries and omit the private virtual column. Unmatched columns use kAssignmentUnmatched; no reference to the input is kept.
    AssignmentOptionsOptional complete-input and online history admission policies. Zero disables the respective optional cap. Each event costs 1+4*n logical entries (one event plus n entries in each of four owned vectors). The cap excludes input copy, final result/potentials/work, vector capacity, scalar metadata and ordinary/transient solver arrays; it is not peak bytes/RAM. Untraced solves ignore the history cap. No partial history is returned on error.
    AssignmentResultMinimum-cost row-to-column permutation and computed total. Owns its values, with the legacy field order and types preserved. Default is an empty, unsolved value; successful solvers require a nonempty square input.
    AssignmentRunFinal permutation, computed potentials and selected producing work. Potentials provide numerical diagnostics: exact arithmetic theory certifies optimality, while floating feasibility/tightness must be checked at a suitable scale. Negative inputs need not be feasible against unintroduced rows during execution; completed rows are handled by the active-prefix invariant.
    AssignmentTraceOwned original costs and actual state history from one solve. History is generated inside the ordinary kernel, never by replaying a solved assignment. Capture costs O(events*n) time/storage in addition to the solver.
    AssignmentWorkSelected actual operation counts from the shared producing kernel. Counts omit input validation, allocations, copies, comparisons, result sum and trace observation. They describe operations, not elapsed time or proof of exact floating-point optimality. Overflow in counters throws rather than wraps.

    Functions

    hungarian()Solve a finite nonempty square minimum-cost assignment. Legacy entry point disables both optional caps; tie choices and ordinary finite arithmetic order are preserved. No mutation, retained references or shared state. Square finite negative costs are allowed; NaN/infinity are rejected. The deterministic ascending-column strict-less tie rule is preserved. Ordinary solve O(n^3) time/O(n) auxiliary storage excluding borrowed n*n input and owned outputs; trace adds its stated copy/history costs. Floating subtraction/addition can round: this is a numerical implementation, not an exact real or integer certificate. Any nonfinite produced slack, potential, finite frontier update or total throws. Maximize values by negating finite entries and interpreting the total sign.
    hungarian_run()Solve once and return computed duals and actual operation counts. Uses optional complete input admission; history cap is ignored. No mutation, retained references or shared state. Square finite negative costs are allowed; NaN/infinity are rejected. The deterministic ascending-column strict-less tie rule is preserved. Ordinary solve O(n^3) time/O(n) auxiliary storage excluding borrowed n*n input and owned outputs; trace adds its stated copy/history costs. Floating subtraction/addition can round: this is a numerical implementation, not an exact real or integer certificate. Any nonfinite produced slack, potential, finite frontier update or total throws. Maximize values by negating finite entries and interpreting the total sign.
    hungarian_trace()Capture actual reprices and augmentations from the shared solve. Each complete event is admitted before its frontier scan or path flip; failure returns no partial result. Input is copied only after complete input validation/admission. No mutation, retained references or shared state. Square finite negative costs are allowed; NaN/infinity are rejected. The deterministic ascending-column strict-less tie rule is preserved. Ordinary solve O(n^3) time/O(n) auxiliary storage excluding borrowed n*n input and owned outputs; trace adds its stated copy/history costs. Floating subtraction/addition can round: this is a numerical implementation, not an exact real or integer certificate. Any nonfinite produced slack, potential, finite frontier update or total throws. Maximize values by negating finite entries and interpreting the total sign.

    AssignmentDiagnosticsNumerical final-state diagnostics, not an exact optimality certificate. Long-double accumulation is converted to finite doubles. Negative minimum slack or nonzero tightness/gap can reflect rounding or an invalid candidate. No acceptance tolerance is imposed; the caller chooses a scale-aware policy.

    Functions

    assignment_diagnostics()Check complete shapes/domains and compute numerical assignment diagnostics. Requires nonempty square finite costs, finite n-entry potentials and a true n-entry assignment permutation; a finite stored total is required but is not trusted as the recomputed primal. O(n*n) work/O(n) validation storage, no solve, mutation, retained references or shared state. Does not prove exact optimality.
    assignment_diagram()Draw the supplied final matching with selected costs and computed potentials. Native boxes/edges use actual supplied costs and computed row/column potentials; Task boxes are reordered to align matched pairs; no matching is recomputed. Complete validation precedes layout. Edges are the supplied permutation, not a claim of exact optimality. O(n) graphic objects; the complete row quota is checked before diagnostic/layout allocation.
    assignment_example_costs()Return the original three-worker assignment cost matrix. Owns its finite integer-valued entries, no retained references or shared state.
    assignment_work_costs()Construct a deterministic diagonal or all-tied square work-control matrix. Diagonal costs zero and off-diagonal one give a strict diagonal optimum; all-tied costs are zero everywhere. These are controlled workloads, not random data or runtime forecasts. Complete n*n admission precedes allocation.

    datamunge/algorithms/id3_diagnostics.hpp

    Classes

    ID3DataOwned integer-coded categorical teaching data and predictor names.
    ID3FrameClassifierID3 with frozen categorical encoding of named numeric or string DataFrame columns. All predictor values are categories, including numeric columns: no thresholds, scaling or ordering assumptions. Dictionaries are learned only on training rows, assigning nonnegative codes in first-occurrence order. New levels map to -1 and use the native local-majority fallback. Nulls and nonfinite numeric predictors are rejected, rather than silently omitted or imputed. Labels are numeric ints. Models own their tree/schema/dictionaries. Const inference has no shared mutation.

    Functions

    id3_branch_table()Weighted branch entropies for one categorical test, including majority labels. Owns results and does not mutate inputs. Work O(n*log(n)), storage O(n).
    id3_evaluate()Accuracy and unseen-branch counts against supplied categorical labels. Baseline always predicts the fitted root majority, never a majority fitted to evaluation labels. A fallback is counted once per query. No mutation/shared state. Work O(n*h*log(b)); temporary storage O(h), plus the one-row output.
    id3_node_table()Inspect every node of a valid categorical tree, with depth and fallback label. Validates that all nodes are reachable once from root zero, with no cycles/shared children and no children on leaves. Empty tree gives a typed zero-row table. O(nodes+edges) work/storage; inputs are unchanged.
    id3_split_table()Empirical entropy and conditional entropy for every candidate root feature. Uses precisely the categorical partition/bit-entropy criterion of id3_train(). Zero-count classes are omitted. Names default to f0, f1, ... . Owns its output, borrows inputs without mutation; O(n*d*log(n)) work and O(n+d) auxiliary storage.
    id3_tennis()Fourteen-row Play Tennis teaching fixture; a constructed example, not a survey. Codes: outlook sunny/overcast/rain=0/1/2; temperature hot/mild/cool=0/1/2; humidity high/normal=0/1; windy false/true=0/1; play no/yes=0/1.
    id3_trace()Explain a categorical prediction through each visited test and final stop. Same visited-path checks as id3_predict(); no mutation/shared state. O(h*log(b)) work and O(h) result storage. Unseen category stops at the current majority.
    plot_id3_tree()Draw a small categorical tree, labelling tests, category edges and leaf classes. Places leaves uniformly and internal nodes at the mean child position. Intended for teaching trees with at most 31 nodes and eight levels; returns an editable plot, never inline SVG bytes. O(nodes+edges) work/storage, no input mutation.

    datamunge/algorithms/index_calculus.hpp

    Classes

    DiscreteLogResultVerified discrete logarithm or an explicit unsuccessful bounded search. Legacy aggregate order/types preserved. Success means g^x=h modulo p; failure is not proof of nonexistence. A valid generator has a logarithm for every nonzero target; bounded relation/rank/query work may still fail.
    IndexCalculusOptionsFinite work budgets and complete allocation/history admission policies. Attempt budgets are exact counts, zero means no attempts. Optional allocation caps use zero to disable. A trace relation/stage costs 1+K logical entries, one record plus the complete K-dimensional slot budget, also reserved for a failed stage with an empty solution. No rejected trial is retained. History cap excludes ordinary matrices, table/output arrays, seed/scalar metadata, vector capacity and byte/peak RAM. Untraced preparation ignores it.
    IndexCalculusPreparationTraceOwned table plus actual accepted relation and linear-stage histories. Records are captured inside the producing precomputation, not by replay. Additional history storage is O((accepted rows+stages)*K); logical caps and exclusions are documented by IndexCalculusOptions.
    IndexCalculusQueryActual bounded target-search result and its successful smooth relation. Trivial h=1 or h=g uses no random trial, leaves relation fields empty/zero. An unready valid table gives failure for other targets. Each call copies the stored query RNG state; queries do not mutate a table or each other.
    IndexCalculusRelationOne accepted smooth relation captured at its actual collection boundary. g^exponent modulo p equals residue and the ordinary integer product of factor-base primes raised to powers. Failed nonsmooth trials are not stored.
    IndexCalculusStageActual prime-field or lifted prime-power solution boundary. Each stage solves modulo the prime field; modulus names the resulting q^j solution modulus after a successful correction lift. A failed rank stage has empty solution. No elimination is performed by dividing nonunits modulo p-1.
    IndexCalculusTableReusable verified factor-base logarithms and deterministic query-start state. Public value storage owns all arrays. Query validates group-factor data, factor-base ordering/primality, dimensions and every supplied logarithm before use, so editing values does not bypass domain checks. Validation has its own cost and is not counted as target search. No hidden cache or shared state.
    IndexCalculusWorkSelected actual precomputation operations, excluding validation/factorization. Modular exponentiation internals, RNG shifts, sieve work, allocations/copies, comparisons and final exponent checks are outside these selected totals. Counter overflow throws. They are operation observations, not CPU time.

    Functions

    index_calculus()Solve one finite-field logarithm with the default bounded index-calculus policy. Legacy signature/result layout and RNG stream retained for ordinary inputs. Validates prime p, primitive nonzero generator and nonzero target before any shortcut. Trivial h=1 or g returns immediately after group validation. Other targets use the same preparation/query kernels; no brute-force/BSGS fallback. Corrected factor bases exclude primes >=p and exact prime-power/CRT solves avoid invalid composite-modulus field assumptions. Bounded failure remains possible; found=false is not a proof that the logarithm does not exist. No mutation, retained references or shared state. See preparation/query for costs; this wrapper performs fresh precomputation for each nontrivial target.
    index_calculus_prepare()Prepare reusable finite-field factor-base logarithms. Requires prime p>=2 and a nonzero primitive generator g modulo p. Complete group-order factorization certifies generator order; it is additional work, not part of a claimed index-calculus runtime. Sieve primes are strictly below p. Collect at most K+surplus rows within the attempt budget, solve modulo each prime factor, lift to its full prime power, combine by CRT and exponent-check every logarithm. Full column rank is required in every prime field. No generic discrete-log fallback. Bounded failure is an explicit status, not nonexistence. Memory includes O(B+(K+surplus)*K) ordinary sieve/matrix and transient field copies; tracing adds actual retained records. No mutation, shared state or retained input references. The fixed B cap/batch/budgets do not implement an asymptotically tuned subexponential or production cryptographic solver.
    index_calculus_prepare_trace()Capture actual preparation of finite-field factor-base logarithms. Requires prime p>=2 and a nonzero primitive generator g modulo p. Complete group-order factorization certifies generator order; it is additional work, not part of a claimed index-calculus runtime. Sieve primes are strictly below p. Collect at most K+surplus rows within the attempt budget, solve modulo each prime factor, lift to its full prime power, combine by CRT and exponent-check every logarithm. Full column rank is required in every prime field. No generic discrete-log fallback. Bounded failure is an explicit status, not nonexistence. Memory includes O(B+(K+surplus)*K) ordinary sieve/matrix and transient field copies; tracing adds actual retained records. No mutation, shared state or retained input references. The fixed B cap/batch/budgets do not implement an asymptotically tuned subexponential or production cryptographic solver.
    index_calculus_query()Search for one target logarithm using a validated reusable table. Normalizes nonzero h after complete table/group checks. Trivial h=1 or g is solved even for an unready valid table, without trials. Other targets need a ready table and a successful smooth shift within max_attempts. The complete table is checked on every public query, including each supplied logarithm; this validation cost is separate from attempts. No refactoring of the group order or rebuilding of the relation matrix is performed. Search costs O(attempts*(K divisions plus log p modular powering)) and O(K) work/output storage, apart from table checks. No mutation/retained references/shared state.

    Types and constants

    IndexCalculusStatusenum Actual bounded precomputation outcome. Rank deficiency or a relation limit is not a discrete-log nonexistence proof. The complete generator domain is validated before collection.

    datamunge/algorithms/informed_search.hpp

    Classes

    InformedSearchExpansionOne non-stale queue removal, recorded before its outgoing edges are relaxed. Values are snapshots owned by InformedSearchTrace; goal removals are included.
    InformedSearchResultWeighted path-search output, distinct from the sorted-array SearchResult type. Owns its path. Unreachable answers have found=false, cost zero and an empty path.
    InformedSearchTraceOwned multi-goal search answer and chronological expansion snapshots. Recording adds O(k) storage for k expansions; no mutable state is shared.

    Functions

    a_star_search()Finds a directed path to one goal with reopening A*. Same semantics and requirements as b_star_search(), with one goal. No shared state.
    b_star_search()Finds a cheapest directed path to a goal set using multi-goal A*. The historical b_star name denotes multi-goal A*, not Berliner's proof-tree B*. Finite nonnegative edges and a finite admissible bound with zero at every goal give an optimal first removed goal (up to floating arithmetic). Admissibility is the caller's responsibility and is not checked. An inconsistent bound is supported: improved vertices reopen. Equal priorities prefer the smaller vertex; equal-cost relaxations retain the first parent. Duplicate goals are allowed. With a consistent bound, O((n+m) log(n+m)) time and O(n+m) storage for m edges; inconsistent bounds can cause exponentially many re-expansions and queued labels. No input mutation or shared state. The expansion count includes the removed goal and repeated expansions, excludes stale queue entries, and is zero only if no entry was expanded. Unreachable results have cost zero and an empty path.
    b_star_search_trace()Records multi-goal A* expansions using the same loop as b_star_search(). All search, tie, reopening and optimality semantics match b_star_search().

    datamunge/algorithms/integer_arithmetic.hpp

    Functions

    int128_text()Convert a signed compiler-supported 128-bit integer to exact decimal text. Handles the minimum signed value without negating it in its signed type. Returns owned locale-independent digits and a leading minus only for negatives. At most 39 division steps plus a sign; independent calls share no mutable state.
    integer_sqrt_u128()Compute the exact floor square root of any unsigned 128-bit integer. Like Python math.isqrt's mathematical contract, with input restricted to the compiler-supported unsigned 128-bit type. Bit-width-bracketed binary search compares by division, never squares a sentinel or converts to floating point. At most63 division comparisons and constant storage for this fixed width; no allocation, mutation or shared state. Zero returns zero and 2^128-1 returns UINT64_MAX. The exclusive upper bound can be 2^64 in the wider type.
    integer_sqrt_u64()Compute floor(sqrt(n)) exactly without floating arithmetic or squared overflow. Binary search uses division comparisons over [0,2^32), taking at most 32 iterations and constant storage. Accepts every uint64, including zero and UINT64_MAX; does not mutate shared state or allocate.
    uint128_text()Convert an unsigned compiler-supported 128-bit integer to exact decimal text. Returns owned digits with no padding or locale dependence. Zero gives "0"; all 128-bit patterns are supported. At most 39 division steps and 39 digits; independent calls share no mutable state.
