    Classes

    InverseIterationOptionsFixed solve count and optional complete-input/retained-vector ceilings. No residual-based early stopping: iterations means exactly that many solves. Zero disables either optional size cap, but zero iterations requests only the normalized start and its Rayleigh diagnostics, without factorization. Complete n*(iterations+1) retained-vector admission precedes numerical work for traces. Caps exclude borrowed input, working LU, scalar metadata, vector capacity and byte/peak RAM. Ordinary runs ignore max_history_values.
    InverseIterationRunFinal pair and actual selected work from one execution. Does not retain input or any intermediate vectors. No shared mutable state. Exactly one LU factorization when iterations>0, otherwise zero; each solve uses that same fixed-shift LU. Diagnostics do not count as inverse solves.
    InverseIterationStepOne actual normalized iterate and its original-matrix diagnostics. All values and vector entries are owned. Residual uses the stored double vector and Rayleigh value; relative_residual divides by (Frobenius(A)+abs(value))*norm(vector), or is zero for a zero denominator. These are numerical backward-error diagnostics, not a convergence guarantee.
    InverseIterationTraceActual chronological normalized iterates from the producing loop. Includes step zero and every completed solve; no repeated-prefix replay. All vectors are owned, and final run diagnostics match the last step.

    Functions

    inverse_iteration()Estimate an eigenpair by a fixed shift and an equal-entry start. Borrowed finite nonempty square A is unchanged. Intended for real symmetric A: convergence to a uniquely nearest eigenvalue requires a nonzero starting component in its eigenspace. Repeated/equidistant eigenvalues, absent start components and nonsymmetric matrices have no such guarantee. Eigenvector sign is arbitrary. Defaults to 50 solves. Zero iterations returns initial diagnostics; negative counts are invalid. Uses one extended-precision partial-pivot LU, robust norm normalization and the Rayleigh quotient divided by x^T*x. Unlike the old implementation, exact zero pivots throw rather than silently regularizing. Rounded near-singular matrices need not have exact zero pivots; residuals must be inspected. Output may differ from the old double elimination. Time O(n^3+k*n^2), workspace O(n^2), without a retained history.
    inverse_iteration_run()Run fixed-shift inverse iteration with optional custom start and selected work. Same numerical semantics/errors as inverse_iteration(). Empty start selects equal positive entries; a supplied finite matching nonzero vector is normalized. Input/start are borrowed only during the call. Complete order admission precedes matrix reads/copying; max_history_values is ignored. No symmetry check or convergence assertion. Extended-precision LU is platform dependent. No mutation or shared state. O(n^3+k*n^2) time, O(n^2) workspace and O(n) returned vector.
    inverse_iteration_trace()Capture each actual fixed-shift iterate including the normalized start. Uses the same producing kernel as inverse_iteration_run(), with complete (iterations+1)*n retained-vector admission before copying/factorization. Zero cap disables this optional ceiling; size arithmetic remains checked. No partial trace returns on failure. Scalars, final duplicate vector, capacity, LU/input and byte/peak RAM are excluded from the vector-entry ceiling. Additional O(k*n) retained entries; no reruns of shorter prefixes.

    iterative_deepening_dfs()Find a shallowest directed unweighted path by iterative deepening. Runs limits zero through min(max_depth,n-1), stopping on the first goal. Retains original per-source arc order, duplicates and self loops. Current-path membership blocks only cycles, never globally marks a vertex across branches. Thus shortest edge depth is guaranteed; weighted cost is not optimized. Empty n/invalid terminals/endpoints are rejected, including unused arcs even for start==goal. Equal terminals produce [start] in the limit-zero pass. Explicit heap frames avoid recursive call-stack growth. Full graph storage O(n+E), membership O(n), active frames O(min(depth,n)), and pass summaries O(min(max_depth,n)) are separate from optional events/input copies. Work can be exponential in permitted simple prefixes. On a complete b-ary tree the visit sum is sum_(k=0)^d (d-k+1)*b^k; constant overhead claims require b>1.     iterative_deepening_dfs_trace()Capture actual directed depth-limited passes and transitions. Runs limits zero through min(max_depth,n-1), stopping on the first goal. Retains original per-source arc order, duplicates and self loops. Current-path membership blocks only cycles, never globally marks a vertex across branches. Thus shortest edge depth is guaranteed; weighted cost is not optimized. Empty n/invalid terminals/endpoints are rejected, including unused arcs even for start==goal. Equal terminals produce [start] in the limit-zero pass. Explicit heap frames avoid recursive call-stack growth. Full graph storage O(n+E), membership O(n), active frames O(min(depth,n)), and pass summaries O(min(max_depth,n)) are separate from optional events/input copies. Work can be exponential in permitted simple prefixes. On a complete b-ary tree the visit sum is sum_(k=0)^d (d-k+1)*b^k; constant overhead claims require b>1. Counters exclude validation, graph construction, comparisons, allocation and copying. No caller mutation, retained references or shared state.

    Types and constants

    DeepeningEventKindenum Actual chronological transition kind in a depth-limited search. Goal stops before its adjacency and leaves the successful stack active; no synthetic leave events are added. Cutoff means a non-goal entry at the limit, even if that vertex has no outgoing arcs. Examine precedes the cycle decision.

    Classes

    ItpOptionsIndependent tolerances, projection allowance and optional retained-record ceiling. Fixed kappa2=2 and kappa1=0.2/initial_width. extra_iterations=n0 allows n_half+n0 projection trials in exact arithmetic; only n0=0 has bisection's worst-case trial bound. This is not a floating interval certificate. A zero residual tolerance disables that test; callback zeros still stop. max_records is an online scalar-record count, admitted before each candidate callback; zero disables it and untraced runs ignore it. Excludes endpoints, capacities, callback-owned storage and byte/peak RAM. No partial trace returns on error.
    ItpRunFinal ITP summary, bracket, actual callbacks and theoretical trial allowance. Terminal endpoints contain the root only under continuity/reliable-sign assumptions. Endpoint/candidate zeros collapse them. Residual acceptance can leave a wide bracket. No retained callable/input references or shared state.
    ItpStepOne actual pre-update bracket and evaluated candidate in the producing loop. projected=true means a projection trial; false is a terminal midpoint call, whose interpolation/truncation/projection fields are zero and unused. Wide scalars avoid double span/product overflow where long double has extra range; precision/range remain platform dependent. radius is max(x-lower,upper-x), not always half the width. All snapshots are owned scalars.
    ItpTraceOwned same-execution scalar history and final ITP diagnostics. No callback replay or repeated shorter runs. Endpoints are not step records; every actual projected/final-midpoint candidate call has one record.

    Functions

    itp()Solve a finite sign-changing bracket with the historical combined tolerance. Uses the same checked kernel as itp_run(), x_tolerance=tol and residual_tolerance=tol, fixed kappa2=2, scaled kappa1=0.2/initial_width, n0=1. Unlike the old blanket claim, its exact-arithmetic worst case allows one extra projection trial over bisection. Rounded near-boundary arithmetic may stop at a projection/precision limit instead of claiming convergence. Inputs are ordered internally; same-sign endpoints return failed defaults, callback zero endpoints return immediately. Continuity and accurate callback signs are unchecked assumptions. Callback zeros/residuals need not certify a mathematical root or coordinate accuracy. Original signature/layout retained; safer wide arithmetic and consistent guards can change last digits/counts. No input mutation, retained callback or shared state; callback side effects and exceptions remain the caller's. O(K+N_half+1) scalar work plus at most K+3 callback calls, constant auxiliary storage, no history.
    itp_run()Run checked ITP with separate coordinate/residual criteria and no history. Same finite/sign/rounding/ownership/numerical policies as itp(). Options expose n0 and independent stopping; no derivative or monotonicity is required. Fixed kappa2=2 and kappa1=0.2/initial_width. Reported residual uses an actual callback; neither continuity nor reliable signs can be checked. A final midpoint callback is additional to the projection-trial budget. max_records is ignored. No mutation, retained references or shared state; independent calls except caller-owned callback state. O(K+N_half+1) scalar work plus callback costs, constant storage. Bounds apply in exact arithmetic, not as an independently rounded interval certificate.
    itp_stop_name()Return a stable program-lifetime literal for an ITP stopping reason. No allocation/mutation/shared state; unknown enum values return "unknown".
    itp_trace()Capture actual I/T/P stages and all terminal-midpoint candidate calls. Same numerical and callback policies as itp_run(). Each actual candidate record is admitted before its callback; max_records=0 disables this optional scalar-record cap. No partial result returns on errors; callback side effects already executed persist. Untraced runs ignore the cap. Additional O(K) history storage, excluding endpoints, capacities, callback storage and byte peak RAM. All snapshots are owned; no solve replay or retained callable.

    Types and constants

    ItpStopenum Actual ITP stopping reason, not an independently certified root claim. Continuity and reliable callback signs remain caller assumptions.

Counts exclude flag workspace, scalar summaries, vector/string capacities, and byte/peak RAM; the byte count admits borrowed inputs and their trace copies once, not as a total allocation quota. No partial trace on failure.
    JaroWinklerRunActual Jaro ingredients, unconditional prefix score and selected work. No input ownership/references. Scores are numerical similarities, not identity probabilities or a metric distance. Odd ordered-mismatch counts retain a half-integer t=mismatches/2, not integer division. Bytes are case sensitive, include NUL/high bytes, and receive no Unicode decoding or normalization.
    JaroWinklerTraceOwned original bytes and chronological events from the producing loop. Inputs are copied once for a self-contained trace, preserving NUL/high bytes. No repeated-prefix scoring or reconstructed matching decisions. Events cover candidate slots, ordered comparisons and actual prefix tests in execution order.
    JaroWinklerWorkSelected actual inspections, excluding bounds/arithmetic/flag writes/allocation. Candidate slots include occupied skips, which do not execute byte equality. Order tests equal matched count; prefix tests include a terminating mismatch. These are logical operations, not physical memory/cache accesses or time.

    Functions

    jaro_similarity()Compute raw-byte Jaro similarity using the original left-to-right greedy rule. Each first-string byte takes the leftmost still-unmatched equal second byte within window max(floor(max length/2)-1,0). Compare the two matched sequences in their own original index order; t is half their disagreement count. Returns0 if no window matches, even when equal bytes occur outside windows; both empty gives1, one empty0. No case folding, Unicode decoding, normalization or C-string termination at NUL. No input mutation, retained references or shared state. Shares the traced kernel but omits prefix inspections/history. O(n+m+n*min(m,2w+1)) work and O(n+m) flag workspace for nonempty inputs; empty exits allocate no flags. Original signature/arithmetic order preserved; overflow-safe window bounds replace unchecked i+window+1.
    jaro_winkler_run()Return both byte-based scores, actual ingredients and work without history. Same retained matching/score/scale policy as jaro_winkler_similarity(). Complete combined input byte admission precedes flags/reads, optional max_events ignored. No copied inputs, mutation, retained references or shared state. O(n+m) flag workspace; quadratic worst-case candidate work, plus at most four prefix tests.
    jaro_winkler_similarity()Compute the retained unconditional raw-byte Winkler prefix refinement. Returns j+l*p*(1-j) for capped byte prefix l<=4. This implementation has no boost threshold. Finite p in[0,.25] is now required before any allocation, correcting previously unbounded/nonfinite outputs. This domain ensures a convex combination with1; at p=.25, a shared four-byte prefix can yield1 for unequal strings. Default p=.1 retains all legacy valid-p arithmetic. Same byte/matching/workspace/ownership policies as jaro_similarity(), plus at most four actual prefix byte tests. No identity/probability guarantee.
    jaro_winkler_trace()Capture actual candidate, order and prefix inspections without scoring replay. Uses the same producing kernel as jaro_winkler_run(). Owns complete input bytes and scalar records; no retained caller references. Complete byte cap precedes copying/flags; each actual event is admitted before its inspection. Zero optional caps disable them; count/container checks remain. No partial output returns on failure. Additional O(E+n+m) owned trace data for E events; default event ceiling one million, not a byte/peak-RAM bound.

    Types and constants

    JaroWinklerPhaseenum Phase of one actual Jaro/Winkler inspection. No hidden matching replay; candidate means a visited window slot, order means comparison of matched byte sequences, prefix means an actual prefix test.

Seed/Pop use u=v; Restore uses u=source. Infinity denotes an absent old label only; finite arithmetic results are checked. After records the committed value.

These limits exclude vector capacities, allocator overhead, byte counts and peak RAM.

Passes include a final unchanged pass. Matrix cells count n*n initialization; restored_cells counts reachable entries only. All counters are checked.

    Functions

    johnson_all_pairs_shortest_paths()Compute directed all-pairs paths by zero-source potentials and lazy binary heaps. Accepts finite weights, loops, parallel edges and disconnected vertices. All h start at zero, equivalent to an implicit zero-edge source reaching every vertex. In-place input-order Bellman-Ford runs at most n passes; a decrease on pass n detects a global negative cycle. Otherwise edges must have nonnegative reduced weight. Each source uses a lazy priority queue ordered by (distance,vertex), strict decreases, input adjacency order and stale-key rejection; restore with d=d'-h[source]+h[target]. Matrix output is owned; input/shared state unchanged. Work O(n*n+n*m+n*(m+1)*log(m+2)), including matrix and all source seeds; O(n*n+n+m) storage plus O(m+1) heap. Lazy parallel edges explain log(m+2). Arithmetic uses long double, rejecting nonfinite intermediates, negative reduced weights and restored results outside finite double range; finite underflow on conversion may round to zero. No tolerance/clamping/exact-real cycle guarantee is promised. Wider arithmetic can change last bits versus the old double kernel.
    johnson_analyze()Compute Johnson paths and selected work without event history. Uses the same kernel/contracts/arithmetic as johnson_all_pairs_shortest_paths(). Complete finite validation precedes n+m/n*n admission and matrix allocation. max_events is ignored. Owned potentials/reduced edges add O(n+m) output.
    johnson_trace()Capture actual potential/edge/heap/restore operations from the shared kernel. Same numeric and complete-admission contracts as johnson_analyze(). Copies the original edges only after admission. Each event is admitted before its operation; a failed call throws and exposes no partial result. Trace adds O(K+m) storage.

    datamunge/algorithms/jump_point_search.hpp

    Functions

    jump_point_search()Find an optimal unit-cost four-neighbor route, compressing only straight corridors. The historical name denotes this corridor-jump A* variant, NOT the full symmetry-pruning rules of published Jump Point Search. Coordinates are (row,column), true cells blocked. Each ray stops at the goal, a possible perpendicular turn/junction, or its last cell before a wall/boundary. Thus intermediate junctions are retained, correcting the old ray-to-wall shortcut that could miss paths. A shortest path cannot turn inside a degree-two straight corridor, so replacing it by a length-weighted edge preserves cost. Manhattan is consistent on these macro edges. Lazy heap ties prefer row-major cell id; directions are down,up,right,left, and equal-cost parents are retained. Output restores every unit step with both endpoints. Blocked/out-of-bounds endpoints return empty/zero/false; empty or ragged grids throw. Start=goal on a free cell returns one coordinate and zero cost. Caller data are unchanged; output is owned, all state local, concurrent calls independent. Dimensions and total cells must fit int; arithmetic/priorities use checked bounds and uint64. Worst-case O(N*L+N*log(N+1)) work for N cells and maximum ray length L, O(N) labels/heap/output storage. Open rooms retain every turn opportunity, so this variant promises neither open-room symmetry pruning nor a speedup.

    k_medoids()Fit Euclidean medoids using random distinct initialization and full best-swap scans. Nonempty positive-dimensional matched finite rows and0<k<=n required. Seeded std::shuffle(mt19937_64) chooses initial identities, not PAM's greedy BUILD. Each scan visits slots then original non-medoids, retaining a proposal only if its rounded cost beats the running incumbent by absolute1e-12. Commit the last retained proposal and recompute its assignment once. Stop on no improvement or max_iterations accepted scans. Zero iterations returns initialization. No global-optimum or outlier-invariance guarantee; distances are Euclidean only. Widened subtraction/hypot avoids raw squared overflow/underflow; final distances and sequential objective are finite doubles or throw. Ordinary last-bit costs can differ from the historical squared-double norm. std::shuffle seed mapping is standard-library-specific. O(n*n*d+I*k*(n-k)*n*k) work and O(n*n+n*d) stored matrix/input geometry (input borrowed); no optional trace copies/shared state.

No partial trace escapes failure; scalar API has neither optional ceiling. Trace cost adds owned input/state/history copies to kernel work.

A zero iteration limit returns the random initialization.

    datamunge/algorithms/kabsch.hpp

    Classes

    KabschAnalysisOwned same-execution paired fit, normalized covariance/key matrix and actual observations. Normalize each input set by its max(1,absolute coordinate), then center in long double. Covariance is the mean outer product in those normalized units. Divide it by covariance_scale to build the dimensionless Horn key matrix; scale zero uses an all-zero key. Eigenvalues are descending and quaternion is the actual normalized principal eigenvector, scalar-first. No second fit or iteration replay. Eigen residual/gap are additional diagnostics, not exact certificates of rank, uniqueness or convergence in exact arithmetic. All vectors own data.
    KabschResultOwned proper-rotation/translation fit mapping source onto corresponding target points. Original field order/types retained. No scale/reflection/permutation fitting. RMSD evaluates the returned double transform on the original paired inputs. Degenerate data can admit multiple equally optimal rotations; one is returned.

    Functions

    kabsch()Fit a proper rigid transform to nonempty finite corresponding point sets. Equal sizes are required, order defines correspondence. Uses Horn's principal quaternion formulation of Kabsch's objective. Independent positive input normalization and long-double mean covariance avoid raw square/product overflow; no additional scale is fitted. A normalized quaternion gives a proper rotation, then t=target_mean-R*source_mean. Numerical degeneracy may choose any optimum; zero covariance chooses the eigensolver's identity basis. Computes residuals using the returned double transform with widened arithmetic and stable incremental RMS norm. Floating normalization/eigensolving are not exact predicates; last bits may differ from the former raw-double kernel. O(n) work, constant-sized eigensolve and O(1) auxiliary storage apart from its fixed-size allocations. Input unchanged, result owned, no shared state.
    kabsch_analyze()Capture actual paired alignment, covariance/key matrix and principal eigensystem once. Same contracts/arithmetic/degenerate conventions as kabsch(). Complete finite validation and pair-count admission precede input/output vector copies. The ceiling counts paired records, not the multiple vectors, bytes/capacities or peak RAM; zero disables the optional cap. O(n) extra owned output, no replay. Residual norms are computed before aligned coordinates are rounded to double, so differ by rounding from norms recomputed on the captured aligned vector.

Does not guarantee exact sums, order independence, a relative-error bound for ill-conditioned cancellation, or sensible compensation after infinity/NaN. No dynamic allocation/shared state.

Values follow normal double IEEE operations; nonfinite values propagate and fast-math reassociation invalidates the method.
    KahanTraceOwned actual one-record-per-value arithmetic and final stream sum. Trace is not a higher-precision sum and retains no input references. O(n) history; optional complete record ceilings exclude capacities/bytes/peak RAM.

    Functions

    kahan_sum()Sum values with the original sequential Kahan correction recurrence. Supports empty input as zero; nonfinite values propagate under ordinary IEEE arithmetic. O(n) work/O(1) storage, no mutation/allocation/shared state. Requires compiler semantics preserving the stated operation order, not unsafe fast-math. Compensation improves many finite sums but need not recover all cancellation losses; a relative bound depends on conditioning sum(abs(x))/abs(sum(x)).
    kahan_trace()Capture actual arithmetic of one Kahan run, not repeated-prefix reconstruction. Complete n admission precedes allocation/updates. Default cap million records; zero disables optional ceiling. No partial trace on failure, owned value copies.

    datamunge/algorithms/karatsuba.hpp

    Classes

    KaratsubaCallActual digit-vector operand lengths, split and result length for one invocation. Calls are entered preorder; parent is an earlier record except root's sentinel parent=size_t max. Low/high/sum roles preserve actual call order. The base case is min(left_digits,right_digits)<=32, Root zero has one digit; recursive zero slices can retain their original widths. No operands/products are re-multiplied to construct the tree.
    KaratsubaOptionsOptional complete input-digit and actual recursion ceilings. Zero disables an optional cap, not size arithmetic. Depth counts root0; a positive ceiling is the largest admitted depth, while0 disables that ceiling. Caps count digits/calls/depth, excluding capacities/temporary vectors/bytes/RAM.
    KaratsubaTraceOwned original operands, actual decimal result and producing recursive call records. Complete original bytes are owned, including leading zeros/empty conventions. Recursion records store lengths/roles rather than full intermediate big integers. O(calls) extra history in addition to kernel digit temporaries and owned input/output.
    KaratsubaWorkSelected actual recursive calls and schoolbook digit products, not total arithmetic/time. Excludes validation, digit additions/subtractions, carries, shifts, copies, allocations and formatting. A zero operand still runs the actual one-digit leaf.

    Functions

    karatsuba_multiply()Multiply unsigned decimal strings with the original crossover32 Karatsuba kernel. Accepts only ASCII digits, with leading zeros normalized; empty is retained as legacy zero. Rejects signs/space/nondecimal bytes. Uses little-endian decimal vectors, splitting at min(lengths)/2; leaf if either length<=32. Computes low, high and sum products, then combines z2*10^(2m)+(zsum-z2-z0)*10^m+z0. Balanced n-digit recurrence gives O(n^log2(3)) arithmetic asymptotically; unequal sizes, crossover/carries and copies must be accounted separately. Conservative live digit storage O((n+m)*log(min(n,m)+2)); no shared state or caller mutation. Legacy optional caps disabled, arithmetic/counters checked.
    karatsuba_trace()Capture the actual recursion tree and selected leaf work from one multiplication. Entire decimal syntax and complete original byte count are checked before normalized digit/owned input copies. Actual calls/depth are admitted at entry, after any caller-created argument temporaries but before that call's body. Failure exposes no partial trace; records never replay multiplication.

    Types and constants

    KaratsubaRoleenum Role of an actual multiplication invocation in its producing parent's three products.

    Classes

    KargerOptionsComplete input/trial ceilings and online owned-history record admission. Zero disables an optional cap, not size arithmetic. History charges n+1 records per contraction snapshot or completed trial partition; edges copied once are covered by complete n+m admission. Capacity/bytes/peak RAM are excluded.
    KargerStepActual selected original edge and owned canonical components after its contraction. Labels are minimum original vertices, not union-find root ids. Crossing list preserves original edge order and parallel multiplicity; chosen_rank is the unbiased accepted word modulo crossing_count. No union/search replay.
    KargerTraceOwned original multigraph, actual contraction histories and every completed trial. No borrowed graph storage or replay. Extra storage O(m+B*n*n) worst case for B trials of n vertices; complete record caps can reject large captures.
    KargerTrialActual completed trial cut/partition and range of contraction records. If no crossing edge remains before two groups, the graph is disconnected; choose component0 against the rest, giving a nontrivial zero cut. First strict best retained on ties; best_changed marks that actual decision.
    KargerWorkSelected actual logical work, excluding validation, union-find internals and trace copies. Edge scans include every original record when rebuilding candidates and counting final cuts, including loops. Random draws include rejected modulo- bias words. Counts are operations, not elapsed time or allocation traffic.
    MinCutResultOwned nontrivial partition and original-edge crossing multiplicity. Undirected parallel edges each count; loops never cross. side_a contains vertex0, both sides sorted. Disconnected graphs may return the exact zero cut. A positive cut is a Monte Carlo candidate, not a proof of optimality. Original legacy field order/types retained.

    Functions

    karger_min_cut()Contract an unweighted undirected multigraph repeatedly and retain the first smallest candidate. Requires n>=2 and in-range endpoints. Loops accepted but never contracted/cut; parallel edges preserve multiplicity. Rebuild crossing list each contraction, sample its rank with mt19937_64 plus rejection to avoid modulo bias, and merge until two groups or no crossing edges. Partition component0 versus others and count original crossings. Independent ideal uniform trials give the classical lower success bound2/(n(n-1)) for connected graphs; a deterministic seeded pseudorandom run is not an observed confidence certificate. Legacy positive trials retained; zero chooses max(1,n*n*ceil(log(n))) with checked arithmetic. Ordinary draw mapping matches the old modulo sampler when no rejection occurs. Expected word work O(B*(n+(n+1)*m*alpha(n))) for B trials using ranked compressed union-find; O(n+m) working/output storage. No input mutation or shared state.
    karger_trace()Capture actual sampled contractions and every trial partition from the shared kernel. Complete endpoint/schedule/input admission precedes graph copies. Before a merge/captured partition, admit its n+1 complete records. Failure throws without exposing partial results. Same sampling/tie/zero-cut contracts as scalar API.

    datamunge/algorithms/karn.hpp

    Classes

    KarnEstimatorEducational Jacobson/Karels RTT smoother with Karn's ambiguity and backoff rules. Clean first sample R sets SRTT=R,RTTVAR=R/2,RTO=3R. Subsequent clean samples update RTTVAR=.75*oldvar+.25*abs(oldSRTT-R), then SRTT=.875*oldSRTT+.125*R, RTO=SRTT+4*RTTVAR. Retransmitted ACKs do nothing; timeouts double current RTO. No timestamp exception, clock granularity, RFC minimum/maximum, TCP sender, packet sequence tracking or scheduling is modeled. Therefore not a complete RFC6298 implementation. Preserves original ordinary-double operation order. Local owned state, no allocation/shared state; mutation requires external synchronization if one instance is used concurrently. Failed updates leave all state unchanged; copied instances evolve independently.
    KarnEventOwned actual pre/post estimator states from one producing transition. Sample is caller-provided for ACK events, zero placeholder for Timeout. No replay, retained input views or inference of network elapsed time.
    KarnStateOwned current RTT smoothing and timeout values in seconds. Uninitialized state has SRTT/variation0 and the positive configured initial RTO. A zero clean sample may produce zero RTO because this educational model has no clock granularity or RFC minimum/maximum clamp. No caller references.

    Types and constants

    KarnActionenum Actual transition category for one accepted API event.

    kmp_prefix_function()Build longest-proper-prefix/suffix lengths of every byte prefix. prefix[i]<=i, with prefix[0]=0. On mismatch fall back through previous prefix entries without backing up i. Empty returns empty; arbitrary embedded NUL/high bytes accepted. O(m) work and owned O(m) output; input unchanged and unretained. Independent calls share no mutable state. This is not Unicode normalization.
    kmp_search()Find all exact byte-string occurrences using the shared KMP prefix/scan kernel. Empty pattern or m>n returns empty without building a prefix table. Otherwise overlapping matches retained in ascending original byte offsets, with no text rewinding. Equality is bytewise, including embedded NUL/high bytes. O(n+m) work, O(m+matches) storage, no input mutation/copies or shared mutable state.

    kmp_search_trace()Capture original bytes and every actual producing prefix/text byte comparison. Same exact byte results and preserved while-then-if comparison order as the scalar kernel.     KMPPhaseenum Producing phase of an actual KMP byte comparison.
    KMPSiteenum Actual comparison site in the preserved while-then-if implementation. While is tested only for positive border length, and a successful while test may be repeated by Extend. Both are actual byte comparisons, not distinct reads.

    datamunge/algorithms/knuth_bendix.hpp

    Classes

    KBRewriteStepOwned actual rule application from deterministic first-rule/leftmost reduction. Rule index is in the original supplied rule order, not an inferred canonical system. before/after strings are actual producing values, not prefix replay.
    KBRewriteTraceOwned actual finite reduction and complete original word/rules. captured_entries counts one initial word, one per input rule and one per application; excludes individual bytes/inner strings/capacities/runtime copies. A trace step stores two whole words, so this record quota is not a byte or peak-memory bound. Rules are validated before copies, and applications admitted before replacement. No second reduction or partial returned trace.
    KnuthBendixResultOwned generated shortlex rules and actual finite completion status. complete=true means the final exhaustive ordered overlap/containment scan joined every critical pair. With strict terminating shortlex rules this gives confluence and a canonical form for the supplied presentation. false means a rule/round ceiling stopped the procedure: equality of reductions is sound, but unequal reductions do not decide inequivalence. Initial rule-limit exits may have processed only a prefix of the supplied equations. No group/monoid finiteness or convergence promise follows from a finite test of words.
    RewriteRuleOwned byte-string rewrite lhs->rhs, required to strictly decrease shortlex for reduction. Shortlex orders length first then std::string lexical order. Equal-length lexical decreases are valid; length need not decrease at every step.

    Functions

    kb_normal_form()Reduce a byte word using the first applicable rule and its leftmost occurrence. Validate every rule first: lhs must be nonempty and strictly greater than rhs in shortlex. This rejects identity/increasing/cyclic rules that could hang the historical unchecked reducer. Termination follows from strict well-founded shortlex descent, including equal-length lexical steps. For arbitrary valid nonconfluent rules the result depends on rule order and is not canonical. Work depends on actual replacements and std::string::find/replace costs, not simply original length. O(max word length) runtime copies; no trace or quota. Caller word/rules unchanged; returned string owns bytes, embedded NUL allowed.
    kb_rewrite_trace()Capture every actual first-rule/leftmost shortlex reduction application once. Same complete rule validation, byte order and termination as kb_normal_form(). Complete initial word/rule count admitted before copies; each application admitted before replacement. Adds owned before/after whole-word histories; record quota excludes their bytes and is not a resource/time guarantee.
    knuth_bendix()Attempt finite shortlex Knuth–Bendix completion of byte-string equations. Orient nontrivial equations by length then std::string lexical order. Empty strings represent identity; empty-equals-empty is ignored. Interreduce rules, then examine ordered suffix/prefix overlaps and contained lhs occurrences on a stable round snapshot. Normalize each pair under the actual growing rules, adding an oriented equation when unequal. Stops complete only after a full no-addition scan; rule ceiling and fixed2000-round guard return incomplete. max_rules must be positive; no result contains more rules than that ceiling. Resource work may be very large: completion is not guaranteed to terminate without ceilings, and these rule/round caps do not bound pairs/word bytes/time. Inputs unchanged, result owns rules, no shared mutable state. Rules strictly decrease shortlex, not necessarily length. Normal forms are canonical only when complete, not merely because finitely many words appeared to agree.

    kosaraju_analyze()Return actual component labels and selected producing work from the shared two-pass kernel. Same checked input, deterministic ordering and O(n+E) contracts as kosaraju_scc(). No original graph/history capture or optional capture quota.
    kosaraju_scc()Partition a finite directed multigraph into strongly connected components by two DFS passes. Require n>=0, exactly n adjacency rows and every target in[0,n), validated before vertex access. Empty graph returns empty. Parallel edges/loops allowed. First DFS uses ascending roots and caller adjacency order, recording exits; transpose rows follow original source order. Second iterative DFS follows reverse finish order and original stack push order, assigning on discovery. Preserves historical valid-input labels and member discovery order. Complete input/count/optional quota admitted before copies/evaluation. No second interpolation or reconstructed products; all histories own their data.

    lagrange_analyze()Return the actual direct interpolation value and selected producing work without history. Same validation/arithmetic/finite-intermediate and O(n*n) contracts as lagrange_interpolate(); no input copies, optional quota or repeated evaluation.
    lagrange_interpolate()Evaluate the direct Lagrange interpolating polynomial at a finite query. Require matched finite x/y arrays and pairwise distinct x values, including signed-zero equality; nodes may be unsorted. Empty returns historical0, even though it does not define a unique polynomial. Query must be finite even then. For each j, start term=y[j], multiply(x-x[k])/(x[j]-x[k]) in original k order, then add to double sum. Preserve ordinary finite-difference arithmetic/order; if either subtraction is nonfinite, compute both differences/ratio in long double then round ratio once. Ratio, every product and every sum must remain finite double or throw: this is not a robust solver for all finite data. No exact-node shortcut/barycentric caching, conditioning guarantee or error estimate. O(n*n) work including duplicate validation, O(1) kernel state beyond borrowed inputs; no optional history/quota/mutation/shared state.

Complete n*n+2*n record count is checked before original copies and full history allocation; default million-entry optional quota, zero disables only that ceiling. O(n*n) owned capture; quota counts records rather than bytes/peak memory.

    datamunge/algorithms/lanczos_analysis.hpp

    Classes

    LanczosRitzAnalysisOwned actual native tridiagonal eigensystem and explicit full-matrix Ritz diagnostics. values are descending native Jacobi approximations; coefficients[j][i] is mode i's coefficient of actual basis vector V[j]. vectors[i] is the formed full Ritz vector. Residuals explicitly evaluate A*y-theta*y, rather than using only terminal_beta*last_coefficient, which omits reorthogonalization/roundoff defects. Orthogonality/projection errors are observed widened maxima, not exact certificates or evidence the supplied result originated from A.

    Functions

    lanczos_demo_matrix()Recreate the original30-by30 symmetric matrix using its exact32-bit LCG fixture. Start uint32 state2024; update s=1103515245*s+12345 modulo2^32 for upper triangle row order; value=((s>>16)%1000)/500.0-1; mirror to lower triangle. Synthetic deterministic fixture, not a random-matrix distribution claim.
    lanczos_ritz_analysis()Form the actual T eigensystem and explicitly evaluate full Ritz vectors/residuals. Complete finite exactly symmetric A, compatible finite actual basis/alpha/beta shapes and mode quota checked before allocations. Does not validate provenance or require exact orthogonality. Uses native Jacobi on T(tolerance1e-13,100 sweeps), forms y=sum_j V[j]*q[j] with widened sums rounded to double, then computes actual residual/norm/Gram/projection diagnostics in long double. No Lanczos rerun or prefix replay. Requires nonzero formed vectors; no universal spectral approximation/convergence guarantee. O(m*n*n+n*m*m+m^3) dense work and O(n*m+m*m) owned/runtime diagnostic storage; max_modes is a count, not bytes/peak RAM.

    LanczosResultOwned producing tridiagonal coefficients and basis vectors, preserving legacy field layout. V[j] is basis vector j, not matrix row j of Q. The leading m=alpha.size() diagonal and first m-1 beta entries define T. Historical beta may additionally contain the actual terminal residual norm on early stop when requested steps exceeded m; that extra value is not a T off-diagonal. No eigenvalues computed.
    LanczosStepOwned actual matrix-product, three-term and final reorthogonalized residual boundaries. Full vectors are producing snapshots, not repeated prefix runs. alpha and beta_previous are actual recurrence values; residual_norm follows the one full reorthogonalization pass and controls the absolute stopping decision.
    LanczosTraceOwned complete original matrix/start, actual output/stages and same-execution selected work. captured_entries counts n*n+n original scalar values, then1+3*n per step and one record per projection. Excludes original row records, scalar fields, result basis/coefficients, runtime copies/capacities/bytes/RAM. Admit complete original geometry before copies, each step before matrix work and each projection before its inner product. No replay or partial returned trace.
    LanczosWorkSelected actual dense Lanczos operations, excluding validation/copies/allocation/time. dot_products counts alpha and reorthogonalization inner products, excluding sum-of-squares norm work. matrix_products counts actual scalar A*v products. Full reorthogonalization is one sequential pass over all current basis vectors.

    Functions

    lanczos_iteration()Build a symmetric Krylov basis and tridiagonal coefficients with full reorthogonalization. Validate a finite square exactly symmetric A, matched finite b and m>=0 before access/allocation. Empty returns empty; m0 returns empty; exact zero b returns empty. Nonzero tiny starts are normalized using a widened norm fallback instead of the old absolute1e-300 rejection. Iterate at most min(m,n), retaining actual full basis, alpha and historical beta layout. For each v compute A*v, alpha, subtract alpha*v+previous_beta*previous_v, then one Gram pass over all stored basis vectors. Stop at absolute residual norm<1e-12, requested steps or full dimension; absolute tolerance is not scale invariant or spectral convergence. Ordinary finite double sum/dot/norm operation order is retained. If initial/ residual sum of squares is nonfinite or underflows to zero for a nonzero vector, use widened hypot; all produced components/coefficients/norms must fit finite double or throw. No guarantee for every finite ill-conditioned/huge input. Dense work O(m*n*n+n*m*m), full-basis O(n*m) output/runtime storage, not a constant-memory three-term-only method. No input mutation/shared state/history quota; rounded reorthogonalization is not an exact orthogonality certificate.
    lanczos_trace()Capture original inputs and actual producing Lanczos stages/Gram coefficients once. Same validation/numerical/ordering/stopping contracts as lanczos_iteration(). Complete input and online step/projection admission follow LanczosTrace; adds owned O(n*n+n*m+m*m) capture beyond the actual result/runtime storage.

    Functions

    lanczos_kernel_weight()Evaluate sinc(distance)*sinc(distance/a) on the open window abs(distance).
    lanczos_resample()Reconstruct every complete finite query through the shared raw window producer. Validate complete nonempty finite samples, all positions and integer geometry before output/evaluation. Empty positions returns empty after validation. Same raw border/integer/nonfinite policies as lanczos_resample_at(); no per-query input copying/validation repetition. O(n+queries*a) work/output.
    lanczos_resample_analyze()Return actual producing raw sums/work and optionally normalize by the actual weight sum. Same validated window/index/arithmetic producer as lanczos_resample_at(). Normalization is an explicit additional mode, never silently changes raw API. Does not remove negative-lobe ringing or implement an antialiasing prefilter. O(n+a) including validation, no optional capture/input copies or replay.
    lanczos_resample_at()Reconstruct one finite query from finite nonempty uniformly indexed samples in raw mode. Clamp the query position to[0,n-1], then examine virtual integer taps floor(p)-a+1 through floor(p)+a, clamping each stored lookup to[0,n-1]. Sum sample*kernel in ascending virtual order. This intentionally retains the unnormalized legacy interior formula: finite kernel weights need not sum1, so constants can have phase-dependent gain. Exact integer queries preserve numeric sample values using explicit integral sinc zeros. Corrects the old outside-position comment/implementation mismatch and unsafe empty/nonfinite casts; huge finite outside positions safely return the border value. No low-pass cutoff adjustment for downsampling, universal superiority to linear interpolation, monotonicity, DC normalization or alias-free claim. Require2*a representable and n-1+a<=min(PTRDIFF_MAX,2^53-1) before integer indexing. Finite raw products/sums required or throw. O(n+a) work including complete sample validation, O(1) query state, no input copies/history/shared state.

    Classes

    LaxWendroffAnalysisOwned actual final grid, computed Courant coefficient and selected same-execution work. allow_unstable records explicit opt-in to abs(Courant)>1, not a stability certificate. Ordinary API and default analysis enforce the CFL domain.
    LaxWendroffCellOwned actual old-state stencil and producing new value for one periodic cell. General terms give value=center-advective_term+diffusive_term, with actual double terms widened for storage or actual widened fallback terms. Copy paths have unused term placeholders0 and use the identified original operand directly. Every cell reads the complete old state, never a previously updated new value.
    LaxWendroffStateActual complete-state time, mass, L2 and extrema observations. Time/mass/L2 use long double arithmetic and are observations, not exact conservation/stability/positivity certificates. L2=sqrt(dx*sum(u*u)).
    LaxWendroffTraceOwned complete original/every actual state, producing stencils and explicit diagnostics. states[0] is original input, followed by every real completed step; no prefix reruns. captured_entries=n+1+steps*(2*n+1): original n values/diagnostic, then n next-state values, one diagnostic and n cell records per step. Excludes fields/capacities/final-result/runtime copies and bytes/RAM. Complete count and quota admitted before copies/evaluation, default million, zero off.
    LaxWendroffWorkSelected actual stencil/update work, excluding validation, copying, allocation and time. stencil_reads counts the three original operand point identities initialized per cell, not physical machine loads. diagnostics_cells counts additional trace-only state observations; ordinary/count-only calls retain0 there.

    Functions

    lax_wendroff_advection()Advect a finite nonempty periodic grid through checked second-order Lax–Wendroff steps. Require finite speed, positive finite dx, nonnegative finite dt, nsteps>=0 and computed abs(a*dt/dx)<=1. Complete input/work geometry checked before copies. Each full old-state update is u[j]-.5*nu*(right-left)+.5*nu*nu*(right-2*u[j]+left). Preserve ordinary finite double formula order. If intermediates are nonfinite, evaluate the same terms in long double and require finite double output. Computed nu0 copies center exactly; nu+1 copies wrapped left and nu-1 wrapped right, avoiding cancellation and making numeric unit-Courant shifts exact. Courant multiplication uses widened fallback if ordinary product/ratio is nonfinite. Zero steps returns original after complete validation. Exact periodic mass conservation and L2 stability do not imply positivity, monotonicity, no ringing or exact floating-point conservation. Second-order consistency requires sufficiently smooth solutions; shocks/steps can oscillate. O(n+nsteps*n) work/O(n) runtime/output, no mutation/history/shared state.
    lax_wendroff_amplification()Compute the periodic Lax–Wendroff Fourier symbol1-i*nu*sin(theta)+nu^2*(cos(theta)-1). Pure analytic reference, not measured solver work or a convergence certificate. Finite coefficients/angle required; unstable nu is allowed for explicit theory controls. abs(G)<=1 for all theta in exact arithmetic when abs(nu)<=1.
    lax_wendroff_analyze()Return actual periodic updates/Courant/work, with explicit optional unstable-control mode. Same finite/geometry/arithmetic contracts as lax_wendroff_advection(). Default enforces CFL; allow_unstable=true explicitly permits abs(nu)>1 for controlled diagnostics, while finite produced values remain mandatory. No input/history copies or state diagnostics, no optional capture quota or prefix reruns.
    lax_wendroff_trace()Capture every actual periodic state, stencil decision and widened state diagnostic once. Same shared producer/explicit CFL policy as lax_wendroff_analyze(). Complete n+1+nsteps*(2*n+1) quota admitted before input/history copies or numerical work. Adds O(nsteps*n) owned observation and diagnostic work beyond the runtime state. No prefix replay or partial returned trace; quota counts records, not peak bytes.

    Types and constants

    LaxWendroffCellKindenum Actual producing arithmetic path used for one periodic advection cell.

    linde_buzo_gray()Fit a checked multiplicative-split, finite-budget generalized Lloyd codebook. Initial center is the global mean. Double via c*(1-epsilon),c*(1+epsilon) until size>=request, preserving the historical rounded-up behavior. Lloyd assigns to earliest nearest center, then updates nonempty means; empty centers retain their values. After at least two passes, stop if previous pre-update distortion minus current pre-update distortion is strictly less than tol*(previous+1e-12), otherwise cap iterations. Final nearest pass at each size makes output labels/objective consistent with returned centroids. Ordinary finite double order retained; centroid sums have widened fallback. Zero-centroid multiplicative splitting may never separate symmetric data. No global optimum, distinct/used centers, nested codebooks, across-size monotonicity, or general convergence/quality guarantee. Empty data valid. Typical O(I*n*K*d) producing work; no input mutation or shared state.

    Functions

    biconjugate_gradient() ×2The biconjugate gradient (BiCG) method: extends conjugate gradient to non-symmetric systems by running two coupled recurrences – one with A and a shadow one with A^T – that keep the residuals bi-orthogonal. It needs no symmetry or definiteness, at the cost of two matrix-vector products per step (one by A, one by A^T) and the risk of breakdown. Like CG it terminates in at most n steps in exact arithmetic.
    conjugate_gradient()Checked dense conjugate gradient for a symmetric positive-definite system. Full finite/square/size and exact stored symmetry validation precedes solving. Positive definiteness is a precondition, not certified: encountered nonpositive curvature returns unconverged. Starts at zero and uses inclusive absolute recomputed residual stopping, including initially. Norms/inner products widen to long double; vector assignments round to checked double. Two products per completed step include a true-residual check. Recursive convergence without true convergence returns unconverged; conjugate_gradient_solve() exposes why. Exact-arithmetic n-step termination is not a floating guarantee. O(kn²) work, O(n) scratch, no input mutation; original result fields/signature are preserved.
    gauss_jordan()Checked legacy full augmented Gauss–Jordan reduction with partial pivoting. Validates all finite square rows and matching finite RHS before indexing or inverse allocation; by-value argument copies can precede validation. Preserves strict earliest pivot ties, absolute pivot test <1e-12 (equality accepted), and ordered full-block double divisions/updates. Failure is not a rank or conditioning certificate: uniform scaling can change acceptance. Empty valid input succeeds. Stored nonfinite arithmetic throws; rounding/underflow and inaccurate inverses remain possible. O(n³) time/O(n²) storage. The explicit identity block adds arithmetic cost; no caller mutation or shared state.
    gauss_seidel()Checked forward in-place Gauss-Seidel from a zero initial iterate. Validates full finite square shape, matching RHS, nonzero diagonal and controls before any sweep. Uses the newest coordinates with widened sums and checked double assignments. Inclusive absolute recomputed residual stopping; empty/zero RHS can converge without a sweep. General matrices need not converge. O(kn²) time and O(n) scratch; no input mutation. Layout/signature remain unchanged.
    gaussian_elimination()Checked legacy Gaussian elimination with earliest-tie partial pivoting. Full square shapes, matching RHS and finite entries are validated before indexing or arithmetic (by-value argument copies can precede validation). Preserves original ordered double operations and absolute pivot test <1e-12; equality is accepted. A cutoff failure returns solved=false/empty x and is not a rank certificate: uniform scaling can change acceptance. Empty valid input succeeds. Nonfinite stored arithmetic throws; roundoff/underflow and element growth remain possible. O(n³) time/O(n²) owned storage, no caller mutation.

    Types and constants

    LinearOperatortype A linear map \(v\mapsto Mv\) supplied as a function, for matrix-free solvers.

    datamunge/algorithms/lis.hpp

    Classes

    LISAnalysisOwned actual deterministic strict-LIS values, source indices and producing work.
    LISInsertionOwned real frontier indices before/after one original value and its actual predecessor link.
    LISProbeOne actual lower-bound comparison against the real current frontier.
    LISTraceOwned original integers, final actual predecessor/frontier arrays and every producing search/update record. Input/predecessor2*n records admitted before copies; each actual probe and insertion record plus before/after frontier members admitted before append, final-tail records before ownership transfer. Complete result or exception. Default million actual records,0 optional cap off; excludes scalar fields, capacities/output/runtime copies and bytes/RAM. Frontier snapshots can take quadratic capture storage despite O(n log n) ordinary producing work.
    LISWorkActual selected strict-LIS binary search, tail updates and witness reconstruction work. Excludes guards/copies/allocation/capture, elapsed time and CPU instructions.

    Functions

    lis_analyze()Return the actual optimal strict-LIS witness, original identities and selected producing work. Same tie, strictness, reconstruction and complete input contracts as the legacy values-only API; no optional frontier/probe history or replay.
    lis_trace()Capture every real minimal-tail comparison/frontier update and actual predecessor state once. Shared producer, no report-side search or index recovery. Actual record quota is checked before copies/appends; failures return no partial result.
    longest_increasing_subsequence()Return one strictly increasing longest integer subsequence with historical deterministic ties. Minimal-tail frontier uses lower_bound on strict<: equal incoming values replace the existing class and do not extend length. Each new parent points to the preceding class's actual earlier identity. Reconstruct from the last tail through those real links. Frontier values are not a witness by themselves. O(n log(n+1)) time/O(n) runtime, no mutation or shared state; no claim of a lexicographically smallest, earliest-index or unique optimal witness.

    datamunge/algorithms/ll1_parser.hpp

    Classes

    LL1BuildWorkActual selected monotone fixed-point and predictive-table construction counts.
    LL1ConflictOwned actual conflicting table-cell witness, with earliest retained and new production identities. Conflicted models remain inspectable but parsing refuses them. Duplicate indexed productions can also conflict; no silent arbitrary-choice recognizer.
    LL1ParseAnalysisActual predictive-parser status and selected real action/input/stack counts.
    LL1ParseEventOwned actual stack/input decision before and after one real parser action.
    LL1ParserOwn a checked grammar, its actual FIRST/FOLLOW predictive table and explicit cell-conflict witnesses. A symbol is nonterminal exactly when used as a production lhs. Grammar start must be a defined nonterminal; lhs/rhs symbols cannot be empty or "$"; epsilon is an empty rhs vector, not a literal empty token. All production indices must fit int. FIRST/FOLLOW use finite monotone insertion fixed points; build work is grammar dependent, not a claimed constant-time preprocessing step. Retain earliest production per table cell and record actual conflicting later indices. is_ll1() means this indexed construction has no conflicts, including duplicate-rule IDs; conflicted models are inspectable but parsing throws. Parsing consumes complete finite string tokens, no lexing/backtracking/error recovery. Explicit action budget separates incomplete computation from a syntax rejection. Owned model has no borrowed grammar lifetime/shared state; independent const inference is safe when no caller mutates the object.
    LL1ParseTraceOwned complete original tokens, native initial stack and every actual bounded parse action. Complete actual run until accept/reject/step budget, or capture exception; budget exhaustion is explicitly represented and not a silent rejection. Capture cap counts original token symbols,2 initial stack symbols and each event record plus actual before/after stack symbols. String characters, scalar fields/capacities/runtime/result copies and bytes/RAM are excluded.

    Functions

    ll1_expression_grammar()Return the original report's arithmetic expression grammar in predictive or left-recursive form. Symbols are id,+,*,(,), with original E/T/F production ordering. The default is right-recursive and nullable-tail LL(1); the left-recursive control has actual table conflicts and is for construction inspection only.

    Types and constants

    LL1ParseActionenum Actual producing parse-stack action recorded for one complete step.
    LL1ParseStatusenum Actual bounded predictive-parser outcome, distinguishing rejection from exhausted action budget.

    datamunge/algorithms/lll.hpp

    Classes

    LLLAnalysisOwned actual equivalent integer basis, exact row transform and floating reduction observations. Checked row subtraction/swap preserves the exact original integer lattice, including incomplete runs. Decisions use double Gram-Schmidt, so completed status and observed inequalities are not a rigorous exact-arithmetic LLL or shortest-vector certificate. Transform overflow can throw even if the basis row would fit; no arbitrary-precision fallback is implied.
    LLLEventActual producing row reduction, Lovasz decision or adjacent swap linked to a real state.
    LLLStateOwned actual basis/transform and computed Gram-Schmidt arrays at one real committed row state.
    LLLTraceOwned complete original basis and every actual bounded row-operation/check/state record. Each actual state counts1+2*n*d+2*n*n+n logical entries; original input counts n*d and each actual event1. Records admitted before snapshot/event copy; unknown future operations are not fabricated. Default million cap, 0 optional cap off. Excludes scalar fields/row headers/capacities/result/runtime copies and bytes/RAM. Complete bounded trace or exception.
    LLLWorkActual selected floating Gram-Schmidt, integer row-operation and outer-loop work. Excludes complete guards, copies/allocation/capture, property-summary comparisons, elapsed time and CPU instruction counts.

    Functions

    lll_analyze()Return actual bounded LLL basis, exact row transform and computed property observations. No mutation, shared state or optional history. Completed loop status is distinct from exact-arithmetic certification; inspect observed property flags.
    lll_reduce()Return the completed historical floating-decision LLL basis with checked exact row operations. Full guards precede Gram-Schmidt and checked integer arithmetic. Ordinary finite double decisions/round-half-away multipliers preserve the historical defined-range path. Default100000 actual outer steps bounds possible numerical cycling; exhaustion throws rather than returning a silently reduced claim. No shortest basis, per-row norm decrease or exact floating reduction theorem.
    lll_trace()Capture every actual bounded integer row operation, computed check and real GS state once. Same shared producer as ordinary/count-only methods. Exact transform and finite-size checks precede committing a size-reduction row; captured states are actual GS evaluations, never repeated original-prefix reductions.

    Types and constants

    LLLEventKindenum Actual producing reduction/check/swap event kind.
    LLLStopenum Actual bounded LLL outer-loop stop, separate from floating property observations.

    Classes

    CosineLSHOwn an immutable finite index with seeded Gaussian hyperplanes and insertion-order buckets. Input data are copied, fixing the historical borrowed-pointer lifetime hazard and stale buckets after caller mutation. Bit agreement has probability1-theta/pi for nonzero vectors and an isotropic continuous plane; finite sampled Gaussian arithmetic is the implementation. Zero vectors use cosine0 and nonnegative sign bits. Query still initializes N dense marks: O(N+L*k*d+V+C*d), with V actual member visits and C distinct candidates.     datamunge/algorithms/merge.hpp

    Classes

    MergeAnalysisOwned sorted output and actual same-execution selected work, without input/history capture.
    MergeHeapStepOwned actual heap operation, original value identity and before/after occupancy. Original identity is(list,index), preserving duplicate multiplicity. Push has emitted=false; Pop records whether its value entered output. This is not a copy of the private heap array or a replayed heap-comparison history.
    MergeTraceOwned complete original runs and actual chronological heap operations/output. captured_entries counts K outer-row records + N original value records + actual push/pop records. Excludes output values, tuple fields, runtime heap/copies, capacities and bytes/RAM. Validate all sorted rows first, then admit complete K+N before input copies and each event before its heap operation. Default million, zero off, no partial trace escapes failure. No merge/heap replay.
    MergeWorkSelected actual heap operations, tuple-comparator calls and output decisions. node_comparisons counts actual calls ordering whole(value,list,index) tuples, not individual integer comparisons, memory reads or elapsed time. Excludes validation, sort checks, copies, allocation and output writes.

    Functions

    k_way_merge()Merge all nondecreasing int runs with a minimum-front heap, preserving every identity. Validate complete sorted rows and total size before heap/output allocation. Tuple ordering(value,list,index) breaks equal-value ties by original list then within-list position. Empty runs ignored, outer empty allowed. Each original identity is pushed/popped once. O(K+N log(R+1)) work for K rows,N values and R nonempty runs, O(R) heap and O(N) output. No caller mutation/input copies/history or shared mutable state. Comparator calls depend on the standard-library heap.
    k_way_merge_analyze()Return actual heap-merge values and selected work without retaining input/history. Shared producer and contracts with k_way_merge()/union_merge(), not estimated comparison formulas or a second merge. Actual tuple comparator invocations are counted, including list/index tie ordering inside each invocation.
    k_way_merge_trace()Capture complete original runs and every actual producing heap push/pop once. Shared kernel/contracts with k_way_merge_analyze(); no second merge or synthetic heap history. Complete input and online operation admission follow MergeTrace. Adds owned O(K+N+events) original/history capture to native heap/output storage.
    simple_merge()Stably merge two nondecreasing int vectors in one linear pass. Validate both complete inputs before allocation. Equal values take a first; multiplicity retained, empty vectors allowed, integer extremes unchanged. O(a.size()+b.size()) work/output, O(1) cursor state, no mutation/shared state.
    union_merge()Produce sorted distinct values through the same minimum-front merge kernel. Same validation/tie/order/complexity as k_way_merge(), but skip a popped value equal to the last emitted one. Every original identity still enters/leaves heap. Output uses O(number of distinct values) storage; no optional capture quota.

    Types and constants

    MergeHeapKindenum Actual heap operation recorded by the shared sorted-run producer.
