    datamunge/algorithms/miller_rabin.hpp

    Classes

    MillerRabinRoundTraceOwned actual sequence of one strong probable-prime round. Early guards have no powering record. For odd n>=3 and an!=0, d is odd, n-1=d*2^s, and residues begin with a^d followed by actual post-powering squares until n-1 is reached or all s-1 squares finish. A pass is not a primality certificate. No constant-time guarantee.

    Functions

    is_probable_prime()Decide primality for the complete unsigned64-bit domain. Screens division by the first twelve primes, then uses these same bases for strong rounds. Their smallest simultaneous strong pseudoprime is 318665857834031151167461, above UINT64_MAX. At most twelve O(log n) fixed-word rounds and O(1) driver storage; no constant-time guarantee.
    is_strong_probable_prime_base()Perform one actual strong probable-prime round with exact modular arithmetic. For odd n>=3, factor n-1=d*2^s and accept a^d=1 or any tested a^(d*2^r)=n-1 for 0<=r<s. Continue all scheduled squares if a residue becomes one without an earlier minus-one. O(log n) word products, O(1) driver storage. A base divisible by n passes vacuously.
    miller_rabin_round_trace()Capture the actual producer's powering and strong-round residues. Same body and early exits as is_strong_probable_prime_base(), without replay. Upfront cap counts powering bit records plus all potentially scheduled strong residues (s); at most64 entries for uint64 candidates. Zero disables the cap. Trace owns its data and uses O(log n) storage; exponent bits are observable.

    datamunge/algorithms/min_conflicts.hpp

    Classes

    NQueensMoveActual initialization choice or repair, with exact candidate costs and RNG words. Initialization has column_before=-1 and no conflicted list/row draw. Repair costs are measured after temporary queen removal, including all n columns. Conflicts count unordered attacking pairs; a pair cannot share two constraints.
    NQueensResultOwned final assignment and honest terminal status of one capped search. One queen per row; columns need not be distinct on an unsuccessful run.
    NQueensTraceOwned inputs, actual initialization/repair history and final assignment. Capture units are three scalar inputs, final n columns, and per move one record plus every stored conflicting-row ID, cost and tied-column ID. Driver occupancy arrays and temporary candidates are not capture units.

    Functions

    min_conflicts_nqueens()Search for nonattacking queens using actual minimum-conflict repairs. Initialize each row in increasing order at a minimum-conflict column, using one MT19937-64 word modulo tie count. Each repair draws a conflicting row, removes its queen, scans every column, then draws among minimum-cost ties. Modulo sampling has finite-word bias. Seed and legacy choices are preserved. Always checks terminal status after the last allowed move, including zero. n=0 is solved. No success guarantee or restart. O(n^2+n*max_steps) work, O(n) driver storage, so no size-independent runtime claim is made.
    min_conflicts_nqueens_trace()Capture actual decisions of the same n-queens search producer. No replay or changed RNG scheduling. Actual capture admission checks units before appending; no partial trace is returned on quota exhaustion. Trace storage is proportional to captured entries; driver work follows ordinary search.

    datamunge/algorithms/minimum_degree.hpp

    Classes

    MinimumDegreeStepActual state immediately before and during one vertex elimination. Neighbors are sorted live vertex IDs; fill contains each newly created undirected edge once, with smaller endpoint first. No numeric factorization.
    MinimumDegreeTraceOwned input, actual elimination order and optional captured decisions. Duplicate references and loops are ignored; asymmetric input is interpreted as its symmetric union. Entry cap counts raw input references, input row records, order IDs, step records, neighbor IDs and fill-edge records.

    Functions

    elimination_natural_order()Construct the natural increasing-ID elimination permutation.
    elimination_trace()Capture actual fill for a prescribed complete elimination permutation. Uses the same fill producer as greedy ordering, replacing only vertex choice. Same normalization, quota units, ownership and worst-case complexity.
    minimum_degree_arrow()Construct the original arrow graph, with center0 adjacent to all others.
    minimum_degree_ordering()Greedily eliminate minimum live degree, breaking ties by smallest ID. Input IDs must be in [0,N); loops/duplicates ignored, asymmetric edges symmetrized. The legacy order is preserved on symmetric valid inputs. Set-based complete degree scans and fill trials give O(N^3 log(N+1)) worst-case work and O(N^2) driver storage. No minimum-fill guarantee.
    minimum_degree_trace()Capture actual greedy elimination, including every newly inserted fill edge. Same producer as minimum_degree_ordering(), without replay. Actual entry admission throws before exceeding the optional quota; no partial trace is returned. Capture storage is proportional to admitted entries. Zero disables.

    datamunge/algorithms/miser.hpp

    Classes

    MiserComparisonOne native replicated original Gaussian MISER-versus-plain comparison.
    MiserNodeActual region, split/allocation and returned estimate for one recursion call. Leaf nodes have pilot_calls=0 and split_dimension=0 placeholder. Child budgets sum to calls minus pilot_calls; pilot observations are not reused in leaves.
    MiserResultIntegral estimate and the native plug-in estimator variance. Leaf variance uses (mean(f squared)-mean(f) squared)/n, clipped to zero; it is not an unbiased sample-variance estimate or a confidence guarantee.
    MiserSampleOne actual callback evaluation, labeled pilot versus retained leaf.
    MiserTraceOwned actual sample and recursive allocation history. Capture units are original2d bounds, each node record plus its2d bounds, and each sample record plus its d coordinates. Quota excludes scalar fields within records and temporary pilot accumulators. All callbacks are observable; a quota failure can occur after earlier evaluations and returns no partial trace.

    Functions

    miser_gaussian()Evaluate the original centered narrow Gaussian over two coordinates.
    miser_gaussian_comparison()Run the original budget/seed comparison in the native library. Plain comparator preserves MT19937-64 seed1000+seed and uniform_real_distribution. Finite-replicate RMS values are observations, not universal superiority/rates.
    miser_gaussian_integral()Return the analytic finite-unit-square integral of the original Gaussian.
    miser_integrate()Integrate a callable over a finite box with an exact evaluation budget. Uses the original xorshift stream,10percent pilots (minimum16), midpoint axis minimizing the sum of pilot SDs, and proportional remaining allocation. Calls below64 are plain leaves. The legacy32-sample allocation clamps are preserved, including leaves smaller than32 when a split budget is64..79. Pilots guide allocation but are discarded from the final estimate. At least two calls are required, correcting legacy silent overspending below two. Successful calls evaluate f exactly calls times. No error-rate or confidence guarantee; quasi-random stream correlations and adaptation remain relevant. Work O(d*calls) excluding callbacks; recursion and scratch O(d*log calls).
    miser_trace()Capture actual callback points and region allocations of the same integrator. Same stream, scheduling and result as miser_integrate(), without replay. Actual quota admission precedes each stored evaluation/region. Earlier callback side effects remain if a later quota or callback fails. History O(d*calls).

    datamunge/algorithms/modular_exponentiation.hpp

    Classes

    ModPowStepOne actual low-bit fold, running-base square and exponent shift. Before the step, accumulator*running^remaining equals the original power modulo m. multiply is the low bit of remaining_before; squared_base is computed even for the final bit. No independent replay is used to obtain these values.
    ModPowTraceOwned scalar inputs, actual exponent-bit states and final modular residue. No replay or shared state. All trace data, including exponent bits, is exposed. Modulus one has result/initial_base zero and no steps/products, regardless of exponent; exponent zero otherwise returns one with no steps/products.
    ModPowWorkActual operation counts of right-to-left square-and-multiply. Each processed bit performs one square, including the final unused square. Set bits additionally multiply the accumulator. Counts exclude input reduction, division internals, copying and allocation; these are not timings.

    Functions

    mod_pow()Compute base^exponent modulo a nonzero modulus by right-to-left binary powering. Exact for every uint64 input/modulus using full 128-bit products. Keeps the existing loop order, including one final unused square. For m>1 and e>0 there are bit_width(e) squares and popcount(e) accumulator products; exponent zero gives one, modulus one gives zero (also for 0^0). O(log(e)+1) word operations and O(1) driver storage. No constant-time or protocol-security claim.
    mod_pow_trace()Record actual right-to-left exponentiation states and operation counts. Uses the same kernel as mod_pow(), without replay. Complete effective bit count (at most64; zero for modulus one) is checked against the cap before allocation or powering. Zero disables only the optional cap. O(log(e)+1) work/storage.
    mul_mod()Compute (a*b) modulo a nonzero modulus without unsigned multiplication wrap. Forms the complete product in unsigned __int128. Inputs may be unreduced and span the full uint64 range; modulus one gives zero. O(1) word operations/storage on this fixed-width implementation, without a constant-time guarantee.

    datamunge/algorithms/monotone_cubic.hpp

    Classes

    MonotoneCubicOwned prepared shape-preserving cubic Hermite model with endpoint clamping. Initial interior tangents average adjacent secants, endpoints use one-sided secants. In left-to-right order, zero secants zero both tangents; wrong-sign tangents are clamped before radial limiting to alpha^2+beta^2<=9. Later updates only decrease shared tangent magnitudes. This sufficient region gives interval monotonicity in exact arithmetic, including local extrema. C1, generally not C2. Floating-point evaluation has roundoff. No smoothing. Preparation O(n), owned storage O(n); each query O(log n). Independent const queries share no mutation. Finite geometry/secants and results are required.
    MonotoneCubicDecisionActual mutations of one interval's shared endpoint tangents. Records precede subsequent intervals, which can further decrease a shared tangent. Final model tangents, rather than an earlier record, define evaluation.

    Functions

    monotone_cubic_interpolate()Prepare and evaluate one shape-preserving cubic query. Same model/limiter as MonotoneCubic, including finite-input guards and endpoint clamping. Preparation O(n), query O(log n), storage O(n). Reuse a prepared model for repeated queries. The ordinary function disables the optional node cap. Wrong-sign limiting and actual endpoint clamping correct legacy defects.

    datamunge/algorithms/montgomery.hpp

    Classes

    MontgomeryContextPrecompute one odd modulus for carry-safe Montgomery arithmetic. R=2^64. Setup computes nprime=-n inverse modulo R using five Newton refinements from the odd seed n, plus R and R squared modulo n. Setup and arbitrary-input reduction use remainder operations; only the reduced-domain REDC kernel avoids division. All inputs/results use unsigned64-bit words, with full128-bit products and an explicit129th sum bit. No constant-time guarantee. Methods do not mutate the context and are independently callable.
    MontgomeryPowerStepActual powering step in the Montgomery domain.
    MontgomeryPowerTraceOwned actual exponentiation states with one shared modulus context. One conversion into the domain and one conversion out surround the binary loop. Counts are actual REDC calls, not CPU instructions or timings.
    MontgomeryReductionActual carry-safe REDC state for a product of two reduced residues. The exact sum T+q*n can require129 bits. sum_carry retains that bit; quotient_low retains the low64 bits after division by2^64. A subtraction occurs if the carry is set or quotient_low>=n. These are owned observations.

    Functions

    montgomery_multiply()Compute an ordinary modular product with a fresh Montgomery context. Setup uses remainder operations on every call; use MontgomeryContext to amortize setup across calls. Exact full-width inputs, O(1) word work/storage.

    datamunge/algorithms/move_to_front.hpp

    Classes

    MTFAnalysisActual linear-search comparisons and shifted alphabet entries. Encode comparisons include the successful test; decoding indexes directly and has zero search comparisons. Alphabet initialization's256 stores are excluded.
    MTFIndexSummaryNative observed rank distribution, including exact count-based median. Median averages the two central ranks for even count. Empty means/median/ entropy are explicit zero placeholders. Entropy is empirical marginal bits per rank, not compressed size or a claim that an entropy coder was run.
    MTFStepActual selected byte/rank before moving it to the alphabet front. Previous front and the selected byte are observed from the same evolving 256-byte permutation as ordinary execution; no Unicode normalization occurs.
    MTFTraceOwned original stream and actual per-byte transform history. Encode retains input_bytes and result.indices; decode retains input_indices and result.bytes. Other two stream fields stay empty. Capture units are one input element, one output element and one step record per byte, exactly3n.

    Functions

    mtf_decode()Decode valid move-to-front ranks with the same evolving alphabet. Validates every rank before indexing/output work; this corrects the legacy out-of-bounds behavior on negative or above255 indices. Empty input gives an empty string. O(256n) work, fixed alphabet plus n owned output bytes.
    mtf_decode_analyze()Obtain actual decoded bytes and work from the ordinary inverse producer. Full rank validation precedes output indexing. Same complexity as mtf_decode().
    mtf_decode_trace()Capture actual byte/rank/front observations during ordinary decoding. Validates all ranks before the complete3n quota preflight and inverse work. Zero disables the optional quota. Same producer as mtf_decode(), no replay.
    mtf_demo_text()Return the original fourfold repetitive sentence as owned bytes.
    mtf_encode()Encode arbitrary bytes to ranks in a moving unsigned-byte alphabet. Initial alphabet is0..255. Search the current rank, emit it, shift preceding entries right and put the byte at front. Exact lossless recoding, not entropy compression; storing ranks as ints can expand the stream. Empty allowed. O(256n) worst-case work, fixed256-byte driver alphabet plus owned n outputs.
    mtf_encode_analyze()Obtain actual encoded ranks and work from the ordinary producer. Same semantics/complexity as mtf_encode(), without replay or trace storage.
    mtf_encode_trace()Capture actual byte/rank/front observations during ordinary encoding. Preflights the complete3n logical-entry quota before copying or transforming. Zero disables the optional quota. Trace owns all data; no replay or shared state.
    mtf_index_summary()Summarize validated ranks using a native fixed-size histogram. O(n+256) work, fixed256-count driver storage. Full validation precedes counts.

    datamunge/algorithms/muller.hpp

    Classes

    MullerEvaluationOne actual finite callback observation, in invocation order.
    MullerRunActual selected callbacks, residual inspections, updates and discriminant clamps. Initial three callbacks count even when x2 already passes or update cap is zero. Inspections include the final cap check, which reuses the last callback value.
    MullerStepActual residual inspection and, when needed, its quadratic proposal. quadratic=false means complete coefficients/discriminant are unavailable; spacing fields can retain an attempted coincident-node check, while unused coefficient fields are zero placeholders and next=x2. updated=false means no callback at next was performed. A final cap check records at_limit=true without fabricating a new quadratic iteration.
    MullerTraceOwned actual seed/controls, callback history and quadratic inspections. Capture units are five seed/control scalars, each actual callback record and each actual inspection record. Optional quota is online; earlier callback side effects remain if later admission fails. No partial trace is returned.

    Functions

    muller()Solve with the retained real Muller quadratic update and residual stopping. Fits the three-point parabola in local h=x-x2 coordinates and chooses the larger-magnitude quadratic denominator to reduce cancellation. Negative discriminants are clamped to zero: this is a real heuristic, not complex Muller iteration. No bracket, step-size acceptance or global convergence guarantee. Smooth simple-root local order~1.839 requires additional regularity, close distinct iterates and the appropriate unmodified quadratic branch. Nonfinite produced arithmetic/callbacks throw. Repeated interpolation nodes stop numerically if a quadratic is needed, after the residual check. Legacy arithmetic order and inspection count are retained on finite valid runs. tol=0 disables acceptance even at callback zero. O(K) scalar work plus callbacks, constant driver storage; zero cap still performs all three seed calls.
    muller_run()Return actual stop and work from the same ordinary Muller producer. No replay or callback changes; same contracts/complexity as muller().
    muller_stop_name()Return a stable display name for a numerical stop.
    muller_trace()Capture actual callbacks and inspections from the ordinary producer. Admits five base scalars then each actual record before its callback/append; no replay. Default1000000 entry cap, zero disables. Storage is proportional to admitted records. Earlier callback effects persist if a later quota fails.

    Types and constants

    MullerStopenum Actual numerical stop, distinct from a root/existence certificate.

    datamunge/algorithms/nagle.hpp

    Classes

    NagleAnalysisActual final packet stream and widened sender accounting. Conservation holds: written=sent+buffered and sent=unacked+acknowledged. Oversized ACK requests saturate at outstanding bytes; no implicit final ACK or flush is supplied. Zero-byte events remain events but emit no zero packet.
    NagleEmissionActual packet emission and its immediate scheduling reason. Reason0=full segment,1=idle partial write,2=ACK-released partial,3=baseline.
    NagleEventOne application write or acknowledgment in an ordinal sender simulation. Events have no timestamps, network window, retransmission or delayed-ACK model.
    NagleStepActual buffer/outstanding states and packet span of one input event.
    NagleTraceOwned original events, actual sender states/emissions and final accounting. Capture units count mss/enabled scalars, original events, step records, result packet sizes and emission records:2+2*events+2*packets.

    Functions

    nagle_analyze()Return actual terminal sender accounting from the ordinary producer. No replay; same complexity and guards as nagle_simulate().
    nagle_demo_events()Generate the original six100-byte writes with one ACK after write four.
    nagle_header_bytes()Count assumed per-packet header bytes for the actually emitted packets only. This excludes unsent buffered bytes and all protocol details beyond a fixed supplied header size. O(1) work/storage, without modifying the analysis.
    nagle_simulate()Simulate full-segment bypass and ACK-gated partial packet coalescing. On writes, emit every available full segment, then emit a remainder only if no bytes are outstanding. An ACK clamps outstanding bytes at zero and releases a held remainder when it clears them. No implicit end flush. Complete type/byte/mss validation precedes packetization. O(events+packets) work, constant driver state plus owned packet output. Widened byte counters reject overflow instead of legacy signed wrapping. No actual networking.
    nagle_trace()Capture actual coalescing or baseline event/packet transitions. Same producer and output as ordinary execution, without replay. Admit the complete2+2*events base before copies and two units per actual emitted packet. History quota failure returns no partial result. Zero disables optional cap.
    no_nagle_simulate()Emit each write immediately, split into positive MSS-bounded payloads. ACKs still update accounting in the common producer but cannot delay output. Same complete validation, complexity and counter guards as nagle_simulate().

    datamunge/algorithms/nearest_neighbor_interpolation.hpp

    Classes

    NearestNeighborDemoOwned original smooth-function demonstration samples.
    NearestNeighborInterpolantOwned prepared one-dimensional nearest-sample interpolant. Equal-size finite node arrays, with strictly increasing xs. Empty arrays are allowed and produce zero by legacy convention; this is not a data estimate. Finite out-of-range queries select the nearest endpoint; exact midpoint ties select the lower index. Ordinates may be nonmonotone. No smoothing or new ordinate values are introduced. O(n) validation/setup/storage, then O(log(n+1)) query work and constant query-driver storage. Const queries do not mutate.
    NearestNeighborStepActual inclusive binary-search bounds and abscissa comparison.
    NearestNeighborStudyOwned native smooth-function interpolation and finite-grid error study. The reference bound1.3*h/2 uses |cos(x)+.3|<=1.3 on the sampled domain. It bounds exact-arithmetic nearest-sample error on[0,6.4], not extrapolation or floating-point roundoff; the reported maximum is only over its query grid.
    NearestNeighborTraceOwned nodes/query and actual binary-search/nearest-choice observations. Capture units are both node arrays, query/result scalar records and actual search-step records:2n+2+steps. Empty result index0 is a placeholder. Route0=empty,1=lower endpoint,2=upper endpoint,3=interior nearest choice. Distances are meaningful only for route3 and use widened arithmetic.

    Functions

    nearest_neighbor_demo()Generate the original nine coarse smooth-function samples natively.
    nearest_neighbor_demo_study()Run the original smooth-function example using one prepared native model. O(nodes+grid_intervals*log(nodes+1)) work and O(nodes+grid_intervals) owned storage. Grid points use6.4*i/grid_intervals to avoid accumulated step drift.
    nearest_neighbor_interpolate()Validate, prepare and evaluate a single nearest-neighbor query. Uses the same producer as NearestNeighborInterpolant, with its optional node cap disabled. O(n) setup plus O(log(n+1)) query work, O(n) copied driver storage. Reuse a prepared model for many queries. Empty matching arrays return zero; complete shape/finiteness/order validation now precedes endpoint indexing.

    datamunge/algorithms/nearest_neighbor_tsp.hpp

    Classes

    NearestTSPAnalysisActual greedy tour and selected scan/sum work counts. Candidate checks include visited IDs; distance comparisons occur only after the first eligible candidate has established a current best. Counts are not matrix-load or CPU-operation totals. Final tour sum includes the closing edge.
    NearestTSPChoiceActual chosen next city and its eligible-trial span.
    NearestTSPEdgeActual post-route sequential edge sum, including closure.
    NearestTSPTraceOwned original matrix/start and actual greedy/summation history. Capture units count start, input rows/weights, result route IDs, eligible trial records, choice records and edge-sum records. Scalar fields within a record are not additional units. Empty input retains start but no route.
    NearestTSPTrialActual eligible candidate and current-best update at one greedy visit. Candidates appear by ascending ID; first=true means no prior best, so no distance comparison occurred. Equal-distance later candidates never replace.

    Functions

    enumerate_tsp()Enumerate all small anchored tours as a bounded optimal-cost reference. Permute remaining IDs in lexicographic order, retaining the first strict cost minimum. Uses the same sequential cost sum order as the greedy call; overflowed candidates saturate to infinity and cannot defeat a finite minimum. This certifies that rounded objective over enumerated tours, not exact real arithmetic for arbitrary noninteger weights. O(n*(n−1)!) work, O(n) driver storage. No pruning or symmetry reduction; directed matrices allowed.
    nearest_neighbor_tsp()Greedily visit the closest unvisited city and return to the start. Complete finite nonnegative square matrix required; asymmetry, zero distances, nonzero diagonal and triangle-inequality violations are allowed. Scan IDs in ascending order and replace only on strict distance improvement, preserving smallest-ID ties and the legacy selected route. No optimality/constant-ratio guarantee for arbitrary matrices. O(n^2) scan work, O(n) driver/output storage, excluding caller's input matrix. Singleton returns[start,start] with its diagonal cost; empty returns zero/empty and ignores start.
    nearest_neighbor_tsp_adversary()Generate a three-city directed nonmetric greedy-trap family. Rows are(0,1,2),(1,0,M),(1,1,0). From0, greedy costs M+2 while the other anchored cycle costs4, so M>=2 makes4 an optimum. Integers in the report avoid floating-sum ambiguity. No symmetry or metric claim is made.

    nested_sampling()Estimate box-prior evidence with deterministic mean-log-mass shrinkage and finite walks. Uses X_i=exp(-i/N), dead shell X_before-X_after, final live weights X_final/N.     Functions

    nest_first_fit_decreasing()Pack finite nonnegative items with exact first-fit-decreasing admission. Validate every size in[0,capacity], sort descending, test bins in creation order and open a bin only if none fits. Exact fixed-size dyadic accumulators remove the legacy absolute1e-12 allowance and rounded-load overfill. Returned loads are correctly rounded summaries, not the admission state. O(n log n+n^2) fixed-width work and O(n) driver/output storage; item count must fit int IDs. Empty returns zero bins. Nonempty all-zero items occupy one bin.
    nesting_analyze()Analyze actual FFD order, trials and exact volume lower bound. Same producer/guards/complexity as nest_first_fit_decreasing(), without replay.
    nesting_demo_sizes()Generate the original thirty sizes from a wrapping32-bit linear congruential stream. Starts at12345, updates state=1103515245*state+12345 modulo2^32, and maps .15+(state%1000)/1000*.7 in the original operation order.
    nesting_feasible()Check a supplied packing certificate using exact binary64 capacities. Requires every original item exactly once. Empty bins are allowed and count as supplied bins; out-of-range/duplicate/missing IDs or exact overfill return false. Input size/capacity validation still throws before checking the assignment. O(items+bins) fixed-accumulator work, O(items) identity-check storage.
    nesting_lower_bound()Compute an exact binary64 volume lower bound for valid packing inputs. Exact nonnegative sum and integer comparisons compute ceil(total/capacity), without floating overflow, epsilon subtraction or rounded ceiling. Zero total gives zero, a valid but loose bound when zero-sized items must be assigned. O(n+log(n+1)) fixed-accumulator work, constant driver storage.
    nesting_trace()Capture actual exact bin comparisons and first-fit placements. No replay. Complete1+4n base units are admitted before history copying, then one per actual trial and per opened bin load. No partial result escapes a failure.     newell_analyze()Return actual Newell vector area and centroid-plane diagnostics. Complete coordinates are checked finite before arithmetic/policy checks.     newton_division_check()Perform the originally claimed100000-case sampled comparison as an actual native study. Each pair draws two top53-bit unit words, two exponent words modulo1001 shifted by-500 and two sign words, in that order, from local MT19937_64. Mantissas are .5+.5*u; quotients remain finite/nonzero in this bounded range. Calls the canonical division producer and compares with built-in double /. O(samples*60) work, constant driver storage, no global RNG state mutation.
    newton_division_demo_pairs()Return the original four signed floating-division worked pairs.

Nonzero magnitudes are separately normalized with frexp. Seed48/17−(32/17)*m_D then updates x<-x*(2-m_D*x), stopping at relative state change<=1e-17 or60 updates. Final ldexp(sign*m_N*x,e_N-e_D) avoids overflowing an intermediate raw reciprocal when the quotient is representable, including equal subnormals. Signed-zero numerator takes a signed-zero quotient shortcut. Actual quotient overflow throws; gradual underflow/rounded zero are permitted and reported. This is a double approximation, not a correctly-rounded division guarantee, hardware speed claim or constant-time primitive. Seed constants/rescaling do not establish a division-free CPU instruction stream. O(60) fixed work, constant driver storage; no input/shared state mutation.

    datamunge/algorithms/ntt_multiplication.hpp

    Classes

    NTTCarryOne actual base-ten carry propagation through the recovered integer convolution.
    NTTMultiplicationOptionsComplete decimal, transform and optional state-history bounds; zero disables a policy.
    NTTMultiplicationRunOwned exact decimal product and actual selected transform work.
    NTTStageOne actual completed transform phase, owning its current residues.

    Functions

    ntt_mul()Return the checked exact NTT decimal product through the preserved signature. Delegates to the same producer/default bounds. Ordinary valid decimal outputs are preserved. Empty/malformed strings, roots beyond the fixed-prime capacity and oversized requests now reject instead of producing unchecked residues.
    ntt_multiply_run()Multiply checked nonnegative decimal integers using one exact fixed-prime NTT convolution. Requires nonempty ASCII digit strings; validates all original characters/counts before a zero shortcut, accepts leading zeros and normalizes them. Uses prime998244353 and primitive root3, with a hard transform capacity2^23. Pads to the smallest power of two at least len(a)+len(b), preserving the historical transform geometry. Checks81*min(normalized lengths)<prime so every base-ten convolution coefficient is recovered as an ordinary integer, then performs actual carry propagation. Zero products return0 without transforms. This is a bounded fixed-prime radix-two method, not an implementation of the original arbitrary-length Schoenhage-Strassen ring algorithm. Actual word-operation work is O(N log N), storage O(N), within the documented root/coefficient bounds. Records count actual bit-reversal visits/swaps, butterflies, root powering products, pointwise/scaling products and carry updates separately; they do not establish wall-clock speedup over another method. Capture geometry is known before allocation:5*N+(3*log2(N)+4)*(N+1) logical coefficient/phase/carry entries; normalized strings and output are intrinsic. Inputs unchanged and outputs owned, no shared state.

    datamunge/algorithms/number_theory.hpp

    Classes

    BsgsTraceA baby-step giant-step run with its operation counts and, optionally, the visited values.
    DiscreteLogThe result of a discrete-logarithm search: whether a solution exists and, if so, an exponent x with base^x ≡ target (mod p).

    Functions

    baby_step_giant_step()The baby-step giant-step algorithm (Shanks): solves the discrete logarithm base^x ≡ target (mod p) for a prime modulus p, in O(sqrt(p)) time and space – a meet-in-the-middle speedup over the O(p) brute-force search. Writing x = i·m + j with m = ceil(sqrt(p-1)), it tabulates the "baby steps" base^j and then takes "giant steps" of size m, looking each up in the table. It returns a valid exponent when target lies in the subgroup generated by base, and reports failure otherwise.
    baby_step_giant_step_trace()Baby-step giant-step with a chosen group order and table size, counting its work.
    element_order()The multiplicative order of g modulo the prime p: the least k > 0 with g^k ≡ 1. It divides p-1, so it is found by factoring p-1 and dividing out each prime while the power stays 1.
    primitive_root()The smallest primitive root modulo the prime p (a generator of the whole group).

    datamunge/algorithms/number_theory_extra.hpp

    Classes

    FermatOutcomeOwned result and actual work counts of bounded Fermat splitting. For odd n, start_a is the exact ceiling root; last_a and last_b are the last actual trial and its exact floor root of a squared minus n. Trials count square tests, including a hit; increments count moves between tested a values, hence trials-1. An even input has zero trials, increments and a/b metadata. Returned_factor matches fermat_factor(); cofactor is n/returned_factor when a square or even branch completes, and zero at TrialLimit. Proper_split requires both factors greater than one. Results own their scalars and share no state.
    FermatStepOne actual odd Fermat square test, owned without input references. Difference is computed in unsigned 128-bit arithmetic before its exact integer root b. Square reports equality of b squared and difference; b is not rounded from floating arithmetic. Rows come from the solver, never a replay loop.
    FermatTraceOwned same-pass Fermat outcome and optional actual trial history. C=captured_entries=rows.size() counts whole FermatStep records, not scalar fields or bytes. Quota admission occurs before square/root work and storing each row. Input/output scalars, vector capacity, allocator and runtime storage are excluded: C is not peak RAM. Copies are independent; editing a row does not recompute outcome. Even inputs capture nothing. Ordinary/work calls store no optional history and impose no history quota.

    Functions

    fermat_factor()Split n by exact Fermat square tests with the historical five-million-trial cap. The original compiled signature is retained and delegates to the same kernel as fermat_factor_work(). Even inputs return two immediately. Odd inputs test successive a from the exact ceiling root; a square gives a-b when it is a proper factor, otherwise n. Returning n also occurs on budget exhaustion and does not prove primality. The first factors need not be prime. Uses exact uint128 differences/roots, O(T) fixed-word work and constant auxiliary storage; at most 63 division comparisons per 128-bit root, not constant arbitrary-bit complexity. Independent calls share no mutable state.
    fermat_factor_trace()Capture actual Fermat trials during the same bounded factorization pass. No replay: outcome is identical to work(n,max_trials) if capture succeeds. Before each square/root test, admit one whole record against max_entries. Default quota1000000 and default trial budget5000000 are independent. Zero max_entries disables only the optional quota; max_trials must stay positive. A quota/allocation failure throws without returning a partial trace. No shared mutable state; owned copies survive other calls and edits independently. Costs O(T) fixed-word work and O(T) records, unlike ordinary constant storage.
    fermat_factor_work()Run bounded exact Fermat splitting and count its actual tests and increments. Shares the ordinary solver's kernel and constant storage with no optional history or history quota. A hit is one test, so odd successful calls take increments+1 tests. Even n bypasses square tests, including n=2 which has no proper split. TrivialPair excludes all earlier odd factor pairs and proves odd n prime; TrialLimit is inconclusive. Positive controls are validated before the even branch. Fixed-word work is O(trials), each root at most63 comparisons.
    fermat_stop_name()Return stable descriptive text for a Fermat termination reason. Literal string views have static lifetime and no allocation or shared mutation. Invalid enum representations give "unknown".

    Types and constants

    FermatStopenum Trial division: the elementary integer-factorization method – try every candidate divisor 2,3,5,7,... up to sqrt(n), dividing it out (with multiplicity) whenever it divides. Any factor left above sqrt(n) is prime. It is O(sqrt(n)) and hopeless for large semiprimes, but it is exact, dead simple, and the right tool for small numbers or for peeling off the small prime factors before a heavier method takes over.

    datamunge/algorithms/number_theory_more.hpp

    Classes

    LucasTermsTerms of a Lucas sequence pair modulo n.
    SelfridgeParametersSelfridge's "method A" parameters for a Lucas test of n.

    Functions

    baillie_psw()The Baillie-PSW primality test: combines a strong (Miller-Rabin) probable-prime test to base 2 with a strong Lucas probable-prime test (Selfridge's parameters, strong_lucas_probable_prime()). Individually each has infinitely many pseudoprimes, but the two families are believed disjoint: no composite is known to pass both, and none exists below 2^64. So although Baillie-PSW is technically a probabilistic test, it is deterministic in practice for 64-bit integers and is what many libraries use as their primality check.
    jacobi_symbol()The Jacobi symbol \((a/n)\) for odd \(n>0\): the product of Legendre symbols over the prime factors of n; 0 when \(\gcd(a,n)>1\).
    lucas_probable_prime()The (standard) Lucas probable-prime test with Selfridge's parameters: n passes when \(U_{n+1}\equiv0 \pmod n\), which holds for every prime with \((D/n)=-1\).
    lucas_sequence_mod()\(U_k\), \(V_k\) and \(Q^k\) modulo the odd number n for the Lucas sequences with parameters P, Q: \(U_0=0, U_1=1, V_0=2, V_1=P\) and \(X_{j+1}=P X_j-Q X_{j-1}\).
    selfridge_parameters()Selfridge's parameters for the odd number n > 1: the first D in 5, -7, 9, -11, ... with \((D/n)=-1\), P = 1 and Q = (1 - D)/4.
    strong_lucas_probable_prime()The strong Lucas probable-prime test with Selfridge's parameters: writing \(n+1=d\cdot2^s\) with d odd, n passes when \(U_d\equiv0\) or \(V_{d2^r}\equiv0 \pmod n\) for some \(0\le r<s\). Perfect squares fail.

    datamunge/algorithms/object_graph.hpp

    Classes

    ObjectGraphOwned directed heap model with ordered roots, reference fields and optional sizes. Objects have dense ids 0..num_objects-1 and exactly one refs row each. Duplicate roots/fields, sharing, self references and cycles are permitted; negative/null ids are not represented (omit an absent reference instead). The optional sizes prefix supplies positive integral units when an algorithm uses sizes; missing entries mean one. Size metadata may be ignored by methods working only in object slots. Copies own all vectors; inputs are not borrowed. This models references and layout, not C++ object lifetime or raw-memory arenas.
    ObjectGraphWorkActual successful checks performed by graph validation, without traversal replay. rows counts every adjacency row, references counts every stored edge even in garbage, roots counts every root slot, and sizes counts supplied metadata only when requested. Empty graphs have zero counts. These are validation visits, not collector payload copying or elapsed-time measurements.

    Functions

    object_size()Read one object's positive size, defaulting to one after the supplied prefix. Validates the nonnegative count, requested id and selected supplied size only; it does not inspect unrelated rows, ids or size entries. No allocation or mutation; constant work/storage. Use validate_object_graph(graph,true) for complete structural and metadata checks.
    reachable_from_roots()Mark every root-reachable object using a checked iterative depth-first traversal. Validates the whole graph before indexing; ignores sizes. Marks on pushing, so duplicate edges, shared objects and cycles add no duplicate stack entries. Empty roots yield all-zero marks, and a default empty graph yields an empty vector. Owns the result and leaves inputs unchanged. Validation plus traversal costs O(N+E+R); dense marks and the explicit stack require O(N) storage. Separate calls share no state; concurrent input mutation is unsupported.
    validate_object_graph()Validate every graph id/row and optionally the positive size prefix before traversal. Rejects negative counts, mismatched adjacency length, and any out-of-range root or field id, including unreachable fields. With check_sizes=true, sizes must contain at most num_objects positive values. Otherwise sizes is entirely ignored, preserving slot-only methods' metadata independence. No allocation or mutation; O(N+E+R) visits plus checked size entries, constant auxiliary storage.

    Functions

    odds_algorithm()Solve the independent last-success optimal stopping problem. Complete finite probabilities in[0,1] are validated before suffix work, including an unvisited prefix. Events must be mutually independent and all probabilities known in advance; no dependence/unknown-probability guarantee. Traverse from the last event backwards until accumulated odds reach1, or until p=1. Certain odds are flagged rather than divided by zero. The result accepts the first success at/after its one-based threshold; no success loses. With Q=no-success and W=exactly-one for the already visited suffix, prepend p through W=p*Q+(1-p)*W, Q=(1-p)*Q. This recurrence avoids a singular odds-times-failure probability formula. Empty input returns historical{0,0}; all-zero nonempty input returns{1,0}. Exact-arithmetic odds-theorem optimality does not certify rounded comparisons or probability error. No inputs are mutated, referenced or globally cached. O(n) validation plus at most n suffix visits; constant ordinary working state.

    datamunge/algorithms/ode.hpp

    Classes

    AdaptiveOdeResultWork counters and the trajectory of an adaptive integration.

    Functions

    backward_euler()The backward (implicit) Euler method: steps y_{n+1} = y_n + h·f(t_{n+1}, y_{n+1}), evaluating the slope at the arrival point. Because y_{n+1} appears on both sides, each step solves an implicit equation – here by Newton's method with a central-difference Jacobian. The reward is A-stability: on a stiff decaying problem it stays bounded for any step size, where forward Euler explodes. It is first-order accurate like forward Euler, but stable.
    backward_euler_adaptive()Backward Euler with step-size control by step doubling.
    stability_function()The stability function \(R(z)\) of a one-step method: applied to \(y'=\lambda y\) with step \(h\), the method gives \(y_{n+1}=R(h\lambda)\,y_n\). The method is stable for that step when \(|R(h\lambda)|\le1\).

    Types and constants

    OdeMethodenum One-step methods whose stability function stability_function() evaluates.

Copies own every time and state value; no input/callback storage is borrowed. Times and state coordinates retain their input units. Default construction is an empty record.

    Types and constants

    OdeSystemtype First-order ODE callback f(t,y), returning the state derivative vector. Receives time and a borrowed const state vector valid only during the call. Return entries have state/time units and the same dimension as y. Euler validates shape/finiteness; validation by other solvers follows their contracts. Higher-order equations can be rewritten as first-order vector systems. The callback may own captured state; its exceptions propagate and concurrent use follows that captured state's thread-safety. No solver retains the callback.

Empty/singleton sample variance and empty mean use historical0 conventions. O(1) work/state per add/merge, no references/callbacks/shared mutable state.     datamunge/algorithms/packrat_parser.hpp

    Classes

    PackratEventActual owned named-rule/expression/choice decision record.
    PackratMemoRecordActual completed named-rule result retained in the final memo table.
    PackratOptionsOptional complete input/grammar and actual work/depth/history controls.
    PackratParserOwned byte PEG interpreter memoizing completed named-rule/position results. Complete grammar validation covers every node/operator/child arity/reference and start name before parsing. Direct/indirect left recursion at an active identical(rule,position) throws rather than recursing forever; right recursion remains subject to actual depth/work limits. Predicates do not consume input; ordered choice never revisits a successful child after a later sequence fails. Empty repetition stops on no progress, preserving original nullable behavior. Uses ordered std::map memo, not constant-time lookup. Only named rules are memoized: repeated greedy expression scans can still be quadratic. Therefore no general linear-time/linear-space packrat bound is promised by this API. Each parse owns its copied input, clears old memo/counters and uses no caller references/callbacks. A failed attempt clears incomplete memo and returns no trace, retaining explicit partial last-attempt counters/completed=false. Copies own grammar/input/cache; concurrent calls on one instance need caller synchronization. Zero disables optional policies, not the finite native stack.
    PackratRunActual last parse-attempt decision and selected counters.
    PackratTraceOwned original input and actual emitted events/final named-rule memo, no grammar replay.
    PegExprOwned byte PEG tree node, preserving original public field order. Literal/Ref require no children; Ref names a defined nonempty rule. Seq/Choice have arbitrary children and no text; unary operators need exactly one child. Constructor validation checks all rules, including unreachable ones. Empty literals/sequences are nullable; empty choice fails. No Unicode normalization.

    datamunge/algorithms/pde_solvers.hpp

    Classes

    FiniteDifferencePoissonResultOwned grid, assembled Poisson system and numerical residual from one native solve. Arrays own their storage; no source callback or caller references are retained. source[i], rhs[i] and residual[i] refer to interior node x[i+1]; x and u include both boundary nodes. The residual is A*u_interior-rhs for the stored binary64 matrix and RHS, evaluated with long-double intermediates, then rounded to double. It measures the discrete solve, not PDE accuracy.

    Functions

    finite_difference_poisson()Solve -u''=f on [0,1] with Dirichlet values by central differences and Thomas elimination. Uses n interior nodes and returns their values with both boundaries. Calls f exactly once at each (i+1)*h in increasing i order; exceptions propagate. Source samples and boundary values must be finite. The signed grid count n+2 must fit int; this is checked before allocation or callback evaluation. O(n) arithmetic/storage plus callback costs, no shared state or input mutation. Nodal error is O(h²) for a sufficiently smooth exact solution (for example C4), apart from rounding; finite output alone does not certify this accuracy. Reuses thomas_solve() on the internally assembled positive-definite system.
    finite_difference_poisson_solve()Solve the same Poisson problem and retain its actual grid, samples, matrix and residual. Shares the ordinary solver's assembly and canonical thomas_solve(), without replaying the solve or reevaluating f. Captures O(n) extra owned numeric output; these arrays describe the solved system, not an iteration history. Recomputed residuals use long-double intermediates and are not a PDE error certificate. No input mutation/shared state; source callback exceptions propagate unchanged.

An empty clause is unsatisfiable, so returns no covers; no clauses has exactly one empty cover. All ids are validated before expansion, even beyond an empty clause. Sorts candidates by cardinality, absorbs supersets, and selects the smallest final terms. Exponential worst-case time/storage; default cumulative generated-product cap is one million.     phase_estimation()Simulate t counting qubits and return the deterministic modal phase estimate. Prepares uniform amplitudes, applies phase 2*pi*phi*2^q to each bit q, then calls the native inverse QFT. This models an already supplied eigenphase; it constructs neither an unknown unitary nor its eigenstate. State-vector memory is exponential; simulated gate work is O(t^2*2^t), not a classical exponential speedup. No random measurement is performed. Borrows no state, retains no references and uses no shared mutable state.

    datamunge/algorithms/pi_and_cordic.hpp

    Classes

    SinCosOwned sine/cosine approximation pair returned by the circular CORDIC model. Original fields and their order/defaults are preserved. Default storage alone has no associated angle; producing calls document count and reduction limits.

    Functions

    bbp_pi_fraction()The fractional part \(\{16^n\pi\}\) by BBP digit extraction, in double precision.
    bbp_pi_hex_digit()The Bailey-Borwein-Plouffe (BBP) formula as a spigot for a single hexadecimal digit of pi. The BBP series pi = sum_k 16^{-k} ( 4/(8k+1) - 2/(8k+4) - 1/(8k+5) - 1/(8k+6) ) has the remarkable property that the n-th hex digit (0-indexed, the digit just after the point being n=0) can be computed directly, without the preceding digits, using only modular exponentiation and a short convergent tail – so it needs no arbitrary- precision arithmetic. It famously computes deep digits of pi in near-constant space.
    bbp_pi_hex_digits()count hex digits of pi starting at zero-based position n, read off one bbp_pi_fraction() evaluation (uppercase, e.g. n = 0, count = 6 gives "243F6A").
    cordic_sincos()Compute circular CORDIC sine/cosine with checked floating-model controls. Preserves the original recurrence/result layout: raw initial (1,0), residual sign >=0 selects +1, N dyadic pseudo-rotations, accumulated inverse gain and final simultaneous sine/cosine sign restoration. Finite theta and counts in [0,1075] are required; zero stages is an unrotated approximation, not an error certificate. No early stop or exact-identity special cases. Uses floating multiplications and cached atan/sqrt constants, not an integer shift engine. Reduction uses remainder(theta,2*pi_double); large angles can have large phase error against true sin(theta)/cos(theta). Theta(1+N) time/O(1) call scratch, after thread-safe one-time immutable table construction. No input mutation.
    gauss_legendre_pi()Legacy fixed-count double AGM pi estimate, with bounded weight use. Preserves ordered arithmetic and initialization(1,1/sqrt2,1/4,1), including left-associated p*delta*delta. Negative counts retain zero-stage compatibility. Counts above gauss_legendre_pi_limit() are rejected before work instead of returning a NaN suffix after weight overflow. Executes every admitted stage; stagnation is not early stopping or a correct-rounding certificate. At the maximum count the final unused p overflows, while all used weights/estimate remain finite. Requires radix-two double at build time. Only one final estimate expression is evaluated; O(max(0,N)) work/O(1) storage, no shared mutable state. Zero stages returns the initialized approximation, not pi.
    pi_hex_digits()The first count hex digits of pi after the point, computed exactly.

    pollard_kangaroo()Attempt g^x=h modulo P for a<=x<=b with native deterministic kangaroos. Reduces g,h modulo P and requires both to be units; composite P is allowed, but no cyclicity, exact base-order or target-membership proof is supplied. Each attempt builds the complete original32-jump seeded tame trail before following the wild walk. Trail collisions can reflect group-period aliases; every candidate is range/equation checked. Failure after finite attempts is not a proof no exponent exists. Exact unsigned128 distances avoid wrapping near UINT64_MAX; returned x still fits the requested uint64 interval. Input is scalar, state is local. Expected square-root behavior is heuristic; actual selected work and trail storage are capped by default.

    Functions

    pollard_p_minus_1()Attempt a proper divisor with the native base-two factorial-exponent schedule. Starts a=2 mod n, then a=pow(a,j,n) and gcd(a-1,n) for j=2,...,B. Thus exponents are j!, not the usual lcm(1,...,B) prime-power stage-one construction. Base order dividing j! is sufficient for divisibility; smooth p-1 alone or reaching its largest prime does not ensure an isolating gcd. Stops at the first proper gcd or full n collapse. Failure is not primality or absence-of-factor evidence. Input is scalar, no shared mutable state.
    pollard_p_minus_one_run()Run the shared factorial-exponent producer with actual count and reason. Work is the sum of O(log j) modular powering steps plus gcd work over executed stages; O(1) producer state beyond fixed-width arithmetic. No history is kept.
    pollard_p_minus_one_trace()Capture each actual residue update and gcd from the shared attempt. Retains one fixed record per executed stage, not a reconstructed factorial.

    datamunge/algorithms/polynomial_gf.hpp

    Classes

    CantorZassenhausOptionsSeed and complete-call work caps for odd-field squarefree factorization. Zero caps mean unlimited. Trials include constant candidates; modular products count multiply-then-reduce calls in polynomial powering/character construction, including DDF. Caps throw before excess work and never return a partial factor list. They do not bound coefficient operations, primality validation, gcd/division or time.
    CantorZassenhausTraceOwned input normalization, factors and actual DDF/EDF provenance without replay. input is normalized but retains its leading coefficient. monic_input is the divided-by-leading-coefficient polynomial. Product(factors)=monic_input; multiply by leading_coefficient to recover input. residual is the final DDF remainder; if nonconstant it is emitted directly as the last irreducible factor. Constants have no factors and residual=[1]. Invalid/zero/repeated-factor inputs throw.
    CantorZassenhausWorkActual high-level work counts from the shared factorization kernel. Counts do not measure scalar field operations or wall time. Gcd calls include squarefree validation, DDF and EDF; modular products count only multiply/reduce requests in powering/character computation. Ordinary calls keep these counters internally but allocate no DDF/EDF records.
    ChienGeneratorTestOne actual generator power test, retaining rejected candidates without replay. q is a distinct prime divisor of p-1; candidate passes this test iff value!=1. A primitive root must pass every distinct-factor test. Records own their values.
    ChienOptionsWhole-call limits for Chien enumeration and generator discovery; zero means unlimited. Point/term caps are checked from the normalized degree before generator work or sweep allocation. Generator steps count trial divisors plus primitive-root power tests, checked before each such operation; scalar arithmetic within a test and repeated division by an accepted factor are not separate steps. All shortcut paths use zero field-point and generator steps. Limits bound these named operations, not primality validation, normalization or elapsed time.
    ChienStepOwned actual coefficient-state vector and evaluation at one nonzero point. terms[j]=input[j]*point^j mod p immediately before the next update; value is their modular sum. The first record has exponent zero and point one. Recording does not re-evaluate the polynomial with Horner's method.
    ChienTraceOwned normalized input, actual generator/recurrence records, roots and work. Zero, constant and linear shortcuts leave generator, multipliers, zero-check and recurrence records empty/default; path identifies them explicitly. For Incremental, zero is checked separately, steps covers p-1 nonzero points, and the retained final update returns final_point=1 and final_terms=input. This is a prime-field implementation, not arithmetic over GF(2^m) for m>1. All records are independent of the input and other calls; nothing is replayed.
    ChienWorkActual named operations, including the legacy constant/closing state updates. Excludes prime testing, coefficient normalization, allocations and integer division/modulo work in factoring p-1. Each modular scalar multiplication is counted once, regardless of its bit cost; additions count all accumulator updates, including zero coefficients. Counters are checked size_t values.
    CZDistinctDegreeStepOne actual distinct-degree step on the current remaining monic polynomial. frobenius is x^(p^degree) modulo remaining_before. bucket is the monic gcd with frobenius-x, possibly the unit [1]. remaining_after is the exact quotient. Previously removed degree buckets are absent. Records own all coefficients.
    CZEqualDegreeTrialOne actual random equal-degree splitting attempt, including rejected constants. Candidate coefficients come from the legacy seeded xorshift stream modulo p; they are deterministic and slightly biased, not ideal independent uniform samples. A constant candidate is rejected without gcd/powering (all following polynomials empty). Otherwise initial_gcd is computed first. A proper gcd is accepted directly; else used_character=true and character is h^((p^d-1)/2) mod target. split_gcd then comes from gcd(character-1,target). quotient is set only for an accepted split.
    PolyDivModOwned normalized quotient and remainder of prime-field long division. For nonzero divisor b, a=q*b+r modulo p, with r zero or lower degree than b. The original aggregate layout is retained; neither vector borrows its inputs.
    PolynomialDivisionOptionsOptional producing-step and retained-scalar policies for division history. Zero disables its corresponding cap; ordinary polynomial division has no history policy.
    PolynomialDivisionStepOne actual leading-term cancellation over the validated prime field. Vectors contain actual normalized before/after producer storage; zero polynomials are empty.
    PolynomialDivisionTraceOrdinary result and actual canonical polynomial cancellation history. All records come from the same divide kernel used by ordinary division and existing polynomial algorithms.

    Functions

    cantor_zassenhaus()Factor a nonzero squarefree polynomial over an odd prime field. Preserves the original signature, default seed, coefficient alias and output traversal policy. Nonmonic inputs are divided by their leading coefficient; returned monic factors reconstruct that monic associate, not the original unit. Nonzero constants return no factors; zero/repeated factors and nonprime/even p throw before random splitting. No squarefree decomposition or GF(2) splitter is supplied. DDF uses incremental Frobenius; EDF uses an explicit depth-first stack. Character powering avoids materializing p^d, so no uint64 exponent wraps. The legacy deterministic modulo-reduced xorshift sampler is retained; ideal uniform-random expected-time claims do not guarantee termination for every seed. Ordinary calls allocate no DDF/EDF records. Inputs are unchanged, result owns coefficients, no shared state. See the configured variant for work/space costs.
    cantor_zassenhaus_trace()Retain actual DDF steps and EDF attempts from one shared factorization run. No factorization/powering is replayed. Character powers use the recurrence e_(j+1)=p*e_j+(p-1)/2 via modular powering, never storing p^d. This fixes wrapped uint64 exponents while retaining coefficient sampling and depth-first order. Input validation and caps match the configured ordinary variant. Owned records add storage proportional to the sum of recorded polynomial lengths across all steps/trials; potentially large traces should use explicit caps. Inputs unchanged.
    cantor_zassenhaus_with_options()Run checked squarefree odd-field factorization with whole-call work caps. Shares the original function's kernel, normalization, ordering and arithmetic. Schoolbook modular products/divisions cost O(n^2) field work. DDF costs at most O(n^3*log(p)); one EDF trial on an m-degree degree-d bucket costs O(d*m^2*log(p)), excluding scalar inversions and sampling. No fixed trial bound follows from the deterministic sampler. Untraced pending polynomials and dense scratch use O(n) coefficient storage, in addition to the output and inputs. Both budgets exclude scalar primality/gcd/division work; no partial factors return.
    chien_search()Find roots by the existing primitive-root Chien evaluation order. Checked prime p; arbitrary signed/trailing-zero coefficients are normalized. Retains the legacy zero-polynomial convention of returning no roots (rather than enumerating the whole field). Constants return empty; linears are solved directly. Higher degrees return zero first if a root, then nonzero roots in successive powers of the smallest primitive root. No sorting or multiplicities. Field enumeration is O(p*n) and generator search trial-factors p-1; intended for small fields, not huge p. Inputs unchanged, owned result, no shared state.
    chien_search_trace()Retain actual generator tests and every coefficient state from the shared Chien search. Same numeric/limit semantics as chien_search_with_options(), including constant and direct-linear shortcuts and the zero-polynomial sentinel. Generator tests and term vectors are captured in the executing kernel, never replayed. Incremental trace storage is O((p-1)*n) coefficient values plus generator tests and roots; max_points/max_term_products also bound that sweep storage. No partial trace escapes on failure; caller inputs are unchanged. Prime checking, trial-factoring p-1 and setup are additional to the O(p*n) sweep.
    chien_search_with_options()Run the legacy Chien root search with explicit whole-call operation limits. Same normalization, shortcuts, distinct-root order and zero convention as chien_search(). Point and state-product forecasts reject before generator search/sweep work; generator-step caps are checked during its actual search. Reaching any cap returns no partial root set. Ordinary calls retain no generator/term provenance. Inputs are unchanged; independent calls share no state.
    poly_derivative_gf()Return the normalized formal derivative, including characteristic-p zeros. Coefficient i becomes i*f[i] modulo p, without narrowing the degree or signed overflow. O(n) work/storage, owned output, borrowed input unchanged.
    poly_divmod_gf()Long division over a checked prime field, accepting arbitrary signed coefficients. Normalizes both operands and rejects a divisor that becomes zero. Remainder degree is strictly smaller than the normalized divisor; division by a nonzero constant returns zero remainder. Schoolbook quadratic field work; inputs unchanged, owned result.
    poly_divmod_gf_trace()Capture actual prime-field long-division cancellations. Coefficients are low-degree first and normalized into[0,p); signed inputs and trailing zeros are accepted. The full signed positive prime range is supported by widened products. Retains the normalized inputs and each actual working remainder and quotient. For degrees m>=n, ordinary work is O((m-n+1)*(n+1)) field operations plus normalization, primality validation and one scalar inverse power; copied histories can require quadratic coefficient storage. No caller storage or shared state is mutated.
    poly_evaluate_gf()Evaluate a polynomial by overflow-safe modular Horner recurrence. Normalizes arbitrary signed coefficients and x. Empty gives zero; O(n) field work and constant extra storage, input unchanged, no shared state.
    poly_gcd_gf()Monic Euclidean polynomial gcd over a checked prime field. gcd(0,0)=0; any nonzero constant gcd normalizes to [1]. O(n^2) schoolbook field work plus leading-coefficient inversion, owned result, inputs unchanged.
    poly_is_irreducible_gf()Deterministically test irreducibility by excluding all small-degree factors. A nonconstant polynomial is reducible iff it has an irreducible factor of degree at most half its degree. Repeated Frobenius powering and gcds test these degrees; zero/constants return false, all linears true. O(n^3*log(p)) schoolbook field operations as an upper bound, O(n) scratch storage, inputs unchanged.
    poly_is_squarefree_gf()Test absence of repeated irreducible factors using gcd(f,f'). Zero returns false; nonzero constants return true. Characteristic-p zero derivatives of nonconstant polynomials return false. Quadratic schoolbook gcd field work, inputs unchanged and no shared mutable state.
    poly_multiply_gf()Schoolbook polynomial product with overflow-safe modular accumulation. Normalizes arbitrary signed inputs; zero times anything is zero. Uses 128-bit intermediates, O(a.size()*b.size()) field operations and O(a.size()+b.size()) result storage. Borrows inputs, owns result, no shared mutable state.
    poly_normalize_gf()Reduce coefficients into [0,p) and trim trailing zeros without signed overflow. O(n) work/storage, owned result, inputs unchanged, no shared state. Validates the signed-64-bit prime using the existing deterministic 64-bit Miller-Rabin API.
    poly_string_gf()Format normalized coefficients as a descending-power ASCII polynomial. Omits zero terms and coefficient one on nonconstant terms; zero is "0". Owned string, inputs unchanged, linear coefficient traversal plus output formatting.

    Types and constants

    ChienPathenum Actual path used by the ordinary/traced Chien kernel after normalization. Shortcuts do not pretend to enumerate points or retain recurrence states.
    GFPolytype Owned low-to-high polynomial coefficients over a checked signed-64-bit prime field. Public functions accept arbitrary int64 coefficients and trailing zeros, then reduce into [0,p) and trim. Empty represents zero; nonzero degree is size()-1. No modulus is stored in this alias. Copies own their coefficients independently.

Peak ordinary auxiliary storage is O(n); owned inputs are unchanged outside this call. State is local.

    datamunge/algorithms/powerset_construction.hpp

    Classes

    PowersetTraceOwned determinised DFA and the actual NFA subset represented by each state. Subsets are sorted/unique and indexed exactly like dfa states; numbering is discovery order, scanning symbols ascending. Only reachable subsets are created. complete records the requested policy, not whether a partial-policy result happens to have every move. The empty initial subset is omitted in partial mode, yielding zero states/start=-1, or retained in complete mode.

    Functions

    powerset_construction()Determinise an epsilon-free NFA by constructing only reachable source subsets. Retains the original signature, discovery numbering and default partial policy. Each move unions source destinations; a subset accepts iff any source state accepts. Duplicates are collapsed. With complete=true the empty subset is a rejecting trap; otherwise empty moves are -1. No initial states in partial mode yields a valid zero-state DFA with start=-1. Validates every source row, start and target before allocation. The vector/map implementation can require exponentially many subsets and stores their explicit members while building; costs depend on generated subsets, union sizes, sorting and map comparisons, not just the number of source states. Results own storage; inputs/shared data are unchanged. There are no epsilon-closure operations.
    powerset_construction_trace()Retain the ordinary construction's actual source subsets and logical work. Shares the ordinary kernel; adds no second determinisation or provenance replay. Retaining subsets extends their lifetime into the owned result. A positive max_states throws before adding an excess subset, with no partial returned DFA; zero is unlimited. This cap is not a byte limit and cannot prevent large union temporaries or validation of the source. Numbering and completion match the ordinary overload, including zero-state partial empty-language output.

    nth_from_end_nfa()Construct the epsilon-free binary NFA accepting words whose nth symbol from the end is1. The original nondeterministic guess is preserved: state0 loops on both symbols and may advance to state1 on1; n-1 remaining symbols lead to the sole accepting state n. Words shorter than n reject. O(n) generator work/storage; it does not determinize or allocate2^n states. Returned storage is owned and no state is shared.

    datamunge/algorithms/primality.hpp

    Classes

    FermatBaseCensusExact exhaustive counts over a specified half-open Fermat base interval. Counts are integer census results, not samples or posterior probabilities. Passes are necessarily coprime, so passes/coprime is the conditional pass fraction only when coprime>0. Passes/total is the unconditioned interval fraction only when total>0. Empty intervals have all counts zero; no fraction is fabricated. Owned scalars and constant driver storage, with no shared state.
    FermatBaseResultOwned exact result of one Fermat congruence and its actual gcd. Tests base^(n-1) modulo n using canonical mod_pow, plus std::gcd. A failure proves n composite; a pass does not establish primality. Noncoprime bases cannot pass. No shared state, retained references or floating arithmetic.
    FermatPrimalityOutcomeOwned result, actual round count and last state of seeded Fermat testing. Requested rounds stay separate from completed rounds; early filters perform zero congruences. Last base/gcd/residue are zero for filters, otherwise actual values from the last tested round. True means prime for SmallPrime and only probable prime for RoundLimit. Scalar ownership has no shared mutable state.
    FermatPrimalityTraceOwned actual seeded round records captured during one Fermat test. C=captured_entries=rows.size() counts whole FermatBaseResult records. The solver admits a record before drawing its base or computing gcd/power; no replay and no nested exponent-bit history. Input/output scalars, capacity, allocators and runtime storage are excluded, so C is not peak RAM. Copies are independent; editing rows does not recompute the stored outcome.

    Functions

    atkin_primes()The Sieve of Atkin (Atkin & Bernstein, 2003): a modern prime sieve that marks candidates by counting solutions to three quadratic forms modulo 60 (4x^2+y^2, 3x^2+y^2, and 3x^2-y^2 with the appropriate residues), toggling each hit, then removes squares of primes. It has a better asymptotic operation count than Eratosthenes – O(limit) with wheel optimization (here O(limit) toggles over the quadratics) – and generates all primes up to limit. Each form is enumerated only over its own region, about 1.04*limit lattice points in all. Defined in sieve_of_atkin.cpp; see sieve_of_atkin.hpp for the forms and operation counts.
    fermat_base_census()Count exact Fermat passes and coprime bases over a bounded explicit interval. Evaluates every base once via fermat_base_test, including noncoprime bases. Use [2,n) for the original report's denominator (coprime bases excluding one), [2,n-1) for the sampler support of odd n>=5, or [1,n) for the full unit-group discussion. Default max_bases1m limits total bases before any arithmetic; zero disables that work cap. Empty [n,n) is valid. No allocation or history; O((last-first) log(n)) word work, constant auxiliary storage. Full ranges for large n are intentionally expensive; a tiny high-base interval is supported.
    fermat_base_test()Test one specified base using an exact power and gcd, with no sampling. A failing residue proves compositeness; a common_divisor greater than one is additionally a proper factor because 1<=base<n. Passing bases, including one, do not prove primality. Canonical mod_pow uses full128bit products; O(log(n)) fixed-word work and constant storage. Does not mutate shared state.
    fermat_primality_stop_name()Describe a seeded Fermat stop using a static literal string view. No allocation or shared mutation. Invalid enum representations give "unknown".
    fermat_probable_prime()Run the seeded Fermat congruence test, preserving its original compiled signature. Uses SplitMix64 and a=2+word%(n-3) for odd n>=5, stopping at the first failed residue. This samples all bases in [2,n-2], including noncoprime bases; hence Carmichael numbers can be rejected. Fixed seed means deterministic output; modulo reduction is generally biased and draws are not guaranteed independent uniform samples. No 2^-rounds error guarantee or cryptographic RNG claim. Uses canonical exact mod_pow and one gcd per actual round, O(R log(n)) fixed-word arithmetic and constant auxiliary storage; no optional history.
    fermat_probable_prime_trace()Capture actual drawn bases and their exact results during the same seeded test. Outcome and prefix match ordinary/work calls when capture succeeds. Admits one whole round record before the draw, gcd and power. Quota defaults to1m; zero disables only capture quota. Nonpositive rounds remain invalid. Capture failures throw without returning a partial trace. No mutable global RNG; results and copies own all storage. O(R log(n)) word work and O(R) records.
    fermat_probable_prime_work()Run the original seeded base stream and expose actual completed rounds and stop. Shares one kernel with the bool and trace calls; no optional allocation or capture quota. Filters draw no bases; a witness round counts as completed. Last-state scalars are actual values, never reconstructed. Seeded modulo sampling is deterministic and does not supply an iid error bound.

    Types and constants

    FermatPrimalityStopenum Actual stop reason for the seeded Fermat congruence test. BelowTwo means not prime (zero and one are not composite). SmallPrime covers two and three; Even rejects larger even inputs. Witness is a failed actual congruence; RoundLimit means all requested rounds passed, not a proof.

    tabular_corridor()Construct the reusable deterministic two-action corridor environment. States0..states-1, reset0. Action0 moves left/clamps0; action1 moves right/clamps the goal. Every step has the supplied finite reward and the last state is terminal. Lambdas capture scalar values only; no mutable environment state is shared.
    tabular_grid()Construct the reusable original square four-action grid environment. Reset is the top-left state0; bottom-right is terminal. Actions0,1,2,3 mean up,right,down,left; blocked moves stay in place. Row-major state ids are preserved. Each transition receives the finite supplied reward. Scalar-capture callbacks have no mutable shared state.
    tabular_policy_rollout()Execute an already chosen deterministic tabular policy through actual callbacks. Validates complete geometry, callback presence and every policy action before reset. O(S+T) native work and O(T) owned trajectory storage plus arbitrary callback work; this finite rollout is not a proof of general policy optimality.
    trailing_return_mean()Compute finite trailing episode-return means with partial initial windows. Element i averages returns[max(0,i+1-window)..i]. Uses a long-double sliding sum, so rounding can differ from repeated double summation; this is descriptive smoothing, not an uncertainty interval or convergence test. O(n) work and output storage, no shared state.

    Classes

    FourierGateOne actual gate call and its immediately resulting complete state. For Hadamard the control equals target and angle is zero; for Swap control/target are the swapped bits.
    QFTOptionsClassical state-vector and retained-entry policies. Zero independently disables either cap; coordinate counts are not peak-byte budgets.

    Functions

    inverse_qft()Apply the inverse native Fourier gate network in place. Uses the existing Hadamard, controlled-phase and bit-swap simulator calls. Forward sign is positive2*pi*i*j*k/N; inverse sign is negative and both use unitary1/sqrt(N) scaling. Complete finite/shape validation precedes gates; n=0 accepts one amplitude. Input need not have unit norm and is not renormalized. Classical work is O(n*n*2^n), ordinary additional storage O(2^n); this does not provide a classical exponential speedup. State is local and no references are retained. Uses default basis policy; successful return replaces state, errors leave it unchanged.
    qft()Apply the native Fourier gate network in place. Uses the existing Hadamard, controlled-phase and bit-swap simulator calls. Forward sign is positive2*pi*i*j*k/N; inverse sign is negative and both use unitary1/sqrt(N) scaling. Complete finite/shape validation precedes gates; n=0 accepts one amplitude. Input need not have unit norm and is not renormalized. Classical work is O(n*n*2^n), ordinary additional storage O(2^n); this does not provide a classical exponential speedup. State is local and no references are retained. Uses default basis policy; successful return replaces state, errors leave it unchanged.
    qft_comb()Construct a normalized finite comb state at offset+k*period. Uses all represented positions below2^n; period need not divide2^n. A nondividing period gives a truncated comb, so exact equally spaced frequency peaks are not promised. O(2^n) storage/initialization; the original N16,period4,offset1 support is1,5,9,13.
    qft_run()Execute the same Fourier network with actual selected gate counts. Uses the existing Hadamard, controlled-phase and bit-swap simulator calls. Forward sign is positive2*pi*i*j*k/N; inverse sign is negative and both use unitary1/sqrt(N) scaling. Complete finite/shape validation precedes gates; n=0 accepts one amplitude. Input need not have unit norm and is not renormalized. Classical work is O(n*n*2^n), ordinary additional storage O(2^n); this does not provide a classical exponential speedup. State is local and no references are retained. No gate histories are retained.
    qft_trace()Execute the same Fourier network with actual selected gate counts. Uses the existing Hadamard, controlled-phase and bit-swap simulator calls. Forward sign is positive2*pi*i*j*k/N; inverse sign is negative and both use unitary1/sqrt(N) scaling. Complete finite/shape validation precedes gates; n=0 accepts one amplitude. Input need not have unit norm and is not renormalized. Classical work is O(n*n*2^n), ordinary additional storage O(2^n); this does not provide a classical exponential speedup. State is local and no references are retained. Captured history includes complete states at every gate and can require O(n*n*2^n) entries.
