    datamunge/algorithms/quickselect.hpp

    Classes

    QuickselectOptionsSelected-work and history bounds; zero disables a size/work cap.
    QuickselectResultOwned answer and selected operations from the actual selection producer.
    QuickselectScalingActual cumulative work for both pivot strategies on identical generated arrays.
    QuickselectStepOne actual three-way partition, including recursive BFPRT pivot searches.

    Functions

    quickselect()Returns the k-th smallest element of data (0-indexed: k=0 is the minimum, k=1 the second smallest, ..., k=n-1 the maximum) – the k-th order statistic – without fully sorting the array. This is Hoare's Quickselect (1961): pick a pivot, partition the array so that everything smaller precedes it and everything larger follows it, note the pivot's final rank p, and then continue into only one strict side, stopping whenever the target rank is in the entire equal-pivot band. Because each step discards one partition instead of recursing into both (as quicksort does), the expected work follows the recurrence T(n) = T(n/2) + O(n) = O(n) on random input, versus O(n log n) to sort the whole array just to read one element. This overload takes data by value precisely because it reorders it internally; the caller's array is untouched. The pivot is chosen by the median-of-three rule (median of the first, middle, and last elements), a cheap deterministic pivot heuristic, though a truly adversarial permutation can still force the O(n^2) worst case – for a guaranteed linear bound use quickselect_mom. Duplicate values stop in one equal band. Delegates to the shared three-way producer without work/history caps.
    quickselect_mom()The median-of-medians (BFPRT) variant of quickselect: identical k-semantics and identical return value, but with a guaranteed worst-case O(n) running time. Blum, Floyd, Pratt, Rivest & Tarjan (1973) removed Quickselect's quadratic worst case by replacing the pivot heuristic with a provably good pivot: split the range into groups of five, find each group's median (a constant-time sort of at most five elements), then recursively take the median of those medians as the pivot. That pivot is guaranteed to be greater than at least (roughly) 3n/10 elements and less than at least 3n/10, so every partition discards a constant fraction of the array. The resulting recurrence T(n) <= T(n/5) + T(7n/10) + O(n) solves to O(n) because 1/5 + 7/10 < 1. The constant is larger than plain Quickselect's, so this variant trades average-case speed for an adversary-proof worst case; both functions always agree on the answer.
    quickselect_run()Select an order statistic using the shared duplicate-safe producer. Median-of-three is deterministic, expected O(n) on suitable random inputs and worst-case O(n^2). BFPRT with groups of five and three-way partitioning is worst-case O(n), including duplicates. Uses an owned O(n) input copy and O(log n) BFPRT recursion. Counters cover all nested pivot searches; operations is a selected event count, not CPU instructions. Input is unchanged.
    quickselect_scaling()Measure both canonical selection strategies on the original seeded uniform workload. Generates keys with one sequential mt19937_64(seed) stream and uniform_int_distribution<int64_t>(0,1000000), traversing sizes then trials. Both canonical producers select rank n/2 on identical copies; no report-local surrogate is used. Every size and total key count is validated before generation. Work/storage scales with actual trials/keys plus native selection; one array pair per trial. Returns actual comparison sums, not timing or a universal expected-time estimate.
    quickselect_trace()Capture actual partition bands from the same selection producer. Includes nested BFPRT pivot-selection partitions, distinguished by depth; histories cost range length plus one per record and are admitted before copying. Zero cap disables that policy. Runtime/storage otherwise match quickselect_run().

    datamunge/algorithms/quicksort.hpp

    Classes

    QuicksortOptionsSelected-work and retained-history limits; zero disables that limit.
    QuicksortResultOwned final keys and counters from the shared native quicksort producer.
    QuicksortScalingOne actual canonical sort measurement on the original sequential seeded workload.
    QuicksortStepOne actual completed partition or insertion-sort range.

    Functions

    quicksort() ×2Sorts data ascending, in place, using Quicksort (Hoare 1961) – the classic divide-and-conquer sort. A pivot is chosen and the range is partitioned so that every element strictly less than the pivot precedes it and everything else follows; the pivot thereby lands in its final sorted position and the two sides are sorted recursively. This implementation makes three refinements that turn textbook Quicksort into a robust one. First, median-of-three pivoting: the pivot is the median of the first, middle, and last elements of the range, which balances already-sorted and reverse-sorted distinct inputs while remaining fully deterministic. It offers no worst-case guarantee. Second, tail-call elimination: after each partition the smaller side is sorted by recursion and the larger side by looping, which bounds the recursion depth to O(log n) and so prevents stack overflow on adversarial inputs. Third, a small-subarray cutoff: ranges of at most sixteen elements are finished with insertion sort, which is faster than recursion on tiny inputs. The average-case cost is O(n log n) comparisons; the worst case is O(n^2) including all-equal inputs and adversarial permutations. Quicksort is in place (O(log n) auxiliary stack, no heap allocation) but not stable: equal elements may be reordered relative to one another. Empty and single-element inputs are returned unchanged.
    quicksort_run()Sort owned keys with the canonical sixteen-key-cutoff quicksort producer. Same median-of-three, Lomuto partition, smaller-side recursion and comparison-count sequence as the historical overload. Expected O(n log n) on suitable random inputs, worst-case O(n^2), including equal keys; live recursion O(log n). Result owns an O(n) input copy. Selected counters are events, not all machine instructions. Input is unchanged.
    quicksort_scaling()Measure canonical quicksort on one sequential native seeded workload. Creates one mt19937_64(seed) stream and consumes raw words modulo1000000 for each requested array in order, matching the original report. Executes the canonical counted producer, never a report mirror. Validates all cumulative key sizes before generation; empty arrays are supported. O(total sort work), O(max size) temporary keys plus result rows. The n log2 n reference is a mathematical scale, not a complexity guarantee for every input.
    quicksort_trace()Capture actual partition and cutoff ranges from the same quicksort producer. Each retained record costs range length plus one scalar/header entries, admitted before copying. Worst-case retained history can be quadratic; policy stops it. All other semantics match quicksort_run().

    datamunge/algorithms/rabin_karp.hpp

    Classes

    RabinKarpOptionsHash parameters and selected-work/history bounds.
    RabinKarpResultOwned exact matches and actual selected work.
    RabinKarpWindowOne actual candidate window, before advancing the rolling hash.

    Functions

    rabin_karp_run()Find exact byte matches using the shared checked rolling-hash producer. Hash equality is always followed by scalar unsigned-byte verification; even composite/small moduli and collisions cannot produce false matches. Embedded NUL/high bytes are supported. Empty pattern matches all n+1 positions; longer pattern visits no windows. Typical rare-collision work O(n+m), worst O(n*m), plus owned matches. Caller strings are unchanged. Default hash is the historical base256/mod1000000007.
    rabin_karp_search()The Rabin-Karp string-matching algorithm (Karp & Rabin 1987). Finds every position in text at which pattern occurs, using a polynomial rolling hash. Each length-m window of the text is treated as an m-digit number in some base b, taken modulo a large prime p; sliding the window one character to the right updates its hash in O(1) – subtract the leading digit's contribution, multiply by the base, add the incoming digit – rather than re-reading the whole window. When a window's hash equals the pattern's, that only suggests a match (two distinct strings can collide modulo p), so the actual characters are compared to confirm it; the returned positions are therefore always exact. Expected running time is O(n + m) when collisions are rare, degrading to O(n*m) in the worst case (adversarial or unlucky inputs that force a verification at every window). Overlapping occurrences are all reported.
    rabin_karp_trace()Capture every actual visited window and verification decision. Same producer as rabin_karp_run(); a record is admitted before the window is visited. One record per empty-pattern position. Retains O(n) records, bounded by policy; zero disables the cap.

    datamunge/algorithms/radix_sort.hpp

    Classes

    RadixSortOptionsAllocation/history limits for owned radix runs; zero disables a cap.
    RadixSortPassOne actual completed stable byte pass on sign-biased keys.
    RadixSortResultOwned ascending keys, stable identities and actual selected pass work.

    Functions

    radix_sort()LSD (least-significant-digit) radix sort for signed 64-bit integers, sorting data ascending in place. Radix sort is a non-comparison sort: instead of asking "is a < b?" it distributes keys by their digits, sidestepping the (\Omega(n \log n)) lower bound that binds every comparison sort. This implementation treats each key as eight base-256 "digits" (its bytes) and makes one stable counting-sort pass per byte, from least to most significant. Because each pass is stable, keys that agree on the current byte keep the order established by the lower bytes already processed – and after all eight passes the array is fully ordered. Signed keys are handled by flipping the sign bit (equivalently, biasing by (2^{63})) so that two's-complement order maps onto plain unsigned byte order; the bias is undone at the end. Runs in (O(d\,(n+b))) time with (d = 8) passes and radix (b = 256), i.e. linear in data 's size, using scratch buffers of size (n). Empty and singleton inputs are returned unchanged.
    radix_sort_run()Stably sort signed 64-bit keys with the shared byte-LSD producer. Flips the sign bit, then executes eight stable counting/scatter passes. Origin identities are moved alongside keys, exposing stability. Empty/singleton inputs perform zero passes. O(8*(n+256)) time and O(n+256) working storage, plus owned output. Input is unchanged. Counters cover selected digit reads, scatter pairs and prefix updates, excluding allocation/initialization and sign conversion.
    radix_sort_trace()Retain every actual histogram, prefix array and stable pass output. Uses the same producer as radix_sort_run(). Each pass costs 2n+514 scalar/header entries, admitted before capture. Pass values are signed decodings of intermediate biased words, not sorted signed arrays until the final pass. History O(8n+8*256), bounded by policy; zero cap disables.

Convert these canonical observations to tensors for neural model computation.
    rbf_fit_output()Fit only the checked output coefficients for caller-selected fixed Gaussian centers. Uses the same native feature/normal-system solver as rbf_train_run(), with no Lloyd placement or width heuristic. Penalizes all output coefficients including bias, permitting a like-for-like independent comparison to an explicitly optimized tensor model. Center inputs are copied; no fitting iterations are hidden. Same shape/value, complexity and error semantics as the native training run after center placement.
    rbf_predict()Predict with a completely checked native closed-form comparison model. Validates every center/weight and finite matching input coordinates before feature evaluation. Width must be finite/positive and weights must match centers. Empty-center model predicts its finite bias. Uses the same widened Gaussian feature formula as fitting; O(K*d) time, constant extra working storage, no model mutation.
    rbf_train()Return the checked canonical closed-form model through the preserved signature. Delegates to rbf_train_run() with the same defaults and model field layout. Complete validation and singular-system failure replace previous unchecked shapes/zero-center indexing and silent coefficient dropping. For tensor neural fitting, use nn::rbf_features() with an explicit optimizer loop and keep this as a separate baseline.
    rbf_train_run()Fit a checked native Gaussian-basis closed-form regression baseline. Validates finite nonempty rectangular inputs and matching finite targets, finite nonnegative ridge and finite width. K=min(requested,n); K0 is an explicit intercept-only baseline without Lloyd. Initializes centers with the historical mt19937_64 random-sample stream and executes exactly the requested Lloyd passes, retaining empty-cluster centers. A positive width is used directly; nonpositive finite width selects the historical maximum-center-distance/sqrt(2K) heuristic, falling back to1. Forms actual bias-first Gaussian design and ridge normal equations, penalizing the bias too. Uses widened arithmetic and checked partial-pivot elimination, throwing on an exact singular system instead of silently dropping its coefficients. Time O(passes*n*K*d+n*K^2+K^3), O(n*K+K^2) working storage; inputs unchanged, outputs owned. This is an independent closed-form comparison for reports whose demonstrated neural fitting uses explicit tensor optimization.
    rbf_train_trace()Capture actual sampled centers, Lloyd passes, design and normal equations. Same single producer as rbf_train_run(). Retained scalar entries count initial center coordinates, real before/after centers and assignments/counts, then actual design/system/right-side values, plus one header for each capture. Admission precedes copies. Zero capture cap disables that bound; diagnostic narrowing may throw if a retained system scalar exceeds finite double range.

    Classes

    Rc4Historical RC4 raw-byte stream state with canonical KSA and PRGA. RC4 has known key-stream biases and is prohibited in TLS by RFC7465; this class is for historical/conformance study, not a modern security construction. A fresh nonempty raw byte key initializes the256-byte identity permutation then256 KSA swaps. Copies duplicate raw state; mutating a shared instance needs synchronization. Constant state storage; constructor O(256), each next O(1). Owns no key/history pointer after construction.

    Rc4StepOne actual PRGA update, swap and output lookup.
    Rc4TraceOwned actual key schedule and output transitions.

    Functions

    rc4_encrypt()XOR raw data with one fresh classic RC4 stream. Encryption and decryption are the same bytewise XOR. Validates a nonempty key even for empty data; embedded NUL/high bytes are preserved. Reusing a key restarts the same keystream; no nonce, authentication or modern security property is supplied. O(256+size) time and owned output, default million-byte allocation policy.
    rc4_keystream()Return the first n actual classic RC4 keystream bytes. Same Rc4 producer as the trace. Nonempty key is validated even for n0; owned output allocation is bounded by the default million-byte policy. Use rc4_trace() to configure capture policies. O(256+n) time and O(n) output.
    rc4_second_byte_study()Run the original deterministic second-keystream-byte experiment natively. Generates key "k"+decimal(uint32(k)*2654435761 mod2^32 mod1000000) for k0..count-1. This preserves the report recipe including32-bit multiplication wrap. Counts exact second bytes, high-nibble groups and distinct strings; the sequence is not iid random keys and finite histograms do not establish a bias theorem. O(256*count) work plus distinct-key storage.
    rc4_trace()Capture actual KSA and PRGA decisions from one canonical stream execution. Complete logical capture admission precedes construction:516 state scalars+256 schedule records+n output records. Returned bytes and step output fields come from the same actual transitions. No inline XML/encoding is produced. O(256+n) time and owned storage.

    datamunge/algorithms/realtime_scheduling.hpp

    Classes

    RTJobActual per-job release, execution, completion and deadline evidence. Job ids are indices in RTTrace::jobs, ordered by release time then input task. Deadlines use int64_t so release+period cannot overflow int. A zero-work job completes at release; an unfinished job has completion=-1 even if already late.
    RTScheduleResultMerged task timeline and deadline verdict for a finite simulation. Timeline covers [0,H) exactly. deadline_missed includes all job deadlines through boundary H; unfinished jobs due after H are not yet misses. Copies own their timeline. A finite clean prefix is not an infinite schedulability proof.
    RTSimulationFinite scheduling outcome and work, with no retained job/tick history. Independent calls leave input unchanged. Runtime retains unfinished jobs; completed jobs are removed. There is no optional capture quota.
    RTSliceAn owned-label interval in a merged task execution timeline. Half-open [start,end); returned slices have nonnegative start and end>start. Adjacent units running the same task are merged, even across job boundaries.
    RTTaskAn independent synchronous periodic task with implicit deadlines. Jobs release at 0,T,2T,... and need C integer processor units by the next release. One fully preemptive processor, zero overhead and no blocking are assumed. APIs require positive period, nonnegative wcet and unique ids other than SIZE_MAX (reserved for idle). C>T is a valid overloaded task.
    RTTraceOwned actual release records and per-unit job selections, without replay. Capture has N task records, H tick selections and J released job records, so captured_entries=N+H+J. Scalars, result timeline, working heap/counters, vector capacity and allocator bytes are excluded: this is not a peak-RAM bound. Retained history uses O(N+H+J) entries; result/runtime memory is additional.
    RTWorkChecked logical counters for the actual unit-granularity simulator. Counts are not elapsed time or scheduler overhead. Preemption means the next unit selects a different job while the previously selected job is unfinished; stopping at the horizon is not a preemption. Zero-work releases complete at once.

    Functions

    edf_schedulable()Test exact rational utilization <=1 for the implicit-deadline EDF model.
    edf_simulate()Return the ordinary EDF merged timeline and deadline verdict.
    plot_rt_schedule()Draw a validated merged task timeline using native RPlot polygons.
    rate_monotonic_bound()Evaluate the Liu-Layland RMS sufficient utilization bound numerically.
    rate_monotonic_priorities()Order RMS task ids by increasing period, then input position.
    rate_monotonic_schedulable()Screen RMS using its sufficient utilization bound.
    rate_monotonic_simulate()Return the ordinary RMS merged timeline and deadline verdict.
    rt_simulate_work()Simulate periodic EDF or RMS without retaining optional history.
    rt_trace()Capture actual released jobs and selected job ids for every simulated unit.
    rt_trace_entries()Validate and count the complete retained history before tracing.
    rt_utilization()Sum periodic processor demand C/T as a floating-point display value.

    Types and constants

    RTPolicyenum Dynamic deadline or fixed period priority, with stable input-order ties. Equal deadlines/periods prefer the earlier input task; jobs of one task run in release order. Task-id numeric order has no scheduling significance.

    Classes

    RecursiveDescentOptionsSource, recursion, selected-call and actual-node policies; zero disables a cap.
    RecursiveDescentResultOwned actual parser value, selected work and optional real syntax tree.
    RecursiveNodeOwned scalar syntax node appended when the native parser actually completes it.

    Functions

    recursive_descent_diagram()Draw a validated actual producing syntax tree with native measured label boxes. Consumes retained nodes from recursive_descent_trace(), validates child ordering, ownership shape, finite values and source byte spans, then delegates layout to Diagram::rooted_tree(). Labels show real token/operator values. This validates display structure, not a caller-edited arithmetic proof. No evaluation or replay populates the tree. Layout follows the canonical rooted-tree complexity, O(N^2+text) time and O(N) working storage; inputs unchanged, returned geometry owned.
    recursive_descent_eval()Return the checked finite scalar through the preserved recursive-descent signature. Delegates to the same native producer. Previously partially converted repeated decimals, embedded NUL and nonfinite arithmetic now reject. Uses default complete-input, call-depth and selected-call policies; use the run API to configure them.
    recursive_descent_run()Evaluate decimal arithmetic using the shared checked recursive-descent producer. Grammar: expr=term((+|-)term)*; term=factor((*|/)factor)*; factor=number|(+|-)factor|(expr). Unary signs bind at factor level; binary operators associate left. Decimal tokens allow one point and at least one digit, without exponents. Converts complete tokens using locale-independent from_chars; embedded NUL, malformed or trailing bytes reject. Every successful scalar operation must remain finite; division by zero throws. O(bytes+actual calls) work plus owned source and bounded call stack; input unchanged, no shared mutable state.
    recursive_descent_trace()Capture the actual syntax tree constructed by the same evaluation producer. Every completed number, unary operation, binary operation or group appends exactly one owned postorder node; child ids are real previously completed nodes. Source offsets refer to the owned unchanged expression. Nodes are admitted before insertion; zero cap disables retained-node policy. O(actual nodes) retained storage in addition to ordinary parsing.

    Types and constants

    RecursiveNodeKindenum Actual arithmetic syntax-node kind.

    datamunge/algorithms/rice_coding.hpp

    Classes

    RiceLengthRowOne exact conditional expected length of actual Rice codewords.

    Functions

    rice_decode_trace()Capture actual Rice decoding codeword spans from the canonical Golomb producer. Rice is the power-of-two Golomb case: quotient unary ones plus zero, followed by exactly k raw remainder bits. Validates k even for empty input and delegates once to the checked native Golomb producer; no replay, decoded prefix excludes unread trailing bits. Encoding checks complete mathematical bit size before allocation. Decoding bounds the complete input, requires exactly count words, and rejects missing complete words even at an input boundary. Time O(actual bit visits+words), owned actual bits/codewords; all fields and overflow semantics follow GolombTrace. The model and count remain external metadata.
    rice_encode_trace()Capture actual Rice encoding codeword spans from the canonical Golomb producer. Rice is the power-of-two Golomb case: quotient unary ones plus zero, followed by exactly k raw remainder bits. Validates k even for empty input and delegates once to the checked native Golomb producer; no replay, decoded prefix excludes unread trailing bits. Encoding checks complete mathematical bit size before allocation. Decoding bounds the complete input, requires exactly count words, and rejects missing complete words even at an input boundary. Time O(actual bit visits+words), owned actual bits/codewords; all fields and overflow semantics follow GolombTrace. The model and count remain external metadata.
    rice_length_study()Reproduce the original finite geometric-weight Rice length study through real native emission. For n=0..largest, use weights2^(-n/half_life), normalize over that finite support, and average each actual emitted codeword span. This is a conditional truncated model expectation, not the full geometric expectation, observed compression of random data, or a bitstream byte serialization. For k=0..max_k each canonical encoding executes once. Time/storage follow actual emitted bits, bounded independently for every model.

    datamunge/algorithms/root_finding.hpp

    Classes

    FalsePositionEvaluationOne owned actual callback evaluation from endpoint initialization or a trial. Records the returned finite value without retaining or calling the function again.
    FalsePositionOptionsIndependent policy, function-unit and coordinate-unit controls for secant bracketing. Zero residual or coordinate tolerance disables that test; callback zeros always stop. Endpoint zeros are checked before sign rejection; endpoint residual-only acceptance is not performed. All controls are validated before callbacks/capture.
    FalsePositionOutcomeOwned result, terminal reason, actual work and true-versus-weighted bracket state. For a trial stop, a/b and their values/weights describe the bracket used to compute the returned estimate, before its terminal update. Endpoint zero collapses that state to the zero endpoint; same-sign rejection keeps original inputs, default RootResult and infinite radius. Input order is retained, so a need not be less than b. Radius is the rounded maximum estimate-to-endpoint distance, possibly infinity for a full-width interval; not an outward-rounded certified error bound. Small residual does not imply small coordinate error. No callback or input reference is retained; independent calls share no state.
    FalsePositionStepActual pre-update bracket, true values, artificial weights and one evaluated trial. Pre-update terminal tests leave replaced=0; weight underflow can follow an actual replacement/halving. Raw signs certify the bracket under caller assumptions; weights only choose the secant. Snapshots own all values and are never reconstructed by another solve.
    FalsePositionTraceOwned outcome and callback/step records captured during the same actual solve. Logical optional capture C=evaluations.size()+steps.size() counts WHOLE records: both endpoints cost2 and each evaluated trial adds2. Metadata, ordinary result, capacities and allocator/runtime bytes are excluded; this is not peak RAM. Quota is admitted before both endpoint calls and before each trial's arithmetic/ callback; zero disables quota only. No partial trace escapes an exception.

    Functions

    false_position()Solve through the historical compiled retained-twice Illinois interface. Shares false_position_work() with policy Illinois, residual tolerance tol and coordinate tolerance disabled. Keeps input orientation and f(a),f(b) evaluation order, including evaluating both before endpoint-zero acceptance. Safe legacy secant arithmetic is retained when nonzero products remain normal; scaled-weight interpolation avoids finite overflow or spurious product-underflow trials otherwise. Exact callback zeros and trial residuals strictly below tol pass. Same-sign endpoints return the default unconverged record. Floating stagnation/weight underflow/budget exhaustion return unconverged. Raw endpoint values stay separate from artificial weights. Continuity and reliable signs are caller assumptions; a small residual alone is no coordinate certificate. O(max_iter) calls and constant auxiliary state, no optional history/quota/shared mutable state. Callback exceptions and side effects belong to the caller.
    false_position_policy_name()Return a stable name for a supported false-position policy. Program-lifetime literal, no allocation or shared mutation; unknown values map to unknown.
    false_position_stop_name()Return a stable name for a false-position stopping reason. Program-lifetime literal, no allocation/shared mutation; unknown values map to unknown.
    false_position_trace()Capture actual finite callback evaluations and steps during one checked bracketing solve. Shares false_position_work()'s kernel, controls, actual calls and terminal rules; no replay or callback retained. C=2+2K whole records for K actual trials, as in FalsePositionTrace. Known initial2 records admitted before either callback; each trial's2 records admitted before interpolation/callback. Default quota1m, zero disables only quota. O(K) owned optional history, no partial result on exceptions; callback side effects may already have occurred before a later failure.
    false_position_work()Execute checked plain or retained-twice Illinois bracketing with actual work counts. Uses the same kernel as false_position(); no optional history/quota. Options specify independent residual and rounded-radius tolerances; zero disables a test. A callback zero stops first, then residual, radius, stagnation and budget. Pre-update stopping tests skip the terminal update; weight underflow instead reports the actual halving that failed. Input orientation and both initial calls are retained. Endpoint-zero/no-bracket outcomes follow FalsePositionOutcome. Finite interpolation guards avoid intermediate overflow; if double precision cannot move the point or retain a nonzero weight, the unconverged stop is explicit. O(budget) callbacks/constant storage. No callback/input alias or shared state.

    Types and constants

    FalsePositionPolicyenum Select plain secant bracketing or the legacy retained-twice Illinois variant. Illinois starts with no previous replacement; damping begins only when the same endpoint is replaced twice consecutively. This differs from the paper's most-recent-point initialization, while retaining its stale-weight mechanism.
    FalsePositionStopenum Distinguish numerical stopping conditions from a mathematical root certificate. Continuity, existence and trustworthy callback signs are caller assumptions; a callback zero or tolerance test alone does not establish those assumptions.

    round_toward_zero()Round one scalar using the TowardZero rule. Returns a floating integer without integer narrowing. NaN and infinities propagate unchanged; signed zero propagates unchanged. Finite input is classified by floor and its widened fractional distance, avoiding x+0.5 rounding before the tie decision. O(1), no mutation or shared state. Ties mean an exact represented fractional half, not a decimal textual approximation.
    round_with()Apply one explicitly selected integer rounding rule. Supports exactly the seven RoundMode enumerators. Finite nearest modes classify the widened original input-minus-floor fraction; directed modes use native floor/ceil/trunc. Nonfinite values and signed zero propagate unchanged. O(1), reentrant, input unchanged.
    rounding_bias()Return the observed mean signed rounding error through the preserved signature. Uses the same checked producer and default million-value bound. Finite samples only; empty returns zero. Uses widened accumulation, without claiming unbiasedness for arbitrary samples.
    rounding_example_ties()Generate a canonical controlled report input. Construct the original60 positive half-integers0.5,1.5,...,59.5 exactly. These deliberately tie-heavy observations illustrate sample-specific signed error, not a universal population bias.
    rounding_run()Compute actual rounding decisions and observed mean error. Validates the supported mode and every input as finite before producing outputs. Empty input has zero mean/ties and empty outputs. The observed mean error describes this supplied sample, not a population bias theorem. O(N) time and output, with one optional retained record per value. Complete max_values admission precedes allocations; zero disables the policy. Inputs unchanged and histories owned.
    rounding_trace()Compute actual rounding decisions and capture their running errors. Validates the supported mode and every input as finite before producing outputs. Empty input has zero mean/ties and empty outputs. The observed mean error describes this supplied sample, not a population bias theorem. O(N) time and output, with one optional retained record per value. Complete max_values admission precedes allocations; zero disables the policy. Inputs unchanged and histories owned.

    ruzzo_tompa()Return native maximal-scoring intervals through the preserved signature. Uses the same direct predecessor-scan producer and default bounds; valid ordinary interval ordering is preserved. Worst-case quadratic work is explicit, replacing the old incorrect linear-time claim.
    ruzzo_tompa_run()Integrate positive scoring intervals through the native direct predecessor scan. Preserves the original candidate-list algorithm: maintain widened cumulative scores; each strictly positive value seeds a candidate. Search existing candidates from right to left for the first smaller left prefix; merge it and all following entries only if its right prefix is also strictly smaller. Emit the final surviving list. Zero/negative values update the actual prefix but do not seed. Maximality uses strict improvement over every proper subinterval, so zero-score extensions are not added. This implementation deliberately measures a direct predecessor scan: worst-case O(N^2), unlike the linear-time linked algorithm in the original paper. Candidate removals themselves total at most N. Optional complete-list histories can be quadratic too. Finite inputs required; widened prefix arithmetic is not an exact-real certificate, and nonzero increments that vanish at its precision reject. Empty/all-nonpositive inputs yield no segments. Borrowed input unchanged, output owned; no callbacks/shared state.
    ruzzo_tompa_trace()Integrate positive scoring intervals with actual candidate histories.     rvm_predict()Evaluate a checked bias-first RBF mean model. Validates complete model geometry, finite weights/centers, positive gamma/beta, active markers/count and input shape before indexing. Empty/unfitted models are invalid. Borrowed storage unchanged; no shared state.
    rvm_predictive()Evaluate actual matched posterior mean and Gaussian predictive variance. Uses the final active covariance stored by the producing run. Latent variance is phi^T Sigma phi; observation variance adds 1/beta. Validates covariance shape, finiteness and symmetry; arbitrary manual edits cannot be certified as a fitted posterior. Tiny negative roundoff is clamped, substantial negative variance fails. These are model-conditional quantities and do not establish empirical uncertainty calibration.
    rvm_sine_example()Return the original noiseless sine study inputs through the native library. Training x=2*pi*i/40 for i=0..40 and grid x=2*pi*i/200 for i=0..200; target/truth are sin(x). Uses no random noise or shared state.
    rvm_train()Fit the checked posterior through the preserved legacy signature. Delegates to the same native producer with default geometry policies and final active-basis refit.
    rvm_train_run()Fit checked sparse Bayesian RBF regression. Builds a bias plus one Gaussian basis per training point. Canonical long-double Cholesky solves Sigma=(diag(alpha)+beta*Phi^T*Phi)^-1 and mu=beta*Sigma*Phi^T*t. Actual gamma_j=1-alpha_j*Sigma_jj updates alpha_j=gamma_j/mu_j^2 and beta=(n-sum gamma)/(SSE+1e-12); nonpositive/nonfinite alpha uses ten times prune_threshold and beta uses inverse(target sample variance+1e-9). Initial alpha=1 and beta=1/(0.1*sample variance+1e-9). Tiny numerical gamma_j excursions are clamped to [0,1]; substantial excursions fail. Stops on maximum log-alpha change after at least three updates or budget. After final selection alpha<threshold, ALWAYS refits the active basis plus bias using the final reported alpha and beta. This fixes historical stale means and supplies covariance matching the pruned mean; finite-budget legacy predictions may change. Zero updates gives the initial posterior. Empty/ragged/nonfinite inputs are rejected. No global evidence optimum, sparsity level, calibration or convergence guarantee. Each solve O((n+1)^3), working O((n+1)^2); trace O(updates*(n+1)). Complete geometry and capture checked before work/copies. Borrowed input unchanged; calls share no mutable state.
    rvm_train_trace()Fit checked sparse Bayesian RBF regression retaining actual fixed-point updates. Builds a bias plus one Gaussian basis per training point. Canonical long-double Cholesky solves Sigma=(diag(alpha)+beta*Phi^T*Phi)^-1 and mu=beta*Sigma*Phi^T*t. Actual gamma_j=1-alpha_j*Sigma_jj updates alpha_j=gamma_j/mu_j^2 and beta=(n-sum gamma)/(SSE+1e-12); nonpositive/nonfinite alpha uses ten times prune_threshold and beta uses inverse(target sample variance+1e-9). Initial alpha=1 and beta=1/(0.1*sample variance+1e-9). Tiny numerical gamma_j excursions are clamped to [0,1]; substantial excursions fail. Stops on maximum log-alpha change after at least three updates or budget. After final selection alpha<threshold, ALWAYS refits the active basis plus bias using the final reported alpha and beta. This fixes historical stale means and supplies covariance matching the pruned mean; finite-budget legacy predictions may change. Zero updates gives the initial posterior. Empty/ragged/nonfinite inputs are rejected. No global evidence optimum, sparsity level, calibration or convergence guarantee. Each solve O((n+1)^3), working O((n+1)^2); trace O(updates*(n+1)). Complete geometry and capture checked before work/copies. Borrowed input unchanged; calls share no mutable state.

Units are two range copies plus event header, and for each partition 24 sampled keys+24 source indices+7 splitters+8 bucket sizes.     Functions

    secant()Return checked native secant diagnostics through the preserved signature. Uses the same producer/default callback bounds. Negative budgets and nonfinite controls now reject; zero attempts still diagnose the initial points. iterations records actual completed correction queries, replacing the former loop-index offset.
    secant_run()Execute checked unbracketed secant iteration. Validates finite initial points, nonempty callback, nonnegative finite tolerance and an int-compatible attempt budget before any callback. Queries both initial points; an initial actual residual success returns its matching point. Each attempt normalizes finite callback values in widened arithmetic before forming the ratio, then uses a convex combination for interpolation or a widened difference for extrapolation. Horizontal secants, a proposal rounded to the current point, unrepresentable arithmetic and exhausted budgets return explicit unconverged outcomes at the last actually queried point. Finite callback returns are required; exceptions propagate synchronously. No sign-changing bracket or global convergence guarantee is assumed; local superlinear order requires a simple regular root and suitable starting points. Time O(actual callback work+attempts), O(1) work plus optional actual query/proposal records, admitted before their work. Inputs unchanged, outputs owned; no retained callback/shared state.

    datamunge/algorithms/sha1.hpp

    Classes

    SHA1BlockOne actual producing sha1 compression block.
    SHA1RoundOne actual producing sha1 working-state round.
    SHA1RunOwned actual sha1 digest and selected compression work.

    Functions

    sha1()Return the checked sha1 raw digest through the preserved signature. Delegates to the same native producer with no optional byte-size policy and no optional history, preserving historical arbitrary-message support within intrinsic FIPS and container bounds.
    sha1_avalanche()Measure actual sha1 output changes for every single input-bit flip. Hashes the unchanged baseline once, then one same-length message per input bit in byte order and least-significant-bit-first order. Native digest-Hamming popcounts feed a full support histogram, without the historical clipped tail bins. Empty input still hashes the baseline once and returns a zero mean and empty flip history. Complete bit count and requested flip cap checked before any hashing. Retains only current message/digest plus owned O(bits+digest_bits) summary. This fixed-message diagnostic is not a security proof or statistical independence test.
    sha1_hex()Return the checked sha1 digest as lowercase hexadecimal. Uses the canonical native digest and hex encoder without a separate hashing implementation.
    sha1_run()Compute checked sha1 on complete raw bytes. Follows FIPS180-4 SHA1 padding, schedule, modulo2^32 round updates and block feed-forward. Empty and embedded-NUL messages are supported. Checks original length fits the FIPS64-bit bit-length field, padded container geometry, selected counters and complete optional capture before allocation or compression. Captured logical units per block are one block header+80 scheduled words+10 chain words+80*(one round header+10 working words+one scheduled-word copy). Does not retain a second padded-message copy in the result. O(bytes) time/intrinsic padded storage; optional history proportional to actual blocks with the stated fixed constants. Borrowed input unchanged; output owns its bytes/history; no shared state. SHA-1 is retained as a historical algorithm, not a collision-resistant security choice. Digest conformance and avalanche diagnostics do not establish resistance to attacks.
    sha1_trace()Compute checked sha1 on complete raw bytes retaining actual schedules and rounds. Follows FIPS180-4 SHA1 padding, schedule, modulo2^32 round updates and block feed-forward. Empty and embedded-NUL messages are supported. Checks original length fits the FIPS64-bit bit-length field, padded container geometry, selected counters and complete optional capture before allocation or compression. Captured logical units per block are one block header+80 scheduled words+10 chain words+80*(one round header+10 working words+one scheduled-word copy). Does not retain a second padded-message copy in the result. O(bytes) time/intrinsic padded storage; optional history proportional to actual blocks with the stated fixed constants.     shannon_fano_elias_run()Construct an exact integer-midpoint Shannon-Fano-Elias codebook. For each positive count f in original symbol order and prior count c, generate L=ceil(log2(total/f))+1 bits of (2*c+f)/(2*total). Length uses integer doubling; bits use exact unsigned128 long division, avoiding floating boundary rounding. Checks complete uint64 total and codeword-bit geometry before generating any words. Zero counts are inactive and receive empty words; an empty alphabet is supported, but a nonempty all-zero alphabet rejects. A singleton active symbol receives word1. Grammar: finite nonnegative decimal literals with at least one digit and at most one dot, binary + - * / ^, whitespace and matched parentheses. Empty input is invalid. Conversion is O(bytes) without optional copied snapshots; evaluation O(tokens) excluding pow implementation.     signed_apply_reversal()Apply one checked inclusive signed reversal to an owned permutation. Reverses the interval and negates each gene. Validates permutation and indices before mutation; O(n) validation and owned output, no shared state.
    signed_breakpoints()Count framed directed breakpoints in a signed permutation. Frames with0 and n+1 and counts b!=a+1. A signed reversal preserves all internal directed adjacencies and changes at most two boundary adjacencies, so ceil(breakpoints/2), not the raw count, lower-bounds distance. Validates genes, supports empty input; O(n) time/storage, no shared state.
    signed_reversal_run()Find an exact shortest signed-reversal sequence. Input must contain each absolute gene1..n exactly once. Empty permutation is identity. BFS visits reversals [i,j] in increasing i then j, storing each first predecessor; first discovered identity is optimal because every edge has unit cost. The reported path comes from those actual stored states, not a separate replay. n genes have at most 2^n*n! states; generating n(n+1)/2 O(n)-copy neighbors and ordered-map lookup per expanded state is exponential. Bounds abort with an exception, never an invented distance or optimality claim. No biological inference from synthetic toy permutations. Owned working storage, no shared state.
    signed_reversal_trace()Find an exact shortest signed-reversal sequence with actual selected predecessor states. Input must contain each absolute gene1..n exactly once. Empty permutation is identity. BFS visits reversals [i,j] in increasing i then j, storing each first predecessor; first discovered identity is optimal because every edge has unit cost. The reported path comes from those actual stored states, not a separate replay. n genes have at most 2^n*n! states; generating n(n+1)/2 O(n)-copy neighbors and ordered-map lookup per expanded state is exponential. Bounds abort with an exception, never an invented distance or optimality claim. No biological inference from synthetic toy permutations. Owned working storage, no shared state.

Fraction in[0,1]; zero magnitude images produce no edges. gx/gy are not inspected. O(pixels) time/output, at most one million pixels, owned indices, no shared state. This is simple thresholding, not Canny suppression/hysteresis or a semantic-edge classifier.
    sobel_run()Correlate a finite rectangular image with the Sobel masks. Unnormalized kx=[[-1,0,1],[-2,0,2],[-1,0,1]], ky=[[-1,-2,-1],[0,0,0],[1,2,1]]. These are correlations, not flipped-kernel mathematical convolutions. gx increases to the right; gy increases down image rows. All outer border responses are forced zero, so no padded boundary gradient is estimated. Empty/zero-width inputs and images below3 in either dimension have no interior work. Finite rectangular input required; nonrepresentable sums/magnitudes throw. O(rows*columns) time/storage, optional actual history O(interior pixels). Complete cell/history geometry checked before computation. Borrowed input and owned output; no shared state.
    sobel_square_example()Generate the original32x32 bright-square fixture. Rows/columns8..23 contain255, all others0. Owned deterministic synthetic image, not a photograph or annotated edge dataset.
    sobel_trace()Correlate a finite rectangular image with the Sobel masks and capture actual contributions. Unnormalized kx=[[-1,0,1],[-2,0,2],[-1,0,1]], ky=[[-1,-2,-1],[0,0,0],[1,2,1]]. These are correlations, not flipped-kernel mathematical convolutions. gx increases to the right; gy increases down image rows. All outer border responses are forced zero, so no padded boundary gradient is estimated. Empty/zero-width inputs and images below3 in either dimension have no interior work. Finite rectangular input required; nonrepresentable sums/magnitudes throw. O(rows*columns) time/storage, optional actual history O(interior pixels). Complete cell/history geometry checked before computation. Borrowed input and owned output; no shared state.

    SOROptionsSOROptions owns actual producer values or explicit invocation policies; fields state units and defaults.
    SORRunSORRun owns actual producer values or explicit invocation policies; fields state units and defaults.

    Functions

    sor()Return the preserved checked SOR solution signature. Same forward producer, inclusive actual absolute residual stopping and default size/work policies. Unlike the historical shortcut, zero-sweep results report the real initial residual.
    sor_run()Solve from a zero initial iterate by actual forward SOR sweeps. Requires finite square A, matching finite b and nonzero diagonal. Every coordinate uses newest available values, forms a Gauss-Seidel candidate, then blends (1-omega)*old+omega*candidate. Uses widened sums and checked double assignments. Independently recomputes absolute residual, stopping at residual<=tolerance; empty and zero RHS may converge at iteration0. For symmetric positive definite A,0<omega<2 ensures convergence; this interval is not sufficient for arbitrary matrices and SPD is not verified. Complete sweep cap returns converged=false, never a convergence certificate from iteration count alone. Time O(k*n^2), working storage O(n) beyond input, optional full-sweep history O(k*n). Borrowed inputs, owned output and no shared state.
    sor_trace()Solve from a zero initial iterate by actual forward SOR sweeps with captured iterates. Requires finite square A, matching finite b and nonzero diagonal. Every coordinate uses newest available values, forms a Gauss-Seidel candidate, then blends (1-omega)*old+omega*candidate. Uses widened sums and checked double assignments. Independently recomputes absolute residual, stopping at residual<=tolerance; empty and zero RHS may converge at iteration0. For symmetric positive definite A,0<omega<2 ensures convergence; this interval is not sufficient for arbitrary matrices and SPD is not verified. Complete sweep cap returns converged=false, never a convergence certificate from iteration count alone. Time O(k*n^2), working storage O(n) beyond input, optional full-sweep history O(k*n). Result.probes counts element inspections including a possible final equality fallback and repeated clamped indices. Comparisons counts executed key-value <, > or == tests: upper main branch one, lower/equal main branch two, fallback one. Transitions counts nonmatching main-loop schedule updates. These exclude index/bound checks, instructions, cache events and timings. No optional history.
    FibonacciSearchProbeOne actual read and pre/post schedule transition in Fibonacci search. Main decisions are+1 for key above value,-1 for key below value,0 for match. Fallback performs only equality and uses decision2 for a miss; it does not compute an unexecuted ordering comparison. Match and fallback preserve sizes and offset. Fields are owned snapshots, never replayed or borrowed.
    FibonacciSearchScheduleInitial exact consecutive Fibonacci sizes for a sorted-array search. For positive length, starts at small=0,middle=1,large=1 and grows until large>=length. Growth_steps counts actual additions, excluded from probes. Empty length has all-zero sizes/counts. Length is checked against ptrdiff_t maximum before arithmetic, making the first covering Fibonacci sum fit size_t. Owns scalar state, no allocation or shared mutation.
    FibonacciSearchTraceOwned actual Fibonacci outcome and chronological element-read records. C=captured_entries=probes.size()=outcome.result.probes counts whole optional records, including repeated positions and final fallback. Metadata, input, capacities, allocators and runtime storage are excluded: C is not peak RAM. No input copy or retained reference. Copies are independent and edits do not recompute outcome. Ordinary/work calls keep no optional history or quota.

    Functions

    eytzinger_layout()Build a complete binary search tree in breadth-first (Eytzinger) array order. Precondition: sorted is nondecreasing; not validated. A complete tree fills its last level left to right; in-order traversal assigns successive source values. The root need not be a median for incomplete last levels. Duplicates retain in-order source rank. Empty input yields empty output. O(N) assignments/output storage and O(log(N+1)) recursion, no optional history/quota. Child existence is checked before index multiplication. Input is unchanged, output owns values; independent calls share no mutable state. No cache/timing benefit is promised.
    eytzinger_layout_trace()Capture actual sorted-rank placements while building the ordinary Eytzinger layout. Shares eytzinger_layout()'s kernel/preconditions/output, without replay. Known C=N whole placement records (EytzingerLayoutTrace) is admitted before either output/history allocation. Default quota one million; zero disables only quota. O(N) additional owned history, no partial result on exceptions; independent calls share no mutable state and retain no input reference.
    eytzinger_search()Find the first equal node encountered in a breadth-first binary search tree. Precondition: layout has the tree order produced by eytzinger_layout(); unchecked. Tests equality first, then moves left for a smaller key or right for a larger one; a missing child returns absent. Duplicate matches need not be the first sorted occurrence. Found index is a layout position, not source rank. Empty input returns false/-1/zero probes. At most floor(log2(N))+1 inspected elements for N>0, O(log(N+1)) fixed-word work and constant auxiliary storage, no history. A probe is an element read, not a primitive comparison, cache miss or time unit. Input is unmodified; concurrent reads require it remain unmodified. No shared mutable state, prefetching, branch-free code or timing guarantee is supplied.
    eytzinger_search_trace()Retain actual node reads and chosen children during the ordinary exact-match search. Shares eytzinger_search()'s equality-first kernel, input precondition, duplicate choice and probe count. Optional C=P whole probe records (EytzingerSearchTrace) are admitted one at a time before reading the next element. Default quota one million; zero disables only quota. O(P) owned history, no input copy, replay or partial result. Empty input consumes zero quota. No cache/timing claim.
    fibonacci_search()Find an exact key in a nondecreasing int vector using Fibonacci offsets. Sortedness is an unchecked precondition; duplicates return the first equal position encountered, not necessarily the first occurrence. The original compiled signature, index choice and probe count are retained. Probe indices clamp at n-1 and may repeat; an equality-only fallback may add one read. Empty input returns absent/-1/zero probes. Safe offset arithmetic avoids the old -1-to-unsigned wrap idiom; signed index capacity is checked before growth. O(log(n+1)) word work, constant storage, additions/subtractions for scheduling with no midpoint division. No hardware speed or cache claim. Calls share no state; concurrent input reads require that the input remain unmodified.
    fibonacci_search_schedule()Compute the covering Fibonacci schedule without allocating an input array. Empty n gives zero sizes/additions. Positive n yields large>=n with consecutive predecessors, using additions only. Rejects lengths above the signed result index domain before growth; never relies on size_t wrap. O(log(n+1)) word work and constant storage, no input mutation or shared state.
    fibonacci_search_trace()Capture actual Fibonacci reads and chosen transitions during the same search pass. Shares ordinary/work semantics and unchecked sorted-input precondition. Admits one whole probe record before reading the next input element; default quota1m, zero disables only optional quota. Captures the equality fallback too. No replay, input copy, shared state or partial result on errors. O(P) owned history for P actual reads, while ordinary/work calls retain constant storage.
    fibonacci_search_work()Run the ordinary Fibonacci kernel and expose actual scheduling/comparison work. Shares exact result, duplicate choice, sorted-input precondition and checked arithmetic with fibonacci_search(). No optional history allocation or quota. Initial additions, element reads, primitive key comparisons and actual main transitions remain separate logical counts; no timing or cache inference.

    BeadFallTick-by-tick simulation of the beads falling.

    Functions

    bead_columns()Heights of the bead columns after the fall: \(\lambda'_j=\#\{i:a_i>j\}\) for \(j=0,\dots,\max a-1\), the conjugate of the partition formed by the values.
    bead_sort()Bead ("gravity") sort of non-negative integers, in place, ascending.
    bead_sort_gravity()Simulates gravity on the bead grid of a, one cell per tick, as an abacus would.
    conjugate_partition()Conjugate (transpose) of a partition: part \(j\) of the result counts the parts of parts that exceed \(j\). Applying it twice sorts parts into non-increasing order and drops zeros.

    Functions

    spectral_layout()Return the preserved spectral graph coordinates. Same actual checked Jacobi producer and defaults. Throws on actual nonconvergence instead of silently returning capped modes; signs and degenerate eigenspaces need not reproduce exact coordinate bytes.
    spectral_layout_run()Embed a graph through its actual low Laplacian modes. Build symmetric L=D-A from undirected endpoints; repeated edges add unit weight, loops are ignored but endpoints still validated. Largest-off-diagonal Jacobi rotations start from identity eigenvectors, use row-major strict maximum ties, then stable ascending eigenvalue order. Select columns1 and2, falling back to column0 for n=1 and repeating column1 for n=2; center and divide both coordinates by maximum radial norm. Empty gives empty converged result. For connected graphs, these are low nonconstant modes; disconnected graphs can select additional zero modes. Degenerate eigenvalues allow rotations/sign changes and layouts are not unique. Approximate finite arithmetic, not a planarity solver. Actual convergence flag is separate from cap exhaustion. Each largest-pivot scan costs O(n^2), each rotation update O(n); up to O(n^2) rotations therefore permits O(n^4) scan work, not an unconditional O(n^3) bound. Dense storage O(n^2), optional history O(rotations*n). Owned outputs and no shared state.

Select columns1 and2, falling back to column0 for n=1 and repeating column1 for n=2; center and divide both coordinates by maximum radial norm. Empty gives empty converged result. For connected graphs, these are low nonconstant modes; disconnected graphs can select additional zero modes. Degenerate eigenvalues allow rotations/sign changes and layouts are not unique. Approximate finite arithmetic, not a planarity solver. Actual convergence flag is separate from cap exhaustion. Each largest-pivot scan costs O(n^2), each rotation update O(n); up to O(n^2) rotations therefore permits O(n^4) scan work, not an unconditional O(n^3) bound. Captured after the actual acceptance/replacement/rejection. next_choice and both maps are post-decision; queue_before is before removing this proposer, queue_after is after any append. decision is accept-free,replace or reject. No regenerated history. kUnmatched denotes no prior incumbent or no newly freed proposer.
    GaleShapleyRunOne matching with actual kernel work. Both ordinary and diagnostic fitting use the same FIFO traversal without replay. The theorem concerns submitted strict complete rankings and stable matchings, not maximum total utility or real-world program constraints.
    GaleShapleyTraceOwned inputs, actual reviewer ranks and actual FIFO proposal events. Whole-request conservative admission follows full preference validation, which may allocate O(n) scratch.     GaleShapleyWorkActual rank construction and FIFO decision counts. Excludes input validation, allocation, history copies, checking stability, rank summaries and enumeration. rank_entries counts only the reviewer rank table used by the matcher. A queue push occurs initially or after rejection/displacement; each real proposal pops one free proposer.
    StabilityDiagnosticsStructural feasibility and all actual blocking pairs for a candidate. A malformed candidate gives feasible=false,complete=false,stable=false and no witnesses. Empty witnesses alone do not certify stability. Valid partial maps may be feasible but are unstable under complete equal-side preferences. Empty valid maps are complete and stable. Proposal metadata is ignored.
    StableBlockingPairA genuine mutually preferred pair from a feasible candidate. All ranks are one-based, with smaller better. An unmatched incumbent has rank n+1. Candidate pair ranks are strictly less than incumbent ranks on both sides. This witness is meaningful only after feasibility validation.
    StableMatchingEnumerationOwned stable perfect candidates from bounded exhaustive search. Candidates are tested in lexicographic proposer-map order. Their proposal metadata is0 because enumeration is not a proposal execution. For n0 there is one empty permutation and one empty stable matching. Shared blocking checks are not an independent correctness oracle.
    StableMatchingProfileOwned complete strict preferences for two equal sides. Both matrices retain original agent and rank order. The fixture and generators produce independent owned rows without shared mutable state.
    StableMatchingRanksOne-based assigned-partner ranks for a perfect candidate. Requires mutual perfect maps; does not itself certify stability. Means are descriptive averages of ordinal ranks, not utility or probabilities. Empty input has has_agents=false and zero mean placeholders, not observed mean satisfaction.
    StableMatchingResultOwned mutual partner maps and proposal-count metadata. Legacy field order/layout retained. A structurally feasible partial matching uses kUnmatched symmetrically; complete strict equal-size inputs produce a perfect matching. Stability ignores proposals, allowing manually constructed candidates. Reversing orientation exchanges the maps and preserves the original execution count.

Build ranks once and use the shared blocking checker, stopping at the first block for each rejected candidate. Each proposer advances monotonically and reviewers retain their best proposal so far. Returns the proposer-optimal/reviewer-pessimal stable perfect matching among stable matchings of these submitted strict complete preferences. Empty sides return empty maps and0 proposals. No input mutation or shared state. Including validation/rank preparation, ordinary time/storage are O(n²), even when only n proposals occur. Supports no capacities, incomplete lists, ties or couples.

Return3n+3n²+Q*(1+5n), not bytes or peak RAM. Excludes ordinary final maps/work/root metadata/working state/allocator bytes. Each proposer advances monotonically and reviewers retain their best proposal so far. Returns the proposer-optimal/reviewer-pessimal stable perfect matching among stable matchings of these submitted strict complete preferences. Empty sides return empty maps and0 proposals. No input mutation or shared state. Including validation/rank preparation, ordinary time/storage are O(n²), even when only n proposals occur. Supports no capacities, incomplete lists, ties or couples. No replay or history retained.
    is_stable()Check feasibility and absence of blocking pairs without unsafe indexing. Validate all preferences first. Malformed map dimensions/ranges/duplicates/noninverse assignments return false; proposals metadata is ignored. Consistent partial assignments may use kUnmatched, treated as worse than every acceptable partner. Under complete equal-side preferences any nonperfect feasible matching is unstable. Empty valid matching is stable. Builds ranks only after feasibility checks and stops at the first actual blocking pair, O(n²) total time/storage. No mutation.
    reverse_stable_matching()Exchange proposer/reviewer orientation with structural validation. Require equal-length mutually inverse partial maps, allowing kUnmatched on both sides.     stable_matching_common_preferences()Generate a deterministic complete strict preference family. Every row on both sides is0..n-1. FIFO makes n*(n+1)/2 proposals. Check2n+2n² row/cell entries and container bounds before allocation; default1m/0 disables only optional quota. Empty input produces two empty sides. O(n²) owned storage/work, no randomness or shared state.
    stable_matching_diagnostics()Inspect feasibility and collect actual blocking-pair witnesses. Validate full preferences, then candidate feasibility. Malformed candidates return all flags false with no pairs or rank-table construction. For a feasible candidate admit the conservative n² pair bound before rank tables and scanning, even if few/no blocks would occur. Default pair cap1m;0 disables only optional cap, not count/container checks. Scan all n² pairs in proposer-major order, retaining genuine mutually preferred pairs; no replay or partial output.
    stable_matching_example_preferences()Construct the original five-resident/five-reviewer synthetic fixture. Use mt19937_64 seed20240927, shuffle iota rows for all proposers then all reviewers. Fixed-size owned data; standard-library shuffle mapping limits bit portability. This is not actual residency data.
    stable_matching_mutual_first_preferences()Generate a deterministic complete strict preference family. Each agent i ranks i first then other IDs ascending, on both sides. FIFO makes n proposals. Check2n+2n² row/cell entries and container bounds before allocation; default1m/0 disables only optional quota. Empty input produces two empty sides. O(n²) owned storage/work, no randomness or shared state.
    stable_matching_permutations()Count all perfect candidate permutations by checked factorial. Return n!, including1 for n0. Count overflow throws promptly without allocation, even for SIZE_MAX input.
    stable_matching_ranks()Summarize assigned-partner ranks for a structurally perfect candidate. Validate complete preferences then mutual perfect maps. Build both inverse-rank tables once; return one-based ranks, first-choice counts and ordinal mean ranks. This does not certify stability. Empty valid inputs give has_agents=false and mean0 placeholders. O(n²) time/storage, no normalization or mutation.

    Types and constants

    kUnmatchedvariable Sentinel for an unmatched agent in either matching orientation. This is size_t(-1), never a valid participant ID. Proposal-count metadata is independent of map feasibility.
    StablePreferencestype Owned preference rows with favorite first. For n agents each row must be a permutation of0..n-1; the two sides have equal n. Empty sides are allowed. Ties, truncated lists, unequal sizes, capacities and couples are outside this model.

    sjt_run()Generate complete Steinhaus-Johnson-Trotter permutations. Values1..n start in increasing order with every direction left.     Functions

    stochastic_universal_sampling()Return the preserved checked stochastic universal index stream. Same actual producer with default bounds. Widened normalized pointers correct extreme-weight overflow/underflow and may differ from legacy repeated double additions at rounding boundaries.
    sus_run()Draw equally spaced stochastic-universal pointers. Finite nonnegative weights, positive total for positive pick count. Empty weights are valid only for zero picks; zero count returns empty indices, zero counts and no random draw after complete weight validation. Divide by the largest weight and accumulate in long double, rejecting a lost positive normalized weight or nonrepresentable geometry. One historical xorshift top53-bit draw determines the offset; zero seed uses its fixed nonzero fallback. Pointer k is (offset+k)*spacing, clamped below total if rounded up; cumulative intervals are half open, so zero-mass rows are never selected. Exact arithmetic and a continuous uniform offset give each row floor or ceil of n*w/sum(w), mean n*w/sum(w) and variance f*(1-f) for fractional expected count f. Finite53-bit draws and floating boundaries only approximate that ideal; no universal variance dominance for arbitrary aggregate statistics. Time O(population+picks), owned linear output/optional histories and no shared state.
    sus_trace()Draw equally spaced stochastic-universal pointers with actual selections. Finite nonnegative weights, positive total for positive pick count. Empty weights are valid only for zero picks; zero count returns empty indices, zero counts and no random draw after complete weight validation. Divide by the largest weight and accumulate in long double, rejecting a lost positive normalized weight or nonrepresentable geometry. One historical xorshift top53-bit draw determines the offset; zero seed uses its fixed nonzero fallback. Pointer k is (offset+k)*spacing, clamped below total if rounded up; cumulative intervals are half open, so zero-mass rows are never selected.     stone_poisson_example()Generate the original manufactured five-point Poisson fixture. Center4 and valid neighbor-1, with zero missing neighbors. Dimensions nonnegative; any zero dimension requires empty vectors and produces a converged empty result. Coefficients beyond each boundary must be zero. Builds the actual SIP incomplete triangular factors in grid order, checking denominator and pivot breakdown; then solves L*rho=r, U*delta=rho and adds delta. Residual is independently recomputed at the zero initial iterate and after every complete correction, so returned x, iteration count and residual refer to the same state. Positive definiteness/convergence are not assumed verified, and residual need not decrease monotonically for arbitrary inputs. Absolute inclusive stopping; cap returns converged=false if unresolved. O(grid cells) work per correction, linear working/result factor storage, optional copied histories O(corrections*cells). Outputs own values, no shared state.
    stone_sip_trace()Factor and solve an actual five-point grid with Stone SIP retaining actual factors/iterates. Row-major p=j*nx+i; all six coefficient/RHS vectors exactly nx*ny, finite.     strand_sort_run()Sort owned keys by actual greedy strands and stable merges. Take the first remaining key, then append every later key not less than the current strand tail; unselected keys retain order. User key operation exceptions propagate; owned results and no shared state.

    Functions

    structured_svm_objective()Evaluate the actual regularized full-data multiclass hinge objective. No fitting or parameter mutation. Validates finite model and complete matching data/labels; an empty evaluation set has mean hinge0 and correct0 but retains model regularizer. Default selected-work bounds apply. Bias weights are included in the squared norm.
    structured_svm_predict()Predict the actual lowest-index highest-scoring class. Validates complete finite model shape and feature width. Empty/unfitted models reject instead of returning an invented class0. Borrowed input/model, constant local state and no mutation.
    structured_svm_run()Train the actual regularized multiclass hinge model. Crammer-Singer special case, not a general sequence/tree structured-output solver. Scores use an augmented unit bias coordinate, which is regularized and shrunk with the other weights. Each epoch makes n independent sampled-with-replacement updates using local mt19937_64; it is not one visit to every row. At t=1,2,... choose the lowest-index maximum of score_c+[c!=truth] before shrink; apply eta=1/(lambda*t), shrink every coefficient by1-eta*lambda, then add/subtract eta*x_aug to truth/violator if different. No Pegasos projection step is implemented. Zero epochs returns zero weights for nonempty valid data; empty matching inputs preserve the legacy empty/unfitted model. Complete finite rectangular inputs, labels and model/update geometry checked before fitting. Full-data initial/post-epoch diagnostics evaluate actual current weights; SGD objectives need not decrease every step/epoch. O(updates*K*(d+1)+epochs*n*K*(d+1)) selected work, owned model and optional model-copy histories; no shared state.
    structured_svm_trace()Train the actual regularized multiclass hinge model with sampled subgradient states. Crammer-Singer special case, not a general sequence/tree structured-output solver. Scores use an augmented unit bias coordinate, which is regularized and shrunk with the other weights. Each epoch makes n independent sampled-with-replacement updates using local mt19937_64; it is not one visit to every row. At t=1,2,... choose the lowest-index maximum of score_c+[c!=truth] before shrink; apply eta=1/(lambda*t), shrink every coefficient by1-eta*lambda, then add/subtract eta*x_aug to truth/violator if different. No Pegasos projection step is implemented. Zero epochs returns zero weights for nonempty valid data; empty matching inputs preserve the legacy empty/unfitted model. Complete finite rectangular inputs, labels and model/update geometry checked before fitting. Full-data initial/post-epoch diagnostics evaluate actual current weights; SGD objectives need not decrease every step/epoch. O(updates*K*(d+1)+epochs*n*K*(d+1)) selected work, owned model and optional model-copy histories; no shared state.
    structured_svm_train()Return the preserved checked multiclass SVM training model. Same actual sampled shrink/subgradient producer with default policies. Bias is regularized; no kernel, projection or generic structured loss-augmented inference is implemented.

    datamunge/algorithms/substrings.hpp

    Classes

    SuffixTreeA suffix tree over a text: the compressed trie of all its suffixes. text is the original string (a unique terminal is handled virtually at index text.size()), and nodes holds the tree with nodes[0] the root. Build it with build_suffix_tree.
    SuffixTreeNodeOne node of a SuffixTree. An edge into this node spans text positions [start, end] inclusive; an end of -1 is the sentinel "current leaf end", i.e. the edge runs to the end of the text (a growing leaf). suffix_link is the Ukkonen suffix link (or -1), and children maps a character code (0..255, or 256 for the virtual terminal) to a child node index.
    SuffixTreeWorkActual Ukkonen construction operation counters.

    Functions

    build_suffix_tree()Ukkonen's algorithm (Ukkonen 1995): constructs the SuffixTree of text in O(n log alphabet) time with ordered transitions, online (processing the text left to right, one character at a time). It maintains an "active point" and suffix links so that all suffix insertions for a new character are performed in amortized constant time, using the tricks of a global growing leaf end, skip/count edge walking, and deferred suffix-link creation. The suffix tree supports (O(m)) substring queries and linear-time computation of many string statistics. A unique terminal symbol is appended virtually so that every suffix ends at a distinct leaf.
    build_suffix_tree_work()Build a byte suffix tree and expose actual construction work. Virtual terminal256 is outside byte alphabet. std::map transitions give O(n log alphabet) construction and O(m log alphabet) lookup; alphabet bounded257. No recursion or shared mutable state.
    distinct_substring_count()Counts the number of distinct non-empty substrings of the tree's text, in time linear in the tree size. It sums the character lengths of all edges (each root-to-position path is a distinct substring) and subtracts the one terminal character carried by each leaf edge.
    suffix_tree_contains()Tests whether pattern occurs as a substring of the text indexed by tree, in (O(|pattern|)) time, by walking pattern down the edges from the root.
    suffix_tree_plot()Draw an actual canonical suffix tree without reconstructing it. Iterative layout uses leaf order and descendant means. Byte labels suit printable input; use numeric diagnostics for binary strings. O(nodes+total displayed edge bytes) output; caller saves figure.
    wildcard_match()Case-sensitive whole-string byte matching with only star and question-mark metacharacters.

    Functions

    sutherland_hodgman_clip()Preserve checked rectangular Sutherland-Hodgman output order. Finite input points and ordered finite inclusive rectangle bounds required; zero-width/height rectangles allowed. Process left,right,bottom,top, carrying each actual output walk to the next phase. Both inside emits current; leaving emits intersection; entering emits intersection then current; both outside emits nothing. Stable intersections reuse the checked widened native Cohen-Sutherland half-plane segment primitive with other finite bounds spanning all double coordinates. No tolerance or topology repair: duplicate boundary points may remain. A simple convex subject yields its clipped convex polygon; a concave subject may encode disconnected pieces as one connected boundary walk with coincident bridge edges, not a general multipolygon boolean result. Input self-intersections are not classified or repaired. Empty input returns empty. Four phases give linear output-sensitive work/storage in input size; actual policies bound emitted/captured geometry. Owned results, no shared state.

    Functions

    symbolic_cholesky()Preserve structural lower-row prediction using checked natural-order fill. Consume a graph pattern only; every neighbor must be a valid int vertex ID. Normalize to an undirected simple graph using union of listed directions, ignoring loops/duplicates. Eliminate columns0..n-1 in natural order. Emit current higher neighbors as structural lower-factor entries, then connect every pair, recording actual new fill edges. This predicts potential structural nonzeros for a generic SPD matrix with that pattern; exact numerical cancellation may remove entries, and this API neither checks positive definiteness nor computes numerical factors. No permutation/ordering optimization is applied. Ordered sets give logarithmic insertion cost; pair attempts can be cubic in n with quadratic fill storage. Complete input and actual fill/pair/history policies are separate; owned output, no shared state.

    Functions

    tarjan_lca_run()Answer offline lowest-common-ancestor queries through actual finish/union states. Requires nonempty n-node undirected tree, root<n, exactly n-1 edges, valid complete edge/query IDs. A separate explicit validation traversal rejects loops, duplicates, cycles and disconnected inputs before query processing; its work is disclosed. Producing explicit-stack DFS marks a node black after its children. For a query whose partner is already black, answer ancestor[find(partner)]. After finishing a child, union its set with the parent by rank and reset the merged representative ancestor to parent. Self queries are installed at both endpoints and may write the same answer twice. Path compression/rank give O((n+q)*alpha(n)) producing work, plus linear validation and owned storage; actual event capture does not perform extra finds. No recursion, caller mutation, shared state or retained pointers.

    tea_decrypt()Preserve the two-word TEA decryption signature. Two uint32 words and four uint32 key words are consumed by value/reference. Executes32 cycles, each with two dependent word updates, modulo2^32 using defined unsigned arithmetic. Encryption increments sum by0x9E3779B9 before each cycle; decryption starts0xC6EF3720 and reverses the half order before decrementing sum. No implicit endian conversion, padding, mode, authentication or key management. TEA has known equivalent-key and related-key weaknesses; XTEA/XXTEA are different algorithms and not a blanket repair of all security issues. This is an educational primitive. Fixed constant work/storage, optional32 actual records; no shared state.

    Functions

    ternary_search_max()Preserve the value-only unimodal max search signature. Requires a nonempty callback, finite ordered lo<=hi, finite nonnegative tolerance and nonnegative iteration cap. Under strict unimodality, each comparison discards an outer third without discarding the extremum; arbitrary functions and broad flat shoulders have no such guarantee. Ties keep the left interval. Evaluate the first interior point before the second, then evaluate the final midpoint once; callbacks may observe this explicit order. Objective values must be finite; callback exceptions propagate and callback side effects are not rolled back. Stable widened span/interpolation supports finite extreme endpoints. Precision exhaustion and iteration exhaustion remain distinct from tolerance convergence. Owned histories and no shared state; O(iterations) evaluations/time, optional linear history.
