    thomas_poisson_example()Generate the original sine-forcing Dirichlet Poisson tridiagonal fixture. n interior nodes on(0,1), zero boundary values, h=1/(n+1), active sub/super-1/h^2 and diagonal2/h^2, RHS=pi^2*sin(pi*x), with unused boundary coefficients zero.     thomas_run()Solve through actual checked tridiagonal elimination. All four vectors must have identical length n and finite entries, including ignored sub[0]/super[n-1]. This no-pivot solver requires nonzero elimination pivots; strict diagonal dominance or SPD structure gives familiar sufficient conditions, while arbitrary nonsingular matrices can still need pivoting. Recompute b-A*x at returned x using original active diagonals. A small residual is not an unconditional forward-error bound.     timsort()Preserve actual stable in-place Timsort through an owned checked run. Copyable keys require strict weak operator<; built-in floating NaN/infinity reject. Detect nondecreasing or strictly descending runs; reverse only strict descent to preserve equal-key order. Extend short runs by stable upper-bound binary insertion and merge adjacent runs preferring the left on ties. Implements both top-three and next-deeper collapse checks; this repairs the old three-run-only stack policy. Galloping is omitted. Standard adaptive stable O(n log n) worst-case comparison behavior and linear scan on already sorted input, with linear scratch/output storage; actual work/capture policies can stop earlier. Owned copies, no shared state; compatibility in-place sort replaces caller vector only on success.

    todd_coxeter_index()Preserve a closed subgroup index or-1 for unresolved coset enumeration. Words use signed1-based generator IDs; positive/inverse symbols map to2g/2g+1. Require ngen>=0, all nonzero word symbols within range, positive max_cosets fitting int and complete word geometry. Empty generator presentation has one coset when all words are empty. HLT scans forward/backward, deduces one-gap links, defines rows for larger gaps, and merges coincidences by an iterative congruence queue over both generator directions. Repeated complete scan/fill passes continue until no actual link/definition/merge changes remain, avoiding unverified closure after earlier-root coincidences. Total ever-defined rows, table cells and selected operations have separate caps. Exhaustion returns an explicit unresolved status with index-1; it is not evidence that the group/index is infinite. A closed complete action table can be independently checked against every relation and inverse. No general polynomial-time/termination guarantee; owns all output and no shared state.

    Functions

    tonelli_shanks()Preserve checked smaller prime-field modular square roots. First validate p as prime over the complete uint64 domain with the existing deterministic twelve-base primality checker, even for n0. Then reduce n modulo p. Handle n0 and p2 directly, reject nonresidues by Euler criterion, and use n^((p+1)/4) for p mod4=3. Otherwise p-1=Q*2^S, choose the first sequential nonresidue z>=2, initialize c=z^Q,t=n^Q,R=n^((Q+1)/2),M=S. Find least i with t^(2^i)=1, set b=c^(2^(M-i-1)), then R*=b,t*=b^2,c=b^2,M=i. M strictly decreases. Private unsigned128 products avoid overflow; return the smaller complementary root. Sequential auxiliary search has its own potentially variable cost; no unconditional O(log^2 p) claim includes this search or full primality validation. Kernel product counts exclude separate validation. No constant-time/security guarantee, owned results and no shared state.

    Functions

    toom3_mul()Preserve checked decimal Toom-3 multiplication with default crossovers. Accept ASCII nonnegative decimal strings, including leading zeros and the legacy empty-string zero convention; reject signs/whitespace/other bytes. Complete byte lengths and positive crossover thresholds checked before parsing. Coefficients are private checked signed128 integers; every add/subtract/multiply is overflow-checked and interpolation divisions must be exact. Split into three coefficient blocks and evaluate at0,1,-1,2,infinity, multiply five times recursively, interpolate c0..c4 and shift/add them before decimal carry. The actual evaluation point is+2, correcting the old private comment saying-2. Default Toom threshold48 delegates to Karatsuba threshold32, so small examples do not execute five products. Fixed crossovers give O(n^log3(5)) arithmetic asymptotically, with smaller-size Karatsuba/schoolbook work and substantial temporary storage. Actual checked coefficient capacity/work budgets can reject large runs; this is not an unlimited-size integer package. Owned results/histories and no shared state.

    Functions

    is_topological_order()Check a proposed order as a complete permutation satisfying every directed edge. Wrong length, duplicate/out-of-range vertex, invalid edge endpoint or backward/self edge yieldsfalse. Valid empty graph/order yieldstrue. O(n+edges) validation time and O(n) positions; no mutation/shared state. This checks a supplied witness and does not run Kahn or impose the producer default budgets.
    topological_sort()Preserve complete Kahn order or empty cyclic result with checked geometry. Validate all endpoints and complete vertex/edge policies before allocating adjacency. Count duplicate edges separately. Seed FIFO sources in increasing vertex order, then visit outgoing edges in input order and enqueue vertices when indegree becomes0. Deterministic for a fixed edge list, but not globally lexicographically minimal and may change after reordering same edges. Each vertex/edge processed at most once, O(V+E) work/storage. If fewer than n vertices emit, a directed cycle exists; blocked leftovers can also be descendants of a cycle, not solely cycle members. Compatibility order is cleared on failure while run.emitted retains actual partial progress. Empty graph is a DAG; self loops are cycles. Owned output, no shared state.
    topological_sort_run()Sort a DAG through the actual checked Kahn FIFO producer. Validate all endpoints and complete vertex/edge policies before allocating adjacency.     topological_sort_trace()Sort a DAG through the actual checked Kahn FIFO producer. Validate all endpoints and complete vertex/edge policies before allocating adjacency.     tournament_run()Select actual tournament winners with producer draw diagnostics. Finite fitness values may be negative because only ordering matters. Require n>=0 and k>0; positive picks require nonempty population. Zero picks validates all fitness and k, returns zero row counts and consumes no RNG word. Each tournament samples k rows independently with replacement using the historical xorshift13/7/17 word modulo population; this finite modulo mapping has bias and is not an exactly uniform bounded draw. Keep the first sampled contender on equal fitness. Under ideal independent uniform draws and strictly ranked population m, rank-r winner probability is((r+1)/m)^k-(r/m)^k for ascending zero-based rank; qualify finite-RNG/modulo effects and ties. Complete n*k geometry checked before work, O(population+n*k) work and owned outputs/optional event history; no shared state.

    transitive_closure()Preserve checked directed Warshall reachability with default policies. Validate every directed endpoint before matrix allocation, then seed all edges and optionally the diagonal. For k,i test current R[i][k]; when true visit every j and assign R[i][j]=R[i][j] or R[k][j]. After k, paths using intermediate vertices0..k are represented. Reflexivefalse means positive-length reachability, not a forced-false diagonal: directed cycles still reach themselves. Empty graph is valid; loops/duplicates allowed and seeded assignment count includes duplicates. Worst-case cubic updates and quadratic bit storage; optional complete phase copies add cubic history. Complete matrix and actual update/capture policies are event/value counts, not wall time/peak bytes. Owned results, no shared state.

    Functions

    trapezoidal_ode()Preserve a complete implicit trapezoidal trajectory or fail on unresolved Newton work. Requires a nonempty finite-valued synchronous scalar RHS, finite y0/t0/t1 and positive requested steps. Backward time is supported. Grid endpoints use stable interpolation and the last time is exactly t1. Each step solves Y-y-h/2*(f(t,y)+f(t_next,Y))=0 using a forward-Euler predictor and finite-difference Newton derivative. Accept a step only if the actual recomputed equation residual is within atol+rtol*max(abs(y),abs(Y)); a small correction alone is insufficient. Zero Newton cap still checks the predictor residual. Zero span copies identical states without RHS calls. Run output distinguishes iteration exhaustion, zero derivative and representational stagnation, retaining only converged accepted trajectory states. Callback exceptions/side effects propagate without rollback and actual values are not replayed. Trapezoidal A-stability is a property of exactly solved linear steps; this finite nonlinear Newton implementation does not certify universal nonlinear convergence and is not L-stable. O(steps*Newton cap) callback work, owned linear step diagnostics plus optional histories, no internal shared state.
    trapezoidal_ode_run()Integrate actual implicit trapezoidal steps with honest Newton outcomes. Requires a nonempty finite-valued synchronous scalar RHS, finite y0/t0/t1 and positive requested steps. Backward time is supported. Grid endpoints use stable interpolation and the last time is exactly t1. Each step solves Y-y-h/2*(f(t,y)+f(t_next,Y))=0 using a forward-Euler predictor and finite-difference Newton derivative. Accept a step only if the actual recomputed equation residual is within atol+rtol*max(abs(y),abs(Y)); a small correction alone is insufficient. Zero Newton cap still checks the predictor residual. O(steps*Newton cap) callback work, owned linear step diagnostics plus optional histories, no internal shared state.

Requires a nonempty finite-valued synchronous scalar RHS, finite y0/t0/t1 and positive requested steps. Backward time is supported. Grid endpoints use stable interpolation and the last time is exactly t1. Each step solves Y-y-h/2*(f(t,y)+f(t_next,Y))=0 using a forward-Euler predictor and finite-difference Newton derivative. Flat histograms and a small modification factor do not certify estimation accuracy; compare the exact binomial density separately. O(moves+checks*N) work, O(N) base state plus bounded capture; no shared state.

    #source
    constexpr std::uint32_t adler32_modulus = 65521U

    The Adler-32 modulus 65521, the largest prime below \(2^{16}\).

    #source
    constexpr std::size_t adler32_nmax = 5552

    The longest run of bytes that adler32_update() sums before reducing modulo 65521.

    Starting from \(A, B < p\), after \(n\) bytes of value at most 255 the second sum is at most \(255\,n(n+1)/2 + (n+1)(p-1)\); 5552 is the largest \(n\) for which that fits in 32 bits (zlib's NMAX).

    enum class BorweinEvaluation

    Algebraically equivalent ways to evaluate Borwein's next y in floating point. Both modes retain the historical seed 6-4*sqrt(2). Rationalisation preserves small y updates when the computed fourth root rounds to one; it does not guarantee a more accurate final pi estimate or undo earlier rounding.

    Example
    const auto mode=dm::algorithms::BorweinEvaluation::rationalised;
std::print("{}\n",mode==dm::algorithms::BorweinEvaluation::rationalised); // true
    See also

    borwein_pi_trace()

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    direct

    Historical (1-r)/(1+r), where r=(1-y^4)^(1/4).

    rationalised

    y^4/((1+r)*(1+r+r^2+r^3)), avoiding subtraction of nearly equal ones.

    #source
    enum class ChienPath

    Actual path used by the ordinary/traced Chien kernel after normalization. Shortcuts do not pretend to enumerate points or retain recurrence states.

    Example
    const auto t=dm::algorithms::chien_search_trace({2,2},5);
std::print("{}\n",t.path==dm::algorithms::ChienPath::Linear); // true
    See also

    ChienTrace

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    Zero

    Legacy zero-polynomial sentinel: no roots enumerated, although every field element is mathematically a root.

    Constant

    Nonzero constant: no roots and no sweep.

    Linear

    One distinct root obtained by inversion, without finding a generator or sweeping.

    Incremental

    Zero checked directly, then all nonzero points visited through primitive-root powers.

    #source
    enum class ChudnovskyStop

    Actual stopping reason for a Chudnovsky evaluation. RequestedTerms means all requested additions ran. TermUnderflow means the recurrence produced a signed zero term; that addition is recorded and every later requested term is skipped. Neither outcome certifies correctly rounded pi or a real-error tolerance. Default storage has not run an evaluation.

    Example
    const auto t=dm::algorithms::chudnovsky_pi_trace(4);
std::print("{}\n",t.stop==dm::algorithms::ChudnovskyStop::RequestedTerms); // true
    See also

    ChudnovskyTrace

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    Unprocessed

    Default storage; no evaluation has occurred.

    RequestedTerms

    All requested terms, including unchanged additions, were evaluated.

    TermUnderflow

    The actual floating term became zero; its addition is included.

    #source
    enum class CipollaPath

    Actual route through the checked Cipolla solver. Shortcuts still validate primality first. NonResidue is a mathematical Euler verdict, while malformed moduli and exhausted work caps throw. Unprocessed describes default storage, without a solved input.

    Example
    const auto t=dm::algorithms::cipolla_sqrt_trace(11,1009);
std::print("{}\n",t.path==dm::algorithms::CipollaPath::NonResidue); // true
    See also

    CipollaTrace

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    Unprocessed

    Default storage; no solve has executed.

    BinaryField

    Direct unique root in F_2.

    Zero

    Direct zero root for an odd prime.

    NonResidue

    Nonzero input fails Euler's criterion and has no root.

    Extension

    Actual nonresidue search followed by quadratic-extension exponentiation.

    #source
    enum class ClarkeWrightDecision

    Actual ordered reason for accepting or rejecting a sorted savings pair. Missing endpoint is checked first, then same route, then capacity. A customer in a route interior has no endpoint slot. Merged records include the committed customer order; rejected records never mutate routes. This is not a proof that another global routing could not use the rejected edge.

    Example
    const auto t=dm::algorithms::clarke_wright_trace({{0,0},{1,0},{2,0}},{0,1,1},2);
std::print("{}\n",t.steps[0].decision==dm::algorithms::ClarkeWrightDecision::Merged); // true
    See also

    ClarkeWrightStep

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    Merged

    Distinct endpoint routes fit capacity and were concatenated.

    MissingEndpoint

    At least one customer was interior to its current route.

    SameRoute

    Both customer endpoints already belonged to the same route.

    CapacityExceeded

    The widened sum of distinct route loads exceeded capacity.

    #source
    enum class ClipAction

    Terminal or edge-replacement decision of one Cohen-Sutherland iteration. Edge priority is Top, Bottom, Right, Left, after the accept/reject tests. The first outside endpoint is selected; otherwise the second is selected.

    Example
    const auto t=dm::algorithms::cohen_sutherland_clip_trace(-1,1,3,1,0,0,2,2);
std::print("{}\n",t.steps[0].action==dm::algorithms::ClipAction::Left); // true
    See also

    CohenSutherlandStep

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    Accept

    Both outcodes are zero; retain the current endpoints.

    Reject

    Outcodes share an outside bit; discard the complete current segment.

    Top

    Replace the selected outside endpoint at y=ymax.

    Bottom

    Replace the selected outside endpoint at y=ymin.

    Right

    Replace the selected outside endpoint at x=xmax.

    Left

    Replace the selected outside endpoint at x=xmin.

    enum class CrtStatus

    Actual outcome of a whole CRT run or one attempted merge. Overflow means a compatible prefix's period exceeds INT64_MAX, without a mathematical verdict on unprocessed constraints. Complete means a compatible, representable merge or a fully solved system, according to its record context.

    Example
    const auto t=dm::algorithms::chinese_remainder_trace({1,0},{2,4});
std::print("{}\n",t.status==dm::algorithms::CrtStatus::Inconsistent); // true

    CrtTrace, CrtMerge

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    Unprocessed

    Default storage; no attempted solve or merge is represented.

    Complete

    All inputs in the record's scope are compatible and their period fits int64.

    Inconsistent

    The actual gcd divisibility test failed.

    Overflow

    A compatible merge has a period above INT64_MAX; no int64 pair is returned.

    #source
    enum class DamerauMove

    Selected prefix-DP move, also identifying a literal byte-edit instruction. Native scripts omit matches. Candidate ties prefer diagonal (match/substitute), insert, erase, then transpose. A DP transpose can bridge deleted/inserted interior bytes; a ByteEdit transpose always swaps exactly two adjacent current bytes.

    Example
    const auto t=dm::algorithms::damerau_levenshtein_trace("ab","ba");
std::print("{}\n",t.cells.back().choice==dm::algorithms::DamerauMove::transpose); // true
    See also

    DamerauCell, ByteEdit

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    match

    Zero-cost equal-byte diagonal, omitted from native scripts.

    substitute

    Unit-cost replacement of one byte.

    insert

    Unit-cost insertion of one byte.

    erase

    Unit-cost deletion of one byte.

    transpose

    DP bridge, or a literal adjacent swap in ByteEdit.

    #source
    enum class DeepeningEventKind

    Actual chronological transition kind in a depth-limited search. Goal stops before its adjacency and leaves the successful stack active; no synthetic leave events are added. Cutoff means a non-goal entry at the limit, even if that vertex has no outgoing arcs. Examine precedes the cycle decision.

    Example
    const auto k=dm::algorithms::DeepeningEventKind::enter;
std::print("{}\n",k==dm::algorithms::DeepeningEventKind::enter); // true
    See also

    DeepeningEvent

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    pass_start

    A new actual limit is about to enter the start.

    enter

    Vertex was marked on the current path and pushed.

    examine

    One original outgoing arc is being considered.

    cutoff

    Non-goal entry reached the current depth limit.

    leave

    A failed/cutoff activation was popped and unmarked.

    goal

    Entered goal ends this pass successfully.

    pass_end

    Actual pass ended; successful path remains active.

    #source
    enum class DepthFirstEventKind

    One actual directed DFS transition, with no synthetic early-stop finishes. Discover occurs after marking/pushing a new vertex; examine before deciding whether to descend; finish after a frame pop; goal after its discovery.

    Example
    const auto t=dm::algorithms::depth_first_search_trace(2,{{0,1}},0,1);
std::print("{}\n",t.events.back().kind==dm::algorithms::DepthFirstEventKind::goal); // true
    See also

    DepthFirstEvent

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    discover

    A previously unseen vertex was marked and pushed.

    examine

    One original adjacency entry is inspected.

    finish

    An exhausted frame was actually popped.

    goal

    Newly entered target terminates search before its adjacency.

    #source
    enum class DepthFirstState

    DFS state at the stopping time or immediately before a scanned arc. Active vertices are exactly the current frame path. Finished vertices have genuinely exhausted adjacency; unseen vertices have never been entered. A successful early stop leaves the goal and its ancestors active.

    Example
    const auto t=dm::algorithms::depth_first_search_trace(2,{{0,1}},0,1);
std::print("{}\n",t.state[1]==dm::algorithms::DepthFirstState::active); // true
    See also

    DepthFirstTrace

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    unseen

    Never entered at stopping time.

    active

    Entered and still on the explicit frame path.

    finished

    All outgoing adjacency entries genuinely exhausted.

    balanced

    neither

    using DifferenceProjection = std::function< std::vector< double >(const std::vector< double > &)>

    Type-erased projection from a borrowed vector to an owned vector of the same size. Outputs must be finite. Callbacks may hold external state; the algorithm validates shape/finiteness but cannot establish nearest-point or set-membership properties.

    #source
    enum class DpllEventKind

    Kind of an actual iterative DPLL transition or terminal node. Enter records root/branch arrival; unit/pure record post-assignment states; conflict identifies a falsified original clause; exhausted means both children failed, not that its own partial state falsifies a clause. Backtrack restores the parent state. Satisfied records a partial state already satisfying every clause, before filling don't-cares in the separate final total model.

    Example
    const auto t=dm::algorithms::dpll_sat_trace(1,{{1}});
std::print("{}\n",t.events.front().kind==dm::algorithms::DpllEventKind::enter); // true
    See also

    DpllEvent

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    enter

    Arrive at a newly numbered node; literal zero at root, signed branch literal otherwise.

    unit

    Assign the sole unassigned occurrence in an unsatisfied original clause.

    pure

    Assign the smallest variable with one polarity among unsatisfied clauses.

    conflict

    A first original clause has all its literals false.

    backtrack

    Return from a failed child; literal is that child's signed decision.

    exhausted

    Both true/false branches failed at this internal node.

    satisfied

    Every original clause already contains a true literal.

    #source
    enum class DpRule

    One satisfiability-preserving variable-removal rule. Unit and pure record the signed true literal; resolution records a positive variable id. Each native step removes that variable entirely. No branching assignment or first-order quantifier procedure is represented.

    Example
    const auto t=dm::algorithms::davis_putnam_trace(1,{{1}});
std::print("{}\n",t.steps[0].rule==dm::algorithms::DpRule::unit); // true
    See also

    DpStep, davis_putnam_trace()

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    unit

    First lexicographically ordered unit clause.

    pure

    Smallest signed literal whose opposite is absent.

    resolution

    Smallest occurring variable, both polarities present.

    #source
    enum class DStarAction

    Actual D* Lite pop classification. A key refresh requeues an old moving-start key; lower sets g=rhs; raise sets g=infinity and recomputes this vertex and its predecessors.

    Example
    dm::algorithms::DStarLiteGrid p({{false}},{0,0},{0,0});
const auto t=p.repair_trace();
std::print("{}\n",t.steps[0].action==dm::algorithms::DStarAction::lower); // true
    See also

    DStarStep

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    rekey

    Old key smaller than current key; refresh without expanding labels.

    lower

    g>rhs; commit improved g and update predecessors.

    raise

    g<rhs; invalidate g and update self/predecessors.

    #source
    using DStarKey = std::pair< std::uint64_t, std::uint64_t >

    Lexicographic integer priority(min(g,rhs)+Manhattan(start,u)+km,min(g,rhs)). Both components use d_star_infinity for an infinite minimum. Remaining heap ties use flattened cell id, which is not part of the mathematical key.

    Example
    const dm::algorithms::DStarKey key{2,0};
std::print("{}\n",key.first); // 2

    enum class EllipsoidStop

    Why the finite optimizer stopped; only two reasons are conditional optimality checks. Valid convex subgradients and an initial enclosing ellipsoid are caller assumptions, not verified by the implementation. Iteration limit and rounded center stagnation do not certify an optimum or the requested tolerance.

    Example
    const auto reason=dm::algorithms::EllipsoidStop::center_stagnation;
std::print("{}\n",reason==dm::algorithms::EllipsoidStop::iteration_limit); // false
    See also

    EllipsoidOutcome

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    iteration_limit

    Reached max_iter, including zero.

    zero_subgradient

    Oracle returned exactly zero; certifies a minimum for a valid convex oracle.

    support_tolerance

    Conditional current objective-gap bound <= requested absolute tolerance.

    center_stagnation

    Positive proposed shift rounded to no coordinate change; no convergence claim.

    #source
    using EqualizationImage = std::vector< std::vector< int > >

    Owned row-major grayscale integer rows, with values clamped by equalization on read. Rectangular shape is required, including all zero-width rows. Empty images are allowed. Integers are not normalized floats or RGB channels; no storage/view borrowing.

    Example
    const dm::algorithms::EqualizationImage x{{100,101},{102,103}};
std::print("{}\n",x.size()); // 2
    See also

    histogram_equalize()

    #source
    enum class ExactCoverEvent

    Kinds of actual search events, including restoration after a found solution. choose_column and dead_end are recorded before covering the chosen column. select_row follows covering all its columns. unselect_row follows restoring its other columns and popping its row; the pivot column remains covered until its frame exits. Thus unselect_row can be cleanup after success as well as a failed branch. solution precedes cleanup; finished follows complete mesh restoration.

    Example
    const auto event=dm::algorithms::ExactCoverEvent::unselect_row;
std::print("{}\n",event==dm::algorithms::ExactCoverEvent::dead_end); // false
    See also

    ExactCoverStep

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    choose_column

    Selected the smallest active minimum-size column.

    select_row

    Actually selected a candidate and covered its other columns.

    unselect_row

    Actually restored the candidate and removed its row.

    dead_end

    Selected column has zero remaining compatible rows.

    solution

    Every required header is covered; output rows retained.

    finished

    All runtime links/sizes restored; search has terminated.

    #source
    enum class FalsePositionPolicy

    Select plain secant bracketing or the legacy retained-twice Illinois variant. Illinois starts with no previous replacement; damping begins only when the same endpoint is replaced twice consecutively. This differs from the paper's most-recent-point initialization, while retaining its stale-weight mechanism.

    Example
    std::print("{}\n",dm::algorithms::false_position_policy_name(dm::algorithms::FalsePositionPolicy::Illinois)); // illinois
    See also

    FalsePositionOptions, false_position_policy_name()

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    Plain

    Ordinary regula falsi: interpolation weights remain actual endpoint values.

    Illinois

    Halve the opposite retained weight after consecutive replacements of the same endpoint.

    #source
    enum class FalsePositionStop

    Distinguish numerical stopping conditions from a mathematical root certificate. Continuity, existence and trustworthy callback signs are caller assumptions; a callback zero or tolerance test alone does not establish those assumptions.

    Example
    std::print("{}\n",dm::algorithms::false_position_stop_name(dm::algorithms::FalsePositionStop::Stagnation)); // stagnation
    See also

    FalsePositionOutcome, false_position_stop_name()

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    NoBracket

    Nonzero actual endpoint values have the same sign; no trial evaluated.

    Endpoint

    An initial callback returned zero; both endpoints were evaluated first.

    ExactValue

    A trial callback returned zero, not necessarily exact mathematical zero.

    Residual

    Positive residual tolerance passed at a trial.

    Interval

    Positive coordinate tolerance passed using the rounded trial-to-endpoint radius.

    Stagnation

    Trial rounded to an endpoint without passing a stopping test.

    WeightUnderflow

    Actual Illinois halving rounded a nonzero artificial weight to zero.

    IterationLimit

    The trial-evaluation budget was exhausted before another stopping test passed.

    #source
    enum class FermatPrimalityStop

    Actual stop reason for the seeded Fermat congruence test. BelowTwo means not prime (zero and one are not composite). SmallPrime covers two and three; Even rejects larger even inputs. Witness is a failed actual congruence; RoundLimit means all requested rounds passed, not a proof.

    Example
    std::print("{}\n",dm::algorithms::fermat_primality_stop_name(dm::algorithms::FermatPrimalityStop::RoundLimit)); // rounds passed
    See also

    FermatPrimalityOutcome, fermat_probable_prime_work()

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    BelowTwo

    Zero or one: not prime, with no drawn bases.

    SmallPrime

    Two or three: known prime, with no drawn bases.

    Even

    Even input greater than two: composite, with no drawn bases.

    Witness

    Actual tested base failed the congruence, proving compositeness.

    RoundLimit

    All requested positive rounds passed; no primality certificate.

    #source
    enum class FermatStop

    Trial division: the elementary integer-factorization method – try every candidate divisor 2,3,5,7,... up to sqrt(n), dividing it out (with multiplicity) whenever it divides. Any factor left above sqrt(n) is prime. It is O(sqrt(n)) and hopeless for large semiprimes, but it is exact, dead simple, and the right tool for small numbers or for peeling off the small prime factors before a heavier method takes over.

    Parameters
    n

    the integer to factor (n >= 1).

    Returns

    the prime factors of n in nondecreasing order, with multiplicity (empty for n=1).

    Reason that a bounded Fermat factorization stopped. Values describe actual work, not a probabilistic primality test. TrivialPair reaches the first odd difference-of-squares pair with smaller factor one; TrialLimit makes no primality claim. Even bypasses square testing.

    Example
    std::print("{}\n",dm::algorithms::fermat_stop_name(dm::algorithms::FermatStop::TrialLimit)); // trial limit
    See also

    fermat_factor_work(), FermatOutcome

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    Even

    Input is even; returned factor two, with no square tests.

    Factor

    An actual square test found a proper split, possibly composite factors.

    TrivialPair

    Odd search reached factors one and n after excluding closer pairs.

    TrialLimit

    Positive trial budget ended before a square hit; no primality conclusion.

    enum class FftWindow

    Window applied to M observed samples before any zero padding. Both windows are deterministic and nonnegative. Periodic Hann uses denominator M, as in scipy.signal.windows.hann(M,sym=False), not the symmetric M-1 convention.

    See fft_spectrum() for both modes and calibrated amplitudes.

    References

    • https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.signal.windows.hann.html

    See also

    fft_spectrum()

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    Rectangular

    Every observed sample receives weight one.

    PeriodicHann

    Weight .5-.5*cos(2*pi*t/M); requires M>=2.

    enum class FrankWolfeStep

    Step-size rule for frank_wolfe.

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    Standard

    \(\gamma_k=2/(k+2)\); vanilla variant only.

    ShortStep

    \(\gamma=\min(\gamma_{\max}, \langle-\nabla f,d\rangle/(L\|d\|^2))\); needs lipschitz.

    LineSearch

    Exact line search: safeguarded regula falsi on \(\langle\nabla f(x+\gamma d),d\rangle\) over \([0,\gamma_{\max}]\).

    enum class FrankWolfeVariant

    Which directions frank_wolfe may take.

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    Vanilla

    Always towards the LMO vertex.

    AwayStep

    Towards the LMO vertex, or away from the worst active vertex, whichever descends faster.

    Pairwise

    Move weight from the worst active vertex straight to the LMO vertex.

    enum class GnomeSortEventKind

    Before all visits, with pointer zero and other fields unused.

    stop

    After all visits, with both pointer fields equal to the input length.

    enum class GoertzelFrequencyMode

    Select the historical offset-truncated bin or evaluate the supplied frequency directly. legacy_bin uses trunc(0.5+double(N)*f/fs), with an int representability check. For nonnegative ordinary requests this chooses the nearest bin with upward half ties; negative requests are asymmetric. unrounded uses omega=2*pi*f/fs without integer quantization. Neither mode guarantees exact floating accuracy.

    const auto m=dm::algorithms::GoertzelFrequencyMode::unrounded;

    See also

    goertzel_run(), goertzel_power_at_frequency()

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    legacy_bin

    Historical truncation of the offset bin expression, including its negative-frequency bias.

    unrounded

    Supplied frequency directly; no integer-bin selection or automatic angle reduction.

    Positive strict residual tolerance passed, possibly in a wide bracket.

    Interval

    Actual returned midpoint's maximum endpoint distance passed x_tolerance.

    IterationLimit

    Caller projection-trial budget exhausted without other acceptance.

    ProjectionLimit

    Computed exact-arithmetic projection bound exhausted without rounded interval acceptance.

    Stagnation

    No interior representable midpoint remained before tolerance acceptance.

    #source
    enum class JaroWinklerPhase

    Phase of one actual Jaro/Winkler inspection. No hidden matching replay; candidate means a visited window slot, order means comparison of matched byte sequences, prefix means an actual prefix test.

    Example
    const auto t=dm::algorithms::jaro_winkler_trace("A","A");
std::print("{}\n",t.events[0].phase==dm::algorithms::JaroWinklerPhase::Candidate); // true
    See also

    JaroWinklerEvent

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    Candidate

    One actually visited candidate slot, including occupied slots skipped without reading bytes.

    Order

    One actual comparison between the two ordered matched-byte sequences.

    Prefix

    One actual equality test while scanning a prefix of at most four bytes.

    #source
    enum class JohnsonAction

    Phase of an actual Johnson operation; metadata meanings are phase-specific.

    Example
    const auto t=dm::algorithms::johnson_trace(1,{});
std::print("{}\n",t.events[0].action==dm::algorithms::JohnsonAction::Seed); // true
    See also

    JohnsonEvent

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    Potential

    Edge attempt: pass, edge, u/v and before/candidate/after potential.

    Reweight

    Edge conversion: edge/u/v, before original weight, candidate=after reduced weight.

    Seed

    Source initialization: source=u=v, before infinity, candidate=after zero.

    Pop

    Actual heap removal: source/u=v, before=after current label, candidate popped key, stale flag meaningful.

    Relax

    Actual outgoing edge attempt: source/edge/u/v and before/candidate/after reduced label.

    Restore

    Reachable output conversion: source/u=source/v, before reduced label, candidate=after original distance.

    #source
    enum class JumpSearchAction

    Actual branch after one block-end or linear-scan read. Advance/Select are block >= comparisons; Continue/Found/Passed are scan equality and optional greater comparisons. No additional relation test is done.

    Example
    const auto t=dm::algorithms::jump_search_trace({1,3,5},3);

    JumpSearchProbe

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    Advance

    Block end below key; advance to next block.

    Select

    Block end >=key; start scanning from this block's beginning.

    Continue

    Scan value below key; continue linearly.

    Found

    Scan equality succeeds; return this first occurrence.

    Passed

    Scan value above key; terminate absent.

    Reference

    Moscato (1989), On Evolution, Search, Optimization, Genetic Algorithms and Martial Arts: Towards Memetic Algorithms, C3P Report826, provides historical memetic context. The retained native MAX-CUT recipe and exact population/local conventions are specified explicitly here.

    #source
    using OdeSystem = std::function< std::vector< double >(double, const std::vector< double > &)>

    First-order ODE callback f(t,y), returning the state derivative vector. Receives time and a borrowed const state vector valid only during the call. Return entries have state/time units and the same dimension as y. Euler validates shape/finiteness; validation by other solvers follows their contracts. Higher-order equations can be rewritten as first-order vector systems. The callback may own captured state; its exceptions propagate and concurrent use follows that captured state's thread-safety. No solver retains the callback.

    Example
    const dm::algorithms::OdeSystem f=[](double,const std::vector<double>& y){return std::vector<double>{-y[0]};};
std::print("{}\n",f(0,{2})[0]); // -2
    See also

    OdeSolution, euler_method()

    Greedy zero-or-more repetitions, stopping on no progress.

    Plus

    Greedy one-or-more matches, nullable child allowed with progress guard.

    Opt

    Optional child, failure consumes nothing.

    And

    Positive lookahead, consumes no input.

    Not

    Negative lookahead, consumes no input.

    #source
     pi_i = \overline{\gamma_1(i)}

    Baum-Welch (EM) parameter re-estimation from one or more observation sequences.

    Starting from an initial guess \(\lambda^{(0)}\), each iteration runs the scaled forward-backward pass on every sequence (E-step) to form the responsibilities \(\gamma_t(i)\) and pair-posteriors \(\xi_t(i,j)=P(q_t=i,q_{t+1}=j\mid O,\lambda)\), then re-estimates (M-step)

    #source
    enum class PlanningEventKind

    Primitive event kinds recorded at the actual search control-flow points. test precedes apply; visit precedes goal/cutoff/repeat/reopen. finish follows successful recursive-return-equivalent propagation, while backtrack follows a failed child. exhausted means all operators of that frame were tested.

    Example
    const auto k = dm::algorithms::PlanningEventKind::reopen;
std::cout << dm::algorithms::planning_event_name(k); // reopen
    See also

    PlanningEvent

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    visit

    Enter an actual heap frame before terminal checks.

    goal

    Accept a state satisfying every goal bit, even at the depth limit.

    cutoff

    Reject a non-goal frame at the complete-step budget.

    repeat

    Prune a state previously expanded at equal or smaller depth.

    reopen

    Expand a prior state with strictly more remaining budget.

    test

    Test the named input operator's positive preconditions.

    apply

    Select an applicable operator and enter its actual successor.

    backtrack

    Pop an operator after its child failed.

    finish

    Propagate a successful child's return along the selected path.

    exhausted

    Reject a frame after testing every input operator.

    #source
    enum class PMinusOneStop

    Exact native stopping reason, not a primality or factor-existence certificate.

    Example
    std::print("{}\n",dm::algorithms::pollard_p_minus_one_run(85,4).stop==dm::algorithms::PMinusOneStop::Collapsed); // true
    EnumeratorValueDescription
    BoundExhausted

    Every j from 2 through B completed without a proper factor or full collapse.

    EvenFactor

    Even n>2 returns divisor two without exponentiation.

    ProperFactor

    Actual gcd lies strictly between one and n.

    Collapsed

    Actual gcd equals n, so this fixed-base attempt stops without a divisor.

    SmallPrime

    Input two has no nontrivial factor and returns divisor zero.

    enum class RhoFactorPhase

    Actual producing polynomial-evaluation phase.

    Example
    const auto t=dm::algorithms::pollard_rho_factor_trace(8051);std::print("{}\n",t.history.evaluations[0].phase==dm::algorithms::RhoFactorPhase::Advance); // true
    EnumeratorValueDescription
    Advance

    Advance y by the current doubling radius before batched comparisons.

    Batch

    Advance y and multiply the actual difference into q.

    Fallback

    Revisit the saved block one polynomial step at a time after gcd(q,n)=n.

    enum class RiddersStop

    Actual stopping reason; interval resolution does not certify a small residual.

std::print("{}\n",static_cast<int>(kind)); // 0
    EnumeratorValueDescription
    NoBracket

    Nonzero endpoint values have equal signs.

    Residual

    Actual zero or positive residual threshold passed.

    Interval

    Positive interval tolerance passed on the actual current bracket.

    Stagnation

    Midpoint rounded to an endpoint before a threshold passed.

    Budget

    Requested actual iteration budget exhausted.

    enum class RoundMode

std::print("{}\n",static_cast<int>(kind)); // 0
    EnumeratorValueDescription
    HalfToEven

    Exact represented halves select an even integer.

    HalfAwayFromZero

    Exact halves select the integer with larger magnitude.

    HalfUp

    Exact halves select the integer toward positive infinity.

    HalfDown

    Exact halves select the integer toward negative infinity.

    TowardZero

    Truncate fractional magnitude.

    Ceil

    Smallest represented integer not below the input.

    Floor

    Largest represented integer not above the input.

    #source
    enum class RTPolicy

    Dynamic deadline or fixed period priority, with stable input-order ties. Equal deadlines/periods prefer the earlier input task; jobs of one task run in release order. Task-id numeric order has no scheduling significance.

    Example
    const auto r=dm::algorithms::rt_simulate_work({{7,2,1}},2,dm::algorithms::RTPolicy::earliest_deadline);
std::print("{}\n",r.work.busy_ticks); // 1
    References

    • Liu and Layland (1973), doi:10.1145/321738.321743.

    See also

    rt_simulate_work()

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    earliest_deadline

    Pick the unfinished job with the earliest absolute deadline.

    rate_monotonic

    Pick the unfinished job from the shortest-period task.

    enum class SampleSortStage

    Actual operation performed on one visited subrange.

std::print("{}\n",static_cast<int>(value)); // 0

    At most sixteen keys, including empty root.

    Partition

    Actual sampled split and concatenation before child sorting.

    WholeBucketFallback

    No progress: one bucket contains the complete parent range.

    DepthFallback

    Recursion policy reached: counted std::sort.

    using SccAdjacency = std::vector< std::vector< int > >

std::cout << a.size(); // 2

    Actual secant stopping branch, distinct from a universal convergence guarantee.

    const auto value=dm::algorithms::SecantStop::Residual;
std::print("{}\n",static_cast<int>(value)); // 0

    Actual callback zero or positive residual threshold passed.

    Horizontal

    Stagnation

    ArithmeticRange

    Budget

    #source
    enum class ShuffleCensusRule

    Exact choice-tree models for permutation-law comparisons, without a random generator. FisherYates is the descending shrinking-range algorithm. AllPositions is the deliberately biased model: visit i=0..n-1 and independently choose j=0..n-1. CyclicShift enumerates only the n rotations (one empty output when n=0).

    Example
    const auto c=dm::algorithms::shuffle_choice_census(3,dm::algorithms::ShuffleCensusRule::CyclicShift);
std::cout << c.outcomes << ' ' << c.permutation_counts.size(); // 3 3
    See also

    shuffle_choice_census()

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    FisherYates

    Every shrinking-range choice sequence, with n! outcomes.

    AllPositions

    Every n-step full-range choice sequence, with n^n outcomes (one at zero).

    CyclicShift

    Every rotation, with max(n,1) outcomes; uniform position marginals for n>0.

    Unbounded

    Improving entering column has no pivot coefficient above tolerance.

    IterationLimit

    Improving column remains when requested pivot limit is reached.

    using StablePreferences = std::vector< std::vector< std::size_t > >

    Owned preference rows with favorite first. For n agents each row must be a permutation of0..n-1; the two sides have equal n. Empty sides are allowed. Ties, truncated lists, unequal sizes, capacities and couples are outside this model.

    Example
    dm::algorithms::StablePreferences p{{0,1},{1,0}};
std::cout << p.size(); // 2
    See also

    gale_shapley(), gale_shapley_trace()

    using StrassenMatrix = std::vector< std::vector< double > >

    Own a finite rectangular row-major double matrix for checked multiplication. Rows own their scalars. Rectangularity and finiteness are checked when consumed by a multiplication function.

    dm::algorithms::StrassenMatrix a{{1,2}};
std::print("{}\n",a[0].size()); // 2
    See also

    strassen_run()

    enum class TerrainHeuristic

    Lower bounds on the cost from a cell to the goal.

    EnumeratorValueDescription
    Zero

    \(h=0\): A* becomes Dijkstra's algorithm.

    Euclidean

    Straight-line horizontal distance.

    Octile

    Shortest 8-neighbour distance on an empty grid: \(\max+(\sqrt2-1)\min\) of the axis offsets.

    OctileClimb

    Octile plus climb_cost times the net height still to gain, \(\max(0,z_{goal}-z)\).
